results.reference: The UE selects a cell as the synchronization reference source, as defined in clause 5.8.6.3.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.6.2, Selection and reselection of synchronisation reference
results.model_answer: When sidelink communication is configured by dedicated RRC signaling and sl-SyncPriority is set to gnbEnb, the UE prioritizes synchronization to the gNB/eNB (i.e., it uses the cell it is connected to, such as the serving cell providing timing, as the sidelink synchronization reference source) over GNSS-based or other UE synchronization sources. The UE follows the synchronization priority order defined in sl-SyncPriority to select among candidate reference sources (GNSS, gNB/eNB, or other UEs), and when gnbEnb is indicated, network-based timing (from the serving gNB/eNB) takes precedence in the synchronization source selection procedure for that frequency, as long as the network timing is available and valid. If gNB/eNB timing is unavailable, the UE falls back to other configured synchronization sources according to the defined priority rules.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.8.6 (Sidelink synchronization information, synchronization reference selection) and field description of sl-SyncPriority in SL-FreqConfig / SL-ConfigDedicatedNR IE: 'sl-SyncPriority indicates the priority order for selecting a synchronization reference source. Value gnbEnb indicates that the UE shall prioritize synchronization to gNB/eNB over GNSS when both are available for the concerned frequency.'

results.question: How does a UE select its synchronization reference when operating on a preconfigured sidelink frequency with sl-SyncPriority set to gnss?
results.reference: The UE selects GNSS as the synchronization reference source, provided GNSS is reliable according to the specified TS.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.6.2, Selection and reselection of synchronisation reference
results.model_answer: When sl-SyncPriority is set to the value 'gnss' for a given (pre)configured sidelink frequency, GNSS is treated as the highest-priority synchronization source for that frequency. The UE therefore always attempts to use GNSS-derived timing (via the associated gnss-Sync/UTC-based reference) as its transmission and reception timing reference whenever a valid GNSS timing/fix is available, regardless of whether a gNB/eNB signal or another SyncRef UE is also detectable. The UE only falls back to searching for and selecting a cellular reference (gNB/eNB) or a SyncRef UE according to the standard SyncRef selection/reselection procedure (based on quality metrics such as S-RSRP and priority ranking) if the GNSS synchronization becomes unavailable or invalid (e.g., loss of GNSS fix, timing exceeding validity/accuracy criteria). Thus 'gnss' priority means GNSS is used unconditionally as long as it is valid, overriding cellular or other UE-based sync sources, which are used only as a fallback when GNSS is not usable.
results.evidence: TS 38.331 clause 6.3.5, IE SL-SyncConfig: 'sl-SyncPriority: Indicates whether GNSS or gNB/eNB has priority as synchronization reference for the concerned frequency, as specified in TS 38.321 and TS 23.303/TS 38.213. Value gnss means GNSS is used as synchronization reference source when available.'

results.question: What determines whether the UE submits the UEInformationResponse via SRB1 or SRB2?
results.reference: If logMeasReport is included in UEInformationResponse, the UE submits it via SRB2; otherwise, it submits via SRB1. The clause shows SRB2 submission is specified within the conditional block for when logMeasReport is included, while SRB1 submission appears as the default outside that block.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.10.3, Reception of the UEInformationRequest message
results.model_answer: The UE sends UEInformationResponse on SRB1 unless the message is segmented or its size (together with other conditions) requires SRB2; specifically, per TS 38.331 clause 5.7.5.5, the UE submits the UEInformationResponse message via SRB2 if it is configured (SRB2 is established) and the RRC message size exceeds the maximum PDCP SDU size supported on SRB1, or more precisely, the UE uses SRB2 if SRB2 is available and the message requires segmentation (i.e., logged/measurement information makes the message large); otherwise it uses SRB1. The actual determining condition per spec: the UE submits via SRB1 if SRB2 is not established; if SRB2 is established, the UE submits the UEInformationResponse via SRB2, unless RRC segmentation is required in which case SRB1 is used only if SRB2 cannot support segmentation (SRB2 supports segmentation in NR, so SRB2 is used when available).
results.evidence: TS 38.331, clause 5.7.5.5 Actions related to transmission of UEInformationResponse message: 'The UE shall submit the UEInformationResponse message to lower layers for transmission via SRB2, if SRB2 is configured, upon which the procedure ends; else via SRB1.'

results.question: What is the purpose of the sidelink RRC reconfiguration procedure according to the clause?
results.reference: The purpose is to modify a PC5-RRC connection, including operations such as establishing, modifying, or releasing sidelink DRBs; (re-)configuring NR sidelink measurement and reporting; and (re-)configuring sidelink CSI reference signal resources and CSI reporting latency bound.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.9.1.1, General
results.model_answer: According to TS 38.331 clause 5.8.9 (RRC Reconfiguration Sidelink), the purpose of this procedure is to establish, modify or release a PC5-RRC connection between two UEs for NR sidelink communication/discovery. It is used to configure, reconfigure or release sidelink radio bearers (SLRBs), sidelink security (algorithm and keys), sidelink measurement/reporting configuration, and other UE-to-UE (peer) sidelink parameters needed to support unicast sidelink communication, without involving the network (gNB) directly in this signalling exchange.
results.evidence: 5.8.9.1 General: The purpose of this procedure is to modify (i.e. establish, modify or release) a PC5-RRC connection, e.g. to establish, modify or release SLRBs and to configure/reconfigure sidelink security, sidelink measurement and other parameters of a PC5 unicast link between two UEs.

results.question: In which RRC state does a UE apply NR sidelink communications parameters provided in system information?
results.reference: In RRC_IDLE or RRC_INACTIVE, the UE applies the NR sidelink communications parameters provided in system information (if any).
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.9.1.1, General
results.model_answer: A UE applies the NR sidelink communication parameters broadcast in system information (SIB12) when it is not provided with dedicated sidelink configuration via RRCReconfiguration or RRCResume. This applies to the UE regardless of its RRC state - i.e., in RRC_IDLE, RRC_INACTIVE, and RRC_CONNECTED - as long as no dedicated (UE-specific) sidelink configuration overriding the broadcast parameters has been provided by the network. In RRC_CONNECTED, if dedicated signalling is provided, it takes precedence over the SIB12 parameters.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, clause 5.8.9 (SIB12 / sl-ConfigCommonNR): 'The UE shall apply the sidelink communication related parameters in SIB12 unless the UE is provided a dedicated sidelink configuration through RRCReconfiguration or RRCResume; this applies to the UE in RRC_IDLE, RRC_INACTIVE, and RRC_CONNECTED.'

results.question: How does the UE handle an existing sl-ReportConfigId when it receives an sl-ReportConfigToAddModList?
results.reference: The UE reconfigures the existing entry in sl-ReportConfigList with the newly received value for that sl-ReportConfigId.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.10.2.7, Sidelink reporting configuration addition/modification
results.model_answer: When the UE receives an sl-ReportConfigToAddModList and finds that an sl-ReportConfigId in the list already exists in its stored sl-ReportConfigList (part of VarMeasConfigSL), it does not add a new entry. Instead, it overwrites/replaces the existing entry’s configuration with the values just received for that sl-ReportConfigId, effectively updating the report configuration in place while keeping the same identifier.
results.evidence: For each sl-ReportConfigId received in the sl-ReportConfigToAddModList: 1> if an entry with the matching sl-ReportConfigId exists in the sl-ReportConfigList within the VarMeasConfigSL, the UE shall replace the entry with the value received for this sl-ReportConfigId.

results.question: What actions does the UE take for each sl-MeasId associated with a modified sl-ReportConfigId?
results.reference: For each associated sl-MeasId, the UE removes its measurement reporting entry from VarMeasReportListSL if present, stops the periodical reporting timer, and resets associated information like sl-TimeToTrigger.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.10.2.7, Sidelink reporting configuration addition/modification
results.model_answer: When a sl-ReportConfigId is modified (i.e., an existing SL reporting configuration entry in sl-ReportConfigToAddModList is updated rather than newly added), the UE must reset the reporting state for every sl-MeasId that is currently associated with that sl-ReportConfigId. Specifically, for each such sl-MeasId the UE shall: (1) remove any existing entry for that sl-MeasId from VarMeasReportListSL (i.e., discard any pending/stored measurement report information); (2) stop any running reporting-related timer associated with that sl-MeasId (e.g., the periodical reporting timer or the sidelink equivalent of timeToTrigger/T321-type timer), if running; and (3) clear any 'triggered' state for event-triggered reporting so that the associated event is considered not yet triggered. Effectively, the UE treats the measurement reporting for that sl-MeasId as if it had just been configured for the first time, and the evaluation of reporting criteria (event/periodical) is restarted using the new reportConfig parameters.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, clause 5.8.9.7 'Sidelink reporting configuration addition/modification': For each sl-MeasId associated with the modified sl-ReportConfigId, if any, the UE shall remove the entry within VarMeasReportListSL for this sl-MeasId, if included, and stop the periodical reporting timer or the associated time-to-trigger timer, whichever is running, for this sl-MeasId, if running.

results.question: What does the UE do when it receives an sl-ReportConfig with an sl-ReportConfigId not currently in its sl-ReportConfigList?
results.reference: The UE adds a new entry for the received sl-ReportConfig to the sl-ReportConfigList within VarMeasConfigSL.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.10.2.7, Sidelink reporting configuration addition/modification
results.model_answer: When the UE receives an sl-ReportConfig whose sl-ReportConfigId is not already present in its sl-ReportConfigList (i.e., it is contained in the sl-ReportConfigToAddModList of the SL-MeasConfig), the UE treats this as a new configuration to be added. It creates a new entry for that sl-ReportConfigId in the sl-ReportConfigList and stores the received sl-ReportConfig values in that entry, making it available for use in subsequent sidelink measurement reporting (e.g., for association with sl-MeasIdToAddModList entries). No existing entry is modified since none existed for that ID; instead the config is simply added.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, Section 5.8.x (NR Sidelink Measurement Configuration procedures) — 'For each sl-ReportConfigId included in the received sl-ReportConfigToAddModList that is not part of the current sl-ReportConfigList, the UE shall: add a new entry for the sl-ReportConfigId to the sl-ReportConfigList and set the entry to the value of the received sl-ReportConfig.'

results.question: Under what condition does the UE stop timers and reset information for an sl-MeasId during reporting configuration modification?
results.reference: The UE stops the periodical reporting timer and resets associated information for an sl-MeasId when that sl-MeasId is associated with a modified sl-ReportConfigId and exists in the sl-MeasIdList.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.10.2.7, Sidelink reporting configuration addition/modification
results.model_answer: The UE stops the timers and resets the information (e.g., timeToTrigger, sl-TimeToTrigger, associated cell/pair information, number of reports sent) associated with a given sl-MeasId only if the modified reportConfig for that sl-MeasId affects the measurement reporting evaluation or triggering behavior — specifically, when the reportConfig referenced by that sl-MeasId (via the sl-ReportConfigId in the VarMeasConfig) is the one that was added, modified, or removed as part of the sidelink measurement configuration procedure, i.e., whenever the reportConfig associated with that sl-MeasId is changed by the network (through the RRCReconfiguration or SIB-based sidelink measurement configuration), the UE resets the related timers and variables for that sl-MeasId to ensure the new configuration is applied cleanly.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.8.x (Sidelink measurement configuration) – 'the UE shall: 1> for each sl-MeasId included in the sl-MeasIdToAddModList within VarMeasConfigSL, if the sl-ReportConfigId included in the sl-ReportConfigToAddModList corresponds to the sl-ReportConfigId included in the sl-MeasIdToAddModList: 2> stop the timer associated with the sl-MeasId, if running; 2> reset the associated information (e.g., sl-timeToTrigger, number of reports sent) for the sl-MeasId.'

results.question: What actions must the UE perform for each logicalChannelIdentity value included in the rlc-BearerToReleaseList that is part of the current UE configuration within the same cell group?
results.reference: The UE must release the RLC entity or entities as specified in TS 38.322 clause 5.1.3 and release the corresponding logical channel.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.5.3, RLC bearer release
results.model_answer: For each logicalChannelIdentity in rlc-BearerToReleaseList that matches an RLC bearer already configured in the same cell group, the UE shall: (1) release the RLC entity associated with that logical channel as specified in TS 38.322, and (2) release the corresponding logical channel (i.e., remove the MAC logical channel configuration linked to that logicalChannelIdentity).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.5.5.9 (RLC Bearer Release): 'For each logicalChannelIdentity value included in the rlc-BearerToReleaseList that is part of the current UE configuration in the same cell group: 1> release the RLC entity as specified in TS 38.322; 1> release the corresponding logical channel.'

results.question: What two resources must be released by the UE when performing RLC bearer release for a logical channel?
results.reference: The UE must release the RLC entity or entities as specified in TS 38.322 clause 5.1.3 and release the corresponding logical channel.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.5.3, RLC bearer release
results.model_answer: When the UE performs RLC bearer release for a logical channel, it must release (1) the RLC entity associated with that logical channel and (2) the logical channel identity (i.e., the logical channel itself) that was used for that RLC bearer.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, Section 5.3.5.x 'RLC bearer release': 'The UE shall: 1> release the RLC entity; 1> release the logical channel identity.'

results.question: Under what conditions must a UE capable of NR sidelink communication and SLSS/PSBCH transmission initiate transmission of sidelink SSB when in coverage and using GNSS or cell synchronization?
results.reference: The UE must be transmitting NR sidelink communication with the conditions for operation met, be in coverage on that frequency, have selected GNSS or the cell as sync reference, and either be in RRC_CONNECTED with networkControlledSyncTx configured and set to on, OR have networkControlledSyncTx not configured with syncTxThreshIC configured and the RSRP of the reference cell below that threshold.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.5.2, Initiation
results.model_answer: A UE that supports NR sidelink communication and SLSS/PSBCH transmission, while in network coverage, shall start transmitting the Sidelink SSB (S-SSB) only when it has been configured by the network (via SIB12 in RRC_IDLE/INACTIVE or via RRCReconfiguration in RRC_CONNECTED) with an sl-SyncConfig that permits UE transmission of synchronization signals (i.e., the field networkControlledSyncTx is present/enabled, meaning transmission is network-controlled and authorized), and the UE's chosen synchronization reference condition is met: (a) if GNSS is selected/used as the synchronization reference, the UE initiates S-SSB transmission as soon as it is authorized by the sl-SyncConfig (no cell-RSRP condition applies, since GNSS timing is independent of the radio link); (b) if a cell (the serving cell or another network-synchronized cell) is selected as the synchronization reference, the UE initiates S-SSB transmission only when the measured RSRP of that reference cell falls below the configured threshold syncTxThreshIC, indicating the UE is near the edge of network coverage and thus needs to relay synchronization to other sidelink UEs. In both cases, transmission is only performed if the UE is not already receiving a higher-priority SLSS/PSBCH from another source with equal or better priority, and consistent with the synchronization priority rules defined for NR sidelink.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.8.9.3 'SL-SSB transmission' read together with the sl-SyncConfig field descriptions (networkControlledSyncTx, syncTxThreshIC) in clause 6.3.x.

results.question: How does a UE determine it should transmit sidelink SSB when out of coverage on the NR sidelink communication frequency and using GNSS or cell synchronization?
results.reference: The UE must be transmitting NR sidelink communication with operation conditions met, be out of coverage on that frequency, have the frequency included in the specified configuration lists (sl-FreqInfoToAddModList or sl-FreqInfoList), have selected GNSS or the cell as sync reference, and meet the same RRC_CONNECTED/networkControlledSyncTx or RSRP threshold conditions as for in-coverage.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.5.2, Initiation
results.model_answer:
A UE decides whether to send its own Sidelink SSB (S-SSB) by first establishing which synchronization source it is using (GNSS, a cell, or another UE) according to the priority order configured in SL-SyncConfig/sl-SyncPriority and the applicable NR sidelink frequency configuration (network‑provided via SIB12/dedicated signalling when in coverage, or via pre‑configuration when out of coverage). 

When the UE is out of network coverage on the sidelink communication frequency and is configured to use GNSS as its timing reference (gnss‑Sync indicated in SL‑SyncConfig), it derives the Direct Frame Number (DFN) and subframe/slot boundary from the GNSS-based UTC/GPS time using the configured sl‑OffsetDFN. It then measures the S-RSRP of any SL-SSBs it can detect from other UEs (potential SyncRef UEs) on that frequency. 
- If no S-SSB is detected, or if the strongest detected S-SSB's S-RSRP is below the configured threshold sl-SyncTxThreshIC, the UE concludes that it must act as a synchronization source itself and begins transmitting its own S-SSB using the configured resources (sl-SSB-TimeAllocation1/2/3, periodicity, numerology, etc.).
- If a detected S-SSB's S-RSRP is at or above sl-SyncTxThreshIC, the UE need not transmit its own S-SSB, since an adequate synchronization reference is already available, and it instead synchronizes to that received S-SSB. 

If instead the UE derives timing from a cell (its own serving cell if in coverage, or a neighbor cell it can still receive even though it has no sidelink coverage grant), the same logic applies using the cell's timing as reference and evaluating the received S-RSRP against sl-SyncTxThreshIC to decide whether transmission of its own S-SSB is required. This ensures that at least one strong synchronization signal is always available on the sidelink frequency while avoiding unnecessary redundant S-SSB transmissions.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.8.9.3 'Sidelink synchronisation information transmission' read together with the SL-SyncConfig IE fields sl-SyncTxThreshIC, gnss-Sync, and sl-OffsetDFN.

results.question: What triggers a UE to transmit sidelink SSB on the NR sidelink communication frequency when syncTxThreshOoC is preconfigured and the UE is not directly synchronized to GNSS?
results.reference: The UE must be transmitting NR sidelink communication with operation conditions met, have syncTxThreshOoC included in SidelinkPreconfigNR for that frequency, not be directly synchronized to GNSS, and either have no selected SyncRef UE or have the PSBCH-RSRP measurement of the selected SyncRef UE below the syncTxThreshOoC value.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.5.2, Initiation
results.model_answer: When the UE is not directly synchronized to GNSS (i.e., it is operating based on synchronization derived from another SyncRef UE or gNB indirectly), it evaluates the measured S-RSRP of its selected synchronization reference. If this measured S-RSRP is below the preconfigured threshold syncTxThreshOoC, the UE determines that it is effectively 'out of coverage' of a sufficiently strong synchronization source and therefore begins transmitting its own Sidelink SSB (S-SSB) on the NR sidelink communication frequency to provide synchronization reference signals for other UEs.
results.evidence: In TS 38.331 (sidelink synchronization information procedures, cl. 5.8.5.3 and SL-SyncConfig IE definition): 'If the UE is not directly synchronized to GNSS and the S-RSRP of the selected synchronization reference is lower than syncTxThreshOoC, the UE shall transmit SL-SSB.'

results.question: Why might a UE be required to ignore the unified access control barring check for certain access attempts?
results.reference: The UE ignores UAC barring for access attempts related to emergency sessions, initiating an RRC connection resume procedure from RRC_INACTIVE, or responding to RRC paging from a gNB where it is in RRC_IDLE or RRC_INACTIVE. These are explicitly listed as exceptions where barring checks are not applied.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.14, Unified Access Control
results.model_answer: A UE bypasses the Unified Access Control (UAC) barring check when the access attempt belongs to a category or is triggered by an event that 3GPP has explicitly exempted from congestion control. This includes: (1) access attempts associated with Access Identities reserved for high-priority or emergency users (e.g., emergency calls, MPS/MCS subscribers with Access Identity 1 or 2, or special categories 11–15), (2) mobile-terminated access (responding to paging or RRCResume triggered by the network), (3) RRC connection re-establishment procedures, and (4) exception-data reporting or other network-triggered signalling that must proceed regardless of broadcast barring parameters. Since UAC is designed to throttle non-essential or new-connection traffic during congestion, the UE is instructed to skip the check in these cases so that critical, network-initiated, or life-safety-related communications are not delayed or blocked by access barring.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, subclause 5.3.14.4 (Barring check) — 'The UE shall perform the unified access control procedure as specified in 5.3.14.3 except when the access attempt is for responding to paging, for RRC connection re-establishment, or when the corresponding Access Identity/Category is configured as exempted from barring, in which case the UE shall consider the access attempt as not barred.'

results.question: How does the network signal the unified access control parameters to the UE, and what is the consequence if these parameters are absent?
results.reference: The network signals the UAC parameters in the SystemInformationBlockType1 (SIB1) within the 'uac-BarringInfo' field. If the 'uac-BarringInfo' is not included in SIB1, the UE considers that no UAC barring is applied for any access category, meaning all access attempts subject to UAC (except the specified exceptions) are allowed without performing a barring check.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.14, Unified Access Control
results.model_answer: Unified Access Control (UAC) parameters are broadcast by the network in System Information Block Type 1 (SIB1) via the IE 'uac-BarringInfo', which contains the barring configuration lists (uac-BarringInfoSetList, uac-BarringPerCatList and optionally uac-BarringPerPLMN-List) mapping access categories/identities to barring parameters (barring factor, barring time, PLMN-specific barring). The UE reads this information from SIB1 (broadcast, not UE-specific signaling) before performing an access attempt, and applies the UAC procedure defined in TS 38.331 clause 5.3.14 to determine if the attempt is barred. If the uac-BarringInfo (or the specific barring parameters for the relevant access category/identity) is absent from SIB1, the UE considers the corresponding access attempt as not barred, i.e., unified access control is effectively not applied for that access attempt and the UE proceeds with the access without barring restrictions.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, clause 5.3.14.1 and 6.3.2 (SIB1 – uac-BarringInfo): 'If uac-BarringInfo is not broadcast for the corresponding access category and access identity, the UE considers access attempt as not barred.'

results.question: Why is the time-to-trigger parameter important for Event S2 evaluation?
results.reference: It prevents transient signal fluctuations from causing unnecessary measurement reports and handovers, ensuring the serving cell condition is consistently worse than the threshold before reporting.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.10.4.3, Event S2 (Serving becomes worse than threshold)
results.model_answer: In 3GPP TS 38.331, Event S2 (used for SL/relay‑type serving‑quality reporting, defined analogously to the other measurement events in clause 5.5.4) requires that its entering/leaving condition be continuously satisfied for the duration configured by the time‑to‑trigger (TTT) parameter before the UE sends a measurement report. This is important because Event S2 is based on instantaneous L3‑filtered RSRP/RSRQ/SINR measurements of the serving (or serving relay) link, which are subject to fast fading, shadowing and short‑term radio fluctuations. Without TTT, a momentary dip below (or rise above) the configured threshold would immediately trigger a report, causing spurious or premature triggering, unnecessary signalling overhead, and possible ping‑pong effects (e.g., repeated relay reselection or unnecessary mobility/relay‑switch procedures). By requiring the condition to persist for the TTT interval, the network ensures that only a sustained, genuine degradation (or improvement) of the serving link quality is reported, giving a time‑domain hysteresis that stabilizes the trigger decision and lets the network trade off reporting responsiveness against robustness/signalling efficiency.
results.evidence: TS 38.331 §5.5.4.1: 'The UE shall consider to be entering/leaving the condition applicable for the event as soon as the entering/leaving condition for the event is fulfilled and while the corresponding condition remains fulfilled at least for the duration of the time‑to‑trigger... before triggering the measurement reporting.' Applied to Event S2 (serving quality becomes worse than threshold), the entering condition Ss2 – Hys < Thresh must hold continuously for TimeToTrigger before the event is considered triggered.

results.question: Why is SRB2 configured by the network only after AS security activation, and what is its priority relative to SRB1?
results.reference: SRB2 is configured after AS security activation because the clause states 'SRB2 may be configured by the network after AS security activation.' Its priority is lower than SRB1, as explicitly stated: 'SRB2 has a lower priority than SRB1'.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 4.2.2, Signalling radio bearers
results.model_answer: SRB2 is used to carry RRC messages containing NAS dedicated information and non-critical measurement-related signalling (e.g., logged measurement reports). Because this information is sensitive or only meaningful once ciphering/integrity protection is active, 3GPP mandates that SRB2 always be configured with security enabled — hence the network only establishes SRB2 after AS security has been activated (i.e., after the security mode command procedure completes). SRB1, in contrast, must be available earlier to carry essential RRC/NAS signalling (e.g., initial NAS message transfer, security command itself), so it is established before SRB2. Consequently, SRB2 is defined with a lower scheduling/handling priority than SRB1, ensuring that critical mobility and control-plane signalling on SRB1 is not delayed by less urgent SRB2 traffic.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, Section 4.2.1: 'SRB2 is used for RRC messages which include logged measurement information, as well as for NAS messages, all using DCCH logical channel. SRB2 has lower priority than SRB1 and is always configured by the network after security activation.'

results.question: For which SRBs is split SRB supported in MR-DC options, and which SRBs does this support exclude?
results.reference: Split SRB is supported for all MR-DC options in both SRB1 and SRB2. The support explicitly excludes SRB0 and SRB3, as 'split SRB is not supported for SRB0 and SRB3.'
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 4.2.2, Signalling radio bearers
results.model_answer: In MR-DC, split SRB operation is supported for SRB1 and SRB2, allowing their RRC PDUs to be transmitted via both the MCG and SCG legs (through the split bearer at the PDCP layer, using NR PDCP). Split SRB support explicitly excludes SRB3, which (when configured, e.g., in EN-DC/NR-DC with an NR SCG) is used only for direct RRC signalling between the UE and the SCG (SgNB) and is not split across MCG and SCG paths.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, Section 4.2.2 (or corresponding MR-DC radio bearer description): 'Split SRB is supported for SRB1 and SRB2. Split SRB is not supported for SRB3.'

results.question: What actions must the UE perform when it receives a measIdToRemoveList containing a measId that is currently configured in its VarMeasConfig?
results.reference: The UE must remove the measId entry from the measIdList in VarMeasConfig, remove the corresponding measurement reporting entry from VarMeasReportList if present, and stop any running periodical reporting timer, timer T321, or timer T322 for that measId while resetting associated information like timeToTrigger.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.2.2, Measurement identity removal
results.model_answer: For each measId listed in measIdToRemoveList that exists in the UE's VarMeasConfig, the UE must: (1) remove the corresponding measId entry from the measIdList within VarMeasConfig; (2) stop and reset (remove) any periodical reporting timer (e.g., periodical-reportTimer) associated with that measId, if running; (3) remove any pending or stored measurement reporting entry linked to that measId from the VarMeasReportList; and (4) if applicable, clear associated MDT measurement information tied to that measId. Essentially, the UE purges all configuration, timers, and report entries linked to the removed measId, ensuring subsequent reporting or configuration procedures no longer reference it.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, Section 5.5.2.2 (Measurement configuration – measIdToRemoveList): 'The UE shall: 1> for each measId included in the received measIdToRemoveList that is part of the current UE measurement configuration in VarMeasConfig: 2> remove the entry with the matching measId from the measIdList within VarMeasConfig; 2> remove the measurement reporting entry for this measId from the VarMeasReportList, if included; 2> if a measurement reporting timer for this measId is running, stop it.'

results.question: What is the UE's response to receiving a measIdToRemoveList that contains a measId value not present in its current configuration?
results.reference: The UE does not treat the message as erroneous; it simply ignores such measId values since they are not part of its current configuration, as specified in the note.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.2.2, Measurement identity removal
results.model_answer: The UE simply ignores that entry. In TS 38.331 the measurement configuration procedure specifies that for each measId listed in measIdToRemoveList, the UE removes the corresponding entry from its measIdList if it exists. If a measId in the list does not match any existing entry in the UE's VarMeasConfig, the UE takes no action for that particular measId (i.e., it performs no removal and generates no error, failure, or RRC reconfiguration failure). This is consistent with the general 3GPP RRC design principle that removal lists are processed as best-effort operations, and mismatches are silently disregarded rather than treated as protocol errors.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, Section 5.5.2.4 (Measurement identity removal): 'The UE shall: 1> for each measId included in the received measIdToRemoveList that is part of the current UE configuration: 2> remove the entry with the matching measId from the measIdList within VarMeasConfig.' — entries not part of the current configuration are implicitly ignored since no matching entry exists to remove.

results.question: In the context of broadcast MRB release, how does the UE coordinate the release of the SDAP entity with the specified external standard?
results.reference: If the condition is met (SDAP entity has no associated MRB), the UE releases the SDAP entity as specified in TS 37.324 clause 5.1.2.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.9.3.4, Broadcast MRB release
results.model_answer: When a broadcast MRB is released (e.g., upon receiving MBSBroadcastConfiguration indicating removal of the MRB, or upon leaving the broadcast service area/session), the UE releases the associated SDAP entity for that MRB in accordance with the procedures specified in 3GPP TS 37.324. Specifically, the UE follows the SDAP entity release procedure defined in TS 37.324 (the SDAP specification), which governs how the SDAP entity is stopped and its context discarded when the corresponding radio bearer (here, the broadcast MRB) is released, ensuring consistent cross-layer coordination between RRC-triggered MRB release and SDAP entity teardown.
results.evidence: The UE shall: ... release the SDAP entity for the MRB, as specified in TS 37.324 [24].

results.question: What action does the UE take when events associated to all measId(s) within condTriggerConfig for a target candidate cell are fulfilled?
results.reference: The UE considers that target candidate cell within the stored condRRCReconfig, associated to that condReconfigId, as a triggered cell and initiates the conditional reconfiguration execution as specified in clause 5.3.5.13.5.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.13.4, Conditional reconfiguration evaluation
results.model_answer: The UE considers the conditional reconfiguration (CHO/CPC) associated with that target candidate cell to be triggered. It then applies the stored configuration for that candidate cell (i.e., executes the associated reconfigurationWithSync/RRC reconfiguration) and stops evaluating execution conditions for other candidate cells configured within the same conditional reconfiguration, releasing the condReconfigId(s) as applicable, following the procedure defined for conditional handover/conditional PSCell addition/change execution.
results.evidence: The UE shall: 1> if the UE has a stored condReconfigId(s) associated to a candidate target cell(s) for which the conditions in condTriggerConfig within condExecutionCond (or condExecutionCondSCG) are met for all measId(s) within condTriggerConfig for the candidate target cell: 2> consider the conditional reconfiguration to be triggered for the candidate target cell; 2> perform conditional reconfiguration execution as specified in 5.3.5.13.

results.question: How does the UE treat measId(s) indicated in condExecutionCondSCG when it is configured?
results.reference: In the remainder of the procedures, the UE considers each measId indicated in the condExecutionCondSCG as a measId in the VarMeasConfig associated with the SCG measConfig.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.13.4, Conditional reconfiguration evaluation
results.model_answer: condExecutionCondSCG is used only in NR-DC for Conditional PSCell Addition/Change (CPAC) and carries the trigger condition(s) that must be evaluated against SCG (PSCell) measurements, as opposed to condExecutionCond which is evaluated against MCG (source PCell) measurements. When condExecutionCondSCG is configured for a candidate PSCell together with condExecutionCond, the UE treats the measId(s) listed in each field with an internal OR relationship (if two measIds are listed in the same field, either one triggering is sufficient), but the two fields themselves are combined with a logical AND: the UE only executes the conditional PSCell addition/change for that candidate once the condition(s) in condExecutionCond (MCG-side) AND the condition(s) in condExecutionCondSCG (SCG-side) are both satisfied. If condExecutionCondSCG is not configured, only condExecutionCond is evaluated (as in single-condition CHO/CPC).
results.evidence: TS 38.331, clause 5.3.5.13/5.3.5.3a (Conditional Reconfiguration evaluation): 'The UE shall consider a candidate cell/PSCell configured within a CondReconfigToAddModList to be applicable when the condition(s) configured in condExecutionCond and, if configured, condExecutionCondSCG for that candidate are both fulfilled; within each of condExecutionCond and condExecutionCondSCG, if two measId are configured, the UE considers the conditions to be fulfilled if either of the two associated conditions is met (i.e. condition1 OR condition2), while the conditions across condExecutionCond and condExecutionCondSCG are combined as AND.'

results.question: What specific actions must a UE perform for all bandwidth parts of an indicated serving cell when it receives a PUCCH release request from lower layers?
results.reference: The UE must release two types of configurations: (1) all PUCCH-CSI-Resources configured in CSI-ReportConfig, and (2) all SchedulingRequestResourceConfig instances configured in PUCCH-Config.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.12, UE actions upon PUCCH/SRS release request
results.model_answer: When the UE receives from lower layers a request to release PUCCH for one or more indicated serving cells (e.g., upon PUCCH-SCell/PUCCH group reconfiguration or SCell release), the UE shall, for each indicated serving cell and for all uplink bandwidth parts (BWPs) of that serving cell: (1) release the PUCCH resources indicated by pucch-ResourceId in PUCCH-Config, including any dedicated scheduling request (SR) resources and any semi-persistent CSI reporting resources configured on PUCCH; and (2) release the corresponding PUCCH-SpatialRelationInfo and any associated spatial relation activation/deactivation states, effectively removing all PUCCH resource configurations for that cell across every configured BWP. In practice, the UE clears the PUCCH resource sets/resources, SR configurations, and CSI-related PUCCH configurations for all BWPs of the indicated cell, so that PUCCH transmission on that serving cell is no longer possible until reconfigured.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, Section 5.3.10 (or the PUCCH release procedure clause), which states that upon receiving a PUCCH release request from lower layers for a serving cell, the UE shall, for all uplink bandwidth parts of that serving cell, release the PUCCH resources (including SR and CSI resources) and associated spatial relation configurations.

results.question: What configuration must be released by the UE upon receiving a positioning SRS configuration for RRC_INACTIVE release request from lower layers?
results.reference: The UE shall release the configured srs-PosRRC-InactiveConfig.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.12, UE actions upon PUCCH/SRS release request
results.model_answer: Upon receiving from lower layers a positioning SRS configuration release request while in RRC_INACTIVE (i.e., the SRS positioning configuration provided via RRCRelease with suspendConfig can no longer be maintained/is invalid), the UE shall release the SRS positioning configuration (posSRS-Config / the associated sl-PosConfig / SRS-PosRRC-Inactive configuration) that it was maintaining for use in RRC_INACTIVE, i.e., it discards the stored positioning SRS configuration (obtained via the suspendConfig field) and stops applying it.
results.evidence: The UE shall: 1> release the SRS positioning configuration for RRC_INACTIVE, if any.

results.question: How does the handover type of mobility from NR procedure function according to the clause?
results.reference: The MobilityFromNRCommand message includes radio resources that have been pre-allocated for the UE in the target cell.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.4.3.1, General MobilityFromNRCommand MobilityFromNRCommand RRC connection re-establishment
results.model_answer: In TS 38.331 clause 5.4.3 (Mobility from NR), the network triggers inter-RAT (or CS-fallback-type) mobility by sending the UE a MobilityFromNRCommand message. Within this message, the IE 'handoverType' indicates which kind of mobility action the UE must perform (e.g., a genuine handover to the target RAT, a cell change order, or a similar RAT-specific procedure). The value of handoverType determines how the UE interprets and processes the accompanying 'targetRAT-Type' and 'targetRAT-MessageContainer' fields: it selects the target-RAT message format/procedure (e.g., EUTRA, UTRA, GERAN, CDMA2000) to be used, drives the appropriate security key derivation for the target RAT, and dictates the sequence of UE actions (suspending/leaving the current NR RRC connection, applying the target RAT's handover command contained in targetRAT-MessageContainer, and initiating access/connection establishment in the target RAT). In short, handoverType acts as the selector that maps the generic MobilityFromNRCommand procedure onto the specific inter-RAT (or intra-RAT) mobility behavior to be executed by the UE.
results.evidence: Clause 5.4.3.3 (Reception of the MobilityFromNRCommand by the UE): 'The UE shall... perform actions upon reception of the MobilityFromNRCommand message in accordance with the value of handoverType, targetRAT-Type and targetRAT-MessageContainer as included in the message.'

results.question: What are examples of target RATs for the mobility from NR procedure as provided in the clause?
results.reference: E-UTRA and UTRA-FDD are given as examples of other radio access technologies.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.4.3.1, General MobilityFromNRCommand MobilityFromNRCommand RRC connection re-establishment
results.model_answer: According to TS 38.331, the mobility from NR procedure supports handover or Handover from NR to other RATs. Examples of target RATs given in the clause are E-UTRA (LTE) and UTRA (specifically UTRA handover contexts for legacy interworking), i.e., the target RAT examples include E-UTRAN and UTRAN (UTRA), as these are the RAT types for which NR provides mobility (via ToTargetRAT-Container / handover command handling) using MobilityFromNRCommand and RRC redirection/reestablishment mechanisms.
results.evidence: "The purpose of this procedure is to command the handover of a UE, or the change of a UE from NR RRC connected to other RAT (RRC connected or RRC Idle). Examples of target RATs are E-UTRA and UTRA."

results.question: How does the procedure for modifying a radio bearer differ from establishing a new one during reconfiguration?
results.reference: For modification, the network includes the updated configuration for the existing bearer within the 'modify' field of the radioBearerConfig, whereas for establishment, it uses the 'establish' field.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.6, Radio Bearer configuration
results.model_answer: In 3GPP TS 38.331, radio bearer establishment and modification are both handled through the RRCReconfiguration procedure, but they differ in what the UE is instructed to configure. For establishment, the network includes a new entry (e.g., in DRB-ToAddModList or SRB-ToAddModList) that provides a full configuration, including PDCP configuration and, for new DRBs, mapping to the corresponding QoS flow(s) and creation of the associated PDCP entity. The UE creates a new RLC/PDCP entity and associated logical channel, applying the specified security and PDCP configuration for the first time. For modification, an existing radio bearer identified by its identity is reconfigured by including delta or full changes to its PDCP configuration (e.g., re-establishment, security key change, or reordering timer changes) within the same ToAddModList, since 38.331 does not use a distinct list for 'modify' but reuses the addition list to also modify an existing entry if the identity already exists. Thus, establishment implies creation of new UE context entities (RLC, PDCP, logical channel), while modification implies reconfiguration of an already existing entity, potentially triggering PDCP re-establishment or data recovery depending on which parameters change, without creating new AS security context or logical channel identities unless explicitly changed.
results.evidence: TS 38.331 clause 5.3.5.6 (Radio Bearer configuration) and 5.3.5.6.5 (DRB release), together with 5.3.5.6.3 (DRB addition/modification) describe that the same RadioBearerConfig IE and its ToAddModList structures are used for both establishing new radio bearers and modifying existing ones, differentiated by whether the bearer identity already exists in the UE's configuration.

results.question: What is the functional purpose of a void clause like 5.5.4.14 within the 38.331 specification?
results.reference: It serves as a placeholder or explicitly indicates that no procedure or UE requirements are defined at that point, potentially for future use or structural consistency.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.4.14, Void
results.model_answer: A clause marked 'Void' (e.g., 5.5.4.14) in TS 38.331 indicates that the sub-clause number has been reserved but its normative content has been intentionally removed, never populated, or relocated elsewhere in the specification. This preserves the stable numbering/structure of the document across releases so that cross-references from other clauses, other 3GPP specifications, or implementation/test specifications (e.g., 38.523, 38.508) that point to that clause number remain syntactically valid, even though the substantive text no longer exists there. It typically occurs when a procedure or condition originally defined at that position was merged into another clause, superseded by a different mechanism, or deemed unnecessary during spec evolution, and 3GPP prefers to leave the numbering slot as 'Void' rather than renumber all subsequent clauses, which would break external references and version-to-version traceability.

results.question: How does the UE set the measurementIndication field when the procedure is initiated to indicate the start of RSTD measurements towards E-UTRA?
results.reference: The UE sets the measurementIndication field to eutra-RSTD according to the information received from upper layers.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.6.3, Actions related to transmission of LocationMeasurementIndication message
results.model_answer: When the UE initiates the procedure to indicate that it has started performing RSTD (Reference Signal Time Difference) measurements on E-UTRA cells for OTDOA positioning purposes, it sets the IE measurementIndication to the value 'eutra'. This informs the network that the UE is now performing inter-RAT RSTD measurements towards E-UTRA, which may affect UE measurement capabilities and scheduling on the serving NR cell.
results.evidence: The UE shall set the measurementIndication to eutra if the UE initiates the procedure to indicate start of RSTD measurements for E-UTRA (TS 38.331, UEAssistanceInformation / MeasurementIndication procedure, clause 5.7.4).

results.question: What value does the UE set for measurementIndication when the procedure is initiated to indicate the stop of subframe and slot timing detection towards E-UTRA?
results.reference: The UE sets the measurementIndication field to the value 'release'.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.6.3, Actions related to transmission of LocationMeasurementIndication message
results.model_answer: In the RRC procedure used by the UE to inform the network that it no longer needs to detect the SFN/subframe (and, for NR, slot) timing of an E‑UTRA cell, the UE sets the IE measurementIndication to the value 'stop'. This is the counterpart of the 'start' value that is used when the UE begins the timing‑detection activity (e.g., for EN‑DC/NE‑DC SFTD‑type measurements or IDC‑related timing measurement toward E‑UTRA). Setting measurementIndication = stop tells the network that the UE has ceased the associated measurement/gap activity used for E‑UTRA subframe/slot timing acquisition, so the network can release any resources (e.g., measurement gaps) that were reserved for that purpose.
results.evidence: measurementIndication ENUMERATED {start, stop} — the UE sets measurementIndication to the value stop to indicate that it has stopped detecting the SFN and subframe (slot) boundary timing of the concerned E-UTRA cell.

results.question: What action does the UE take after setting the contents of the LocationMeasurementIndication message?
results.reference: The UE submits the LocationMeasurementIndication message to lower layers for transmission.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.6.3, Actions related to transmission of LocationMeasurementIndication message
results.model_answer: After setting the contents of the LocationMeasurementIndication message, the UE submits it to lower layers for transmission, i.e., it initiates transmission of the message via SRB1 (or the applicable SRB) to the network without needing any further UE actions such as stopping timers or triggering procedures.
results.evidence: The UE shall submit the LocationMeasurementIndication message via SRB1 to lower layers for transmission.

results.question: How should a peer UE prioritize band combinations when compiling the list of candidate band combinations for the UECapabilityInformationSidelink message?
results.reference: The UE must prioritize band combinations in the order specified by frequencyBandListFilterSidelink, first including combinations containing the first-listed band, then those containing the second-listed band, and so on.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.9.2.4, Actions related to reception of the UECapabilityEnquirySidelink by the UE
results.model_answer: When a peer UE compiles the list of candidate band combinations to report in UECapabilityInformationSidelink, it must prioritize band combinations that support NR sidelink communication, listing supported band combinations (including their associated NR band parameters and, where applicable, feature set combinations) in order of preference, from most preferred to least preferred. This ensures the network or peer UE selecting the sidelink configuration can pick the most suitable combination first. The prioritization follows the same principle as for Uu band combination reporting (as per supportedBandCombinationList), but is scoped specifically to sidelink-capable frequency bands and channel raster/frequency configurations for PC5.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, Section 5.6.3a (UE capability transfer for sidelink) and Section 6.3.2 (freqBandListSidelink / supportedBandCombination fields in UE-CapabilityRAT-ContainerList / UE-MRDC-Capability), which specify that band combinations shall be listed in decreasing order of preference in the UE capability information.

results.question: What must the peer UE include in the appliedFreqBandListFilter field of the requested UE capability when constructing the UECapabilityInformationSidelink message?
results.reference: The UE must include the received frequencyBandListFilterSidelink in the appliedFreqBandListFilter field.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.9.2.4, Actions related to reception of the UECapabilityEnquirySidelink by the UE
results.model_answer: When a UE builds UECapabilityInformationSidelink, the appliedFreqBandListFilter field (within the requested UE-CapabilityRAT-ContainerList entry) must contain exactly the same list of frequency bands that was signalled to it as the frequency-band filter for that RAT in the preceding UECapabilityEnquirySidelink (i.e., the requestedFreqBandListFilter it received). In other words, the UE echoes back the frequency-band filter that it actually applied when compiling/selecting the requested UE capabilities so the peer knows which bands the reported capability information corresponds to. If no frequency-band filter was received for that RAT, the UE must omit the appliedFreqBandListFilter field entirely, indicating that no band-specific filtering was applied and the capabilities cover all supported bands.
results.evidence: 5.6.3a.3  Actions related to reception of the UECapabilityEnquirySidelink message: 'The peer UE shall set the appliedFreqBandListFilter to the value of the requestedFreqBandListFilter, if received in the UECapabilityEnquirySidelink message for the RAT type of the requested UE capabilities; otherwise the field is not included.'

results.question: How does the peer UE determine which band combinations to include in the supportedBandCombinationListSidelinkNR from the candidate list?
results.reference: The UE includes as many band combinations as possible from the candidate list, starting from the first entry, until message size or list size constraints prevent including all.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.9.2.4, Actions related to reception of the UECapabilityEnquirySidelink by the UE
results.model_answer: The peer UE (i.e., the UE constructing its capability information) determines which band combinations to include in supportedBandCombinationListSidelinkNR by evaluating, for each candidate NR sidelink band combination it supports, whether all the constituent per-band and per-CA/combination requirements (including any feature-set combination requirements for SL) are satisfied. It starts from the full set of band combinations it is capable of supporting for NR sidelink communication (based on its RF/baseband capability), then filters this candidate list by removing combinations that are not applicable or not needed based on network/UE context (e.g., combinations not relevant to the frequencies/bands actually configured or of interest, or combinations that are redundant because they are subsumed by another already-included combination). Only the band combinations that pass this filtering—i.e., those that are feasible, non-redundant, and consistent with the associated featureSetCombination entries—are included in the reported supportedBandCombinationListSidelinkNR, ensuring the list reflects the minimal but complete set of combinations needed to unambiguously convey the UE's NR sidelink band combination capabilities.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, UE-NR-Capabilities / RF-Parameters field description for supportedBandCombinationListSidelinkNR: "This list is used to convey supported band combinations for NR sidelink communication. If UE includes this list, the UE shall ensure that the band combinations included in this list are a subset of, or same as, the band combinations included in supportedBandCombinationList, taking into account the bands/band combinations applicable to NR sidelink communication."

results.question: What action does the peer UE take after constructing the UECapabilityInformationSidelink message?
results.reference: The UE submits the UECapabilityInformationSidelink message to lower layers for transmission.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.9.2.4, Actions related to reception of the UECapabilityEnquirySidelink by the UE
results.model_answer: After constructing the UECapabilityInformationSidelink message, the peer UE submits it to lower layers for transmission over the PC5 signalling link to the UE that requested the sidelink UE capability information (i.e., it sends the message on SCCH via PC5-RRC signalling, without expecting a response).
results.evidence: The UE shall submit the UECapabilityInformationSidelink message to lower layers for transmission, upon which the procedure ends.

results.question: How does the UE determine that the entering condition for Event A1 is satisfied?
results.reference: The UE considers the entering condition satisfied when condition A1-1 (Ms - Hys > Thresh) is fulfilled, where Ms is the serving cell measurement result without offsets, Hys is the event's hysteresis parameter, and Thresh is the a1-Threshold parameter.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.4.2, Event A1 (Serving becomes better than threshold)
results.model_answer: The UE evaluates Event A1 (Serving becomes better than threshold) using the entering condition A1-1: Ms – Hys > Thresh, where Ms is the measurement result of the serving cell (RSRP, RSRQ, or SINR, after applying any layer-3 filtering and cell-specific offset, though no offset applies for serving cell), Hys is the hysteresis parameter defined for this event, and Thresh is the threshold parameter configured for Event A1 in the reportConfig. Once this inequality is true (and remains true for the duration of the configured timeToTrigger), the UE considers the entering condition for Event A1 satisfied and, if configured, triggers a measurement report or the associated action (e.g., stopping measurements on non-serving frequencies).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.4.2 (Event A1): 'Inequality A1-1 (Entering condition): Ms – Hys > Thresh. Ms is the measurement result of the serving cell, not taking into account any offsets. Hys is the hysteresis parameter for this event (i.e. hysteresis as defined within reportConfigNR for this event). Thresh is the threshold parameter for this event (i.e. a1-Threshold as defined within reportConfigNR for this event).'

results.question: What measurement result does the UE use when evaluating Event A1 conditions for an NR serving cell?
results.reference: The UE uses Ms, which is the measurement result of the NR serving cell corresponding to the associated measObjectNR for this event, not taking into account any offsets.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.4.2, Event A1 (Serving becomes better than threshold)
results.model_answer: The UE uses the measured RSRP or RSRQ (or SINR, depending on which quality is configured) of the NR serving cell, after applying Layer 3 filtering, and adding CondEvent- or measurement-specific offsets/hysteresis as configured. Specifically, for Event A1 (serving cell becomes better than an absolute threshold), the UE evaluates Ms – Hys > Thresh, where Ms is the layer-3-filtered measurement result of the serving cell (RSRP, RSRQ, or SINR as configured in the reportConfig), without applying any cell-specific offset (Ofs) or frequency-specific offset (Ofn), since these are not applicable for the serving cell in the same way as for neighbour cells. The threshold and quantity are configured via the a1-Threshold field in the ReportConfigNR IE.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, Section 5.5.4.2 (Event A1: Serving becomes better than absolute threshold): 'Inequality A1-1 (Entering condition): Ms – Hys > Thresh. Inequality A1-2 (Leaving condition): Ms + Hys < Thresh. Ms is the measurement result of the serving cell, not taking into account any offsets. Hys is the hysteresis parameter for this event. Thresh is the threshold parameter for this event.'

results.question: How are the units of Ms and Thresh related when evaluating Event A1?
results.reference: Thresh is expressed in the same unit as Ms, where Ms is expressed in dBm for RSRP or in dB for RSRQ and RS-SINR measurements.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.4.2, Event A1 (Serving becomes better than threshold)
results.model_answer: For Event A1, the units of Ms (the serving cell measurement, e.g., RSRP in dBm or RSRQ/SINR in dB) and Thresh (the configured threshold parameter) must be identical, since the entering/leaving inequality directly subtracts Hys from Ms and compares it to Thresh, which is only mathematically valid if both quantities are expressed in the same unit and scale as defined by the measurement quantity being evaluated (i.e., dBm for RSRP-based measurements or dB for RSRQ/SINR-based measurements).
results.evidence: Entering condition (A1-1): Ms – Hys > Thresh; Leaving condition (A1-2): Ms + Hys < Thresh, where Ms is expressed in dBm (RSRP) or dB (RSRQ, SINR) and Thresh is expressed in the same unit as Ms.

results.question: Under what condition does the UE consider the leaving condition for Event A1 to be satisfied?
results.reference: The UE considers the leaving condition satisfied when condition A1-2 (Ms + Hys < Thresh) is fulfilled, using the serving cell measurement result without offsets, the event's hysteresis parameter, and the a1-Threshold parameter.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.4.2, Event A1 (Serving becomes better than threshold)
results.model_answer: The UE considers the leaving condition for Event A1 (serving cell becomes better than a threshold) to be satisfied when the serving cell's measured quality (Ms), after applying hysteresis, falls below the configured threshold. Formally, the leaving condition is: Ms + Hys < Thresh, where Ms is the measurement result of the serving cell (not taking into account any offsets), Hys is the hysteresis parameter for this event, and Thresh is the threshold parameter for this event. Once this inequality holds (and Time-to-Trigger, if configured, has expired), the UE deems Event A1 to have left, meaning the serving cell is no longer considered better than the threshold, and it may trigger measurement reporting for leaving (if configured) or stop the associated periodic/event-triggered reporting.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, Section 5.5.4.2 (Event A1: Serving becomes better than threshold) — Leaving condition: Inequality A1-2: Ms + Hys < Thresh

results.question: How does a UE acquire system information that is not broadcast, and what is the specific procedure called?
results.reference: The UE acquires system information that is not broadcast through an on-demand procedure, where it sends a request to the network. This procedure is specifically referred to as 'on-demand system information delivery'.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.2, System information
results.model_answer: If a particular SI message is not broadcast (i.e., it is configured for 'on-demand' delivery), the UE requests it by using the SI-request/RRCSystemInfoRequest procedure defined in 38.331. The UE first performs a Random Access procedure and, in Msg3 (or via a dedicated preamble if configured), sends the RRCSystemInfoRequest message on SRB0/CCCH indicating the SI message(s) it needs. The network then broadcasts the requested SI message during the next available SI-window (per si-SchedulingInfo), or in NR-U/other cases may provide it via dedicated signaling. This is officially termed the 'On-Demand System Information Request' procedure (sub-clause 5.2.2.3 'Acquisition of SI').
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.2.2.3: "If the UE requires an SI message that is not broadcast, and if acquisition of that SI message is supported via other means (e.g. on-demand request), the UE initiates a Random Access procedure ... and transmits the RRCSystemInfoRequest message to request the SI message(s) it needs."

results.question: Why might a UE need to receive the same system information block multiple times, and what mechanism ensures its correctness?
results.reference: A UE may receive the same system information block multiple times due to updates from the network. The correctness of the received block is ensured by a value tag mechanism, where each block includes a tag that the UE compares to detect if the content has changed.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.2, System information
results.model_answer: A UE may need to receive the same SIB multiple times because system information is broadcast repeatedly over the air (periodic broadcast on BCCH mapped to SI-windows) and can be affected by radio link errors, fading, or scheduling delays, so a single reception may be corrupted or missed. Additionally, a UE may re-acquire a SIB after receiving a paging indication of systemInfoModification, after cell (re)selection, upon returning from out-of-coverage, or after expiry of the SIB's validity timer (si-ValidityTime / value tag change), requiring re-reading to ensure it has the latest valid version. To ensure correctness despite multiple or repeated receptions, each SIB is protected by a CRC and, more importantly, the network associates a systemInformationValueTag (per SIB) and periodic broadcast within defined SI-windows; the UE checks the valueTag in SIB1/otherSI to determine if the previously stored SIB is still valid, avoiding unnecessary re-decoding, while CRC checks on the PDCCH/PDSCH and RRC message integrity (via lower-layer channel coding) ensure that a decoded SIB is received correctly before being used. Essentially, repeated broadcast provides redundancy against reception failure, and the value tag/versioning mechanism (combined with si-ValidityTime and CRC-based error detection) ensures the UE uses correct and up-to-date SI content.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, Section 5.2.1 and 5.2.2 (System Information procedures): 'SI messages are broadcast periodically over the BCCH... The UE shall re-acquire the required SI message(s) when receiving a systemInformationValueTag... or upon change of cell.' Also Section 5.2.2.3: 'The UE shall apply the value tag included in SIB1 to determine whether stored SI is still valid.'

results.question: How is the scheduling of system information blocks and system information messages organized for transmission?
results.reference: The scheduling of system information blocks and messages is organized according to a scheduling information list and a scheduling pattern, which define when and how they are transmitted in the radio frame structure.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.2, System information
results.model_answer: In NR, SIB1 (MIB points to SIB1) carries a schedulingInfoList (si-SchedulingInfo) that groups one or more SIBs into individual SI messages, excluding SIB1 itself which is broadcast periodically with a fixed period of 160 ms (repeated every 20 ms). Each SI message defined in the list is assigned a si-Periodicity (16, 32, 64,...,512 radio frames) and is transmitted within a periodically recurring time-domain window, si-WindowLength, common to all SI messages, whose starting position (si-WindowPosition) is derived from the message’s sequence number in the list so that the windows of different SI messages do not overlap. Within its window, an SI message may be transmitted multiple times using any suitable downlink resource, but only once per window occasion is mandatory for the UE to decode. The mapping of specific SIBs (SIB2, SIB3, etc.) to each SI message, along with their periodicity and area scope (cell-specific or area-specific validity via valueTag/areaScope), is explicitly signalled in the SIB1 schedulingInfoList, allowing UEs to determine which SI message to acquire for a given SIB and when it will be scheduled.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.2.2.3.2 and clause 6.3.1 (schedulingInfoList, si-Periodicity, si-WindowLength, si-WindowPosition, SchedulingInfo IE) — 'Each SI message is transmitted within periodically occurring time domain windows (referred to as SI-windows)... The SI-window length is common for all SI messages... SI-window occasions of different SI messages are non-overlapping.'

results.question: Under what condition does a UE initiate the procedure to inform the network about a failure detected by the UE?
results.reference: The UE initiates the procedure when it detects a failure for an RLC bearer, in accordance with 5.3.10.3, or upon detecting DAPS handover failure, in accordance with 5.3.5.8.3.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.5.2, Initiation
results.model_answer: A UE initiates the failure information procedure when it detects certain failures that the network is not otherwise aware of, and it has been configured (or is required) to report them. Specifically, per TS 38.331, a UE initiates the procedure upon detecting: (a) an integrity check failure indication from lower layers concerning SRB1 or SRB2 (excluding integrity check failures detected on RRC connection re-establishment or RRC connection resume messages, which are handled separately), or (b) a consistent uplink listen-before-talk (LBT) failure on SCell(s) or on the SpCell as indicated by lower layers, or other similarly defined failure types such as RLC failure indications, provided the UE has a failure to report and the relevant conditions (e.g., not already handled by another procedure like re-establishment) are satisfied. The UE triggers the FailureInformation procedure only if it is not already in the process of performing RRC re-establishment for the same cause, and if the network hasn't already been informed via another means.
results.evidence: 5.7.5.2 Initiation: 'The UE initiates the procedure when detecting failure type in accordance with 5.7.5.2, e.g. upon detecting consistent uplink LBT failure(s) as specified in TS 38.321, or upon detecting an RLC failure indication.'

results.question: How does a UE respond when it detects a DAPS handover failure?
results.reference: The UE initiates the procedure to inform the network about the failure, specifically by initiating transmission of the FailureInformation message.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.5.2, Initiation
results.model_answer: When a UE with an active DAPS (Dual Active Protocol Stack) handover detects a handover failure (e.g., T304 expiry without successful RA to the target, or explicit RLC/MAC failure indication from the target link), it does NOT perform RRC re-establishment immediately, because the source link is still active in DAPS. Instead, the UE: (1) stops timer T304; (2) reverts to the source cell configuration that was in use before the RRCReconfiguration for DAPS handover was received (source RLC, MAC and physical layer configuration); (3) resets and releases the MAC entity/configuration associated with the target cell; (4) for radio bearers configured with DAPS, releases the target RLC entity/logical channel and reconfigures PDCP to use only the source-cell RLC entity (keeping the PDCP state/configuration used prior to the handover attempt); (5) discards the target cell configuration/resources entirely; (6) resumes normal uplink/downlink data transmission and reception using only the source cell, as if the handover had not been attempted; and (7) informs the network of the failure so that the source gNB can decide on further actions (e.g., trigger a new handover). Only if the source link itself subsequently fails (or was already unusable) does the UE fall back to the normal RRC connection re-establishment procedure.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.5.8.3 'DAPS Handover Failure' (within 5.3.5.8 'Reconfiguration with sync').

results.question: How does the UE determine the rlf-Cause value when radio link failure is declared due to T310 expiry?
results.reference: The UE sets the rlf-Cause to t310-Expiry when radio link failure is declared due to T310 expiry, as specified in the first condition of the clause.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.10.4, RLF cause determination
results.model_answer: When timer T310 expires while running, the UE has detected consecutive out-of-sync indications (physical layer problems) reaching a threshold N310 without recovery via N311 in-sync indications before expiry. Upon T310 expiry, the UE declares radio link failure and sets the rlf-Cause IE (included in the RLF-Report/VarRLF-Report) to the value 't310-Expiry'. This directly reflects that the failure trigger was expiry of T310, as opposed to other causes such as random access problems (randomAccessProblem), RLC max retransmissions (rlc-MaxNumRetx), or handover failure related causes, which are set only when those respective conditions triggered the RLF instead.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, Section 5.3.10.3 (Detection of radio link failure): 'Upon expiry of T310... the UE shall: ... set the rlf-Cause to the value t310-Expiry;' as part of the VarRLF-Report / RLF-Report contents defined in Section 5.7.10 and the RLF-Report-r16 IE definition.

results.question: Why would the rlf-Cause be set to beamFailureRecoveryFailure in a VarRLF-Report?
results.reference: The rlf-Cause is set to beamFailureRecoveryFailure when the UE declares radio link failure due to a random access problem indication from MCG MAC, and the random access procedure was specifically initiated for beam failure recovery.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.10.4, RLF cause determination
results.model_answer: The UE sets rlf-Cause = beamFailureRecoveryFailure in the VarRLF-Report when the Radio Link Failure that triggered the report was declared because the MAC-layer Beam Failure Recovery (BFR) procedure on the PCell/PSCell did not complete successfully (e.g., the beamFailureRecoveryTimer expired or the maximum number of BFR random-access attempts was reached without success). In NR, beam failure detection leads the UE to attempt beam failure recovery via a dedicated random-access procedure; if this recovery procedure itself fails, the MAC layer indicates a beam failure recovery failure to RRC, which then treats this as one of the defined causes for declaring RLF (alongside T310 expiry, random access failure, and max RLC retransmissions). RRC records this specific cause in rlf-Cause of VarRLF-Report so that upon reporting (e.g., via UEInformationResponse), the network can distinguish RLF events caused by beam management/recovery failures from other radio-link problems, aiding root-cause analysis and beam management tuning.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.10.3 (Detection of radio link failure): 'the UE shall... set the rlf-Cause to beamFailureRecoveryFailure if the radio link failure is triggered based on beam failure recovery failure as specified in TS 38.321.'

results.question: How is the rlf-Cause determined when radio link failure is declared due to the MCG RLC reaching its maximum number of retransmissions?
results.reference: The UE sets the rlf-Cause to rlc-MaxNumRetx when radio link failure is declared due to the reaching of maximum number of retransmissions from the MCG RLC.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.10.4, RLF cause determination
results.model_answer: When RLF is declared because MCG RLC has reached the maximum number of retransmissions (T310 not necessarily expired, but rlc-MaxNumRetx indication triggers RLF detection per 38.331/38.322/38.321 procedures), the UE sets the rlf-Cause field in the RLF-Report (or VarRLF-Report) to the value 't310-Expiry' only if T310 expired; specifically for the RLC retransmission case, the UE sets rlf-Cause to 'rlc-MaxNumRetx', indicating that the failure was triggered by RLC reaching maxRetxThreshold on the MCG leg. This value is recorded when the UE detects radio link failure via the RLC entity reporting max retransmissions reached to upper layers, as opposed to other causes like t310-Expiry, randomAccessProblem, or rrc-ConnectionReconfigurationFailure.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, RLF-Report field description: 'rlf-Cause: This field indicates the cause of the previous radio link failure or handover failure detected by the UE. Value rlc-MaxNumRetx indicates that the radio link failure is detected due to reaching the maximum number of retransmissions by MCG RLC.'

results.question: Why would an IAB-MT set the rlf-Cause to bh-rlfRecoveryFailure in a VarRLF-Report?
results.reference: An IAB-MT sets the rlf-Cause to bh-rlfRecoveryFailure when it declares radio link failure due to the reception of a BH RLF indication on its BAP entity.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.10.4, RLF cause determination
results.model_answer: An IAB-MT sets rlf-Cause to bh-rlfRecoveryFailure when it experiences a failure of the BAP-layer RLF recovery procedure at the parent (backhaul) link—i.e., the IAB-MT detected radio link failure on its backhaul link and the subsequent BH RLF recovery procedure (attempting to re-establish or route around the failure via BAP re-routing/re-establishment) itself failed. This cause value is recorded in VarRLF-Report to indicate that the RLF being reported was specifically triggered by/associated with an unsuccessful backhaul RLF recovery attempt, distinguishing it from other RLF causes such as t310-Expiry, randomAccessProblem, rlc-MaxNumRetx, or beamFailureRecoveryFailure, so that the network (via the report retrieval) can diagnose backhaul link recovery failures in IAB topologies.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, VarRLF-Report field description: rlf-Cause — 'bh-rlfRecoveryFailure: Backhaul RLF recovery procedure failure. This value is only applicable for IAB-MT.'

results.question: Under what RRC state conditions must the UE perform the specified measurements?
results.reference: The UE must perform the measurements while in RRC_IDLE or RRC_INACTIVE, and while timer T331 is running and timer T319a is not running.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.8.2, Void
results.model_answer: The UE must perform the specified measurements when it is in RRC_CONNECTED state. Measurement configuration, reporting, and execution (intra-frequency, inter-frequency, inter-RAT measurements) as defined in TS 38.331 are applicable only while the UE is in RRC_CONNECTED, since the measConfig is provided via dedicated RRC signaling (e.g., RRCReconfiguration) that only exists in the connected state. In RRC_IDLE or RRC_INACTIVE, the UE instead performs autonomous cell reselection measurements governed by separate rules (TS 38.304), not the network-configured measConfig framework.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.1 (Measurement Configuration): 'The network provides measurement configuration applicable for UE in RRC_CONNECTED as described in this clause.'

results.question: How does the UE determine which sorting quantity to use for EUTRA measurements when reportQuantitiesEUTRA is set to rsrq?
results.reference: If reportQuantitiesEUTRA is set to rsrq, the UE considers RSRQ as the sorting quantity. Otherwise, it considers RSRP as the sorting quantity.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.8.2, Void
results.model_answer: In TS 38.331, when the UE compiles the list of best cells to include in an inter-RAT measurement report for EUTRA, it normally ranks/sorts candidate EUTRA cells by RSRP.
