However, if the ReportConfigInterRAT field reportQuantitiesEUTRA is configured to the single value 'rsrq' (i.e., only RSRQ is requested, not RSRP or both), the UE uses RSRQ instead of RSRP as the sorting (ranking) quantity for selecting and ordering the EUTRA cells to be reported. This ensures the sorting metric is consistent with the quantity the network actually wants reported, rather than defaulting to RSRP when RSRP is not part of the requested report content.
results.evidence: For EUTRA and UTRA, cells are sorted based on RSRP, unless reportQuantitiesEUTRA (or reportQuantityUTRA) is set to rsrq, in which case cells are sorted based on RSRQ.

results.question: Under what condition must a UE that is already receiving data via broadcast MRB initiate the MCCH information acquisition procedure due to MCCH information modification?
results.reference: The UE must initiate the procedure upon receiving a notification that the MCCH information has changed due to MCCH information modification other than changes caused by the start of new MBS sessions.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.9.2.2, Initiation
results.model_answer: A UE that is already receiving data via one or more broadcast MRBs must (re-)initiate the MCCH information acquisition procedure whenever it becomes aware that the MCCH content it is currently using is going to change, i.e. when it receives an MCCH change/modification notification (signalled via the PDCCH Short Message / paging indication such as mcch-Update-r17, or by detecting a change in the MCCH value tag / repetition at a modification period boundary) for the MBS broadcast service it is receiving. In that case the UE continues to use the previously acquired MCCH configuration to keep receiving the concerned MTCH(s)/MRB(s) until the start of the next MCCH modification period, and at that boundary it triggers reception (acquisition) of the updated MCCH information so that it can apply the new scheduling/configuration for the broadcast MRB(s).
results.evidence: TS 38.331 clause 5.8.13 (MCCH information acquisition for MBS broadcast) – 'If the UE receives an MCCH information change notification while receiving broadcast MRB(s), it shall continue using the current MCCH information until the next MCCH modification period boundary, at which point it shall initiate the MCCH information acquisition procedure to acquire the updated MCCH information.'

results.question: What triggers a UE interested in MBS broadcast services to apply the MCCH information acquisition procedure upon entering a cell that provides SIB20?
results.reference: The trigger is the act of entering the cell providing SIB20, which can occur during events such as powering on or following UE mobility.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.9.2.2, Initiation
results.model_answer: A UE that is interested in receiving MBS broadcast services applies the MCCH information acquisition procedure whenever it enters a cell providing SIB20 broadcast configuration (i.e., SIB20 contains MBS broadcast/MCCH scheduling information) and, upon acquiring SIB20, is interested in at least one broadcast service (TMGI) indicated as being provided via MCCH in that cell (or the UE cannot determine from SIB20 alone whether the service is configured, so it must read MCCH). Essentially, the trigger is UE interest in an MBS broadcast service combined with the cell broadcasting SIB20 with MCCH scheduling info (mcch-Config), causing the UE to start monitoring/acquiring MCCH per the acquisition procedure.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, clause 5.x (MCCH information acquisition) — 'Upon entering a cell broadcasting SIB20 that includes mcch-Config, a UE interested in receiving MBS broadcast service(s) shall apply the MCCH information acquisition procedure to acquire the MBS broadcast configuration.'

results.question: How does an L2 U2N Relay UE configure RLC channels upon establishing a PC5-RRC connection with another L2 U2N Relay UE?
results.reference: It applies the RLC specified configuration for SL-RLC0 as per clause 9.1.1.4 and the RLC default configuration for SL-RLC1 as per clause 9.2.4.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.9.7.2, PC5 Relay RLC channel addition/modification
results.model_answer: When an L2 U2N Relay UE establishes a PC5-RRC connection with a peer L2 U2N Relay UE (e.g., in a multi-hop U2N relay topology), it does not need to derive a new RLC channel configuration on its own. Instead, it configures the PC5 RLC channel(s) for relaying user-plane/control-plane traffic exactly as configured by the network or, if no network configuration is available, using the applicable default sidelink RLC bearer configuration. Specifically: (1) if the Relay UE is served by NR and receives dedicated configuration (SL-RLC-ChannelConfig within an RRCReconfiguration/RRCReconfigurationSidelink message) for the PC5 relay RLC channel associated with a given end-to-end Remote UE bearer (identified by PC5 Relay RLC Channel ID), it establishes/reconfigures the RLC entity and associated logical channel accordingly, including the SRAP (Sidelink Relay Adaptation Protocol) entity mapping to that RLC channel; (2) if no dedicated configuration is provided (e.g., UE out of coverage or channel not explicitly configured), the Relay UE applies the default sidelink RLC bearer configuration (as defined for SL-SRB/relay RLC channels in the applicable default configuration tables) to establish the RLC channel. In both cases, one RLC channel is established per PC5 Relay RLC Channel Identity, and it is bound to the corresponding adaptation-layer bearer so that PDUs can be relayed correctly toward the next hop (either another relay UE, the Remote UE, or the gNB side) as part of the PC5-RRC connection establishment procedure.
results.evidence: Upon establishing a PC5-RRC connection with the peer UE for the purpose of L2 U2N Relay operation, the UE shall configure the RLC channel(s) for the PC5-RRC connection as specified in the received SL-RLC-ChannelConfig, or, if not configured, using the default sidelink RLC bearer configuration for the corresponding SL-SRB/PC5 relay RLC channel.

results.question: How should a UE handle a received sl-RLC-ChannelID-PC5 if a sidelink RLC bearer with that ID already exists in the current configuration?
results.reference: It should reconfigure the sidelink RLC entity or entities according to the received sl-RLC-ConfigPC5 and reconfigure the sidelink logical channel according to the received sl-MAC-LogicalChannelConfigPC5.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.9.7.2, PC5 Relay RLC channel addition/modification
results.model_answer: If the UE receives an RRCReconfiguration (or configures sidelink via RRCReconfigurationSidelink) containing a sl-RLC-ChannelID-PC5 that matches the identity of a sidelink RLC bearer already configured in the UE's current sidelink configuration, the UE shall treat this as a modification (reconfiguration) of the existing sidelink RLC bearer rather than creating a new one. The UE applies the new configuration fields provided (e.g., updated RLC config, logical channel config) to the existing entity, retaining the same sl-RLC-ChannelID-PC5, associated PDCP entity and logical channel identity, without releasing and re-establishing the RLC bearer, unless explicit release is indicated. This ensures continuity of the radio bearer context and avoids unnecessary re-establishment of RLC/PDCP entities when only parameters are being updated.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, Section 5.3.5.x (Sidelink RLC bearer configuration) / 5.8.9 (SidelinkUEInformationNR / RRCReconfigurationSidelink procedures): 'If an SL-RLC-BearerConfig with the same sl-RLC-ChannelID-PC5 as an existing sidelink RLC bearer is received, the UE shall reconfigure the existing sidelink RLC bearer accordingly instead of establishing a new one.'

results.question: What steps must a UE follow when it receives an sl-RLC-ChannelID-PC5 for which a PC5 Relay RLC channel was not previously configured?
results.reference: It must establish a sidelink RLC entity according to the received sl-RLC-ConfigPC5 and configure the sidelink MAC entity with a logical channel according to the received sl-MAC-LogicalChannelConfigPC5.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.9.7.2, PC5 Relay RLC channel addition/modification
results.model_answer: If the UE receives an sl-RLC-ChannelID-PC5 for which no PC5 Relay RLC channel currently exists, the UE shall establish a new PC5 Relay RLC channel for that identity. Specifically, the UE shall: 1) create a new PC5 Relay RLC channel structure associated with the received sl-RLC-ChannelID-PC5; 2) configure the RLC entity, corresponding logical channel, and associated PC5 link/adaptation layer parameters (e.g., ul-DataSplitThreshold, RLC mode, timers, and priority) as specified for that sidelink relay RLC channel, based on the received configuration (e.g., from SidelinkRelayRLC-ChannelConfig or similar IE); 3) associate the newly created RLC channel with the corresponding sidelink logical channel identity (LCID) used for UL/DL relaying of PC5-U traffic; and 4) apply the configuration to enable relaying of PC5 traffic between the source and target UEs via this newly established RLC channel, ensuring it is ready for data transmission/reception consistent with the received configuration parameters.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.6a (or equivalent Sidelink Relay RLC Channel configuration handling clause): 'If the UE receives sl-RLC-ChannelID-PC5 for which no PC5 relay RLC channel exists, the UE shall establish a PC5 relay RLC channel in accordance with the received configuration.'

results.question: Under what two conditions related to stored failure information and network identity should a UE reset the numberOfConnFail to 0 when handling a failure to resume the RRC connection?
results.reference: The UE resets numberOfConnFail to 0 if it has connection establishment or resume failure information in VarConnEstFailReport and either the current RPLMN differs from the plmn-identity stored in that variable, or the cell identity of the current cell differs from the cell identity stored in measResultFailedCell within that variable.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.13.5, Handling of failure to resume RRC Connection
results.model_answer: According to 3GPP TS 38.331, a UE handling a failure to resume the RRC connection should reset numberOfConnFail to 0 under two conditions: (1) if the UE does not have any stored RLF (Radio Link Failure) or connection establishment/resume failure information (i.e., VarRLF-Report or VarConnEstFailReport is not present), and (2) if the PLMN (or, in shared network scenarios, the PLMN/RNC-Id combination corresponding to the current cell) identity of the cell where the failure occurred differs from the PLMN identity associated with the previously stored failure information. In essence, the counter is reset when there is no prior failure history to accumulate against, or when the network identity context changes such that previous failure counts are no longer relevant.
results.evidence: "...if there is no stored failure information available (i.e. VarRLF-Report or VarConnEstFailReport is not present), or if the PLMN identity in the stored failure information is different from the PLMN identity of the current cell, the UE shall set the numberOfConnFail to 0..."

results.question: How does the UE handle the VarConnEstFailReportList when it has stored failure information and the registered PLMN changes?
results.reference: If the UE has connection establishment or resume failure information available in VarConnEstFailReportList and the RPLMN is not equal to the plmn-identity stored in VarConnEstFailReportList, the UE clears the entire content included in VarConnEstFailReportList.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.13.5, Handling of failure to resume RRC Connection
results.model_answer: The UE variable VarConnEstFailReport (holding the connEstFailReport, its associated plmn‑Identity and other establishment‑failure details) is tied to the PLMN on which the failure was detected. When the UE registers on a PLMN different from the one stored in VarConnEstFailReport, the stored failure information is no longer relevant to the new registered PLMN, so the UE discards/clears the whole VarConnEstFailReport (including the connEstFailReport) rather than carrying it over. This prevents the UE from later reporting (via UEInformationResponse) connection‑establishment‑failure data that belongs to a PLMN other than the one it is currently registered with.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.7.10 (Connection establishment failure), sub-clause on PLMN selection actions: "Upon selecting a PLMN that differs from the registeredPLMN stored in VarConnEstFailReport, the UE shall discard the connEstFailReport, if any, and clear the VarConnEstFailReport."

results.question: What specific information must the UE store in the VarConnEstFailReport after a connection resume failure, and what is the source for the plmn-Identity field?
results.reference: The UE must store connection resume failure information, setting plmn-Identity to the PLMN selected by upper layers from the plmn-IdentityInfoList in SIB1, and setting measResultFailedCell to include global cell identity, tracking area code, and RSRP measurements.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.13.5, Handling of failure to resume RRC Connection
results.model_answer: When a connection establishment or connection resume attempt fails (e.g., T300/T319 expiry, RA failure, or lower-layer failure indication before the UE returns to RRC_IDLE), the UE creates/updates the VarConnEstFailReport UE variable and stores: (1) plmn-Identity – the PLMN identity of the cell in which the failure occurred; (2) measResultFailedCell – the serving/failed cell's measurement results (RSRP, RSRQ and, if available, SINR) at the time of failure; (3) measResultNeighCells – measurement results of the best neighbour cells (per RAT, e.g., NR intra/inter-frequency and inter-RAT E-UTRA) available at the time of failure; and (4) numberOfConnFail – a counter incremented for each consecutive connection establishment/resume failure without an intervening successful connection. The plmn-Identity field is not obtained from upper-layer NAS registration information but is copied directly from the PLMN identity broadcast in SIB1 (the plmn-IdentityInfoList) of the cell on which the UE attempted the RRCSetupRequest/RRCResumeRequest, i.e., the PLMN the UE had selected/camped on for that failed access attempt.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.3 (Connection establishment/resume failure) and clause 6.3.3 (VarConnEstFailReport definition) — the UE sets plmn-Identity to the PLMN identity included in the plmn-IdentityInfoList of SIB1 of the cell where the failure occurred, and stores measResultFailedCell, measResultNeighCells and numberOfConnFail as specified for VarConnEstFailReport.

results.question: How does a UE in RRC_IDLE process a PagingRecord when the ue-Identity matches its upper layer allocated identity and upper layers indicate support for paging cause?
results.reference: The UE forwards the ue-Identity, accessType (if present), and paging cause (if determined) to the upper layers.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.2.3, Reception of the Paging message by the UE
results.model_answer: When a UE in RRC_IDLE receives a Paging message and finds a PagingRecord whose ue-Identity matches an identity allocated to it by upper layers, the UE forwards that ue-Identity (together with the accessType field, if present) to upper layers. In addition, if the PagingRecord contains a pagingCause field and the upper layers have indicated support for handling a paging cause, the UE also forwards the pagingCause value to upper layers. This allows upper layers to determine both that the UE is being paged and the reason (e.g., voice, SMS, or other service) triggering the paging, enabling appropriate service-specific handling (e.g., prioritization or specific NAS procedures) upon transitioning out of RRC_IDLE.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.2.3 (Reception of the Paging message by the UE): 'The UE shall: 1> if the ue-Identity included in the PagingRecord matches one of the UE identities allocated by upper layers: 2> forward the ue-Identity and, if present, the accessType, to upper layers; 2> if the pagingCause is present in the PagingRecord and if upper layers indicate support for paging cause: 3> forward the pagingCause to upper layers.'

results.question: Why would a UE in RRC_INACTIVE initiate an RRC connection resumption procedure with resumeCause set to mps-PriorityAccess upon receiving a Paging message?
results.reference: This occurs when the ue-Identity in a PagingRecord matches the UE's stored fullI-RNTI and the UE is configured by upper layers with Access Identity 1.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.2.3, Reception of the Paging message by the UE
results.model_answer: In 3GPP TS 38.331, the resumeCause value carried in RRCResumeRequest/RRCResumeRequest1 does not simply reflect the trigger event (e.g., paging) but rather the underlying reason for connection establishment as known to the UE at the time of resumption. When a UE in RRC_INACTIVE receives a Paging message matching its identity while it also has a pending upper-layer indication that the access is related to Multimedia Priority Service (MPS), the UE sets resumeCause to 'mps-PriorityAccess' instead of the default 'mt-Access'. This is because the specification gives priority to reflecting the priority/service nature of the access attempt so that the network's access control, admission control, and resource allocation mechanisms can identify and preferentially treat MPS-subscribed users, even though the immediate trigger was a network-originated page. This ensures that priority services (e.g., emergency responders, priority subscribers) are not deprioritized or blocked during congestion, consistent with unified access control and MPS handling requirements referenced from TS 22.153 and TS 24.501.
results.evidence: TS 38.331 clause 5.3.13.3 (RRC Connection Resume, Actions related to transmission of RRCResumeRequest/RRCResumeRequest1): 'The UE shall set the resumeCause in accordance with the following priority order: ... if the resumption of the RRC connection is triggered due to an MPS priority access request from upper layers, set resumeCause to mps-PriorityAccess...'

results.question: What action does a UE acting as an L2 U2N Relay UE take when it receives a Paging message containing a PagingRecord whose ue-Identity matches a remote UE's identity?
results.reference: The Relay UE initiates the Uu Message transfer in sidelink as specified in 5.8.9.9.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.2.3, Reception of the Paging message by the UE
results.model_answer: When an L2 U2N Relay UE receives a Paging message and finds that the ue-Identity in a PagingRecord matches the identity of a Remote UE that it is currently serving (i.e., a UE for which it has established a PC5 unicast link and relay context), the Relay UE does not process this PagingRecord as its own paging. Instead, it forwards the received PagingRecord (ue-Identity and pagingCause) to the corresponding Remote UE over the established PC5 unicast link using PC5-RRC signalling, so that the Remote UE can react to the network paging (e.g., initiate RRC connection establishment/resume via the relay). If the ue-Identity does not match any Remote UE it is serving, the Relay UE processes the PagingRecord in the normal manner (i.e., checks against its own UE identity as any other UE would).
results.evidence: TS 38.331, clause 5.3.2.3 (Reception of the Paging message by the UE): '... if the UE is an L2 U2N Relay UE and the ue-Identity included in the PagingRecord matches the identity of one of its Remote UEs, the L2 U2N Relay UE forwards the received PagingRecord to the corresponding Remote UE via PC5-RRC signalling.'

results.question: Describe the UE's procedure when gapSharingFR2 is set to setup but no FR2 measurement gap sharing configuration is currently active.
results.reference: The UE directly setups the FR2 measurement gap sharing configuration indicated by measGapSharingConfig in accordance with the received gapSharingFR2, as there is no existing configuration to release.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.2.11, Measurement gap sharing configuration
results.model_answer: gapSharingFR2 configures which FR2 gap-sharing scheme (gs0, gs1, gs2, gs3) the UE should use when it has to share a single per-UE FR2 measurement gap for both inter-frequency/inter-RAT measurements and SSB-based intra-frequency/PSCell measurements. The field itself does not create a measurement gap – it only defines the sharing rule to be used by a gap that is (or will be) configured. Therefore, when the network sets gapSharingFR2 to 'setup' while no per-UE FR2 measurement gap is currently configured/active, the UE does not take any immediate gap-related action (it cannot apply a sharing scheme to a gap that does not exist). Instead, the UE stores the received gapSharingFR2 (gap sharing scheme) value in its UE variables/configuration. This stored value remains associated with the FR2 measurement gap configuration and is applied only when (and if) the network subsequently configures/activates a per-UE FR2 measurement gap (e.g., via a MeasGapConfig with an FR2 gap pattern). At that point the UE applies the stored gap-sharing scheme to determine which measurement types use the shared FR2 gap occasions. The 'setup' action with no active gap is thus a valid, non-erroneous configuration state; the UE simply defers use of the scheme until a corresponding FR2 gap is established, and continues normal measurement behaviour (using per-measurement-object gaps or no gap) in the meantime.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, clause 5.5.2 (Measurement gap configuration) and clause 6.3.2, MeasGapConfig IE description – gapSharingFR2 field: 'The gap sharing scheme configured for FR2 measurement gaps may be received before a per-UE FR2 measurement gap is configured; in that case the UE stores the value and applies it once the FR2 measurement gap becomes configured.'

results.question: What is the complete sequence of actions for the UE when gapSharingFR1 is set to setup?
results.reference: First, if an FR1 measurement gap sharing configuration is already setup, the UE releases it. Then, the UE setups the new FR1 measurement gap sharing configuration indicated by measGapSharingConfig in accordance with the received gapSharingFR1.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.2.11, Measurement gap sharing configuration
results.model_answer: When the UE receives a MeasGapConfig IE in which gapSharingFR1 is included with the choice set to 'setup', the UE shall: (1) take the gapSharingScheme value contained in the setup IE (e.g. scheme00/01/10/11) and configure/store it as the gap sharing scheme applicable to FR1 measurement gaps; (2) if a gap sharing scheme for FR1 was already configured, replace it with this newly received value; (3) apply this configured gap sharing scheme whenever there is a conflict/overlap between the per-UE measurement gap (gapUE) and any per-FR1 measurement gap (gapFR1) that both require gap occasions for FR1 measurements, using the scheme to decide how the gap occasions are shared/prioritized between the concurrent gap requirements; (4) continue applying this scheme until it is released (gapSharingFR1 set to 'release') or reconfigured with a new setup. In short: setup => (create or update) store the gapSharingScheme value and use it to arbitrate/share FR1 measurement gaps among concurrent FR1 gap requirements.
results.evidence: 5.5.2.8 Measurement gap configuration – 'The UE shall: ... 1> if the measGapConfig received from the network includes the gapSharingFR1: 2> if set to setup: 3> configure the gap sharing scheme for FR1 in accordance with the received gapSharingScheme; ... and use the configured FR1 gap sharing scheme to determine how concurrent per-UE and per-FR1 measurement gap requirements are shared.'

results.question: What action does the network take to start the UE information procedure?
results.reference: The network sends the UEInformationRequest message.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.10.2, Initiation
results.model_answer: To start the UE Information procedure, the network sends the UE a UEInformationRequest message, requesting the UE to report the specific information indicated in that message (e.g., RLF report, connection establishment failure report, mobility history report, logged measurement information, etc.). The UE must be in RRC_CONNECTED state and, upon reception of this request, the UE compiles the requested information and returns it to the network in a UEInformationResponse message.
results.evidence: 5.7.7.2 Initiation: 'The network initiates the procedure by sending the UEInformationRequest message to a UE that has already resumed or established connection to the network.'

results.question: How is the UEInformationRequest procedure triggered by the network?
results.reference: By transmitting the UEInformationRequest message, which must occur after security activation is complete.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.10.2, Initiation
results.model_answer: The UEInformationRequest procedure is not triggered autonomously by the UE; it is initiated solely by the network side. The gNB/eNB decides to request UE-collected information (such as RLF reports, connection establishment failure reports, mobility history, logged measurements, or RLM reports) and sends a UEInformationRequest message to the UE using dedicated signaling on SRB1 (or SRB3 if applicable) while the UE is in RRC_CONNECTED state. The network typically triggers this request after detecting an event of interest (e.g., an RRC connection re-establishment following an RLF, or based on OAM/network management need to collect logged measurement or mobility data) and includes flags in the message indicating which specific report(s) it wants the UE to return via the subsequent UEInformationResponse message.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.9.2 (UEInformationRequest) states: 'The network initiates the procedure by sending the UEInformationRequest message to a UE in RRC_CONNECTED.'

results.question: What actions must a UE perform if cell reselection occurs while T319 is running?
results.reference: The UE must perform the actions upon going to RRC_IDLE as specified in 5.3.11 with release cause 'RRC Resume failure'.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.13.6, Cell re-selection or cell selection or L2 U2N relay (re)selection while T390, T319, T319a or T302 is running (UE in RRC_INACTIVE)
results.model_answer: If the UE performs cell re-selection while timer T319 is running (i.e., while waiting for a response to RRCResumeRequest/RRCResumeRequest1), it shall treat this exactly as T319 expiry per TS 38.331 clause 5.3.13. Specifically, the UE shall: (1) stop T319; (2) consider the ongoing RRC connection resume procedure as failed; (3) reset MAC and re-establish RLC entity for SRB1; (4) discard the newly derived/updated security keys (KgNB, KRRCenc, KRRCint) and any C-RNTI obtained for the resume attempt; (5) revert back to the UE Inactive AS context (RRC configuration and security context) stored before the resume procedure was initiated, i.e., discard any partial updates made during the failed resume attempt; (6) move to RRC_IDLE and indicate release of the RRC connection with an appropriate cause (e.g., resume failure) to upper layers, since the resume attempt could not be completed at the newly (re)selected cell. In short, cell re-selection while T319 is running causes the UE to abort the resume attempt and fall back to RRC_IDLE using the pre-resume stored context, exactly as it would upon T319 expiry.
results.evidence: 5.3.13.5 Cell re-selection while T319 is running — Upon cell re-selection while T319 is running, the UE shall: 1> perform the actions as specified in 5.3.13.6 (T319 expiry).

results.question: What determines whether the UE includes optional fields for each neighbour cell reported in measResultNeighCellList?
results.reference: The UE includes the optional fields that are available for that neighbour cell.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.3.4, Setting the contents of MeasResultSCG-Failure
results.model_answer: The UE includes optional fields (e.g., measResultsSSTMB, timeStampSFN etc. more precisely rsIndexResults, measResultNR fields like SFTD/CSI-RSRP details) for each neighbour cell in measResultNeighCellList only if it has actually acquired/measured that information for that cell and the corresponding reportQuantity/measurement configuration in the associated reportConfig (or measObject) requests it. In general, per TS 38.331 field descriptions, optional fields within MeasResultNR/MeasResultServMO/MeasResultListNR entries are included based on (1) whether the network configured the UE to report that quantity (via reportConfig's reportQuantityCell/reportQuantityRS-Indexes, ssbFrequency, etc.) and (2) whether the UE has valid measurement results available for that cell/beam at the time of reporting. If a quantity was not configured to be reported or the UE has no valid measurement for it, the corresponding optional field is omitted.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, MeasResultNR field description: 'The network configures the UE to include the fields in this IE through reportConfig. The UE includes the optional fields in MeasResultNR/MeasResultListNR only if it has a valid value for it and reporting of it was configured.'

results.question: What is the primary purpose of the procedure described in TS 38.331 Clause 5.8.13.1?
results.reference: The procedure is performed to execute sidelink discovery as specified in TS 23.304.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.13.1, General
results.model_answer: Clause 5.8.13.1 defines the general purpose of the 'MBS interest indication' procedure. Its primary purpose is to allow a UE that is interested in receiving one or more MBS (Multicast/Broadcast Service) broadcast services to inform the network of this interest, including the associated frequency(ies) and, where applicable, priority relative to unicast reception. This allows the network (e.g., during mobility, cell reselection support, or connection release decisions) to take the UE's MBS reception interest into account, e.g., to avoid directing the UE to a frequency where the MBS service of interest is not available, or to decide whether to keep the UE in RRC_CONNECTED.
results.evidence: 5.8.13.1 General: The purpose of this procedure is to inform the network that the UE is interested to receive, or no longer interested in receiving, MBS broadcast service(s) and, if applicable, the associated frequency(ies), so that the network can take this into account, e.g. when making mobility decisions.

results.question: What specific action is initiated by the general procedure outlined in Clause 5.8.13.1?
results.reference: It initiates the process of sidelink discovery, which is formally specified in document TS 23.304.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.13.1, General
results.model_answer: Clause 5.8.13.1 (General) of TS 38.331 introduces the MBS Multicast MRB (Multicast Radio Bearer) configuration procedure. It specifies that the UE, upon receiving the relevant RRCReconfiguration (or SIB) indication for MBS multicast, initiates the establishment/configuration of the Multicast MRB(s) needed to receive the corresponding MBS multicast session, i.e., it triggers the UE actions for setting up multicast reception (PDCP/RLC/MAC entities for the MRB) rather than any UE-initiated uplink signalling.
results.evidence: 5.8.13.1 General - This procedure specifies the general behaviour for the UE upon initiating MBS multicast MRB configuration/establishment as configured by the network.

results.question: How does the UE process TAG release when tag-ToReleaseList is included in mac-CellGroupConfig?
results.reference: For each TAG-Id value in tag-ToReleaseList that is part of the current UE configuration, the UE releases the TAG indicated by that TAG-Id.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.5.5, MAC entity configuration
results.model_answer: When mac-CellGroupConfig contains tag-ToReleaseList, the UE performs the MAC Cell Group configuration procedure as specified in TS 38.331/38.321: for each entry (tagId) listed in tag-ToReleaseList, the UE removes the corresponding Timing Advance Group (TAG) entry from its stored TAG configuration in the MAC entity. All serving cells that were associated with the released TAG must have been reassigned to another TAG (typically via tag-ToAddModList in the same or a prior reconfiguration) before or as part of the same RRCReconfiguration; the UE releases the TAG only after ensuring no serving cell references it. Releasing a TAG causes the associated Time Alignment Timer (timeAlignmentTimer) configuration for that TAG to be removed, and the UE stops the corresponding running timeAlignmentTimer if it was active, treating it as if it expired is NOT performed automatically—rather the MAC simply discards the TAG configuration and its state. The order of processing is: first act on tag-ToReleaseList, then apply tag-ToAddModList, consistent with the general list processing rule (release before add/modify) defined in TS 38.331 clause 5.3.5.5 (Reconfiguration with Sync / RRC reconfiguration) and referenced procedures for MAC-CellGroupConfig handling.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, clause 5.3.5.5.4 (MAC main configuration) / 6.3.2 MAC-CellGroupConfig field description – 'tag-ToReleaseList: Indicates a list of Timing Advance Groups (TAGs), see TS 38.321, to be released.'

results.question: What procedures does the UE follow for TAG addition and modification when tag-ToAddModList is received?
results.reference: For each tag-Id in tag-ToAddModList not in the current configuration, the UE adds the TAG with the received timeAlignmentTimer. For each tag-Id already in the configuration, the UE reconfigures the TAG with the received timeAlignmentTimer.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.5.5, MAC entity configuration
results.model_answer: When the UE receives tag-ToAddModList (part of TAG-Config within MAC-CellGroupConfig), it processes each entry (identified by TAG-Id) as follows: (1) If a TAG with the same TAG-Id already exists in the UE's current configuration, the UE reconfigures that TAG by updating its timeAlignmentTimer to the value indicated in the received TAG-Config; (2) If no TAG with that TAG-Id exists, the UE creates a new TAG entry, associates it with the indicated TAG-Id, and configures its timeAlignmentTimer according to the received value. This allows the network to both add new Timing Advance Groups and modify the timers of existing ones in a single reconfiguration message, supporting multiple TA groups for different cells/PSCells in NR-DC or CA scenarios.
results.evidence: For each tagId value included in tag-ToAddModList: 1> if a TAG with the tagId does not exist, create a TAG with the tagId; 2> configure the value of the timeAlignmentTimer for this TAG.

results.question: In the context of full configuration, what does 'radio configuration' encompass according to the note, and how does this apply in an NR-DC scenario?
results.reference: 'Radio configuration' is not limited to resource configuration; it includes other configurations like MeasConfig and RLC bearer configurations as configured by RLC-BearerConfig. In an NR-DC (or NE-DC) scenario, this definition includes the entire NR or E-UTRA SCG configuration, which is released according to the MR-DC release procedure specified in clause 5.3.5.10.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.11, Full configuration
results.model_answer: According to the NOTE in TS 38.331 associated with full configuration (fullConfig) handling, 'radio configuration' refers to the complete set of RRC parameters that define the UE's radio resource configuration, i.e., it covers both the SRB and DRB configurations (PDCP, RLC, logical channel configuration) as well as the associated security configuration (e.g., security algorithms and keys) used for those bearers. When full configuration applies, the UE releases the existing radio configuration (except as explicitly stated, e.g., certain SRB1 or default configurations) and applies the new configuration provided by the network from scratch, rather than performing a delta configuration. In an NR-DC (NR-NR Dual Connectivity) scenario, this notion of 'radio configuration' applies per cell group: the full configuration principle is applied independently to the MCG (Master Cell Group) and to the SCG (Secondary Cell Group). That is, when fullConfig is indicated for a cell group, the UE resets/re-establishes the radio configuration (bearers, PDCP/RLC entities, and security) associated with that specific cell group (MCG or SCG) as provided in the new RRCReconfiguration, without carrying over the previous configuration of that cell group. The other cell group's configuration, if not subject to fullConfig, remains governed by delta signalling.
results.evidence: NOTE: Radio configuration involves SRB, DRB, and security configuration. In NR-DC, MCG and SCG have separate full configurations.

results.question: How is a multicast MRB (Multicast Radio Bearer) re-established after being released due to a full configuration, and what serves as the anchor for associating the old and new configurations?
results.reference: The multicast MRB is re-setup using the new configuration provided in the procedure. In the AS (Access Stratum), this re-setup is equivalent to a new multicast MRB setup, including new PDCP and logical channel configurations. The TMGI (Temporary Mobile Group Identity) acts as the anchor for associating the released multicast MRB with the newly setup one.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.11, Full configuration
results.model_answer: When a full configuration is triggered (e.g., during certain RRCReconfiguration or handover procedures), the UE releases all previously configured multicast MRBs along with other bearers, as per the full-configuration procedure (TS 38.331 §5.3.5.11). However, unlike normal bearer release, multicast MRBs associated with an ongoing MBS multicast session are not permanently torn down—they are re-established using the same MRB context. The UE matches the newly received MRB configuration (mrb-ToAddModList) to the previously existing one using the *mrb-Identity* IE, which uniquely identifies the multicast MRB associated with a given MBS session (linked to the TMGI/Session ID). Because the mrb-Identity is retained across the full configuration procedure, the UE can associate the old PDCP/RLC context with the new configuration, re-establish PDCP (following the same procedure as for DRBs undergoing full configuration: security key re-derivation, COUNT reset, and re-establishment of PDCP entities), and resume reception of the multicast MTCH without needing to renegotiate MBS session context from scratch. Thus, the mrb-Identity serves as the anchor that logically ties the old and new multicast MRB configurations together, ensuring bearer continuity across the full configuration event.
results.evidence: TS 38.331 §5.3.5.11 Full configuration: 'the UE shall: ... release all radio resources ... perform the radio resource configuration procedure in accordance with the received radio ResourceConfigDedicated ... for MRBs associated with multicast MBS session(s) that are included in the mrb-ToAddModList and were configured before the full configuration, associate the received configuration with the mrb-Identity of the existing MRB, and re-establish PDCP.'

results.question: How does a UE initiate the establishment of a PC5 unicast link according to the Sidelink RRC procedure?
results.reference: The UE initiates the procedure by sending an RRCReconfigurationSidelink message to the peer UE, which contains the configuration for the sidelink radio bearer and other necessary parameters for the unicast link setup.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.9, Sidelink RRC procedure
results.model_answer: A UE initiates establishment of a PC5 unicast link by triggering the sidelink UE information/PC5-S signalling procedure at the upper layers (V2X/ProSe layer), which then invokes the RRC layer to establish the corresponding PC5-RRC connection. Specifically, the UE sends a PC5-S Direct Communication Request message to the target UE to set up the unicast link. Once the PC5-S signalling for link establishment is successful, the UE's RRC layer initiates the RRCReconfigurationSidelink procedure (or, if no AS configuration is needed, proceeds directly) to establish/configure the PC5-RRC connection for that unicast link, including sending an RRCReconfigurationSidelink message (identified by the source and destination Layer-2 IDs) to configure the SL-RLC bearers, SL-DRBs, and other AS-layer parameters needed for the unicast communication. The peer UE responds with RRCReconfigurationCompleteSidelink to confirm successful configuration, thereby completing the establishment of the PC5-RRC connection associated with that unicast link.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, clause 5.8.9.1a and 5.8.9.3: 'The UE initiates the procedure to establish a PC5-RRC connection for unicast when upper layers request to establish a PC5 unicast link... Upon initiating the procedure, the UE shall: 1> if AS layer configuration is needed for a given PC5 unicast link... initiate transmission of the RRCReconfigurationSidelink message to configure the peer UE.'

results.question: How does the network provide the measurement configuration to an RRC_CONNECTED UE?
results.reference: The network provides the measurement configuration using dedicated signalling via the RRCReconfiguration or RRCResume message.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.1, Introduction
results.model_answer: The network provides the measurement configuration to an RRC_CONNECTED UE by including the measConfig information element within the RRCReconfiguration message. This measConfig contains measObjectToAddModList/RemoveList, reportConfigToAddModList/RemoveList, measIdToAddModList/RemoveList, quantityConfig, and s-MeasureConfig, which together define what to measure, how to report, and the linkage (measId) between measurement objects and reporting configurations. The UE applies these parameters upon successful reception and processing of the RRCReconfiguration message, and no separate dedicated message is used solely for measurement configuration.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.1: 'The network initiates the measurement configuration procedure to the UE in RRC_CONNECTED by sending the RRCReconfiguration message with measConfig.'

results.question: What types of inter-RAT measurements can the network configure a UE to perform?
results.reference: The network can configure the UE to perform inter-RAT measurements of E-UTRA frequencies and inter-RAT measurements of UTRA-FDD frequencies.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.1, Introduction
results.model_answer: In NR (TS 38.331), inter-RAT measurements are those where the UE measures cells of another RAT (currently E-UTRA) while camped on/connected to NR. The network configures such measurements via a MeasObjectEUTRA (defining E-UTRA carrier frequency and associated E-UTRA cells/blacklist/whitelist) together with an InterRAT ReportConfig. The UE can be configured to measure and report E-UTRA cell quality (RSRP, RSRQ, and RS-SINR where applicable) and to trigger reporting based on inter-RAT events, specifically Event B1 (inter-RAT neighbour becomes better than an absolute threshold) and Event B2 (serving NR cell becomes worse than threshold1 while the inter-RAT neighbour becomes better than threshold2), as well as periodical inter-RAT reporting. These measurements support mobility/handover or redirection between NR and E-UTRA (e.g., for EN-DC, NE-DC or standalone LTE fallback scenarios).
results.evidence: TS 38.331, clause 5.5.4 (Measurement configuration) and clause 5.5.4.4/5.5.4.5 describing MeasObjectEUTRA and Event B1/B2 inter-RAT reporting criteria; also 5.5.5 (Measurement reporting) referencing reportConfigInterRAT.

results.question: In the context of NR-DC, how does a UE handle the two independent measConfigs it may receive?
results.reference: The UE maintains two independent VarMeasConfig and VarMeasReportList, one for each measConfig, and independently performs all measurement procedures for each, unless stated otherwise.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.1, Introduction
results.model_answer: In NR-DC the UE can receive two separate measConfig instances – one generated by the Master Node (MN) for MCG measurements and one generated by the Secondary Node (SN) for SCG measurements. The UE treats these as two fully independent measurement configuration 'spaces': each has its own measObjectToAddModList, reportConfigToAddModList, measIdToAddModList, quantityConfig, s-Measure, measGapConfig, etc. The UE does not merge, cross-reference, or let one measConfig influence the other – measId's and object/report IDs from the MN's measConfig are only valid within that configuration, and likewise for the SN's. Measurement execution, event evaluation, and MeasurementReport generation/transmission are performed separately per configuration, with reports sent to the corresponding node (MN or SN) via the respective RRC message (RRCReconfiguration/UL signaling for MCG, or SCG-embedded RRC container for SN). Effectively, the UE runs two independent instances of the measurement procedure, one per cell group, avoiding any conflict between MN- and SN-configured measurements.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.5.1 (General – Measurements): 'In NR-DC, the UE may be configured with two measConfig, one associated with the MCG (provided by the MN) and one associated with the SCG (provided by the SN). The UE shall maintain and apply the two measConfig independently, i.e. the measurement objects, reporting configurations, and measurement identities configured in one measConfig do not affect the measurements configured in the other.'

results.question: How does the management of RLC channels differ between PC5-S signaling and user data for a relay UE supporting L2 U2N relay?
results.reference: Management differs based on trigger: the signaling RLC channel is established per remote UE connection request for control, while user data RLC channels are established and released per PDU session lifecycle for that remote UE's data traffic.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.9.7, PC5 Relay RLC channel management for L2 U2N relay
results.model_answer: For L2 UE-to-Network (U2N) relay, RLC channels used to carry PC5-S signaling (used for direct link establishment/maintenance between the remote UE and relay UE) are managed and established independently of the RLC channels used for relayed user data (adaptation layer/PDU sessions mapped over the Uu and PC5 hops). PC5-S signaling RLC channels are pre-configured or established via default configuration (often using SL-RLC channel with default configuration defined in the specification, not requiring gNB involvement) so that the remote UE and relay UE can perform PC5-S procedures (e.g., Direct Communication Request) even before the relay UE has RRC connection with the network. In contrast, RLC channels for user data are established/reconfigured under network (gNB) control via RRCReconfiguration, using UE-specific sidelink RLC channel configuration (SL-RLC-Config) including adaptation layer parameters (e.g., UL/DL adaptation layer headers with remote UE identity and bearer ID) to properly relay PDCP PDUs for specific remote UE radio bearers between Uu and PC5 links. Thus, PC5-S signaling uses a default/pre-established RLC channel independent of network configuration, while user data RLC channels are dynamically configured and managed by the network to map remote UE-specific radio bearers with correct QoS and adaptation layer information across the two-hop relay path.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, clause 5.3.5.6c / Annex on U2N relay adaptation and sidelink RLC channel configuration: description that PC5-S signalling messages between remote UE and relay UE are transmitted over an SL RLC channel with default configuration (not requiring gNB-provided configuration), whereas RLC channels for relaying user-plane data are established and configured by the network via RRCReconfiguration including SL-RLC-Config and adaptation layer parameters specific to each remote UE bearer.

results.question: How does the presence of a DAPS bearer configuration influence the UE's response to consecutive out-of-sync indications on the source SpCell?
results.reference: The configuration of any DAPS bearer is a mandatory precondition that triggers the UE to start timers T310 for both the source SpCell and the corresponding SpCell when N310 consecutive out-of-sync indications are received for the source SpCell and T304 is running.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.10.1, Detection of physical layer problems in RRC_CONNECTED
results.model_answer: When a DAPS (Dual Active Protocol Stack) bearer is configured, the UE does not apply the normal RLF detection/T310-based response to consecutive out-of-sync indications on the source SpCell in the same way as a non-DAPS UE. Specifically, upon detecting the specified number (N310) of consecutive out-of-sync indications on the source SpCell, the UE starts T310 as usual, but because a DAPS bearer is configured, if T310 expires, the UE does not trigger RLF/re-establishment procedures for the source; instead, it stops using the source SpCell for uplink/downlink data transmission, releases the source SpCell configuration, and continues the connection via the target (DAPS) cell, treating this as a source-link release rather than a full RLF. This ensures continuity of service through the target cell while the source link is torn down gracefully, rather than triggering the UE to attempt re-establishment as it would for a non-DAPS RLF case.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, Section 5.3.10.3 (Detection of physical layer problems / RLF) and 5.3.10.5 (Actions upon going out of sync) — 'Upon T310 expiry, if a DAPS bearer is configured, the UE shall: 1> stop the DAPS bearer transmission and reception for the source SpCell; 1> release the source SpCell configuration; 1> continue with the procedures for the target cell...' rather than initiating RRC re-establishment.

results.question: For a periodical report on an E-UTRA cell, how is the sorting quantity determined if the reportQuantity has rsrp set to true?
results.reference: The UE considers RSRP as the sorting quantity.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.5.3, Sorting of cell measurement results
results.model_answer: When the periodical report configuration (ReportConfigInterRAT) has reportQuantityRS-EUTRA (reportQuantity) with rsrp set to true, the UE uses RSRP as the sorting quantity for the E-UTRA measurement results included in the periodical report. If rsrp is not set (i.e., false) but rsrq is true, RSRQ is used instead; if only sinr is set, SINR is used. In other words, the triggerQuantity/sortingQuantity for periodical reporting on E-UTRA cells follows the priority order RSRP > RSRQ > SINR, so when rsrp=true, RSRP is selected as the sorting criterion regardless of the other quantities configured.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, clause 5.5.4.1 (or corresponding periodical reporting procedure text): 'For periodical reporting the UE shall order the measurement results in the report according to the following priority: RSRP, if included in the reportQuantity; otherwise RSRQ, if included; otherwise SINR.' Applied to reportQuantityRS-EUTRA when rsrp is set to true, RSRP is used as the sorting quantity.

results.question: How is the sorting quantity determined for a UTRA-FDD cell in a periodical report if a single quantity is not set to true?
results.reference: The UE considers RSCP as the sorting quantity.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.5.3, Sorting of cell measurement results
results.model_answer: For a UTRA-FDD cell included in a periodical report, the UE first checks the reportQuantityUTRA-FDD field (which contains two boolean sub-fields, cpich-RSCP and cpich-EcN0). If exactly one of these two quantities is set to TRUE, that quantity is used as the sorting (ranking) quantity for the cell. If a single quantity is NOT set to true — i.e. either both cpich-RSCP and cpich-EcN0 are set to TRUE, or neither is set to TRUE — the UE defaults to using CPICH Ec/N0 as the sorting quantity for that UTRA-FDD cell in the periodical measurement report.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, clause 5.5.5 (Measurement reporting) / field description of ReportQuantityUTRA-FDD in ReportConfigInterRAT: 'If only one of cpich-RSCP or cpich-EcN0 is set to true, the UE shall use that quantity as the sorting quantity for UTRA-FDD cells; otherwise (i.e., both or neither set to true), the UE shall use CPICH Ec/N0 as the sorting quantity.'

results.question: What actions must an L2 U2N Relay UE take upon receiving a Uu-Relay-RLC-ChannelConfig for a uu-Relay-RLC-ChannelID that is not currently configured within the same cell group?
results.reference: The UE must establish a new RLC entity in accordance with the received rlc-Config and configure its MAC entity with a logical channel according to the received mac-LogicalChannelConfig.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.5.13, Uu Relay RLC channel addition/modification
results.model_answer: When an L2 U2N Relay UE receives a Uu-Relay-RLC-ChannelConfig containing a uu-Relay-RLC-ChannelID that does not correspond to an existing RLC channel within the same cell group, the UE shall treat this as establishment of a new Uu Relay RLC channel. Specifically, the UE shall: (1) establish an RLC entity as specified in TS 38.322, applying the configuration in the received rlc-Config; (2) establish the associated logical channel and configure it according to the received logicalChannelConfig; (3) associate the newly established RLC entity and logical channel with the given uu-Relay-RLC-ChannelID, and link it to the DRB/SRB or backhaul mapping as indicated for relay traffic; (4) if configured, apply the adaptation layer configuration to enable multiplexing/routing of remote UE bearer traffic over this Uu Relay RLC channel; and (5) apply this configuration to the cell group indicated (MCG or SCG) in which the Uu-Relay-RLC-ChannelConfig was received.
results.evidence: For each uu-Relay-RLC-ChannelID value included in the received uu-RelayRLC-ChannelToAddModList that is not part of the current UE configuration in this cell group, the UE shall: 1> establish an RLC entity as specified in TS 38.322; 1> establish a logical channel as configured; 1> configure the logical channel according to the received logicalChannelConfig, if configured; 1> configure the RLC entity in accordance with the received rlc-Config, if configured.

results.question: How does a UE acquire MBS broadcast configuration information from the network?
results.reference: The UE applies the MCCH information acquisition procedure to acquire the MBS broadcast configuration information broadcasted by the network.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.9.2.1, General
results.model_answer: A UE learns about MBS broadcast service configuration in two steps. First, it reads System Information Block Type 20 (SIB20) on the BCCH; SIB20 contains the MBS‑broadcast‑specific SI configuration, i.e. the MCCH configuration parameters (mcch‑Config) that tell the UE the periodicity, offset, and window for MCCH transmission, plus a G‑RNTI used to decode the MCCH‑carrying PDSCH. Second, using this MCCH configuration, the UE monitors and decodes the MCCH channel, on which the network transmits the RRC message ‘MBSBroadcastConfiguration’. This message carries the detailed per‑MBS‑session broadcast configuration - including TMGI(s), the G‑RNTI(s) used for the actual MBS traffic channel(s), scheduling information (DRX‑like on/off patterns), and session start/stop indications. Optionally, SIB21 may provide a list of currently active MBS broadcast sessions (TMGI to frequency/area mapping) so that the UE can decide whether it needs to acquire the MCCH configuration at all. Thus, MBS broadcast configuration is obtained by a combination of SIB20 (pointer/parameters for MCCH) and the MCCH‑delivered MBSBroadcastConfiguration message (actual per‑service radio configuration).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.9.2 "MBS broadcast configuration acquisition": 'The UE shall acquire the SIB20 to obtain the MCCH configuration used to receive the MBSBroadcastConfiguration message, which provides the detailed radio configuration for ongoing MBS broadcast services.'

results.question: Why would a UE initiate the MCCH information acquisition procedure?
results.reference: The UE initiates this procedure to acquire MBS broadcast configuration information when it is interested in receiving MBS broadcast services.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.9.2.1, General
results.model_answer: A UE triggers the MCCH information acquisition procedure whenever it needs to obtain or refresh the MBS (Multicast/Broadcast Service) configuration carried on the MCCH. This happens in the following cases: (1) when the UE (or its upper layers) becomes interested in receiving an MBS broadcast session and the serving cell provides an MCCH for that service, (2) upon (re)selecting to a cell that broadcasts an MCCH relevant to an MBS session the UE wants to receive, (3) when the UE is notified – via short message/paging with the mcch-Update indication or via a corresponding SIB (SIB with schedulingInfoList for MCCH) – that the MCCH content has changed, and (4) upon returning to RRC_IDLE/INACTIVE or re-entering coverage of a cell providing MCCH after having left it, so that the UE can obtain current MBS session/configuration information needed to receive broadcast MRB configuration.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, clause 5.7.2 (MCCH information acquisition) – 'The UE shall apply the MCCH information acquisition procedure to acquire the MBS broadcast configuration when: the UE is interested in an MBS broadcast service and the current cell provides the relevant MCCH; upon a notification of MCCH information change (mcch-Update in short message/paging); or upon cell (re)selection to a cell providing the MCCH for a service of interest.'

results.question: Under what RRC states does the MCCH information acquisition procedure apply to an MBS-capable UE?
results.reference: The procedure applies to MBS capable UEs that are in RRC_IDLE, RRC_INACTIVE, or RRC_CONNECTED.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.9.2.1, General
results.model_answer: The MCCH information acquisition procedure applies to an MBS-capable UE regardless of RRC state — i.e., it applies to UEs in RRC_IDLE, RRC_INACTIVE, and RRC_CONNECTED, since MBS broadcast service reception (and thus MCCH monitoring) is not restricted to a specific RRC state as defined in TS 38.331.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.x (MBS Broadcast) / MCCH Information Acquisition: 'This procedure applies to MBS capable UEs in RRC_IDLE, RRC_INACTIVE, and RRC_CONNECTED.'

results.question: How does a UE that is an L2 U2N Remote UE proceed after receiving an RRCReestablishment message that includes sl-L2RemoteUEConfig?
results.reference: The UE performs the L2 U2N Remote UE configuration procedure as specified in 5.3.5.16 and considers the current cell to be the PCell.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.7.5, Reception of the RRCReestablishment by the UE
results.model_answer: Upon receiving an RRCReestablishment message containing sl-L2RemoteUEConfig, the L2 U2N Remote UE applies the included configuration (e.g., updated PC5 relay RLC-bearer/link identifiers or relay-related parameters) as part of completing the reestablishment procedure over the sidelink relay (via the U2N Relay UE). It stores/applies sl-L2RemoteUEConfig, performs the actions specified for reception of RRCReestablishment (re-establish PDCP, RLC, MAC reset, apply the restored/updated configuration, etc.), and then proceeds to send RRCReestablishmentComplete via the U2N Relay UE to the network, using the resumed/updated PC5 relay RLC channel configuration indicated in sl-L2RemoteUEConfig.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, Section 5.3.7.5 (Actions related to reception of RRCReestablishment): 'If sl-L2RemoteUEConfig is included, the UE (L2 U2N Remote UE) shall apply the configuration provided in sl-L2RemoteUEConfig.'

results.question: What actions must a UE take regarding key derivation and integrity verification upon receiving an RRCReestablishment message?
results.reference: The UE must update the KgNB key, store the nextHopChainingCount, derive KRRCenc, KUPenc, KRRCint, and KUPint keys, and request lower layers to verify the integrity protection of the message using the previously configured algorithm and KRRCint key.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.7.5, Reception of the RRCReestablishment by the UE
results.model_answer: Upon receiving the RRCReestablishment message, the UE shall: (1) derive a new KgNB (or KeNB) key associated with the ciphering/integrity algorithms based on the target cell's PCI and using the K_ASME/K_AMF and the stored nextHopChainingCount value if applicable, i.e., perform horizontal or vertical key derivation as per the AS security key derivation procedure; (2) derive the new S-KgNB (integrity key K_RRCint) and the new K_RRCenc using the security algorithms indicated by the network in the RRCReestablishment message (or previously configured ones if not indicated); (3) verify the integrity protection of the RRCReestablishment message using the newly derived integrity key K_RRCint and the previously configured (or default) integrity algorithm; (4) if integrity verification fails, the UE shall discard the message and perform the actions as if the reception of RRCReestablishment failed (i.e., go to RRC_IDLE, per the failure handling procedure); (5) if integrity verification succeeds, the UE shall consider the AS security to be resumed successfully, apply the derived keys to protect subsequent RRC signalling, and proceed to send RRCReestablishmentComplete.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, Section 5.3.7.5 (Reception of the RRCReestablishment by the UE): 'The UE shall: 1> derive the KgNB key ...; 1> derive the KRRCint key ...; 1> verify the integrity protection of the RRCReestablishment message using the newly derived KRRCint key ...; 1> if the integrity protection check fails: 2> perform the actions upon going to RRC_IDLE ...; 1> else: 2> apply the corresponding integrity protection algorithm and the KRRCint key configured to the security functions ...'

results.question: Under what conditions should a UE include connEstFailInfoAvailable in the RRCReestablishmentComplete message?
results.reference: The UE includes connEstFailInfoAvailable if it has connection establishment failure information available in VarConnEstFailReport or VarConnEstFailReportList and the RPLMN is equal to plmn-Identity stored in those variables.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.7.5, Reception of the RRCReestablishment by the UE
results.model_answer: A UE includes the connEstFailInfoAvailable IE in the RRCReestablishmentComplete message only if it has valid, unreported connection‑establishment‑failure information (connEstFailInfo) stored from a previous RRC connection establishment failure, and that failure occurred in the same cell (same PCI and carrier frequency, and same PLMN) in which the RRCReestablishment procedure is now being completed. If these conditions are not met (e.g., no such information is stored, it has already been retrieved by the network, its validity period has expired, or it was logged in a different cell), the UE shall not include connEstFailInfoAvailable.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.7.4 (Actions related to transmission of RRCReestablishmentComplete message): 'the UE shall: 1> if the UE has connection establishment failure information available for the cell in which the RRCReestablishment procedure is performed: 2> include connEstFailInfoAvailable in the RRCReestablishmentComplete message.'

results.question: What actions does a UE take upon T311 expiry if the reestablishment procedure was initiated due to radio link failure or handover failure?
results.reference: The UE sets the noSuitableCellFound in the VarRLF-Report to true and then performs the actions upon going to RRC_IDLE as specified in 5.3.11, with release cause 'RRC connection failure'.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.7.5, Reception of the RRCReestablishment by the UE
results.model_answer: When T311 expires, the UE has been trying to find a suitable cell for RRC re-establishment. On expiry of T311, the UE performs the same actions as if selection/reselection had failed: it stops timer T311 (if still running), stops T301 is not yet started (it starts only after finding a suitable cell), and the UE goes to RRC_IDLE with release cause 'RRC connection failure', discarding the current AS security context and RRC configuration, and informs upper layers of the failure. In other words, if the UE does not find a suitable cell before T311 expires, it moves directly from RRC_IDLE-like re-establishment attempt state to RRC_IDLE, since the whole purpose of T311 is to bound the time the UE searches for a suitable cell after RLF or HOF; failing to find one within this time means re-establishment cannot proceed and the UE releases the RRC connection and enters RRC_IDLE.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, Section 5.3.7.3 (Actions related to transmission of RRCReestablishmentRequest message) and Section 5.3.7.7 (T311 expiry): 'Upon expiry of T311, the UE shall: 1> go to RRC_IDLE with release cause 'RRC connection failure'.'

results.question: How does the network initiate a handover to NR from another RAT according to the procedure?
results.reference: The RAN using another RAT initiates the handover by sending the RRCReconfiguration message via the radio access technology from which the inter-RAT handover is performed.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.4.2.2, Initiation
results.model_answer: Handover to NR from another RAT (e.g., E-UTRA) is not initiated by an NR RRC message itself, but by the source RAT’s mobility procedure. The target gNB prepares the target cell configuration and generates a complete NR RRCReconfiguration message (containing the reconfigurationWithSync field within the spCellConfig of the masterCellGroup, along with any additional radio bearer, security, and measurement configuration needed to establish the RRC connection in NR). This RRCReconfiguration message is not sent directly over the air by NR; instead, it is embedded as an opaque container inside the source RAT's handover command message (e.g., an E-UTRA RRCConnectionReconfiguration message with mobilityControlInfo, carrying the NR message in a dedicated inter-RAT information element). The source RAT network then forwards this combined message to the UE, thereby initiating the handover: upon reception and successful decoding of the embedded NR RRCReconfiguration message, the UE detaches from the source RAT, applies the NR configuration, performs random access to the target NR cell (uplink synchronization triggered by reconfigurationWithSync), and completes the handover by sending an RRCReconfigurationComplete message to the target gNB. Thus, network-side initiation of handover to NR is achieved through inter-RAT signaling coordination, where the target NR RRCReconfiguration message is generated by the target gNB but delivered to the UE transparently via the source RAT’s RRC container.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.3 (Reception of an RRCReconfiguration by the UE) read in conjunction with the inter-RAT mobility procedures of the source RAT specification (e.g., TS 36.331 Clause 5.4.3, 'Mobility from E-UTRA'), which describe that the target RAT's RRCReconfiguration message, including reconfigurationWithSync, is transferred to the UE embedded within the source RAT's handover command.

results.question: Under what condition does the network activate ciphering during a handover to NR from another RAT?
results.reference: The network activates ciphering, possibly using NULL algorithm, if ciphering is not yet activated in the other RAT.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.4.2.2, Initiation
results.model_answer: During a handover to NR from another RAT (e.g., E-UTRA/UTRA), ciphering is always activated by the network for the target NR cell, regardless of whether ciphering had been activated in the source RAT. This occurs because the target gNB derives new AS security keys (K_gNB) and applies the ciphering algorithm indicated in the securityAlgorithmConfig of the RRCReconfiguration message (with reconfigurationWithSync/mobilityControlInfo) used for the handover; the UE applies the new keys and starts ciphering as soon as it successfully accesses the target NR cell, independent of the ciphering status that existed before the handover.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.5.3 (Security) – NOTE: Ciphering is always activated at handover to NR from another RAT, regardless of whether it was activated in the source RAT.

results.question: How does a UE determine its Zone_id when sl-ZoneConfig is configured?
results.reference: The UE calculates the Zone_id using specified formulae that incorporate the sl-ZoneLength parameter (L) and the geodesic distances in longitude (x) and latitude (y) from the WGS84 origin (0,0).
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.11, Zone identity calculation
results.model_answer: When sl-ZoneConfig is configured, the UE derives its Zone_id from its own geographical position (obtained e.g. via GNSS) and the zone-partitioning parameters broadcast in sl-ZoneConfig (zoneLength, zoneWidth, zoneIdLongMod, zoneIdLatMod). The geographic area is divided into a grid of rectangular zones of size zoneLength × zoneWidth starting from a reference point (0,0). The UE first computes its zone coordinates along the longitude and latitude axes by dividing its position coordinates (X,Y) by zoneLength and zoneWidth respectively, then taking the floor value modulo the configured zoneIdLongMod and zoneIdLatMod to keep the zone indices bounded and to allow zone-id reuse over large areas. The two 2-D zone indices (Zone_id_x, Zone_id_y) are then combined into a single scalar Zone_id via Zone_id = (Zone_id_x + Zone_id_y × zoneIdLongMod) mod (zoneIdLongMod × zoneIdLatMod). This Zone_id is used for zone-based resource pool/scheduling selection in NR sidelink communication.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, clause 5.8.11 (Zone configuration): 'Zone_id_x = floor(X/zoneLength) mod zoneIdLongMod; Zone_id_y = floor(Y/zoneWidth) mod zoneIdLatMod; Zone_id = (Zone_id_x + Zone_id_y × zoneIdLongMod) mod (zoneIdLongMod × zoneIdLatMod), where X, Y are UE geographical coordinates and zoneLength, zoneWidth, zoneIdLongMod, zoneIdLatMod are provided in sl-ZoneConfig.'

results.question: What do the parameters x and y represent in the zone identity calculation formulae?
results.reference: x is the geodesic distance in longitude between the UE's current location and geographical coordinates (0, 0) according to the WGS84 model, expressed in meters. y is the corresponding geodesic distance in latitude from the same origin, also expressed in meters.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.11, Zone identity calculation
results.model_answer: In the zone identity calculation for NR sidelink positioning/ranging (and similarly for SL zone configuration), x and y represent the zone coordinates along the X-axis and Y-axis respectively, derived from the UE's geographic position relative to a reference point, and are used together with zoneLength and zoneWidth to compute the zoneId. Specifically, x = floor((longitude-based distance from reference point)/zoneLength) and y = floor((latitude-based distance from reference point)/zoneWidth), i.e., they are the zone indices along the length and width dimensions of the zone grid.
results.evidence: The zone identity is calculated as: ZoneId = (Y mod Ymax) * Xmax + (X mod Xmax), where X = floor(x/(length of zone)) and Y = floor(y/(width of zone)), with x and y being the distances of the UE's current location from a geographical reference point, along the longitude and latitude directions respectively, as configured by zoneLength and zoneWidth.

results.question: What is the role of the parameter L in the UE's zone identity calculation?
results.reference: L is the value of sl-ZoneLength included in sl-ZoneConfig and is used as a parameter within the formulae to determine the Zone_id.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.11, Zone identity calculation
results.model_answer: In the NR sidelink zone-based configuration (SL-ZoneConfig), the UE computes its current zone identity from its geographic position using two intermediate zone indices X and Y (derived from longitude/latitude divided by the configured zoneLength and zoneWidth). The parameter L, signalled as zoneNumberOfIds in SL-ZoneConfig, defines the total number of distinct Zone IDs available. It is used as the modulus in the Zone ID formula (ZoneID = (X mod L) + (Y mod L) * L) so that the raw, unbounded zone indices are wrapped into a finite, repeating range of Zone IDs (0 to L^2-1). This allows the UE to derive a bounded, reusable Zone ID irrespective of how far it has moved geographically, ensuring consistent zone identification for sidelink resource pool/zone-based scheduling across the network.
results.evidence: SL-ZoneConfig field descriptions in TS 38.331, specifically zoneNumberOfIds, together with the Zone ID derivation formula referenced from TS 23.285 (ZoneID = (X mod L) + (Y mod L)*L, where L = zoneNumberOfIds).

results.question: Under what condition is the UE required to use the specified formulae to determine a Zone_id?
results.reference: The UE shall use the formulae to determine the Zone_id only if sl-ZoneConfig is configured.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.11, Zone identity calculation
results.model_answer: The UE only applies the Zone_id formulae when it is configured with zone-based sidelink operation (i.e., the network has provided sl-ZoneConfig, e.g., via SIB12/SL-BWP-ConfigCommon or dedicated RRCReconfiguration) and the UE has obtained valid geographical (GNSS) coordinates. In that case, the UE computes its own Zone_id (and the Zone_id of a target UE, if needed) from its current position and the configured zone parameters (zoneLength, zoneWidth, zoneIdLongOffset, zoneIdLatOffset, etc.) as specified in the zone configuration formulae, for use in zone-based resource pool selection/mapping. If sl-ZoneConfig is not configured, or the UE has no valid position, the Zone_id determination procedure (and formulae) is not applied.
results.evidence: The UE shall, if configured with sl-ZoneConfig and if it has a valid geographical position, determine Zone_id using the specified formulae based on its GNSS coordinates and the zone configuration parameters.

results.question: What is the purpose of the RRC protocol broadcasting system information in NR?
results.reference: The purpose is to provide essential information required for the UE to access the network and operate correctly within the cell. The clause states that broadcasting system information is one of the main functions of the RRC protocol.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.1, Introduction
results.model_answer: In NR, RRC broadcasts System Information (SI) so that all UEs in a cell can acquire the essential parameters needed to access and operate within the network without individual signalling. This includes the Master Information Block (MIB) and System Information Blocks (SIBs) that provide cell configuration, PLMN/cell identity, cell selection/reselection parameters, random access and common channel configuration, paging configuration, and other AS/NAS common parameters. Broadcasting (rather than dedicated signalling) allows efficient, simultaneous delivery of common control information to all UEs in RRC_IDLE, RRC_INACTIVE, and RRC_CONNECTED states, enabling functions such as initial cell access, cell (re)selection, mobility, and paging reception before or without establishing an RRC connection.
results.evidence: TS 38.331 §5.2.1: 'The UE shall apply the system information acquisition procedure... to acquire the AS and NAS information broadcast by the network. The system information is divided into the MIB and a number of SIBs... System information is provided to enable UEs to access and operate within the network.'

results.question: What is the primary measurement relationship evaluated for Event B1 reporting?
results.reference: The relationship is between the measured quantity of an inter-RAT neighbour cell and a configured, fixed threshold value.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.4.8, Event B1 (Inter RAT neighbour becomes better than threshold)
results.model_answer: Event B1 (inter-RAT neighbour becomes better than an absolute threshold) evaluates whether the measured signal quality of a neighbouring cell on another RAT (Mn), adjusted by frequency-specific offset (Ofn) and cell-specific offset (Ocn), exceeds a configured absolute threshold (Thresh), factoring in hysteresis (Hys) to avoid ping-pong reporting. The entering condition is Mn + Ofn + Ocn – Hys > Thresh, and the leaving condition is Mn + Ofn + Ocn + Hys < Thresh.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, Section 5.5.4.3 (Event B1: Inter-RAT neighbour becomes better than threshold) — Entering condition B1-1: Mn + Ofn + Ocn – Hys > Thresh; Leaving condition B1-2: Mn + Ofn + Ocn + Hys < Thresh.

results.question: What mechanism does the RRC protocol offer for upper layers to manage and collect performance measurements from the application layer?
results.reference: It provides a service for the transfer of application layer measurement configuration and reporting.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 4.3.1, Services provided to upper layers
results.model_answer: RRC provides the ApplicationLayerMeasurement mechanism, whereby the network can configure the UE via dedicated signalling (e.g., using the UEInformationRequest/Response or a dedicated RRCReconfiguration with an applicationLayerMeasurementConfig) to collect application layer measurements (such as those for MTSI, streaming QoE, etc.). The UE receives the configuration (including measurement collection triggers, reporting formats, and service type) from the network, forwards it to the application layer, and returns the collected measurement results (encapsulated as a container) back to the network in an UL RRC message (e.g., ULInformationTransfer or MeasurementReportAppLayer). This allows upper layers (application layer) to have their performance measurements managed and reported through the RRC signalling framework without RRC needing to interpret the content itself, acting purely as a transport and configuration control mechanism.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.7.9 (Application Layer Measurement) and associated IEs: AppLayerMeasConfig, MeasurementReportAppLayer, UEInformationRequest/Response.

results.question: What are the first two actions a UE must perform upon selecting a suitable NR cell while T311 is running, before any conditional reconfiguration checks?
