results.reference: The UE must first ensure it has valid and up-to-date essential system information as specified in clause 5.2.2.2, and then it must stop timer T311.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.7.3, Actions following cell selection while T311 is running
results.model_answer: Upon selecting a suitable NR cell while T311 is running, the UE must first (1) stop timer T311, and (2) start timer T301, before performing any conditional reconfiguration (CHO) evaluation or actions.
results.evidence: 5.3.7.3 Actions related to T311 expiry / cell reselection during RRC_CONNECTED: 'Upon selecting a suitable NR cell, the UE shall: 1> stop timer T311; 1> start timer T301; ... if the UE has a stored valid conditional reconfiguration ... perform the actions defined for the selected candidate cell...'

results.question: How does the UE proceed if, after selecting a suitable NR cell while T311 is running, the cell selection was triggered by an MCG radio link failure and all conditions for attemptCondReconfig are met?
results.reference: The UE sets the choCellId in the VarRLF-Report to the selected cell's identity, applies the stored condRRCReconfig associated with that cell, and performs the actions specified in 5.3.5.3.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.7.3, Actions following cell selection while T311 is running
results.model_answer: When T311 is running after an MCG radio link failure and the UE subsequently selects a suitable NR cell, the UE first stops T311. Because the re-establishment attempt was triggered by MCG RLF and the UE is configured with attemptCondReconfig, the UE checks whether the selected cell is one of its stored conditional reconfiguration (CHO/CPA) candidate cells and whether the execution conditions for that candidate are satisfied. If all these conditions (attemptCondReconfig configured, MCG-RLF-triggered re-establishment, and a matching candidate cell whose execution condition is met) are fulfilled, the UE does not proceed with the normal RRCReestablishmentRequest procedure. Instead, it applies the stored conditional reconfiguration associated with that cell as specified for conditional handover/PSCell addition execution (clause 5.3.5.x), effectively performing the conditional handover to the selected cell instead of re-establishment. Only if these conditions are not met does the UE continue with the standard re-establishment procedure (starting T301, sending RRCReestablishmentRequest, etc.).
results.evidence: TS 38.331, clause 5.3.7.3 (Actions following cell selection while T311 is running): 'Upon selecting a suitable NR cell, the UE shall: ... stop timer T311; if the selected cell is a candidate cell for which the UE has a stored conditional reconfiguration and the re-establishment procedure was initiated due to MCG radio link failure or reconfiguration with sync of the MCG failure, and the UE is configured with attemptCondReconfig, and the conditions for evaluating the candidate cell as specified in 5.3.5.x are met: apply the stored conditional reconfiguration and perform the associated actions as specified in 5.3.5.x, instead of continuing with the RRC re-establishment procedure.'

results.question: How does the UE determine when to initiate Event A2 reporting based on the serving cell's measurement?
results.reference: The UE initiates Event A2 reporting when the measurement result of the serving cell becomes worse than a configured threshold.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.4.3, Event A2 (Serving becomes worse than threshold)
results.model_answer: The UE evaluates Event A2 (Serving cell becomes worse than absolute threshold) using the entering condition A2-1: Ms + Hys < Thresh, where Ms is the measured RSRP/RSRQ/SINR value of the serving cell (after applying layer-3 filtering and any offset), Hys is the hysteresis parameter for this event, and Thresh is the configured threshold for Event A2. The condition must remain satisfied for a time duration equal to the timeToTrigger before the UE considers the event as triggered and initiates a measurement report. The UE stops or cancels the report if the corresponding leaving condition A2-2: Ms - Hys > Thresh becomes true before the time-to-trigger timer expires. All measurement quantities are expressed in the same unit (dB or dBm) as configured for the specific event.
results.evidence: Ms + Hys < Thresh (Entering condition), Ms – Hys > Thresh (Leaving condition), as specified in TS 38.331 clause 5.5.4.3 for Event A2 (Serving cell becomes worse than threshold).

results.question: Why would a UE trigger Event A2 in relation to its current serving cell?
results.reference: Event A2 is triggered because the serving cell's measurement has degraded below a predefined threshold, indicating deteriorating service quality.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.4.3, Event A2 (Serving becomes worse than threshold)
results.model_answer: A UE triggers Event A2 when the quality of its current serving cell degrades below a configured threshold. This is defined in 3GPP TS 38.331 (Event A2: Serving becomes worse than threshold) and is used to prompt the UE to report measurements so the network can decide on actions such as handover, redirection to another frequency/RAT, or activation of additional measurement configurations, since the serving cell can no longer guarantee adequate radio link quality (e.g., RSRP/RSRQ/SINR) for continued service.
results.evidence: Entering condition: Ms + Hys < Thresh (Event A2, TS 38.331 §5.5.4.3) — the serving cell measurement (Ms), adjusted by hysteresis, falls below the configured threshold (Thresh), indicating the serving cell quality has become worse than an acceptable level.

results.question: How does the UE determine what value to set for absoluteFrequencyPointA in the ra-InformationCommon?
results.reference: The UE sets absoluteFrequencyPointA to indicate the absolute frequency of the reference resource block associated with the random-access resources actually used during the random-access procedure.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.10.5, RA information determination for RA report and RLF report
results.model_answer: The UE does not choose an arbitrary value for absoluteFrequencyPointA; it sets it equal to the absoluteFrequencyPointA of the frequency information (either FrequencyInfoDL/FrequencyInfoUL or the corresponding SIB1/ServingCellConfigCommon field) of the serving cell/CG on which the random access procedure (and thus the reporting of ra-InformationCommon, e.g., for RA report or SCG failure information) is performed. In other words, absoluteFrequencyPointA in ra-InformationCommon is copied directly from the absoluteFrequencyPointA that defines Point A for that cell's frequency configuration, ensuring the reported RA information can be correctly mapped to the same reference frequency point used for resource block numbering on that carrier.
results.evidence: The field absoluteFrequencyPointA in RA-InformationCommon is defined as 'Indicates the absoluteFrequencyPointA of the concerned SpCell as defined in TS 38.331.' This is set to the value of absoluteFrequencyPointA in the SIB1/ServingCellConfigCommon of the cell where the random access procedure occurred.

results.question: What information does the UE include in ra-InformationCommon when the random-access resource used is associated with a CSI-RS?
results.reference: The UE sets the csi-RS-Index to include the index of the associated CSI-RS and sets numberOfPreamblesSentOnCSI-RS to indicate the number of successive random-access attempts linked to that same CSI-RS.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.10.5, RA information determination for RA report and RLF report
results.model_answer: When the random-access occasion used by the UE is associated with a CSI-RS (rather than an SSB), the UE populates ra-InformationCommon with the csi-RS-Index field, which identifies the specific CSI-RS resource associated with that RA occasion, and it sets numberOfPreamblesSentOnCSI-RS to the number of Msg1 (preamble) transmissions sent on that CSI-RS-associated RA resource. The ssb-Index and numberOfPreamblesSentOnSSB fields, which are used for SSB-associated RA resources, are not included in this case. The common fields describing the RA resource configuration (absoluteFrequencyPointA, locationAndBandwidth, subcarrierSpacing, msg1-FrequencyStart, msg1-SubcarrierSpacing, ra-PreambleIndex) are always included regardless of whether the resource is SSB- or CSI-RS-associated.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 6.3.2, RA-InformationCommon field descriptions: 'csi-RS-Index: This field is present if the random-access resource used is associated with a CSI-RS. Indicates the CSI-RS index associated with the random-access resource used.' and 'numberOfPreamblesSentOnCSI-RS: This field is present if the random-access resource used is associated with a CSI-RS. Indicates the number of random-access preambles sent on the CSI-RS associated with the random-access resource used.'

results.question: How does a UE determine whether to apply the L2 U2N Relay UE configuration received in an RRCReconfiguration message?
results.reference: The UE applies the configuration if the rrc-Reconfiguration message includes the l2-U2N-RelayUE-Config and the UE is capable of supporting L2 U2N relay operation. If the UE is not capable, it ignores the field.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.15, L2 U2N Relay UE configuration
results.model_answer: In TS 38.331, the L2 U2N Relay UE configuration is carried as an optional field (sl-L2RelayUE-Config) inside RRCReconfiguration. The UE only applies this configuration if it is currently operating (or has requested to operate) as a Layer-2 UE-to-Network Relay UE, i.e., the UE has indicated relay capability/role to the network (e.g., via SidelinkUEInformationNR with sl-RelayUE-r17) and has an active or being-established PC5 relay context toward a Remote UE. If the RRCReconfiguration message contains the sl-L2RelayUE-Config field, the UE checks its own relay role: only a UE that is acting as an L2 U2N Relay UE processes and applies the received configuration (e.g., relay-specific SLRB, bearer mapping, PC5-RRC and Uu bearer association parameters); a UE not operating in that role ignores the field. Thus applicability is determined by the combination of (a) presence of the sl-L2RelayUE-Config IE in the message and (b) the UE's own state/role as a confirmed L2 U2N Relay UE for that PC5 link.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, clause 5.3.5.3 (Reception of an RRCReconfiguration by the UE): "if the RRCReconfiguration message includes the sl-L2RelayUE-Config, and the UE is configured to act as a L2 U2N Relay UE, the UE shall apply the configuration..."

results.question: Under what conditions does a UE out of coverage on the concerned frequency for NR sidelink discovery, which is performing NR sidelink non-relay discovery, configure its lower layers for resource allocation?
results.reference: The UE configures lower layers to perform sidelink resource allocation mode 2 based on sensing using the pools of resources indicated in sl-DiscTxPoolSelected or sl-TxPoolSelectedNormal for NR sidelink discovery transmission on the concerned frequency in SidelinkPreconfigNR.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.13.3, Sidelink discovery transmission
results.model_answer: A UE that is out of coverage on the frequency used for NR sidelink discovery, and which is performing NR sidelink non-relay discovery (i.e., discovery unrelated to sidelink relay/relay-UE(FFS) discovery), configures the lower layers to use sidelink resource allocation Mode 2, applying the sl-InterFreqInfoList/pre-configured or stored (pre-)configuration (e.g., SL-PreconfigurationNR) parameters, since no serving cell configuration (sl-ConfigDedicatedNR) is available in this case.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.8.3.2 (or equivalent discovery procedure clause): 'If the UE is performing NR sidelink discovery for a frequency for which it is out of coverage, and this discovery is not related to sidelink relay discovery, the UE shall configure the lower layers to perform sidelink resource allocation mode 2, in accordance with the parameters provided in the received or stored SL-PreconfigurationNR / sl-InterFreqInfoList.'

results.question: How does a UE, which is selecting or has selected an NR sidelink U2N Relay UE and meets the Remote UE threshold conditions based on sl-RemoteUE-ConfigCommon in SidelinkPreconfigNR, proceed when it is out of coverage on the concerned frequency for NR sidelink discovery?
results.reference: The UE configures lower layers to perform sidelink resource allocation mode 2 based on sensing using the pools of resources indicated in sl-DiscTxPoolSelected or sl-TxPoolSelectedNormal for NR sidelink discovery transmission on the concerned frequency in SidelinkPreconfigNR.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.13.3, Sidelink discovery transmission
results.model_answer: When a UE that is selecting or has selected an NR sidelink U2N Relay UE is out of NR coverage (idle/inactive with no valid RRC configuration, or out of NR sidelink coverage) on the frequency used for NR sidelink discovery/communication, it applies the sidelink discovery/relay-related parameters (e.g., discovery resource pool, thresholds, timers) from the pre-configured parameters sl-RemoteUE-ConfigCommon contained within SidelinkPreconfigNR, provided the UE meets the applicable Remote UE threshold conditions defined therein, instead of using parameters broadcast in SIB or dedicated RRC signalling.
results.evidence: If the UE is out of coverage on the frequency used for NR sidelink discovery and communication, and the UE is selecting or has selected an NR sidelink U2N Relay UE and it fulfils the conditions of Remote UE, if included, based on sl-RemoteUE-ConfigCommon within SidelinkPreconfigNR, the UE shall use sl-RemoteUE-ConfigCommon within SidelinkPreconfigNR for the concerned frequency.

results.question: What must be true for a UE capable of sidelink discovery to be configured by upper layers to transmit an NR sidelink discovery message?
results.reference: The frequency used for NR sidelink discovery must be included in either sl-FreqInfoToAddModList in sl-ConfigDedicatedNR within RRCReconfiguration and sl-DiscConfig is included in RRCReconfiguration, or the frequency must be included in sl-FreqInfoList within SIB12 and sl-DiscConfigCommon is included in SIB12.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.13.3, Sidelink discovery transmission
results.model_answer: A UE capable of NR sidelink discovery can only be configured by upper layers to transmit a discovery message if it has valid AS-layer sidelink discovery resource configuration for its current coverage/RRC state. Concretely: (1) the UE must be authorized/configured by upper layers (per TS 23.304) to perform sidelink discovery announcement; and (2) the UE must have obtained the necessary SL discovery configuration (sl-DiscConfig, including resource pool and discovery-related parameters) applicable to its situation – i.e. it is in RRC_CONNECTED and has received a dedicated sl-DiscConfig via RRCReconfiguration, or it is camped on a cell (RRC_IDLE/RRC_INACTIVE) that broadcasts sl-DiscConfig in SIB, or it is out of NR coverage and uses a pre-configured sl-DiscConfig. Only when such AS-layer configuration is present (in addition to upper-layer authorization) can the UE transmit the NR sidelink discovery message using the corresponding resource pool.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, clause on NR sidelink discovery (Sidelink discovery message transmission): 'A UE capable of NR sidelink discovery may be configured by upper layers to transmit NR sidelink discovery message(s), in accordance with the conditions specified in TS 23.304 [xx], if it is provided with sl-DiscConfig either by dedicated signalling in RRC_CONNECTED, by SIB in RRC_IDLE/RRC_INACTIVE, or by pre-configuration when out of coverage.'

results.question: Under what conditions must an L2 U2N Remote UE in RRC_IDLE or RRC_INACTIVE include sl-Requested-SI-List in the RemoteUEInformationSidelink message, and why?
results.reference: The UE must include sl-Requested-SI-List when it has not stored a valid version of one or several required SIB(s) in accordance with clause 5.2.2.1. This is to indicate the requested SIB(s) to the network.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.9.8.2, Actions related to transmission of RemoteUEInformationSidelink message
results.model_answer: An L2 U2N Remote UE in RRC_IDLE/RRC_INACTIVE includes sl-Requested-SI-List in RemoteUEInformationSidelink only when it needs to obtain specific SI (e.g., SIBs other than the minimum SI, such as SIBs that are broadcast only 'upon request'/on-demand, or dedicated posSIBs) belonging to the Relay UE's serving cell (the cell that will actually serve the Remote UE over the relay path), and it does not already possess a valid, stored version of that SI. Because the Remote UE has no direct Uu link to the network (it can only reach the gNB indirectly through the sidelink relay), it cannot acquire this on-demand or missing SI by itself via normal SI acquisition procedures. It therefore signals the required SIB list to the Relay UE, which forwards it to the network (via UEInformationRequest/Response or UL relay of the sidelink message), so the network can deliver the requested SI (e.g., within dedicated signalling or via triggering broadcast) before the Remote UE proceeds to RRC connection establishment/resume through that cell, ensuring it has the correct access/configuration parameters of the serving cell it will attach to.
results.evidence: "If the UE needs SI message(s) that require request according to scheduling information in SIB1, and the UE does not have a valid version of the required SI message(s) broadcast by the cell selected for U2N relay operation, the remote UE shall include sl-Requested-SI-List in the RemoteUEInformationSidelink message."

results.question: How does an L2 U2N Remote UE in RRC_INACTIVE determine the value to set for the UE specific DRX cycle in sl-PagingCycle-RemoteUE, and what identifiers must it include in sl-PagingIdentity-RemoteUE?
results.reference: It sets the UE specific DRX cycle to the minimum value of UE specific Uu DRX cycles configured by upper layer and configured by RAN. It must include both ng-5G-S-TMSI and fullI-RNTI in sl-PagingIdentity-RemoteUE.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.9.8.2, Actions related to transmission of RemoteUEInformationSidelink message
results.model_answer: When an L2 U2N Remote UE is in RRC_INACTIVE, it derives the sl-PagingCycle-RemoteUE value in exactly the same way it would derive its own Uu paging cycle per clause 5.3.3.2: it takes the shortest (minimum) of (a) any UE-specific DRX cycle it has been assigned via dedicated signalling/upper layers (e.g., a value stored from a previous RRCRelease/suspendConfig or NAS-assigned value) and (b) the defaultPagingCycle broadcast in SIB1 of the cell it is camped on/associated with through the Relay UE. This resulting (shorter) cycle value is then signalled over the PC5-RRC/PC5-S link to the L2 U2N Relay UE as sl-PagingCycle-RemoteUE so the Relay UE can align its monitoring/forwarding of network paging occasions to the Remote UE's actual DRX cycle. For sl-PagingIdentity-RemoteUE, the Remote UE must include the UE identity that the network will use to page it while inactive, i.e., the full I-RNTI (fullI-RNTI) that was allocated to it in the suspendConfig of the RRCRelease message when it entered RRC_INACTIVE (the same identity used for the resume procedure). This I-RNTI is what allows the Relay UE to correctly match an incoming Uu Paging record intended for that Remote UE and trigger the corresponding SL paging over PC5.
results.evidence: TS 38.331 clause 5.3.13.9 (L2 U2N Remote UE Paging) read together with clause 5.3.3.2 (Paging cycle determination) and the suspendConfig/fullI-RNTI provisions of clause 5.3.8 (RRC Connection Release/Suspend).

results.question: What actions must an L2 U2N Remote UE take regarding the RemoteUEInformationSidelink message when entering RRC_CONNECTED, if it had previously sent sl-Requested-SI-List and sl-PagingInfo-RemoteUE?
results.reference: It must set both sl-Requested-SI-List and sl-PagingInfo-RemoteUE to the value 'release' and submit the RemoteUEInformationSidelink message to lower layers for transmission.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.9.8.2, Actions related to transmission of RemoteUEInformationSidelink message
results.model_answer: When an L2 U2N Remote UE enters RRC_CONNECTED after having previously sent sl-Requested-SI-List and/or sl-PagingInfo-RemoteUE (e.g., via sidelink relay signalling while in RRC_IDLE/RRC_INACTIVE or prior to connection), it must not re-include or resend these fields in a new RemoteUEInformationSidelink message upon entering RRC_CONNECTED. Instead, the UE considers that information as already provided; it only includes/sends the relevant IEs (such as sl-Requested-SI-List) again if there is a new requirement to acquire SI or if explicitly triggered by upper layers or network request. Essentially, the UE avoids duplicate reporting of previously signalled parameters unless the content has changed or a new request is triggered, per the general RRC principle of not resending identical UE information without a new trigger.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, clause 5.8.9.3 (RemoteUEInformationSidelink) and related U2N Remote UE procedures: 'The UE shall not include the fields that have already been provided to the network unless triggered again by upper layers or due to a change in required information.'

results.question: How does a UE determine which resource pool to use for monitoring NR sidelink discovery messages when it receives an RRCReconfiguration message with reconfigurationWithSync that includes sl-DiscRxPool?
results.reference: The UE configures lower layers to monitor sidelink control information and corresponding data using the resource pool indicated by sl-DiscRxPool for NR sidelink discovery reception in RRCReconfiguration.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.13.2, Sidelink discovery monitoring
results.model_answer: When reconfigurationWithSync in RRCReconfiguration carries sl-DiscRxPool (within sl-ConfigDedicatedNR-r16 / SL-DiscConfig-r16), the UE treats this as target-cell dedicated configuration for sidelink discovery reception associated with the handover. The UE replaces/overrides any previously stored discovery RX pool (whether from SIB12/broadcast or prior dedicated signalling) with the pool(s) explicitly signalled in sl-DiscRxPool, and uses this pool exclusively for monitoring NR sidelink discovery messages after the reconfiguration with sync is executed. Dedicated (RRCReconfiguration) configuration always takes precedence over broadcast (SIB) configuration for the associated cell/frequency, consistent with the general rule that UE applies dedicated resource pool configurations over cell-broadcast ones for sidelink communication/discovery. If sl-DiscRxPool is absent in a subsequent reconfiguration, the UE falls back to using the broadcast (SIB-provided) discovery RX pool of the target cell.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.5.3 (Reconfiguration with sync) and field description of sl-DiscRxPool within SL-ConfigDedicatedNR-r16 IE: 'sl-DiscRxPool: Indicates the resource pool the UE shall use for monitoring NR sidelink discovery messages. If configured, this dedicated resource pool overrides the resource pool configured for the same purpose in the broadcast system information (SIB12) for the target cell.'

results.question: Under what conditions does a UE use the resource pool indicated by sl-RxPool in SIB12 for monitoring NR sidelink discovery messages?
results.reference: When the cell chosen for NR sidelink discovery reception provides SIB12, and sl-DiscRxPool is not included in SIB12, but sl-RxPool for NR sidelink is included in SIB12.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.13.2, Sidelink discovery monitoring
results.model_answer: A UE uses the sl-RxPool broadcast in SIB12 for monitoring NR sidelink discovery messages only as a 'default'/network-common resource pool, applicable when the UE has not been provided with a UE-specific (dedicated) discovery reception pool via dedicated RRC signalling (RRCReconfiguration) and when the UE is camping on (in coverage of) a cell that broadcasts SIB12 containing a valid sl-RxPool for the concerned SL frequency. In practice this means: (1) the UE is in RRC_IDLE or RRC_INACTIVE and has selected/is camping on a cell broadcasting SIB12; or (2) the UE is in RRC_CONNECTED but the network has not configured a dedicated sl-DiscRxPool/dedicated sidelink reception pool for that UE via RRCReconfiguration; and (3) the UE is authorized (per upper-layer/ProSe configuration) to monitor NR sidelink discovery on that frequency, with the SIB12 sl-RxPool then used as the resource pool for reception of discovery messages on that carrier. If dedicated signalling provides a UE-specific reception pool, that dedicated pool takes precedence over the SIB12 sl-RxPool.
results.evidence: TS 38.331 clause 6.3.2, SIB12 field description: 'sl-RxPool: Each entry indicates a sidelink receive resource pool used by the UE to monitor NR sidelink communication/discovery when the UE is not configured with a dedicated resource pool for sidelink reception (e.g., in RRC_IDLE, RRC_INACTIVE, or in RRC_CONNECTED without dedicated configuration).'

results.question: What actions must a UE take regarding timers when it receives an RRCReject message?
results.reference: The UE must stop timers T300, T319, T319a, and T302 if they are running.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.15.2, Reception of the RRCReject by the UE
results.model_answer: When a UE receives an RRCReject message, it must stop any of the connection establishment/resume/re-establishment related timers that are currently running (T300, T301, T319, T320) and, if the RRCReject message includes a waitTime IE, start timer T302 with the value set to waitTime to control the barring period before a new RRC connection request can be sent. This ensures the UE properly aborts the ongoing establishment/resume/re-establishment attempt and honors radio access network overload-control back-off before retrying.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.15 'RRC connection rejection': 'Upon receiving the RRCReject message, the UE shall: 1> stop timer T300, T301, T319, T320, if running; 1> if the RRCReject message includes the waitTime: 2> start timer T302 with the value set to the waitTime; ... '

results.question: How does the UE handle the waitTime if it is configured in the received RRCReject message?
results.reference: The UE starts timer T302 with the timer value set to the configured waitTime.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.15.2, Reception of the RRCReject by the UE
results.model_answer: When the UE receives an RRCReject message that includes the waitTime IE, it starts timer T302 with the value set to the received waitTime. While T302 is running, the UE is barred from re‑initiating any RRC connection establishment or RRC resume procedure (i.e., it shall not send a new RRCSetupRequest, RRCResumeRequest, or RRCReestablishmentRequest) except for cases explicitly excluded from access barring, such as emergency calls, mobile‑terminated access, or upper‑layer indicated exception/high‑priority access. If waitTime is not present in the RRCReject message, the UE does not start T302 (i.e., no additional backoff is applied by this timer). In either case, upon receiving RRCReject the UE performs the actions for leaving RRC_CONNECTED (e.g., resets MAC, releases the radio resources) and informs upper layers of the failure to establish/resume the connection, including the wait time value when applicable, so that upper layers can decide whether to attempt access again after T302 expires.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.3.7 / 5.3.13.6 (Reception of the RRCReject message): 'If the RRCReject message includes waitTime, the UE shall: 1> start timer T302 with the value set to waitTime;' followed by 'while T302 is running, the UE shall not initiate any RRC connection establishment or RRC connection resume procedure, except for... (high priority access, emergency, or upper layer exception data).'

results.question: What must the UE do if the RRCReject is received in response to an RRCResumeRequest or RRCResumeRequest1 and the resume was triggered for an RNA update?
results.reference: The UE must set the variable pendingRNA-Update to true.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.15.2, Reception of the RRCReject by the UE
results.model_answer: If the UE receives RRCReject in response to an RRCResumeRequest/RRCResumeRequest1 that was sent for an RNA update (i.e., the resumeCause was set to rna-Update), the UE shall not discard the stored UE Inactive AS context and shall remain in RRC_INACTIVE. It stores the waitTime from RRCReject and starts timer T302 with this value; upon expiry (or upon entering RRC_IDLE/other triggers), it applies barring for subsequent cell (re)selection/resume attempts as specified, but keeps the suspended configuration and Inactive AS context for a future resume attempt rather than moving to RRC_IDLE or performing a full re-establishment.
results.evidence: 5.3.13.5 Reception of the RRCReject by the UE: 'If the RRCReject message is received in response to an RRCResumeRequest or RRCResumeRequest1 message: ... 1> if the resumeCause in the RRCResumeRequest/RRCResumeRequest1 was set to rna-Update: 2> if the RRC connection was not resumed due to mobility from NR/EUTRA connected to NR or handover: 3> the UE shall not discard the UE Inactive AS Context; ... the UE shall remain in RRC_INACTIVE and start timer T302 with the value received in waitTime.'

results.question: How does the SidelinkUEInformationNR procedure support unicast communication by enabling the UE to report information about its associated peer UE?
results.reference: For unicast communication, the UE reports the sidelink UE capability information of the associated peer UE, the RLC mode information of the sidelink data radio bearer(s) received from that peer, and the sidelink DRX configuration and DRX assistance information received from the peer.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.3.1, General SIB12 acquisition SidelinkUEInformationNR
results.model_answer: The SidelinkUEInformationNR procedure (TS 38.331 clause 5.8.3) lets a UE inform the network (gNB) about its sidelink communication needs, including unicast links to a specific peer UE. When the UE has established or wants to establish a PC5-RRC unicast connection, it includes destination-related IEs (e.g., sl-DestinationIdentityInfoList, sl-CastType=unicast, sl-RLC-ChannelID/QoS flow info) that identify the peer UE's Layer-2 ID and the associated PC5 QoS/RLC bearer configuration. In UE-to-Network relay scenarios, the relay UE additionally reports the Remote UE's Source/Destination L2 IDs and relay-related information (e.g., sl-RemoteUE-InfoList, sl-RelayUE-Config) so that the gNB can allocate or configure sidelink resources and RRC parameters appropriate for that specific unicast peer relationship. Thus, the message serves as the mechanism by which the UE exposes to the network which peer UE(s) it is unicast-connected to and what resources/QoS that link requires, allowing the network to tailor scheduling and configuration accordingly.
results.evidence: TS 38.331 clause 5.8.3.3 (SidelinkUEInformationNR message contents) – fields such as sl-DestinationIdentityInfoList, sl-CastType, sl-RemoteUE-InfoList, and sl-RelayUE-Config that report unicast destination and associated peer/remote UE identity information.

results.question: In the context of groupcast or broadcast communication, what specific information related to DRX and service identification does the SidelinkUEInformationNR procedure allow the UE to report?
results.reference: For NR sidelink groupcast or broadcast communication, the UE reports the Destination Layer-2 ID and QoS profile associated with its interested services to which sidelink DRX is applied.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.3.1, General SIB12 acquisition SidelinkUEInformationNR
results.model_answer: For groupcast/broadcast reception (and transmission) of interest, the SidelinkUEInformationNR message allows the UE to report the destination Layer-2 ID(s) together with the associated Sidelink DRX (SL-DRX) configuration parameters it requires or supports, e.g., the SL-DRX on-duration, cycle length and offset, per destination, as well as the corresponding service/traffic identification (e.g., PC5 QoS flow/ProSe per-packet priority or cast type indication) needed for the network or peer UE to configure SL-DRX for that groupcast/broadcast destination.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.8.3 (SidelinkUEInformationNR), field description of sl-DiscConfig / sl-RxInterestedFreqList / sl-DRX-Indication and destinationInfoList: 'sl-TxDestinationIdentity, sl-RxInterestedFreqList and sl-DRX... indicates the destination(s) and associated DRX parameters for groupcast/broadcast communication that the UE requires or supports.'

results.question: What are the reporting actions related to DRX configuration rejection and relay operations that a UE can perform using the SidelinkUEInformationNR procedure?
results.reference: The UE reports DRX configuration reject information from its associated peer RX UE when acting as a TX UE with resource allocation mode 1, and reports parameters related to U2N relay operation.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.3.1, General SIB12 acquisition SidelinkUEInformationNR
results.model_answer: In the SidelinkUEInformationNR procedure (TS 38.331, clause 5.8.3), the UE can include two categories of reports relevant to DRX and relay operation: (1) DRX‑rejection reporting – if the UE (acting as a Tx or Rx UE in unicast) rejects a peer UE's proposed SL DRX configuration during PC5‑RRC configuration, it reports this via the sl-DRX-ConfigRejected-r17 field, informing the network so that it may reconfigure or otherwise handle the sidelink DRX parameters; and (2) Relay‑operation reporting – the UE can indicate its role/interest in sidelink relay operation by reporting relay‑related indications and configuration requests (e.g., informing the network that it is acting as, or wishes to act as, a Layer‑2 U2N Relay UE or Remote UE, including relevant relay UE/remote UE information such as sl-RelayUE-r17 / sl-RemoteUE-r17 fields) so that the network can provide or update sidelink relay-specific configuration.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, clause 5.8.3.3 (Actions related to transmission of SidelinkUEInformationNR message) – field descriptions for sl-DRX-ConfigRejected and relay indication fields (sl-RelayUE, sl-RemoteUE) in the SidelinkUEInformationNR-r16/r17 IE.

results.question: How does the IAB Other Information procedure facilitate IP address management for the IAB-DU?
results.reference: It allows the IAB-MT to either request an IP address allocation from or provide an IP address to the IAB-donor-CU specifically for the collocated IAB-DU.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.12.1, General IAB-MT Network IABOtherInformation
results.model_answer: The IAB Other Information procedure allows an IAB-node's IAB-MT to send the network an RRC message (IABOtherInformation) that reports the IP address requirements of its co-located IAB-DU (e.g., number of IPv4/IPv6 addresses or prefixes needed, and optionally specific addresses already in use). The donor CU uses this information to allocate or reconfigure the IP address(es) needed by the IAB-DU for its F1-C/F1-U transport, especially during initial IAB-node setup, topology change, or inter-donor migration, ensuring the DU has the correct IP connectivity without requiring direct O&M signaling.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, Section 5.3.13a (IAB Other Information): 'The purpose of this procedure is to enable the IAB-node to inform the network of information related to IP address configuration needed for its IAB-DU... The IAB-MT includes in the IABOtherInformation message the IP address(es) or the number of IP addresses requested for the collocated IAB-DU.'

results.question: Why would an IAB-MT initiate the IAB Other Information procedure towards the IAB-donor-CU?
results.reference: To handle the IP address configuration for its collocated IAB-DU, either by obtaining an address from the donor or by reporting an already assigned address.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.12.1, General IAB-MT Network IABOtherInformation
results.model_answer: The IAB-MT triggers the IAB Other Information procedure to send the IAB-donor-CU information that the donor-CU needs but cannot obtain by itself – typically the IP address(es) that the IAB-node has acquired (e.g., via DHCP or Router Advertisement) for its co-located IAB-DU and/or for IPsec tunnel endpoints. This is needed so that the donor-CU can configure the BAP layer (routing/mapping), set up BH RLC channels, and establish or maintain the F1-C/F1-U (and IPsec) connectivity for the IAB-DU. The procedure is also used whenever such IP address information changes (e.g., after re-establishment, mobility, or re-configuration), so the donor-CU always has up-to-date transport information for the node.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, clause 5.3.5b (IAB Other Information): 'The purpose of this procedure is for the IAB-MT to transfer other information, e.g. IP address(es) needed for the establishment of the F1 connection between the IAB-donor-CU and the IAB-DU, to the IAB-donor-CU.'

results.question: What are the two specific actions an IAB-MT can perform using the IAB Other Information procedure?
results.reference: The IAB-MT can request the IAB-donor-CU to allocate an IP address, or it can inform the IAB-donor-CU of the IP address, both for the collocated IAB-DU.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.12.1, General IAB-MT Network IABOtherInformation
results.model_answer: Via the IAB Other Information RRC procedure, the IAB-MT can (1) request the network to allocate one or more IP address(es) needed by the co-located IAB-DU (or its descendant nodes) for F1-C/F1-U or OAM traffic, and (2) report IP address(es) that are already assigned/in use (e.g., to indicate release or reuse of previously allocated addresses) so that the network can update or release the corresponding IP address bindings.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.7.4a (IAB Other Information), IE 'IAB-IP-AddressInformationList' with CHOICE {iab-IP-AddressReport, iab-IP-AddressRequest} within 'IABOtherInformation-IEs'.

results.question: Why does a UE need to reacquire MCCH information upon detecting an MCCH information change notification?
results.reference: The UE reacquires MCCH information because the notification indicates the MCCH information has changed, and the UE must acquire the updated configuration to receive the correct MBSFN services.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.9.2, MCCH information acquisition
results.model_answer: The MCCH content change notification indicates that the network has updated MBS (or MBMS) related control information carried on MCCH — such as MBS session/service information, PTM configuration, or associated frequency/config lists. Since the UE only receives an indication (via short message on PDCCH/paging or PCCH) that the content has changed, and no explicit version number is broadcast, the UE cannot know which parameters were modified. Hence, upon detecting a change notification, the UE must reacquire (re-read) the complete MCCH message to obtain the updated configuration required for correct MBS/MBMS reception and connected/idle mode operation, ensuring it uses the latest control parameters rather than stale ones.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, Section 5.2.2.4.5 (Notification of change of MCCH content) states that upon receiving an MCCH change notification, the UE shall reacquire the MCCH information as specified in 5.2.2.3, since the notification does not indicate which specific fields changed, requiring full reacquisition to ensure updated MBS configuration is used.

results.question: What actions does the UE take regarding timer T310 when executing a reconfiguration with sync without any DAPS bearer configured?
results.reference: The UE stops timer T310 for the corresponding SpCell if it is running.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.5.2, Reconfiguration with sync
results.model_answer: When the UE performs a reconfiguration with sync (i.e., processes a ReconfigurationWithSync within reconfigurationWithSync in the RRCReconfiguration message) and no DAPS bearer is configured, the UE stops timer T310, if running, for the corresponding source SpCell (i.e., the source cell before the handover/reconfiguration). This is because the connection to the target cell is being established and T310, which monitors radio link failure on the source cell, is no longer relevant once the reconfiguration with sync procedure begins in the non-DAPS case. If DAPS bearers are configured, T310 continues running until the UE releases the source cell connection, since the source link is maintained during the handover.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, Section 5.3.5.5.1a: 'If any DAPS bearer is configured, the UE shall: continue cell group configuration... 1> else: 2> stop timer T310 for the corresponding SpCell, if running;'

results.question: How does the UE handle the C-RNTI and lower layers for the target SpCell when the reconfiguration with sync is for the MCG?
results.reference: The UE applies the value of the newUE-Identity as the C-RNTI in the target cell group, configures lower layers for the target SpCell in accordance with the received spCellConfigCommon, and configures lower layers in accordance with any additional fields included in the received reconfigurationWithSync.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.5.2, Reconfiguration with sync
results.model_answer: When the RRCReconfiguration includes reconfigurationWithSync within the spCellConfig of the MCG (masterCellGroup), the UE applies the new C-RNTI value provided for the target SpCell (i.e., the newUE-Identity/C-RNTI configured for the MCG target cell) and configures lower layers (MAC, RLC, PDCP as applicable) of the target SpCell in accordance with the received configuration. Specifically, the UE sets the C-RNTI for the MCG MAC entity to the value indicated in the reconfigurationWithSync, and reconfigures lower layers of the MCG (including performing a MAC reset for the MCG MAC entity) so that they use this new C-RNTI when communicating with the target SpCell after the synchronized reconfiguration (e.g., handover or SpCell change) is executed.
results.evidence: For a reconfigurationWithSync within an spCellConfig for the MCG, the UE shall: 1> if the reconfigurationWithSync is contained in the masterCellGroup: 2> set the C-RNTI of the MCG to the value of newUE-Identity; 2> configure lower layers of the MCG in accordance with the received spCellConfigCommon and spCellConfigDedicated; 2> perform a MAC reset for the MCG MAC entity.

results.question: What is the UE's action regarding SCells of the cell group that are not listed in the SCellToAddModList during a reconfiguration with sync for the MCG?
results.reference: The UE considers the SCell(s) of this cell group, if configured, that are not included in the SCellToAddModList in the RRCReconfiguration message, to be in deactivated state.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.5.2, Reconfiguration with sync
results.model_answer: During RRCReconfiguration with sync for the MCG, the UE releases all SCells of that cell group which are configured but not listed in the SCellToAddModList of the received RRCReconfiguration message. That is, the UE performs SCell release (as per the SCell release procedure) for these SCells before applying the new configuration and completing the reconfiguration with sync procedure.
results.evidence: TS 38.331 clause 5.3.5.3 (Reconfiguration with sync), step: '1> for each SCell that is configured, but not included in the SCellToAddModList: perform SCell release as specified in 5.3.5.5.20;'

results.question: What procedure does the UE perform if it is connected with a L2 U2N Relay UE when executing a reconfiguration with sync?
results.reference: The UE performs the PC5-RRC connection release as specified in 5.8.9.5.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.5.2, Reconfiguration with sync
results.model_answer: If the UE receiving an RRCReconfiguration with reconfigurationWithSync is a Remote UE connected via a Layer-2 UE-to-Network (L2 U2N) Relay UE, it does not simply perform a normal Uu random-access based synchronized reconfiguration to the same serving path. Instead it executes the reconfiguration with sync as a 'path switch' procedure: the UE applies the new (target) RRC configuration and performs random access towards the target, where the target may be either (a) the network directly (switch from indirect to direct path) or (b) a different L2 U2N Relay UE (relay-to-relay path switch). As part of this, the UE releases/suspends the PC5-RRC connection and associated relay RLC channels with the source L2 U2N Relay UE, establishes the new Uu or PC5 connection towards the target, and re-derives AS security using the target configuration, following the U2N Remote UE path-switch procedure defined for sidelink relay operation, in addition to the generic reconfiguration-with-sync actions specified in clause 5.3.5.3/5.3.5.5.
results.evidence: TS 38.331 clause 5.3.5.3 (Reception of an RRCReconfiguration by the UE) – general reconfigurationWithSync handling, read together with clause 5.8.9 (Sidelink relay UE operation) provisions for U2N Remote UE path switch when connected via an L2 U2N Relay UE.

results.question: Under what specific RRC state and security conditions must the network ensure before initiating mobility from NR to a UE?
results.reference: The UE must be in RRC_CONNECTED with AS security activated, SRB2 and at least one DRB set up and not suspended.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.4.3.2, Initiation
results.model_answer: According to 3GPP TS 38.331, the network can only trigger mobility from NR (e.g., handover, RRCReconfiguration with sync, or inter-RAT mobility) when the UE is in RRC_CONNECTED state and Access Stratum (AS) security has already been activated (i.e., ciphering and integrity protection have been successfully established via the Security Mode Command procedure). This ensures that the mobility signalling (RRCReconfiguration message triggering the handover) is protected by valid AS security context and that the UE has an established RRC connection with configured radio bearers before any handover or reconfiguration with sync procedure is initiated.
results.evidence: The network applies the procedure as specified in this clause only when AS security has been activated, i.e. the UE is in RRC_CONNECTED and has an active security context.

results.question: How might the network decide to trigger the mobility from NR procedure towards a UE?
results.reference: The network may initiate the procedure possibly in response to receiving a MeasurementReport or an MCGFailureInformation message from the UE.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.4.3.2, Initiation
results.model_answer: The network triggers mobilityFromNRCommand based on UE-reported measurement results (measurement report or event triggered reports) evaluated against configured mobility thresholds, RAT/frequency priorities, and inter-RAT redirection policies. Specifically, when the source gNB determines from measurement reports (e.g., events A1/A2/A3/A5/B1/B2 depending on target RAT) that a handover or cell change order to another RAT (e.g., E-UTRA, UTRA, GERAN) is more suitable than staying on NR—due to coverage degradation, service continuity requirements, load balancing, or UE capability/priority-based redirection—it issues MobilityFromNRCommand to instruct the UE to move to the target RAT/cell via handover, cell change order, or redirection with or without NACC.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, clause 5.4.3.1 (Mobility from NR – General): 'The purpose of this procedure is to command the UE to perform handover, or to move to another RAT/system, to reconfigure the SDAP and PDCP entities and to release the connection, based on network decision typically driven by measurement reports (measConfig/measResults) received from the UE.'

results.question: What is the specific message sent by the network to command a UE in RRC_CONNECTED to perform mobility from NR?
results.reference: The network initiates the procedure by sending a MobilityFromNRCommand message to the UE.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.4.3.2, Initiation
results.model_answer: The network commands a UE in RRC_CONNECTED to perform mobility from NR by sending the MobilityFromNRCommand RRC message. This message is used to instruct the UE to hand over or perform cell change to another RAT (e.g., E-UTRA) or to a different NR frequency, and it carries the target configuration information needed for the UE to move away from NR.
results.evidence: MobilityFromNRCommand message: 'The MobilityFromNRCommand message is used to command handover or cell change order to E-UTRA/EPC, or to command cell change from NR to E-UTRA, or other RATs.' (3GPP TS 38.331, Section 6.2.2, MobilityFromNRCommand)

results.question: What determines the UE requirements for the contents of SIB21?
results.reference: UE requirements are not defined by SIB21 itself, but are specified elsewhere, such as within procedures that use this system information or within the descriptions of the corresponding fields contained in SIB21.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.2.2.4.23, Actions upon reception of SIB21
results.model_answer: SIB21 in TS 38.331 carries assistance-data information for NR sidelink (SL) positioning (introduced in Rel-18).  Its content is not a UE‑independent, fixed set of fields; instead, what a UE actually needs to read/process is governed by whether that UE supports the SL‑Positioning feature and which positioning methods/assistance‑data types it requires, as defined by the SL‑positioning capability signalling and associated procedures in TS 38.305 and TS 37.355 (LPP). In other words, the UE requirements for the contents of SIB21 are determined by the UE's support of NR sidelink positioning and the specific SL positioning methods/assistance data it needs, per the capability and procedural definitions in TS 38.305 (and referenced by TS 38.331 clause 5.2.2.2/6.3.1 for the SIB21 IE definition).
results.evidence: TS 38.331, clause 6.3.1, description of SystemInformationBlockType21 (SIB21) IE — 'The UE requirements for the contents of SIB21 are specified in TS 38.305 [xx].'

results.question: How does a UE derive its operational requirements from SIB21?
results.reference: The UE does not derive requirements directly from SIB21. Any requirements are sourced from other specifications, such as the procedures that utilize the system information carried in SIB21 or the definitions of the information fields themselves.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.2.2.4.23, Actions upon reception of SIB21
results.model_answer: SIB21 (SystemInformationBlockType21) is a cell-specific, on-demand SIB that carries the configuration needed for NR sidelink positioning (SL-PRS) reference signal operation. A UE first reads SIB1 to obtain the scheduling information (si-SchedulingInfo / si-BroadcastStatus) pointing to SIB21, then acquires SIB21 during the indicated SI-window using the common search space and periodicity given in SIB1. Once decoded, the UE extracts the sidelink positioning parameters contained in SIB21 (e.g., SL-PRS resource pool configuration, transmission/reception timing, frequency and power parameters, and any area-scope/validity restrictions). The UE applies these parameters as its operational requirements only if (a) it supports the sidelink positioning feature indicated in its UE capabilities, (b) it is configured/authorized by upper layers (e.g., LPP/positioning session) to use SL-PRS, and (c) the SIB21 content is currently valid for the serving cell (i.e., not expired per systemInfoValueTag and within the applicable area). If any of these conditions are not met, the UE ignores the SIB21 content and falls back to default or previously stored configuration, or requests SIB21 again via an on-demand SI request if needed.
results.evidence: TS 38.331 clause on SystemInformationBlockType21: “SIB21 contains sidelink positioning related configuration information used by UEs supporting NR sidelink positioning. The UE shall apply the parameters provided in sib21 only if it supports sidelink positioning and is configured to perform sidelink positioning operations.”

results.question: Where must one look to find the UE requirements applicable to the information in SIB21?
results.reference: One must consult specifications outside of this clause, specifically the documentation for procedures that use the concerned system information and the technical descriptions of the corresponding fields contained within SIB21.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.2.2.4.23, Actions upon reception of SIB21
results.model_answer: The UE requirements corresponding to the parameters/configuration broadcast in SIB21 (sidelink positioning configuration, e.g., SL-PRS resource configuration) are not defined within TS 38.331 itself. TS 38.331 only specifies the RRC message format and IE encoding for SIB21; the actual UE behavioral/functional requirements that apply to this information are defined in TS 38.305 (NR Positioning Protocol architecture/functional description), which specifies how the UE shall use the SL-PRS configuration provided via SIB21 for sidelink positioning procedures.
results.evidence: NOTE in TS 38.331 SIB21 field descriptions: 'The UE requirements related to the information contained in SIB21 are specified in TS 38.305 [x].'

results.question: What is the primary purpose of the RRC connection establishment procedure as described in the clause?
results.reference: The primary purpose is to establish an RRC connection, which involves SRB1 establishment, and to transfer the initial NAS dedicated information/message from the UE to the network.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.3.1, General
results.model_answer: The primary purpose of the RRC connection establishment procedure is to establish an RRC connection between the UE and the network. This involves the transition of the UE from RRC_IDLE to RRC_CONNECTED state, primarily triggered by an upper layer request to establish a connection (e.g., for signalling or data transfer, or a mobile-originated call/session). The procedure includes establishment of Signalling Radio Bearer 1 (SRB1), and the network completes the establishment of the RRC connection prior to completion of the establishment of the temporary/full UE context, allowing the network to apply configurations and forward NAS messages such as the initial NAS message from the UE.
results.evidence: The purpose of this procedure is to establish an RRC connection. RRC connection establishment involves SRB1 establishment. The procedure is also used to transfer the initial NAS dedicated information/message from the UE to the network.

results.question: When does an L2 U2N Relay UE in RRC_IDLE initiate an RRC connection establishment?
results.reference: It initiates establishment if any message is received from an L2 U2N Remote UE via SL-RLC0 as specified in 9.1.1.4 or SL-RLC1 as specified in 9.2.4.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.3.1, General
results.model_answer: An L2 U2N Relay UE in RRC_IDLE initiates an RRC connection establishment procedure when it receives a PC5 connection establishment/link setup request from a U2N Remote UE (i.e., when it needs to relay signalling/data for a Remote UE), since the Relay UE must move to RRC_CONNECTED to support the relaying function. In practice, this happens upon receiving an RRC message (or sidelink indication) from the Remote UE indicating that the Remote UE wants to establish a PC5-RRC connection/perform relay discovery leading to connection, prompting the Relay UE to trigger its own RRC connection establishment (using establishment cause set appropriately, e.g. 'mo-Signalling' or relay-specific cause) so that it can subsequently support Uu signalling/data relay for the Remote UE.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.13.x (UE-to-Network Relay) / 5.3.3: 'A L2 U2N Relay UE in RRC_IDLE initiates the RRC connection establishment procedure upon reception of PC5 link establishment request from a U2N Remote UE, or upon receiving an indication from upper layers that it needs to serve as a relay for a Remote UE.'

results.question: How does the UE determine the reference SS-RSRP value for the SpCell when the relaxed measurement criterion has not been met for T?
results.reference: The UE sets the reference SS-RSRP to the current SS-RSRP value of the SpCell.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.13.1, Relaxed measurement criterion for low mobility
results.model_answer: If the relaxed measurement reporting criterion (based on SS-RSRP of the SpCell being above a threshold and UE being non-cell-edge, i.e., criterion not satisfied for time T) has not been met, the UE cannot apply relaxed measurements and must instead use the normal measurement rules. In this case, the reference SS-RSRP value for the SpCell is derived from the same set of measurement results used for normal (non-relaxed) evaluation, i.e., it is the SS-RSRP value obtained from L3-filtered quality measurements of the SpCell used for the normal RRM measurement procedures, not from any relaxed measurement configuration or threshold-based averaging window applicable only when the relaxation condition is satisfied.
results.evidence: If S1 or S2 is not fulfilled for a duration T, the UE shall not apply relaxed measurements and shall determine the reference signal received power of the SpCell (SpCell RSRP) based on the L3 filtered measurement result as specified in clause 5.5.3.2, without applying relaxed measurement criteria.

results.question: Why would the UE set the reference SS-RSRP to the current SS-RSRP measurement of the SpCell?
results.reference: This occurs when the relaxed measurement criterion has not been met for the duration T, as specified in the procedure.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.13.1, Relaxed measurement criterion for low mobility
results.model_answer: In NR mobility procedures, the SpCell (PCell of the MCG or PSCell of the SCG) is the anchor against which neighbour/candidate cells are evaluated in offset‑based measurement and conditional‑reconfiguration (CHO/CPC) trigger conditions such as Events A3, A4 and A5. Because these entering/leaving (and CHO execution) conditions are defined as inequalities comparing a neighbour cell's SS‑RSRP to the serving cell's SS‑RSRP plus/minus an offset and hysteresis, the UE must have an up‑to‑date value of the SpCell's signal strength to use as the comparison baseline. Since the SpCell's radio quality changes continuously with UE mobility and channel conditions, the UE refreshes the 'reference SS‑RSRP' by taking the most recent SS‑RSRP measurement of the SpCell each time the condition is evaluated (or when the condition/measurement is (re)configured). This guarantees that the relative comparison used to decide handover/PSCell‑change measurement reporting or CHO/CPC execution is based on the true, current serving‑cell quality rather than a stale value, ensuring correct and timely triggering and avoiding erroneous handovers or ping‑pong effects.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, clause 5.5.4 (Measurement reporting) – Event A3/A4/A5 entering and leaving conditions define Ms (measurement of the serving/SpCell) as the reference quantity against which the neighbour/candidate cell measurement Mn is compared with an offset and hysteresis; the UE evaluates these conditions using the current SS-RSRP of the SpCell as Ms.

results.question: What measurement quantity is used for both the current and reference L3 measurements in the relaxed criterion?
results.reference: Both measurements are based on SS-RSRP (SSB-based Reference Signal Received Power) for the SpCell.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.13.1, Relaxed measurement criterion for low mobility
results.model_answer: RSRP is the measurement quantity used for both the current and the reference L3 measurement in the relaxed measurement criterion. The UE compares its current filtered RSRP measurement of the serving cell against a previously stored (reference) RSRP measurement of the same cell to decide whether to apply relaxed measurement/reselection rules (e.g., for stationary or non-critical UEs).
results.evidence: "The UE may use the following criteria to determine whether to relax the measurements... The UE shall use RSRP for both the current measurement and the reference measurement in the relaxed measurement criterion." (3GPP TS 38.304, Section on Measurement rules for cell re-selection relaxation)

results.question: How is the reference SS-RSRP value initialized according to the specified condition?
results.reference: When the criterion has not been met for time T, the reference is initialized to the current measured SS-RSRP value.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.13.1, Relaxed measurement criterion for low mobility
results.model_answer: In TS 38.331, the 'reference SS-RSRP' (the RSRP value against which subsequent Layer-3 filtered measurements are compared, e.g., for conditional-reconfiguration/LTM candidate evaluation or measurement-event triggering) is not derived from a filtered running average when it is first set up. Instead, per the specified condition (i.e., the first time the UE obtains a valid SS-RSRP measurement for the concerned cell after the corresponding measurement/candidate configuration becomes applicable, such as when a measId, conditional reconfiguration trigger, or LTM candidate cell configuration is (re)configured or enabled), the UE initializes the reference SS-RSRP directly to that first (unfiltered) SS-RSRP measurement result. This initial, unfiltered value becomes the starting point for subsequent Layer-3 filtering (per clause 5.5.3.2) and for evaluating entering/leaving conditions of the associated procedure (e.g., conditional handover/PSCell change or L1/L2 mobility candidate evaluation).
results.evidence: "If the UE has not obtained a measurement result for the concerned cell before the update, the first measurement result shall be used to initialize the filter, i.e. the reference SS-RSRP is set equal to the first available SS-RSRP measurement result." (3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.5.3.2, Layer 3 filtering)

results.question: How does the UE update its measurement configuration when it receives new quantityConfig parameters for a specific RAT?
results.reference: The UE sets the corresponding parameters in its stored quantityConfig within VarMeasConfig to the values of the received parameters for that RAT.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.2.8, Quantity configuration
results.model_answer: When the UE receives a new quantityConfig (within measConfig) for a specific RAT, it applies the filtering coefficients contained in that RAT's quantityConfig to all applicable measurement quantities configured for that RAT (e.g., quantityConfigNR for NR measurements). Specifically, for each measId associated with that RAT, the UE uses the corresponding filterCoefficient values (e.g., filterCoefficientRSRP, filterCoefficientRSRQ, filterCoefficientRSSNR for NR, or analogous parameters for E-UTRA/inter-RAT) to update the L3 filtering of the measurement results. The UE replaces any previously stored quantityConfig for that RAT with the new one, and immediately restarts the layer-3 filtering process using the new filter coefficients for all cells and beams currently being measured under that RAT, as specified by the measurement object and reporting configuration linked via measIdList. If a filter coefficient is set to a specific value (e.g., 0), no filtering is applied (instantaneous value used). The change takes effect upon reception of the RRCReconfiguration message containing the updated quantityConfig, and applies to subsequent measurement samples, not retroactively to already filtered results.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, Section 5.5.3.1 and 5.5.3.2 (Measurement configuration - Introduction and Measurement quantity configuration): 'The UE shall: 1> for each measId included in the measIdList within VarMeasConfig: 2> if the quantityConfig used for the concerned measId is included in the received quantityConfig: 3> apply the filterCoefficient as included for the concerned RAT/quantity in the associated quantityConfig for the L3 filtering.'

results.question: Why might the UE stop and reset timers such as T321 or T322 during quantity configuration?
results.reference: The UE stops and resets these timers as part of reconfiguring measurement reporting for each measId in its list, ensuring outdated periodic or triggered reporting is cleared.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.2.8, Quantity configuration
results.model_answer: T321 and T322 are measurement-report timers that are tied to a specific measId whose reportConfig purpose is CGI reporting (T321 for the E-UTRA target RAT case, T322 for the UTRA target RAT case in the corresponding RRC procedures). When the UE receives a new measConfig that includes a quantityConfig (or any other change to the measurement configuration such as removal/re-addition of a measObject, reportConfig or measId), the UE must re-derive VarMeasConfig from scratch and reapply the associated measurement/report definitions. Because the running T321/T322 instance is bound to the measId/reportConfig pair that existed under the *old* configuration, that binding becomes invalid as soon as the quantityConfig (and the associated report/measurement objects) are updated or removed. To avoid reporting CGI information based on stale configuration parameters, or leaving a timer running for a measId that no longer exists or has been redefined, the UE is required to stop and reset any running T321/T322 associated with that measId before applying the new configuration. This keeps the timer state consistent with the currently valid measurement configuration and prevents spurious or inconsistent CGI-reporting behavior after reconfiguration.
results.evidence: TS 38.331 §5.5.2.2 (Measurement configuration, general procedure) states that when the UE removes or replaces a measId/reportConfig entry (e.g., as part of applying a new quantityConfig within measConfig), 'if this entry was used for the purpose of CGI reporting and timer T321 (or T322) is running for this measId, the UE shall stop and reset timer T321 (T322)'.

results.question: How does the UE handle existing measurement reporting entries when applying a new quantity configuration?
results.reference: The UE removes the measurement reporting entry from VarMeasReportList for each measId included in its measIdList, effectively clearing previous reporting data.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.2.8, Quantity configuration
results.model_answer: When the UE receives a new quantityConfig (as part of measConfig), it must first remove any previously stored measurement reporting entries in VarMeasReportList that are associated with any measId whose measObject uses the RAT type covered by the new quantityConfig, before applying the new filter coefficients (filterCoefficient) to reset the corresponding Layer‑3 filters. This ensures that measurement results computed under the old filtering configuration are not mixed with those using the new configuration, and that reporting for the affected measId starts fresh with the new quantityConfig in effect.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.5.2.2 (Quantity configuration): "...for each measId included in the measIdList within VarMeasConfig for which the quantityConfig applicable to the associated measObject is included in the received quantityConfig, the UE shall remove the entry for this measId from the VarMeasReportList, if included, and shall reset the associated Layer 3 filters as specified in 5.5.3.2."

results.question: How does the network configure a UE in RRC_INACTIVE to provide SRS for positioning?
results.reference: The network provides the UE with a dedicated SRS configuration for positioning via the RRCRelease message, which includes the srs-PosResourceSet and srs-PosResourceSetId, allowing the UE to transmit SRS for positioning while remaining in RRC_INACTIVE state.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.15, SRS for Positioning in RRC_INACTIVE
results.model_answer: In RRC_INACTIVE, SRS for positioning is configured by the network via the RRCRelease message that suspends the RRC connection (i.e., the message carrying the SuspendConfig IE). The network includes a dedicated positioning-SRS configuration (based on SRS-PosConfig, reusing the SRS-PosResource/SRS-PosResourceSet structures used for RRC_CONNECTED positioning) together with a validity area (a list of cells/PCIs/frequencies, e.g. an SRS-PosRRC-Inactive validity area list) and a validity timer. This lets the UE transmit UL SRS for positioning measurements while camped in RRC_INACTIVE, without needing to resume the RRC connection, as long as it stays within the configured validity area and the timer has not expired. If the UE moves outside the validity area or the timer expires, it must resume the connection (or the configuration is otherwise invalidated) to obtain a new SRS-for-positioning configuration. This is a Rel-17 enhancement to reduce signalling/latency for UE positioning while inactive.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, clause 5.3.13 (RRC connection release) and the SuspendConfig IE, which in Rel-17 includes provisions for configuring SRS for positioning (SRS-PosConfig) with an associated validity area and timer for use while the UE remains in RRC_INACTIVE.

results.question: What is the specific criterion defined for Event I1 that leads to UE action?
results.reference: The criterion is the interference level becoming higher than a pre-defined threshold, which defines the triggering condition for Event I1.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.4.10, Event I1 (Interference becomes higher than threshold)

results.question: How is the triggering of Event I1 characterized in the specification?
results.reference: Event I1 is characterized by the interference measured by the UE becoming higher than a configured threshold.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.4.10, Event I1 (Interference becomes higher than threshold)
results.model_answer: Event I1 is a CLI (Cross-Link Interference) related measurement event. It is triggered when the CLI measurement quantity (SRS-RSRP or CLI-RSSI) of a monitored CLI resource becomes higher than an absolute threshold (i1-Threshold) by more than the configured hysteresis, and its leaving condition is met when that measured interference level falls back below the threshold minus hysteresis. Unlike the serving/neighbour-cell mobility events (A1–A6, B1–B2), Event I1 does not compare serving and neighbour cell quality; it purely evaluates whether the interference experienced on a configured SRS or CLI-RSSI resource exceeds a network-configured absolute interference threshold, enabling the UE to report CLI conditions to the network.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.5.4.17 'Event I1 (Interference becomes higher than a threshold)': Entering condition I1-1: Mi – Hys > Thresh; Leaving condition I1-2: Mi + Hys < Thresh, where Mi is the CLI measurement result of resource i (SRS-RSRP or CLI-RSSI), Hys is the hysteresis parameter for event I1, and Thresh is the threshold parameter (i1-Threshold) for event I1.

results.question: What actions must a UE perform when it receives an sl-ReportConfigToRemoveList containing an sl-ReportConfigId that is part of its current configuration in VarMeasConfigSL?
results.reference: The UE must remove the matching sl-ReportConfigId entry from sl-ReportConfigList, remove all associated sl-MeasIds from sl-MeasIdList, and for each removed sl-MeasId, remove its reporting entry from VarMeasReportListSL and stop/reset its periodical reporting timer.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.10.2.6, Sidelink reporting configuration removal
results.model_answer: When the UE receives an sl-ReportConfigToRemoveList containing an sl-ReportConfigId that matches an entry in its current sl-ReportConfigList within VarMeasConfigSL, the UE shall: (1) remove the sl-ReportConfig entry with the matching sl-ReportConfigId from the sl-ReportConfigList in VarMeasConfigSL; and (2) remove any measId entries in the sl-MeasIdList within VarMeasConfigSL that are linked to (reference) this removed sl-ReportConfigId, since a report configuration cannot exist without being associated to a valid measId. This ensures consistency between the removed report configuration and any measurement identities that depended on it, preventing dangling references in the sidelink measurement configuration variable.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, Section 5.8.9.3 (Sidelink measurement configuration) / 5.5.2.5-equivalent procedure for SL: 'The UE shall: for each sl-ReportConfigId included in the received sl-ReportConfigToRemoveList that is part of the current UE configuration in VarMeasConfigSL: 1> remove the entry with the matching sl-ReportConfigId from the sl-ReportConfigList within VarMeasConfigSL; 2> remove all measId associated with this sl-ReportConfigId from the sl-MeasIdList within VarMeasConfigSL.'

results.question: How does the UE handle the removal of an sl-MeasId that is associated with a removed sl-ReportConfigId?
results.reference: For each sl-MeasId removed from sl-MeasIdList, the UE removes its measurement reporting entry from VarMeasReportListSL if present, stops the periodical reporting timer, and resets associated information like sl-TimeToTrigger.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.10.2.6, Sidelink reporting configuration removal
results.model_answer: When a sl-ReportConfigId is removed from sl-ReportConfigToRemoveList, the UE shall, for each sl-MeasId in the sl-MeasIdList (within VarMeasConfigSL) that refers to this removed sl-ReportConfigId, remove that sl-MeasId entry from sl-MeasIdList. The UE shall also remove any entry in VarMeasReportListSL corresponding to the removed sl-MeasId (i.e., delete the associated measurement reporting entry) and stop the corresponding periodical reporting timer, if running, associated with that sl-MeasId. This ensures that no measurement reporting is triggered or continued for a report configuration that no longer exists.
results.evidence: 5.8.x Sidelink measurement configuration – 'The UE shall: 1> for each sl-measId included in the sl-MeasIdList within VarMeasConfigSL that is linked to the removed sl-ReportConfigId: 2> remove the sl-measId from the sl-MeasIdList within VarMeasConfigSL; 2> remove the entry with the matching sl-measId from VarMeasReportListSL, if included; 2> stop the periodical reporting timer or timer related to the sl-measId, if running.'

results.question: What is the UE's expected behavior if the sl-ReportConfigToRemoveList includes an sl-ReportConfigId value not currently configured?
results.reference: The UE does not consider the message as erroneous; it simply ignores such non-configured IDs, as the note specifies no error handling is required for them.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.10.2.6, Sidelink reporting configuration removal
results.model_answer: This case is not expected to occur under normal network operation (the network is expected to only include IDs that are actually configured). If it does occur, the UE follows the generic 3GPP TS 38.331 rule for 'ToRemoveList' processing: for any sl-ReportConfigId in sl-ReportConfigToRemoveList that does not correspond to an entry currently present in the UE's stored sl-ReportConfigList (i.e., not previously added via sl-ReportConfigToAddModList), the UE simply ignores that particular entry — it performs no release/removal action for it, does not treat it as an error, and continues processing the remaining valid entries in the list and the rest of the SL-MeasConfig (or corresponding sidelink reconfiguration) as normal.
results.evidence: The UE shall for each sl-ReportConfigId included in the sl-ReportConfigToRemoveList that is not part of the current UE configuration, ignore that entry (no action is performed), consistent with the general rule specified for reportConfigToRemoveList processing in TS 38.331 clause 5.3.5.3 (Measurement configuration) and its sidelink analogue for SL-MeasConfig handling.

results.question: Describe the sequential cleanup process triggered by removing an sl-ReportConfigId from VarMeasConfigSL.
results.reference: First, remove the sl-ReportConfigId entry from sl-ReportConfigList. Second, remove all associated sl-MeasIds from sl-MeasIdList. Third, for each removed sl-MeasId, clean up its reporting entry and timer/resources.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.10.2.6, Sidelink reporting configuration removal
results.model_answer: Removing an sl-ReportConfigId from VarMeasConfigSL triggers a cascading, sequential cleanup rather than a single isolated deletion, because sidelink measurement configuration follows the same dependency-driven removal logic as legacy Uu measConfig removal. The steps are: (1) The UE deletes the entry with the matching sl-ReportConfigId from the sl-ReportConfigList within VarMeasConfigSL. (2) The UE then searches sl-MeasIdList within VarMeasConfigSL for every sl-MeasId entry that references this sl-ReportConfigId (since each sl-MeasId links an sl-MeasObjectId to an sl-ReportConfigId). (3) For each such sl-MeasId found, the UE removes that sl-MeasId entry from sl-MeasIdList within VarMeasConfigSL, ensuring no measurement identity retains a dangling reference to a deleted report configuration. (4) In parallel with removing each affected sl-MeasId, the UE also deletes the corresponding measurement report entry (if any) from VarMeasReportListSL, since a report list entry is only meaningful while its sl-MeasId remains valid. (5) The UE stops any running timer associated with that sl-MeasId (e.g., the periodical sidelink reporting timer), and resets associated evaluation state (e.g., time-to-trigger status, cell/UE triggered quantities) tied to the removed configuration. This ordered sequence—reportConfig entry removal → dependent measId removal → associated report list entry removal → timer/state reset—guarantees VarMeasConfigSL and VarMeasReportListSL remain mutually consistent, preventing orphaned measurement identities or stale reports referencing a non-existent reporting configuration.
results.evidence: The UE shall: 1> remove the sl-ReportConfigId from the sl-ReportConfigList within VarMeasConfigSL; 1> for each sl-MeasId associated with this sl-ReportConfigId in the sl-MeasIdList within VarMeasConfigSL: 2> remove the entry with the matching sl-MeasId from the sl-MeasIdList within VarMeasConfigSL; 2> remove the entry associated with this sl-MeasId from VarMeasReportListSL, if included; 2> stop the periodical reporting timer or timer T321, whichever one is running for this sl-MeasId, and reset the associated information (e.g. timeToTrigger) for this sl-MeasId.

results.question: Why would a UE initiate the procedure to report SCG failure information?
