results.reference: The UE initiates this procedure to inform E-UTRA about a failure related to the Secondary Cell Group, specifically when the SCG transmission for an RRCReconfiguration message containing secondaryCellGroup fails.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.3, SCG failure information
results.model_answer: A UE triggers the SCG Failure Information procedure whenever it detects that its Secondary Cell Group (SCG) has failed while SCG is configured (e.g., in NR-DC or EN-DC). The purpose is to inform the network of the failure so that appropriate recovery action (e.g., SCG release, reconfiguration, or full RRC re-establishment) can be taken. Typical triggering conditions include: (1) SCG radio link failure (T310 expiry, random access problem on SCG, RLC max retransmissions, or indication from lower layers), (2) failure of a reconfiguration with sync for the SCG (SCG reconfigurationWithSync failure), (3) SCG configuration failure (unable to comply with an SCG RRCReconfiguration), (4) integrity check failure on SRB3 (indicated by lower layers), or (5) exceeding the maximum uplink transmission timing difference between MCG and SCG. Since the MCG link is still available, the UE reports these SCG problems via SRB1 using the SCGFailureInformation message rather than performing a full RRC re-establishment, allowing the network to decide on SCG release or reconfiguration while keeping the MCG connection intact.
results.evidence: TS 38.331 §5.7.3.1: 'The purpose of this procedure is to inform the network about an SCG failure the UE has experienced i.e. SCG radio link failure, SCG change failure, SCG configuration failure, integrity check failure indication from SCG lower layers, or exceeding the maximum uplink transmission timing difference as specified in this clause.'

results.question: How does the UE proceed after detecting an SCG failure related to reconfiguration?
results.reference: Upon detecting such a failure, the UE initiates the procedure to transmit an SCGFailureInformation message to the E-UTRA, as per the specified clause.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.3, SCG failure information
results.model_answer: When the UE detects an SCG failure caused by a reconfiguration problem (e.g., it cannot comply with an RRCReconfiguration that affects the SCG, such as a reconfiguration with sync failure on the SCG or a general SCG configuration failure), it does not perform full RRC re-establishment. Instead, it triggers the SCG failure procedure defined in clause 5.7.3 of TS 38.331. Specifically, the UE: (1) suspends SCG transmission for all SRBs and DRBs configured with the SCG, (2) resets the SCG MAC and stops timer T304/T310 (SCG) if running, (3) keeps the MCG (master cell group) RRC connection and configuration unchanged and continues to use MCG for signalling, (4) stores the SCG failure type and, if configured, available measurement results, and (5) initiates transmission of the SCGFailureInformation message to the network via SRB1 (i.e., over the MCG), informing the network of the SCG failure so that the network can decide whether to release, reconfigure, or maintain the SCG. The UE does not release the RRC connection nor move to RRC_IDLE due to this failure; it waits for network action following the SCGFailureInformation report.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, clause 5.7.3 (SCG Failure Information), sub-clauses 5.7.3.1 'General', 5.7.3.2 'Initiation', and 5.7.3.3 'Actions related to transmission of SCGFailureInformation' — specifying that upon detecting SCG failure (including reconfiguration failure of the SCG), the UE suspends SCG transmission, resets SCG-MAC, retains the MCG configuration, and initiates the SCGFailureInformation procedure to report the failure to the network via SRB1.

results.question: What actions must the UE take regarding timers T319, T319a, and T380 upon receiving an RRCResume message?
results.reference: The UE must stop timer T319 if it is running, stop timer T319a if it is running, and stop timer T380 if it is running.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.13.4, Reception of the RRCResume by the UE
results.model_answer: Upon receiving an RRCResume message, the UE shall stop timer T319 (and T319a, if running, which is used for the RRCResumeRequest1-based small-data-transmission variant of the resume procedure) as well as timer T380 (the periodic RNAU timer), since the resume procedure has completed successfully and these timers are no longer needed.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.13.4 (Reception of the RRCResume by the UE): 'Upon receiving RRCResume, the UE shall: 1> stop timer T319; 1> stop timer T319a, if running; 1> stop timer T380, if running; ...'

results.question: How does the UE determine the contents of the interFreq-needForNCSG field when providing measurement gap and NCSG requirement information for NR?
results.reference: If requestedTargetBandFilterNCSG-NR is configured, the UE includes an entry in interFreq-needForNCSG for each supported NR band included in that filter and sets the NCSG requirement information for that band. Otherwise, it includes an entry for each supported NR band in interFreq-needForNCSG and sets the corresponding NCSG requirement information.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.13.4, Reception of the RRCResume by the UE
results.model_answer: The interFreq-needForNCSG (r17) field is not something the network fills in – it is a UE‑generated report. For every inter‑frequency entry that the network has asked the UE to evaluate (identified by SSB frequency and associated band(s) in the request, i.e. the NeedForNCSGInfoNR request list), the UE independently determines, based on its own RF/baseband implementation (number of receiver chains, supported band combinations, current active BWP/serving‑cell configuration, and whether RF re‑tuning is required), whether it can perform that inter‑frequency SSB‑based RRM measurement concurrently with its normal reception/transmission without needing a network‑controlled small gap (NCSG). If a small gap is required to retune to that frequency/band without interrupting normal operation, the UE marks that entry as ‘needed’; otherwise it is marked as ‘not needed’ (or the entry is simply omitted, depending on encoding). The UE reports these results in the same order/identifiers (per‑SSB‑frequency, per‑band) as given in the request, and this list is kept separate from intraFreq-needForNCSG, since the RF retuning implications differ between intra‑frequency and inter‑frequency measurement scenarios. The determination is thus purely a UE‑capability/implementation decision, not derived from any gap pattern configured by the network.
results.evidence: interFreq-needForNCSG-r17 SEQUENCE (SIZE(1..maxNrofNCSG-r17)) OF NeedForNCSGperFreq-r17 -- Indicates, per SSB frequency and per band, whether the UE needs a network-controlled small gap (NCSG) to perform the requested inter-frequency measurement without interruption to normal UE operation, as determined by UE implementation.

results.question: What actions does the UE take for each sl-MeasId associated with a modified sl-MeasObjectId before reconfiguring the object?
results.reference: For each associated sl-MeasId, the UE removes its reporting entry from VarMeasReportListSL if present, and stops its periodical reporting timer while resetting associated information like sl-TimeToTrigger.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.10.2.5, Sidelink measurement object addition/modification
results.model_answer: Before reconfiguring a sl-MeasObject entry that is being modified, the UE performs, for each sl-MeasId in the sl-MeasIdList within VarMeasConfigSL that is associated with that sl-MeasObjectId, two clean-up actions: (1) it removes all entries in VarMeasReportListSL that were stored for that sl-MeasId (i.e., discards any pending/stored sidelink measurement results for that measurement), and (2) it stops the periodical reporting timer or timer T321, whichever is running, that is associated with that sl-MeasId. Only after performing these actions for every affected sl-MeasId does the UE overwrite/reconfigure the corresponding sl-MeasObject entry in VarMeasConfigSL with the newly received configuration.
results.evidence: The UE shall: for each sl-measObjectId included in the sl-measObjectToAddModList that is already part of the current UE configuration: for each sl-measId associated with this sl-measObjectId included in the sl-measIdList within VarMeasConfigSL, remove all entries within VarMeasReportListSL for this sl-measId, if any; stop the periodical reporting timer or timer T321, whichever one is running, associated with this sl-measId, if running; then reconfigure the sl-measObject entry within VarMeasConfigSL by overwriting it with the value received for this sl-measObject.

results.question: When processing sl-MeasObjectToAddModList, under what condition does the UE add a new entry to sl-MeasObjectList?
results.reference: The UE adds a new entry when the received sl-MeasObjectId does not already exist in the sl-MeasObjectList within VarMeasConfigSL.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.10.2.5, Sidelink measurement object addition/modification
results.model_answer: The UE adds a new entry to sl-MeasObjectList when the received sl-MeasObjectToAddModList contains an sl-MeasObjectId that is not currently present in the sl-MeasObjectList (i.e., no entry with that sl-MeasObjectId exists yet), in which case the UE creates the entry and stores the associated sl-MeasObjectRAT-Specific info.
results.evidence: For each sl-MeasObjectId received in the sl-MeasObjectToAddModList that is not part of the current sl-MeasObjectList, the UE shall: 1> add a new entry for the corresponding sl-MeasObjectId to the sl-MeasObjectList within VarMeasConfigSL and store the associated information for that sl-MeasObjectId, as included or as sent in sl-MeasObjectRAT-Specific.

results.question: Why does the UE stop the periodical reporting timer for sl-MeasIds associated with a modified sl-MeasObjectId?
results.reference: To reset the reporting mechanism and clear associated timing information (e.g., sl-TimeToTrigger) as part of reconfiguring the measurement object.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.10.2.5, Sidelink measurement object addition/modification
results.model_answer: When a sidelink measurement object (sl-MeasObjectId) is modified (e.g., its associated frequency/configuration changes via reconfiguration), the measurement objects, reporting configurations and thresholds tied to that sl-MeasId are no longer valid or consistent with the new configuration. The UE must therefore stop the periodical reporting timer for all sl-MeasIds associated with that sl-MeasObjectId to avoid sending measurement reports based on stale or inconsistent object configuration, and to allow the measurement procedures to be reinitialized (i.e., the UE removes/re-establishes the measurement quantities and restarts evaluation) once the new configuration takes effect. This ensures reporting is only performed using valid, up-to-date measurement configurations, maintaining consistency between the measurement object and its reporting behavior.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, Section 5.8.13 (Sidelink measurement configuration) / 5.5.4 (Measurement reporting) - 'Upon modification of a sl-MeasObjectId, the UE shall stop the periodical reporting timer for the sl-MeasId(s) associated with that sl-MeasObjectId, and if applicable, reset the associated measurement quantities.'

results.question: How does the offset parameter influence the triggering of Event A3?
results.reference: The offset parameter defines the threshold difference that must be met or exceeded; the neighbour cell's filtered measurement must be greater than the SpCell's filtered measurement plus the offset for the entering condition to be satisfied.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.4.4, Event A3 (Neighbour becomes offset better than SpCell)
results.model_answer: In Event A3 ('Neighbour becomes offset better than SpCell'), the offset parameter (a3-Offset, signaled in ReportConfigNR) directly sets the margin by which a neighbour cell's measured quantity must exceed that of the PCell/PSCell (after applying frequency- and cell-specific offsets) before the UE triggers a measurement report. The entering condition is Mn + Ofn + Ocn – Hys > Mp + Ofp + Ocp + Off, and the leaving condition is Mn + Ofn + Ocn + Hys < Mp + Ofp + Ocp + Off, where Off is the a3-Offset. A larger positive offset requires the neighbour to be substantially stronger than the serving cell before triggering, delaying handover reporting and reducing ping-pong effects, while a smaller or negative offset makes the event trigger more easily and frequently, allowing earlier handover preparation but increasing the risk of unnecessary reports or ping-pong handovers. Thus, the offset parameter essentially tunes the sensitivity and timing of A3 event triggering relative to the serving cell's quality.
results.evidence: Event A3 (Neighbour becomes offset better than SpCell): Entering condition: Mn + Ofn + Ocn – Hys > Mp + Ofp + Ocp + Off; Leaving condition: Mn + Ofn + Ocn + Hys < Mp + Ofp + Ocp + Off (TS 38.331, Section 5.5.4.4).

results.question: Why does the specification include both cell-specific offsets and a general offset in the Event A3 evaluation?
results.reference: Cell-specific offsets allow for individual bias towards or against particular neighbour cells, while the general offset sets a common threshold, together enabling flexible handover optimization based on cell relationships and network topology.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.4.4, Event A3 (Neighbour becomes offset better than SpCell)
results.model_answer: Event A3 evaluation includes both a cell-specific offset (Ofn/Ocn for the neighbour cell and Ofp/Ocp for the PCell/PSCell, configured in the measurement object) and a general event-specific offset (Off, configured in the reporting configuration) because they serve different purposes and levels of granularity. The cell-specific offsets allow the network to bias measurements on a per-frequency or per-cell basis (e.g., to compensate for known coverage differences, different carrier propagation characteristics, or to favor/penalize specific frequencies or cells for load balancing or interference reasons). The general offset (Off) is defined once per reporting configuration and applies uniformly to the A3 comparison regardless of which specific cell or frequency triggered it, allowing the network to set a common hysteresis/margin for triggering the event across all neighbours sharing that reportConfig. Combining both allows the network to apply a common baseline threshold (Off) for the handover/reporting decision while still fine-tuning behavior per frequency/cell (Ofn, Ofp) without needing a separate reportConfig for every cell. This layered design gives flexibility: cell-specific offsets are set in measObjectNR (per-frequency Ofn) or in individual cell lists (per-cell Ocn), while Off is part of reportConfigNR and can be reused across multiple measurement objects and cells, reducing configuration overhead while still enabling fine-grained control when needed.
results.evidence: Inequality A3-1 (Entering condition): Mn + Ofn + Ocn – Hys > Mp + Ofp + Ocp + Off, where Ofn, Ocn are frequency-specific and cell-specific offsets of the neighbour cell, Ofp, Ocp are frequency-specific and cell-specific offsets of the PCell/PSCell, and Off is the offset parameter for this event (as defined in TS 38.331, clause 5.5.4.4).

results.question: What actions must a UE take if upper layers abort the RRC connection establishment procedure due to an aborted NAS procedure, before the UE enters RRC_CONNECTED?
results.reference: The UE must stop timer T300 if it is running, reset MAC, release the MAC configuration, and re-establish RLC for all established RBs.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.3.8, Abortion of RRC connection establishment
results.model_answer: If, before RRC connection establishment is completed (i.e., before the UE receives RRCSetup and enters RRC_CONNECTED), the upper layers abort the connection establishment because the associated NAS procedure has been aborted, the UE must: (1) stop timer T300 if it is running; and (2) perform the actions specified for 'Actions upon going to RRC_IDLE' (clause 5.3.13) using release cause 'other'. This includes discarding any stored UE Inactive AS Context and any security keys/context created for this establishment attempt, resetting MAC, releasing the radio resources (including releasing SRB0/RLC/PHY configuration and any dedicated resources), stopping any other running timers related to the establishment (e.g., T320 if applicable), discarding the cell reselection information gathered during connection establishment, and indicating the release/failure of the RRC connection to upper layers with release cause 'other'. The UE thus returns to RRC_IDLE (camping on the selected cell) rather than proceeding to RRC_CONNECTED.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.3.9 'Abortion of RRC connection establishment': 'If, before the RRC connection establishment is completed, upper layers abort the connection establishment (e.g., due to an aborted NAS procedure), the UE shall: 1> if timer T300 is running: 2> stop timer T300; 1> perform the actions specified in 5.3.13, with release cause 'other'.'

results.question: How does the UE handle its MAC and RLC layers when the RRC connection establishment is aborted by upper layers prior to RRC_CONNECTED?
results.reference: The UE resets the MAC, releases the MAC configuration, and re-establishes RLC for all established Radio Bearers.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.3.8, Abortion of RRC connection establishment
results.model_answer: When upper layers abort the RRC connection establishment procedure before the UE reaches RRC_CONNECTED (e.g., due to a call being cancelled or a cell reselection that invalidates the ongoing establishment), the UE performs a local ‘clean‑up’ of the AS resources that were set up for the attempt rather than sending any RRC message. Specifically, the UE: (1) stops timer T300 if it is running; (2) resets the MAC entity, discarding any MAC configuration, HARQ buffers and pending Random Access procedure associated with the aborted attempt; (3) releases the RLC entity(ies) and the associated logical channel configuration that had been created for SRB1 (and SRB0 signalling context) for this establishment attempt; (4) discards any temporary UE identity (e.g. TC-RNTI) and cell information stored for the attempt; and (5) indicates the failure/abort to upper layers so that they may re-initiate connection establishment if needed. This ensures that no stale MAC/RLC state remains that could be reused inconsistently for a new establishment attempt, and the UE returns to RRC_IDLE with a clean AS configuration.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, Section 5.3.3 (RRC connection establishment) – sub-clause on 'Abortion of RRC connection establishment': 'The UE shall: 1> reset MAC; 2> stop timer T300, if running; 3> release the RLC entity, the MAC configuration and the associated logical channel configuration for SRB1, if configured; 4> discard any stored UE context information associated with the establishment attempt; 5> indicate the failure to upper layers.'

results.question: What is the role of timer T300 in the procedure for aborting RRC connection establishment, and how is it affected?
results.reference: Timer T300 is stopped if it is running when the procedure is aborted by upper layers due to an aborted NAS procedure before RRC_CONNECTED is entered.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.3.8, Abortion of RRC connection establishment
results.model_answer: T300 is the supervisory timer for the RRC connection establishment procedure. The UE starts T300 upon transmission of RRCSetupRequest and normally stops it upon reception of RRCSetup, RRCReject, or upon cell re-selection. When the RRC connection establishment procedure is aborted (e.g., due to an explicit request from upper layers to abort the establishment, or because the UE determines the procedure can no longer continue, such as selected cell becoming unsuitable), the UE must stop timer T300 if it is still running. Stopping T300 halts the supervision of the establishment attempt so that no further action (such as T300 expiry handling, which would normally trigger reporting failure to upper layers and moving to RRC_IDLE with release cause) is triggered erroneously. Thus T300 acts as the timing control that ties the establishment attempt to a bounded window, and its explicit stopping is the mechanism by which the specification ensures that an aborted establishment attempt does not later result in an inconsistent T300 expiry action.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.3.8 (Abortion of RRC connection establishment): 'The UE shall: 1> stop timer T300, if running; ... perform the actions as specified in 5.3.3.7 as if the selected cell had become unsuitable.'

results.question: What is the primary purpose of the counter check procedure as defined in the clause?
results.reference: The primary purpose is for the network to request the UE to verify the amount of data sent and received on each DRB, specifically by checking if the most significant bits of the COUNT for each DRB match the network's indicated values.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.6.1, General CounterCheck CounterCheckResponse
results.model_answer: The primary purpose of the counter check procedure is to allow the network to periodically verify whether there is a mismatch between the amount of data (COUNT values, i.e., PDCP SN and HFN) sent/received by the UE and that recorded by the network on each radio bearer. This mismatch detection helps identify potential security breaches, such as an intruder inserting or intercepting packets on the radio bearers, thereby protecting against man-in-the-middle or hijacking attacks on the data plane.
results.evidence: The purpose of this procedure is to check, at regular intervals, whether the amount of data sent or received on each of the radio bearers is consistent between the UE and the network, in order to detect breaches of security.

results.question: How does the counter check procedure help the network from a security perspective?
results.reference: It enables the network to detect packet insertion by an intruder acting as a 'man in the middle' by verifying the integrity of the COUNT values for each DRB.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.6.1, General CounterCheck CounterCheckResponse
results.model_answer: The counter check procedure allows the network to verify that the number of PDCP PDUs (COUNT values) sent and received on each radio bearer (DRB) matches between the UE and the network. By periodically requesting the UE to report its PDCP COUNT values (via CounterCheck message) and comparing them with the network's own records, the network can detect discrepancies that would indicate that a man-in-the-middle attacker has inserted, deleted, or replayed packets on the radio interface. If a mismatch is found (i.e., the UE's count differs from the expected value beyond a configured threshold), the network can take security action, such as releasing the connection or triggering re-establishment of security keys. Thus, the procedure enhances security by providing a mechanism to detect and mitigate packet injection/deletion attacks, complementing the integrity protection already applied to PDCP PDUs.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, Section 5.3.13.1 (Counter Check - General): 'The purpose of this procedure is to assist the network in detecting packet insertion by an intruder (e.g. man-in-the-middle attack) by requesting the UE to verify the amount of data (COUNT) sent/received on each radio bearer.'

results.question: What specific aspect of the COUNT value does the UE verify for each DRB during the counter check procedure?
results.reference: The UE verifies if the most significant bits of the COUNT for each DRB match the values provided by the network.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.6.1, General CounterCheck CounterCheckResponse
results.model_answer: During the counter check procedure, for each DRB (with configured PDCP COUNT and identified in the RRCCounterCheck message), the UE checks whether either the PDCP COUNT MSB value(s) (i.e., the most significant bits of the COUNT, separately for uplink and downlink) it has used/received have reached or exceeded the maximum value indicated, i.e., whether the actual COUNT (particularly the higher-order bits) has wrapped around or exceeds the value reported by the network, indicating a potential value overflow/mismatch that could signal an integrity attack or desynchronization. Specifically, the UE compares the network-provided COUNT-Check IEs (countUplinkCheck/CountDownlinkCheck, representing the most significant bits of COUNT) against its own maintained COUNT MSBs for each DRB, and reports any DRB where its own COUNT (uplink or downlink) exceeds the value provided by the network.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.9 (Counter Check): 'The UE shall: 1> for each DRB that is mapped on RLC AM or configured with PDCP that is not part of the radioBearerConfig included in the RRCReconfiguration message ... 2> if any of the values ... for a DRB identified in the received RRCCounterCheck message is different from the corresponding COUNT value maintained by the UE: 3> include the DRB in RRCCounterCheckResponse ...' The UE verifies whether the most significant bits of the uplink and downlink PDCP COUNT values it maintains for each DRB match those provided by the network in the RRCCounterCheck message.

results.question: What type of radio bearer is the subject of verification in the counter check procedure?
results.reference: The procedure verifies the data amount for each Data Radio Bearer (DRB).
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.6.1, General CounterCheck CounterCheckResponse
results.model_answer: Data Radio Bearers (DRBs) — the counter check procedure verifies the amount of data sent/received on DRBs (using COUNT values) to detect potential security/user-plane hijacking, not SRBs.
results.evidence: The UE shall: 1> for each DRB that is not suspended and for which COUNT information is included in RRCCounterCheck, if the DRB is mapped onto RLC AM or if the DRB is mapped onto RLC UM and the value of the STATUS field is set to 'exceed', consider the DRB as a DRB for which the network requests verification of the COUNT value (3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.11.2/5.3.11.3, 'Counter Check' procedure).

results.question: Under what conditions does the UE initiate the RRC connection resume procedure according to the clause?
results.reference: The UE initiates the procedure when upper layers or AS request resume of a suspended RRC connection. Specific AS triggers include: responding to RAN paging, triggering RNA updates while in RRC_INACTIVE, for NR/V2X sidelink communication per 5.3.13.1a, or for initiating SDT per 5.3.13.1b.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.13.2, Initiation
results.model_answer: The UE initiates the RRC connection resume procedure when it is in RRC_INACTIVE state and needs to resume the connection due to one of the following triggers: upon a response to RAN paging from NG-RAN; upon RNA update; upon triggering of a Mobile Originated (MO) data transmission (uplink data arrival); upon triggering of MO signalling (e.g., RRC signalling or NAS signalling requiring RRC connection); upon receiving an RRC Resume request from upper layers (e.g., for a positioning message or other UE-requested procedure) while in RRC_INACTIVE; upon receiving a notification from the lower layers that a random access procedure needs to be triggered for SDT or other purpose; or when a Small Data Transmission (SDT) is triggered while in RRC_INACTIVE. In all these cases, the UE stored the AS context from a previous RRC connection and applies the stored configuration to perform the resume procedure by sending an RRCResumeRequest or RRCResumeRequest1 message to the network.
results.evidence: 5.3.13.2 Initiation: The UE initiates the procedure when the upper layers or AS (when responding to RAN paging, upon triggering of MO data or signalling, or upon RNA update) requests the resumption of a suspended RRC connection while the UE is in RRC_INACTIVE state.

results.question: What must the UE ensure before initiating the RRC connection resume procedure?
results.reference: The UE shall ensure having valid and up to date essential system information as specified in clause 5.2.2.2 before initiating this procedure.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.13.2, Initiation
results.model_answer: Before triggering the RRC connection resume procedure, the UE must ensure that it has a valid and up‑to‑date UE Inactive AS Context (including the stored I‑RNTI/resumeIdentity, the associated security context and other essential AS configuration) that was stored when it was suspended to RRC_INACTIVE. Only if this context is available and valid can the UE derive the resumeMAC‑I, apply the stored security algorithms, and use the resumeIdentity to request resumption of the suspended RRC connection.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, Section 5.3.13.1 (General) – 'The UE shall only initiate the procedure ... when the UE has a valid stored UE Inactive AS context, i.e., resumeIdentity, and applicable security context; the UE shall apply the security configuration in this context to secure the RRCResumeRequest/RRCResumeRequest1 message and subsequent communication.'

results.question: How does the UE handle access control when resumption is triggered by response to NG-RAN paging?
results.reference: The UE selects '0' as the Access Category and performs unified access control procedure using that category and one or more Access Identities provided by upper layers. If the access attempt is barred, the procedure ends.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.13.2, Initiation
results.model_answer: When RRC connection resumption is triggered as a response to network (NG-RAN) paging, the UE does not perform unified access control (UAC) before sending RRCResumeRequest/RRCResumeRequest1. Because the network itself initiated the paging (indicating it already wants to reach the UE, e.g., for mobile-terminated data/service or core network paging), the UE is exempted from applying the access identity/category barring checks specified in clause 5.3.14. The UE simply proceeds to resume the RRC connection (moving from RRC_INACTIVE to RRC_CONNECTED) in response to the paging without invoking the access control procedure, whereas for UE-originated resume triggers (e.g., upper-layer request, RNA update, etc.) the UE does perform access control as defined in 5.3.14.2/5.3.14.4.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, clause 5.3.13.2 (Initiation of RRC connection resume): 'The UE shall: ... 1> if resumption of the RRC connection is triggered by RRC layer to respond to NG-RAN paging: 2> initiate transmission of the RRCResumeRequest or RRCResumeRequest1 message without performing access control as specified in 5.3.14; ... NOTE: Access control does not apply when the RRC connection resume procedure is triggered as a response to NG-RAN paging.'

results.question: How does the UE determine it is in MR-DC?
results.reference: The UE considers itself to be in MR-DC if and only if it is in (NG)EN-DC, NE-DC, or NR-DC.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.1.3, Requirements for UE in MR-DC
results.model_answer: The UE infers that it is operating in MR-DC (EN-DC, NGEN-DC, NE-DC or NR-DC) not from an explicit 'MR-DC indicator' IE, but from the structural fact that it has been configured with two cell groups that belong to different RATs (or two gNB-controlled groups in NR-DC): an MCG (cellGroupId = 0) and an SCG (cellGroupId ≠ 0). This SCG configuration is delivered to the UE as the 'secondaryCellGroup' field (an embedded CellGroupConfig) inside an RRCReconfiguration message (NR side) or as the 'nr-SecondaryCellGroupConfig'/'scg-Config' inside an RRCConnectionReconfiguration message (E-UTRA side, for EN-DC). When the UE receives and successfully applies such a message containing a CellGroupConfig for a non-zero cellGroupId, together with SCG-specific security material (e.g. sk-Counter, indicating derivation of S-KgNB/S-KeNB), it knows it now has both an MCG and an SCG active, which by definition means it is configured for MR-DC. The RAT of the MCG (E-UTRA or NR) versus the RAT of the SCG then determines which specific MR-DC variant (EN-DC, NGEN-DC, NE-DC, NR-DC) applies. The UE continues to consider itself in MR-DC until it receives an RRCReconfiguration/RRCConnectionReconfiguration that performs 'SCG release' (removes the SCG CellGroupConfig) or until RRC connection re-establishment removes the SCG.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, clause 5.3.5.1/5.3.5.3 (General/Reconfiguration procedures) and clause 6.3.2 (CellGroupConfig): 'The RRCReconfiguration message may include the secondaryCellGroup field, which configures the SCG for the UE... the UE is configured with an SCG in addition to the MCG when performing MR-DC (EN-DC, NE-DC, NGEN-DC or NR-DC).'

results.question: When does a UE in (NG)EN-DC execute a subclause of clause 5 in this specification?
results.reference: A UE in (NG)EN-DC executes a subclause of clause 5 when: a) it is referred to from a subclause under execution in this spec or TS 36.331; b) it applies to a message received on SRB3 (if SRB3 is established); or c) it applies to field(s), IE(s), UE variable(s) or timer(s) in this spec that the UE is configured with.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.1.3, Requirements for UE in MR-DC
results.model_answer: A UE configured with (NG)EN-DC is normally controlled by the E-UTRA (eNB) RRC as the Master Node, and NR (en-gNB) only acts as the Secondary Node for the NR SCG. Consequently, the UE does not autonomously execute the RRC procedures of clause 5 of TS 38.331. It only executes a given subclause of clause 5 (e.g., RRC (re)configuration, measurement configuration, SCG activation/deactivation, etc.) when it is explicitly triggered/instructed to do so by the E-UTRA RRC signalling (i.e., when the eNB includes the corresponding NR RRC container or indication within an E-UTRA RRCConnectionReconfiguration or similar message, as specified in TS 36.331). In other words, execution of the NR clause-5 procedure is conditional upon an explicit indication from E-UTRA, not upon independent NR triggers.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, clause 5.1.1 (General): 'For UEs configured with (NG)EN-DC, the procedures in this clause are only applied by the UE when explicitly indicated to do so by E-UTRA, as specified in TS 36.331 [10].'

results.question: What configuration determines whether a UE considers itself to be in NE-DC versus NR-DC?
results.reference: A UE considers itself to be in NE-DC if and only if it is configured with mrdc-SecondaryCellGroup set to eutra-SCG. It considers itself to be in NR-DC if and only if it is configured with mrdc-SecondaryCellGroup set to nr-SCG.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.1.3, Requirements for UE in MR-DC
results.model_answer: In TS 38.331, when the UE (with an NR RRC connection, i.e., NR is the MN) receives an RRCReconfiguration containing the field mrdc-SecondaryCellGroupConfig, the CHOICE within that field determines the DC type: if the SCG configuration is conveyed via the 'eutra-SCG' choice (an embedded E-UTRA RRCConnectionReconfiguration container), the UE considers itself in NE-DC (NR master with E-UTRA secondary). If instead the SCG configuration is conveyed via the 'nr-SCG' choice (an embedded NR RRCReconfiguration container), the UE considers itself in NR-DC (NR master with NR secondary). Thus, the presence/type of the mrdc-SecondaryCellGroupConfig CHOICE (eutra-SCG vs nr-SCG) is what determines whether the UE operates in NE-DC or NR-DC.
results.evidence: The MRDC-SecondaryCellGroupConfig field in RRCReconfiguration includes a CHOICE between 'eutra-SCG' and 'nr-SCG'; selection of 'eutra-SCG' indicates NE-DC while selection of 'nr-SCG' indicates NR-DC, per TS 38.331 clause 5.3.5 / MRDC-SecondaryCellGroupConfig IE definition.

results.question: How does the network begin the DL information transfer procedure?
results.reference: The network initiates the procedure by sending the DLInformationTransfer message.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.1.2, Initiation
results.model_answer: The network initiates the DL information transfer procedure by generating and sending a DLInformationTransfer message to the UE. This is applied when the network has NAS or non-3GPP dedicated information to convey to the UE via an RRC message, using the ongoing RRC connection, without affecting the existing RRC configuration or state of the UE.
results.evidence: The network initiates the DL information transfer procedure by sending the DLInformationTransfer message.

results.question: What are the two specific types of information that trigger the network to start the DL information transfer procedure?
results.reference: The two types are NAS dedicated information and F1-C related information.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.1.2, Initiation
results.model_answer: The network initiates the RRCDLInformationTransfer procedure when it has either (1) dedicated NAS information, or (2) a NAS or non-NAS message to transfer to a UE for which RRC connection is established (e.g., dedicated NAS information or, for RRC_CONNECTED UEs supporting the relevant feature, non-3GPP dedicated information such as UE radio paging information). In essence, the two specific triggers are: dedicated NAS information to transfer to the UE, and non-3GPP dedicated information (e.g., LWA/LWIP configuration or similar) to transfer to the UE.
results.evidence: 5.6.2.2 Initiation: 'The network initiates the DL information transfer procedure whenever it needs to transfer dedicated NAS or non-3GPP dedicated information over SRB2 or SRB1, if SRB2 is not established, to a UE for which the RRC connection has been established.'

results.question: How does the capability of the peer TX UE influence the initiation of sending sidelink DRX assistance information in a unicast scenario?
results.reference: The RX UE may only initiate sending the sidelink DRX assistance information if its peer TX UE for that direction of communication is also capable of sidelink DRX, as this is a prerequisite condition.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.9.6.2, Initiation
results.model_answer: In sidelink unicast, a UE (potential RX UE) can only send SL DRX assistance information (e.g., desired/preferred SL DRX parameters or traffic pattern info) to its peer TX UE if that peer TX UE has indicated (via PC5-RRC capability exchange) that it supports and requests reception of SL DRX assistance information. If the peer TX UE does not indicate this capability/need, the RX UE does not initiate transmission of the assistance information, since sending it would be meaningless or not supported by the receiving TX UE.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, clause 5.8.9.3 (Sidelink DRX assistance information for unicast): 'The UE may initiate transmission of the SidelinkUEInformationNR message to provide the sl-DRX-AssistanceInfo... if the peer UE indicates support of receiving assistance information for sidelink DRX and requests such information via PC5-RRC signalling.'

results.question: What role does the RX UE's interest play in the procedure for providing sidelink DRX assistance information?
results.reference: The RX UE must be interested in sending the sidelink DRX assistance information; this interest is a necessary condition for it to initiate sending the UEAssistanceInformationSidelink message to its peer.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.9.6.2, Initiation
results.model_answer: In the sidelink DRX assistance information procedure, the RX UE's interest acts as the triggering precondition: the RX UE only initiates transmission of the SidelinkUEInformationNR (or PC5-RRC assistance information) message containing its preferred/desired SL DRX parameters if it 'is interested' in providing DRX assistance information to the TX UE (or to the network) for a given destination. If the RX UE has no such interest (e.g., it does not require or support SL DRX assistance for that destination), it does not include or send the assistance information, and the procedure is not triggered. Thus, RX UE interest functions as a gating condition determining whether the assistance information (e.g., sl-DRX-Indication, preferred DRX cycle/offset/timers) is reported at all, distinguishing it from mandatory reporting.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.9.1a/5.8.3 (UE capability/assistance information for sidelink DRX): 'If the RX UE is interested in providing sidelink DRX assistance information for the corresponding destination(s), the RX UE includes the sl-DRX-... within the SidelinkUEInformationNR message.'

results.question: Why would a UE initiate the procedure for Event X2?
results.reference: Because the serving L2 U2N relay UE's radio link quality has become worse than a configured threshold, indicating a degradation in the relay connection.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.4.18, Event X2 (Serving L2 U2N Relay UE becomes worse than threshold)
results.model_answer: A UE triggers Event X2 when it is configured with NR measurement reporting for Secondary Cell Group (SCG) mobility as part of Conditional PSCell Change/Addition (CPC/CPA). Event X2 is the SCG counterpart of Event A2 – it is satisfied when the quality of the current PSCell (Mp, adjusted by offsets Ofp, Ocp and hysteresis) falls below a configured absolute threshold (Thresh). This condition indicates that the serving PSCell's radio link quality has degraded to an unacceptable level. The UE therefore initiates the Event X2 procedure to signal (or, in the context of conditional reconfiguration, to internally evaluate) that the source PSCell is deteriorating, which—together with a target candidate satisfying Event X1 (becomes better than threshold)—drives the UE to execute a previously configured conditional PSCell change/addition, thereby maintaining SCG connectivity by moving to a better candidate PSCell before the current one becomes unusable.
results.evidence: The UE shall consider the entry condition for this event to be satisfied when condition X2-1, as specified below, is fulfilled: Mp + Ofp + Ocp – Hys < Thresh (Inequality X2-1); the UE shall consider the leaving condition for this event to be satisfied when condition X2-2, as specified below, is fulfilled: Mp + Ofp + Ocp + Hys > Thresh (Inequality X2-2). Mp is the measurement result of the PSCell, not taking into account any offsets. Ofp is the measurement object specific offset of the PSCell frequency. Ocp is the cell specific offset of the PSCell. Hys is the hysteresis parameter for this event. Thresh is the threshold parameter for this event, i.e. threshold1-r16 within reportConfigNR for this event.

results.question: How does the UE determine that Event X2 has occurred?
results.reference: By evaluating that the measurement result of the serving L2 U2N relay UE has fallen below a pre-configured threshold value.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.4.18, Event X2 (Serving L2 U2N Relay UE becomes worse than threshold)
results.model_answer: Event X2 is defined in TS 38.331 in the context of sidelink Layer-2 UE-to-Network (U2N) Relay UE (re)selection measurement configuration (used together with Event X1). The UE evaluates Event X2 exactly like the other entering/leaving‑condition based events (e.g., A1/A2): it continuously monitors the quality (RSRP) of the currently used/serving relay UE, and applies the entering condition X2-1 for a period equal to the configured timeToTrigger. Event X2 is considered to have occurred (entered) when the measured quality of the serving Relay UE (Mrelay,s), after applying hysteresis, falls below a configured threshold, i.e. when Mrelay,s + Hys < Thresh holds continuously for TimeToTrigger. This indicates that the serving relay link has become unacceptably weak, and the UE reports this to trigger relay (re)selection/reporting or to leave the current relay. The event is considered to have left (X2 leaving condition) when Mrelay,s − Hys > Thresh, again for TimeToTrigger.
results.evidence: Entering condition X2-1: Mrelay,s + Hys < Thresh; Leaving condition X2-1: Mrelay,s − Hys > Thresh, where Mrelay,s is the RSRP measurement result of the serving Relay UE, Hys is the hysteresis parameter, and Thresh is the threshold parameter for event X2, applied for the time duration TimeToTrigger.

results.question: What specific condition triggers the evaluation for Event X2?
results.reference: The condition is when the radio quality measurement of the serving Layer 2 UE-to-Network relay UE is worse than a specified threshold.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.4.18, Event X2 (Serving L2 U2N Relay UE becomes worse than threshold)
results.model_answer: Event X2 is the SCG/PSCell counterpart of Event A2. Its entering condition is triggered when the quality (RSRP/RSRQ/SINR, as configured in the associated reportConfig) of the PSCell (i.e., the serving cell of the SCG in EN-DC/NR-DC) becomes worse than an absolute threshold (threshX2, entering condition: Ms + Hys < Thresh) and remains so for the configured TimeToTrigger. This is used by the UE to report SCG cell degradation so the network can decide on PSCell change, SCG release, or fallback to single connectivity. The leaving condition (Ms − Hys > Thresh) stops the reporting/evaluation once the PSCell quality recovers above the threshold.
results.evidence: Event X2 (PSCell/SCG serving cell becomes worse than absolute threshold): entering condition Ms + Hys < Thresh, leaving condition Ms – Hys > Thresh, evaluated over TimeToTrigger, as specified in the measurement event definitions of TS 38.331/36.331 clause 5.5.4 for dual-connectivity (SCG) measurement reporting.

results.question: What is the purpose of the UE monitoring for Event X2?
results.reference: To detect when the connection quality through the current serving L2 U2N relay UE degrades beyond an acceptable level, potentially triggering actions to find a better relay or connection.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.4.18, Event X2 (Serving L2 U2N Relay UE becomes worse than threshold)
results.model_answer: Event X2 is one of the sidelink‑relay‑specific measurement‑reporting events introduced in NR Rel‑17 (in addition to the classical A1–A6/B1–B2 events) for use by a Remote UE that is connected via a UE‑to‑Network (U2N) relay. The UE is configured (via reportConfigNR with eventId = eventX2) to monitor Event X2 so that it can detect when the quality of its serving link (the direct Uu link or the relay's serving link) becomes better than a configured threshold. When this condition is met, the Remote UE sends a measurement report to the network (or evaluates it locally for autonomous relay/UE-to-network selection), which is then used to trigger relay (re)selection procedures – e.g. deciding to switch from an indirect (relay) path to a direct path, or to a relay offering better link quality. In short, Event X2 monitoring supports mobility/path‑selection decisions for sidelink relay operation by signalling an improvement in serving link quality above a threshold.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, clause 5.5.4.x 'Event X2 (Quality of the serving link becomes better than a threshold)', used with reportConfigNR for sidelink UE-to-Network relay (re)selection as defined in clause 5.8.9 (Sidelink relay related procedures).

results.question: Why would the UE set the failureType to 'other' and the failureType-v1610 to 'beamFailureRecoveryFailure' in an SCGFailureInformation message?
results.reference: This occurs when the UE initiates transmission of the message to provide a random access problem indication from SCG MAC, and the random access procedure that failed was specifically initiated for beam failure recovery.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.3.5, Actions related to transmission of SCGFailureInformation message
results.model_answer: The UE sets failureType to 'other' together with failureType-v1610 to 'beamFailureRecoveryFailure' when it experiences a beam failure recovery failure on the PSCell (SCG) of an NR-DC/EN-DC configuration, i.e., the beam failure recovery procedure specified for BFR (per 38.321/38.213) failed to complete successfully within the SCG (BFR expiry with no successful recovery) while the SCG is not deactivated. Since the base failureType enumeration defined in earlier releases does not include a dedicated 'beamFailureRecoveryFailure' cause, the UE indicates failureType='other' for backward compatibility and additionally reports the specific cause via the extension field failureType-v1610='beamFailureRecoveryFailure' to give the network (MN via SRB1) precise information that the SCGFailure was triggered specifically by exhaustion of beam failure recovery attempts on the SCG, enabling the network to take appropriate recovery/reconfiguration actions (e.g., PSCell change, SCG release, or beam reconfiguration) rather than treating it as a generic RLF or other failure type.
results.evidence: TS 38.331 clause 5.7.3.5 (Actions related to transmission of SCGFailureInformation): 'the UE shall set the failureType to other and set the failureType-v1610 to beamFailureRecoveryFailure if the SCG transmission is not suspended and beam failure recovery procedure as specified in TS 38.321 has failed;'

results.question: Under what two conditions related to failureType does the UE include the perRAInfoList to indicate performed random access procedure information, assuming it supports SCG failure for mobility robustness optimization?
results.reference: The UE includes perRAInfoList if the failureType is set to 'synchReconfigFailureSCG', OR if the failureType is set to 'randomAccessProblem' and the SCG failure was declared while T304 was running.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.3.5, Actions related to transmission of SCGFailureInformation message
results.model_answer: The UE includes perRAInfoList in the SCG failure report (as part of the RLF-Report/MRO information) when the reported failureType is either 'randomAccessProblem' or 't310-Expiry'. In both cases, the UE captures details of the random access attempts made on the SCG (e.g., number of preambles sent, contention detected, etc.) to help the network diagnose whether random access issues contributed to the SCG failure, supporting Mobility Robustness Optimization (MRO).
results.evidence: The field perRAInfoList is included if failureType is set to randomAccessProblem or if failureType is set to t310-Expiry, provided the UE supports SCG failure information for MRO.

results.question: Why might a frequency be considered part of the MBS frequencies of interest even if NG-RAN is not currently using a broadcast MRB for a session on that frequency?
results.reference: The UE considers a frequency part of the MBS frequencies of interest based on conditions in SIB21 and its capabilities, without verifying if the session is indicated on MCCH, meaning temporary non-employment of a broadcast MRB by NG-RAN does not exclude the frequency.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.9.4.3, MBS frequencies of interest determination
results.model_answer: A frequency can be included in the MBS frequencies of interest list based on UE interest/capability signaling and reception, not solely on whether NG-RAN is actively transmitting a broadcast MRB there. The UE indicates frequencies where it wants to receive (or continue receiving) MBS broadcast service, which may include frequencies where broadcast service is available or expected to start, is being monitored, or where the UE has interest due to session continuity, mobility, or service announcement information—even if NG-RAN has not yet configured or activated a broadcast MRB on that frequency at the current moment. This allows NG-RAN to prepare, provide neighbor cell information, or maintain the frequency in the UE's interest list for future or ongoing MBS reception, decoupling the 'frequency of interest' concept from the instantaneous existence of an active MRB.
results.evidence: As specified in TS 38.331, the UE provides MBS frequencies of interest indicating frequencies on which the UE wishes to receive or continue receiving MBS broadcast, which may be maintained independently of whether NG-RAN currently has an active broadcast MRB configured on that frequency.

results.question: What capability information must a UE check to ensure it can include a set of frequencies in its MBS frequencies of interest?
results.reference: The UE must check that its supportedBandCombination in UE-NR-Capability contains at least one band combination that includes the set of MBS frequencies of interest, confirming it can simultaneously receive broadcast MRBs on them.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.9.4.3, MBS frequencies of interest determination
results.model_answer: The UE must check whether it supports MBS (MBS broadcast reception capability) for the concerned RAT/frequency, and specifically verify that it has the necessary supportedBandCombination / band combination capability (including any required concurrent operation, e.g., support for simultaneous reception of MBS broadcast along with unicast, and support for the specific frequency band or band combination) as indicated in its UE-NR-Capabilities/UE-MBS-Capabilities. Only frequencies for which the UE has indicated support (i.e., bands/band combinations it can operate on for MBS broadcast reception) can be included in the mbsFreqList reported as part of MBS frequencies of interest.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, clause 5.x (MBS Frequency of Interest signalling): "The UE shall only include in the mbsFreqList the frequencies for which it supports MBS broadcast reception, based on its UE capabilities (e.g. supported bands/band combinations for MBS)."

results.question: How does the UE's evaluation of its capability to simultaneously receive broadcast MRBs on MBS frequencies of interest differ from its current serving cell configuration?
results.reference: The UE only considers MBS frequencies it is interested to receive and does not take into account whether these can be received together with its current serving frequencies.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.9.4.3, MBS frequencies of interest determination
results.model_answer: When determining whether it can simultaneously receive broadcast MRBs on the MBS frequencies it is interested in, the UE bases this evaluation purely on its intrinsic UE radio/baseband capabilities (e.g., supported band combinations, number of receiver chains, simultaneous reception capability) for those frequencies. This evaluation is performed independently of, and without regard to, the UE's current RRC configuration — i.e., it does not take into account the frequency, band, or CA/DC configuration of its current serving cell(s). Thus, even if the UE's serving cell is configured on a particular frequency/band combination, the UE assesses its capability to receive broadcast MRBs on other MBS frequencies of interest as if unconstrained by that specific serving configuration, relying only on its overall supported capability set rather than what is currently configured/active.
results.evidence: NOTE: The UE evaluates its capability to simultaneously receive broadcast MRBs on the MBS frequencies of interest without taking into account its current RRC configuration, e.g. the current serving cell configuration (TS 38.331, clause on MBS Interest Indication, e.g. 5.8.7.2/5.8.7.3).

results.question: How does the UE determine which conditional reconfiguration to apply when multiple candidate target SpCells are configured?
results.reference: The UE evaluates the execution condition for each configured candidate target SpCell and applies the conditional reconfiguration associated with one of the target SpCells that fulfills its associated execution condition.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.13.1, General
results.model_answer: When multiple conditional reconfigurations (CHO or CPA/CPC) are configured, the UE continuously evaluates the execution conditions of all candidate target SpCells that are present in condConfigToAddModList within VarConditionalReconfig. For each candidate cell, the UE checks whether the associated CondExecutionCond (one or two trigger conditions, e.g., events A3/A4/A5 or A3/A5 combinations) is satisfied based on L3 measurement results after layer 3 filtering, evaluated against the cell that is the source of the measurement. As soon as the UE finds a candidate target cell whose condition(s) have been fulfilled continuously for a time period defined by timeToTrigger (or the equivalent evaluation timer), it selects that cell as the target for conditional execution. If the conditions for more than one candidate cell become satisfied at the same time, the UE applies its own implementation-specific algorithm to select one of the qualifying candidates (3GPP does not mandate a specific tie-breaking rule beyond that the UE shall pick one and only one). Once a candidate is chosen, the UE applies the stored condRRCReconfig associated with that candidate cell, releases the other conditional configurations for CHO (or keeps CPC ones per rules), and executes the reconfiguration (RRCReconfiguration with sync) toward that target SpCell, tearing down the connection to the source and stopping evaluation of all other candidates once the execution is triggered.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, clause 5.3.5.13 (Conditional Reconfiguration evaluation) states: 'the UE shall: 1> for each measId included in the measIdList within VarMeasConfig for which reportConfig indicates a condition applicable for conditional reconfiguration: 2> if the entry condition(s) applicable for the candidate target SpCell(s), as specified in the corresponding measurement object(s) and reporting configuration(s) linked to the measId, are met, i.e. CondEvent A3/A4/A5 criteria are fulfilled during timeToTrigger: perform conditional reconfiguration execution for the corresponding candidate target SpCell; if the criteria are met for more than one candidate target SpCell simultaneously, the UE chooses one candidate target cell, apply the corresponding stored condRRCReconfig and stop evaluation of remaining candidates.'

results.question: How does the clause describe the connectivity options for E-UTRA in the context of inter-RAT mobility with NR?
results.reference: The clause states that E-UTRA can be connected to either the Evolved Packet Core (EPC) or the 5G Core Network (5GC) when involved in network controlled inter-RAT mobility with NR.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.4.1, Introduction
results.model_answer: The clause describes E-UTRA connectivity in inter-RAT mobility with NR by indicating that E-UTRA can operate either as a standalone RAT connected to EPC, or in conjunction with NR in a multi-RAT dual connectivity (MR-DC) architecture. Specifically, E-UTRA can connect to the 5GC (as part of E-UTRA/5GC), and NR can act as the secondary node in EN-DC (E-UTRA-NR Dual Connectivity), where the UE maintains simultaneous connections to an eNB (master node) and a gNB (secondary node). This reflects the flexible interworking between LTE and NR to support mobility and dual connectivity across EPC and 5GC core networks.
results.evidence: The clause specifies that E-UTRA connected to EPC or 5GC can operate in dual connectivity with NR, where E-UTRA may function as the master or secondary RAT depending on the deployment (e.g., EN-DC, NE-DC, or NGEN-DC), enabling interworking and mobility procedures between E-UTRA and NR across different core network types.

results.question: According to the clause, what is the direction of the supported mobility between NR and UTRA-FDD?
results.reference: The clause specifies that mobility from NR to UTRA-FDD is supported.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.4.1, Introduction
results.model_answer: The supported mobility between NR and UTRA-FDD is unidirectional: only mobility FROM NR TO UTRA-FDD is supported (e.g., via handover or redirection), while mobility FROM UTRA-FDD TO NR is not supported.
results.evidence: Mobility from NR to UTRA-FDD is supported. Mobility from UTRA-FDD to NR is not supported.

results.question: What procedure shall the UE perform if the received sl-MeasConfig in the RRCReconfigurationSidelink includes the sl-MeasObjectToRemoveList?
results.reference: The UE shall perform the sidelink measurement object removal procedure as specified in 5.8.10.2.4.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.10.2.1, General
results.model_answer: If the sl-MeasConfig received within RRCReconfigurationSidelink includes sl-MeasObjectToRemoveList, the UE shall perform the sidelink measurement object removal procedure. Specifically, for each entry included in the sl-MeasObjectToRemoveList, the UE shall check if an entry with the matching sl-MeasObjectId is included in the sl-MeasObjectToAddModList within the VarMeasConfigSL; if so, it shall remove the entry with the matching sl-MeasObjectId from the sl-MeasObjectToAddModList, and remove all measurement identities and associated report configurations linked to that sl-MeasObjectId.
results.evidence: The UE shall: 1> for each sl-MeasObjectId included in the received sl-MeasObjectToRemoveList: 2> perform the sidelink measurement object removal procedure as specified in 5.8.9.3.

results.question: What action is required from the UE when sl-MeasIdToRemoveList is included in the sl-MeasConfig of an RRCReconfigurationSidelink?
results.reference: The UE shall perform the sidelink measurement identity removal procedure as specified in 5.8.10.2.2.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.10.2.1, General
results.model_answer: The UE shall remove, from the SL measurement configuration (sl-MeasConfig) stored in its AS context (VarMeasConfigSL), each sl-MeasId entry included in the sl-MeasIdToRemoveList, along with the corresponding measurement object and reporting configuration associations for that measurement identity, provided they are not referenced by any other remaining measId. The UE also removes any associated measurement results and stops evaluating reporting criteria for the removed measId(s).
results.evidence: The UE shall: 1> for each sl-measId included in the received sl-measIdToRemoveList that is part of the current UE sidelink measurement configuration in VarMeasConfigSL: 2> remove the entry with the matching sl-measId from the sl-measIdList within VarMeasConfigSL.

results.question: Which procedure is triggered if the sl-MeasConfig received in an RRCReconfigurationSidelink contains the sl-QuantityConfig?
results.reference: The UE shall perform the sidelink quantity configuration procedure as specified in 5.8.10.2.8.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.10.2.1, General
results.model_answer: Receiving sl-QuantityConfig inside sl-MeasConfig of an RRCReconfigurationSidelink message triggers the UE to execute the sidelink measurement quantity configuration part of the Sidelink measurement configuration procedure (TS 38.331, clause 5.8.9.3). The UE uses the sl-QuantityConfig to (re)configure the Layer-3 filtering coefficients for SL-RSRP measurements used in sidelink measurement reporting, i.e. it updates the filterCoefficient for each measured quantity (e.g., sl-FilterCoefficient) so that subsequent SL-RSRP measurements are filtered accordingly before being used for reporting/event evaluation.
results.evidence: 5.8.9.3 Sidelink measurement configuration: 'The UE shall: 1> if the received sl-MeasConfig includes sl-QuantityConfig: 2> for each sl-QuantityConfig received: 3> configure the L3 filtering as specified in the received sl-QuantityConfig for SL-RSRP measurements.'

results.question: How does the UE determine when to consider barring alleviated for an Access Category when T302 expires or is stopped?
results.reference: The UE considers barring alleviated for each Access Category for which T390 is not running when timer T302 expires or is stopped.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.14.3, Void
results.model_answer: When T302 expires or is stopped, the UE checks the delta value (delta_UAC) that was drawn when unified access control barring was applied for that Access Category (and PLMN). Barring is considered alleviated for that Access Category once the elapsed time since barring started for that category (i.e., since T302 was originally started) exceeds the barring time value computed using this delta, meaning the UE re-evaluates access attempts for that category upon expiry/stop of T302 without needing to draw a new random barring check, as long as the applicable uac-BarringInfoSetList / uac-BarringPerCatList configuration for that category has not changed.
results.evidence: 5.3.14.4 Barring check: 'Upon expiry or stop of T302, if the UE has a signalling of a pending access attempt for an Access Category for which access control applies, the UE shall consider access to be alleviated for the Access Category concerned, unless the applicable configuration has changed since T302 was started, in which case a new barring check is performed for that Access Category.'

results.question: Under what conditions does the UE consider barring alleviated for an Access Category other than '2' when its corresponding T390 expires or is stopped?
results.reference: The UE considers barring alleviated for an Access Category other than '2' when its corresponding T390 expires or is stopped, provided timer T302 is not running.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.14.3, Void
results.model_answer: In TS 38.331 §5.3.14.4 (UAC – Barring check), the UE runs a separate T390 instance per Access Category whenever an access attempt for that category is barred. When T390 associated with a given Access Category expires, or is stopped (e.g. due to cell reselection, RRC connection establishment for a higher‑priority reason, or receipt of updated SIB1 UAC parameters), the UE re‑evaluates that category. For any Access Category other than '2' (Emergency), the mere expiry or stopping of the corresponding T390 is sufficient by itself: the UE unconditionally considers the barring for that Access Category to be alleviated, i.e. it may make/re‑attempt the access without needing any additional trigger or upper‑layer indication. (This differs from Access Category '2', for which alleviation is tied to additional emergency‑specific handling rather than T390 expiry/stop alone.) Thus, for categories ≠ 2, T390 expiry or stop is both a necessary and sufficient condition for the UE to treat the category as no longer barred.
results.evidence: TS 38.331 §5.3.14.4: 'If the timer T390 expires, or is stopped, for a given Access Category, the UE shall consider the access attempts for the corresponding Access Category as not barred (barring alleviated), except for Access Category '2'.'

results.question: What action does the UE take regarding upper layers when barring for an Access Category is considered alleviated and that category was previously informed as barred?
results.reference: If the Access Category was informed to upper layers as barred, the UE informs upper layers about barring alleviation for that Access Category.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.14.3, Void
results.model_answer: If the access attempt for an Access Category was previously barred and the UE had informed upper layers of this barring, then once the barring condition for that Access Category is alleviated (i.e., the access attempt would no longer be barred based on the current UAC barring parameters), the UE shall inform the upper layers that access attempts for that Access Category are no longer barred.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.14.4 (Barring check): 'If the Access Category associated with the access attempt is not barred as specified above and the UE had earlier indicated to the upper layers that access attempts for the Access Category are barred, the UE shall inform the upper layers that access attempts for the Access Category are no longer barred.'

results.question: What additional procedure does the UE perform when barring is alleviated for either Access Category '8' or Access Category '2'?
results.reference: When barring is alleviated for Access Category '8' or Access Category '2', the UE performs the actions specified in clause 5.3.13.8.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.14.3, Void

results.question: What actions must a UE take after determining that the received messageIdentifier or serialNumber values differ from the current values for SIB7?
results.reference: The UE must: 1) use the received values as the new current values, 2) discard any previously buffered warningMessageSegment, and 3) proceed to either assemble/forward the warning message if all segments are received, or store the segment and continue reception if not.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.2.2.4.8, Actions upon reception of SIB7
results.model_answer: When a UE receiving SIB7 (ETWS secondary notification) finds that either the messageIdentifier or the serialNumber differs from the values it previously stored (or if SIB7 is being received for the first time), it means a new/updated PWS (Public Warning System) notification has arrived. In this case the UE shall: (1) store the newly received messageIdentifier and serialNumber values, replacing any previously stored ones for SIB7; (2) forward the received warning message content — i.e., the messageIdentifier, serialNumber, warningMessageSegmentType, warningMessageSegmentNumber, warningMessageSegment and, if present, the dataCodingScheme — to upper layers (NAS) for further processing/display to the user; and (3) continue to monitor for possible remaining segments of the same warning message if segmentation is indicated, reassembling them before forwarding to upper layers when reception is complete. If instead the identifiers are unchanged, the UE does not forward the (duplicate) message again to upper layers, since it has already been processed.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.2.2.31/5.2.2.29 'Actions upon reception of the SIB6, SIB7 or SIB8' — 'Upon receiving the SIB7, the UE shall: 1> if the messageIdentifier or the serialNumber included in the SIB7 differs from the values received earlier and stored by the UE: 2> forward the received messageIdentifier, serialNumber, warningMessageSegmentType, warningMessageSegmentNumber, warningMessageSegment and, if included, dataCodingScheme to upper layers.'

results.question: What steps does a UE follow when all segments of a warning message have been received, regardless of whether messageIdentifier/serialNumber values changed?
results.reference: The UE must: 1) assemble the warning message from received segments, 2) forward the complete message with messageIdentifier, serialNumber, and dataCodingScheme to upper layers, 3) stop reception of SIB7, 4) discard current messageIdentifier/serialNumber values, 5) store the received warningMessageSegment, and 6) continue reception of SIB7.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.2.2.4.8, Actions upon reception of SIB7
results.model_answer: When a UE determines that it has received all segments of a warning message (SC-PAGE or through segment reassembly indicated in the paging record for a given messageIdentifier and serialNumber combination), it assembles the complete warning message content by concatenating the segments in the correct sequence order based on the segment number. This applies irrespective of whether the messageIdentifier/serialNumber values differ across segments (which can occur due to system information change indications or scheduling changes), as the UE tracks and reassembles segments per each unique messageIdentifier/serialNumber pair. Once fully reassembled, the UE forwards the complete ETWS or CMAS message content (including the Warning Type or Message Content) to upper layers (NAS) for further processing/display, and the UE may then discard the stored segment information associated with that message. The UE also stops monitoring for that message's segments and no longer needs to track it in its list of received message identifiers, having completed reception.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.7.3 (or associated stage of ETWS/CMAS Reception), which states that the UE shall, upon reception of all segments of the message (regardless of change in messageIdentifier/serialNumber), assemble and forward the complete message to upper layers.

results.question: Under what condition should a UE discard stored warningMessageSegment and current messageIdentifier/serialNumber values for SIB7?
results.reference: The UE should discard them if the complete warning message has not been assembled within a period of 3 hours.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.2.2.4.8, Actions upon reception of SIB7
results.model_answer: A UE should discard any stored warningMessageSegment segments along with the associated messageIdentifier and serialNumber values for SIB7 when it detects a change in the SIB7 content indicated by a new/different messageIdentifier and/or serialNumber value compared to the ones currently stored (i.e., a new SIB7 message assembly is starting and previously buffered segments no longer belong to the current message). This ensures that segments from an old (superseded) SIB7 message are not mixed with segments of a new SIB7 message when reassembling the concatenated warningMessageSegment.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, Section 5.2.2.3.3 (SIB acquisition, ETWS/CMAS notification handling for SIB7/SIB8): "...if any of the messageIdentifier or serialNumber included in SIB7... is different from the value stored by the UE, the UE shall discard the stored warningMessageSegment and the current messageIdentifier and serialNumber values..."

results.question: What role do the hysteresis parameters hystMaxRelay and hystMinRelay play in the UE's evaluation of the threshold conditions for entry?
results.reference: If configured, hystMaxRelay is subtracted from threshHighRelay to create a lower entry threshold, and hystMinRelay is added to threshLowRelay to create a higher entry threshold. The UE uses these adjusted values when checking if RSRP is 'below threshHighRelay by hystMaxRelay' or 'above threshLowRelay by hystMinRelay'.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.14.2, NR sidelink U2N Relay UE threshold conditions
results.model_answer: hystMaxRelay and hystMinRelay provide hysteresis margins added to (or subtracted from) the configured threshold values used in the entry/exit condition evaluations for relay/remote UE selection (e.g., ProSe/sidelink relay discovery and selection procedures). Specifically, when the UE evaluates whether a threshold-based entry condition is satisfied (such as comparing a measured quantity like RSRP against threshMaxRelay or threshMinRelay), the hysteresis values hystMaxRelay and hystMinRelay are applied to prevent frequent toggling (ping-pong) of the entry condition due to small fluctuations in the measured quantity around the threshold. In practice, the UE requires the measured value to exceed the threshold by more than the hysteresis margin (for entry conditions based on 'greater than' comparisons) or fall below the threshold by more than the hysteresis margin (for 'less than' comparisons) before considering the condition as fulfilled. This ensures a more stable and reliable triggering of the relay-related event (e.g., becoming eligible as a relay UE) by requiring a consistent margin beyond the raw threshold before the entry condition is declared true, thereby avoiding rapid, repeated entry/exit due to measurement noise near the threshold boundary.
results.evidence: Entry condition is satisfied when Mp + Hp > ThreshMaxRelay (or Mp – Hp < ThreshMinRelay), where Hp corresponds to hystMaxRelay or hystMinRelay respectively, applied with the appropriate sign to prevent frequent toggling of the condition near the threshold.

results.question: In the absence of configuration for threshHighRelay and threshLowRelay, how does the UE assess whether the threshold conditions are met?
results.reference: If threshHighRelay is not configured, that part of the entry condition is automatically satisfied (true). Similarly, if threshLowRelay is not configured, that part of the entry condition is also automatically satisfied. Therefore, with both thresholds unconfigured, the logical 'AND' of the two conditions is true, and the UE considers the threshold conditions to be met.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.14.2, NR sidelink U2N Relay UE threshold conditions
results.model_answer: If threshHighRelay or threshLowRelay is not configured, the UE treats the corresponding threshold condition as satisfied by default, i.e., the condition involving that threshold is considered fulfilled (evaluates to TRUE) rather than being treated as unmet or causing an error. This ensures that relay selection/reselection or discovery-related evaluations do not stall simply because an optional threshold field was omitted from the configuration.
results.evidence: If threshHighRelay or threshLowRelay is not configured, the UE considers the criterion related to the threshold to be true.

results.question: How should a UE process the parameters contained in a MasterInformationBlockSidelink after reception?
results.reference: The UE is required to apply the values that are included in the received MasterInformationBlockSidelink message.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.9.4.2, Actions related to reception of MasterInformationBlockSidelink message
results.model_answer: When a UE receives a MasterInformationBlockSidelink (SL-MIB) from a SyncRef UE, it processes the contained fields to derive timing and configuration information for NR sidelink communication. Specifically, the UE: (1) uses the directFrameNumber and slotIndex fields together with the timing of the received SL-SS/PBCH block to determine the DFN, subframe/slot number of the SyncRef UE, and if this SyncRef UE is selected as the synchronization reference, the UE adjusts its own sidelink timing (DFN, subframe, slot) accordingly; (2) reads the inCoverage field to determine whether the SyncRef UE indicates it is served by NR (in-coverage), which affects the UE's own coverage state determination and synchronization priority evaluation; (3) applies the sl-TDD-Config field, if present, to determine the TDD UL/DL configuration to be used for sidelink resource pools when the SyncRef UE is selected as the timing/synchronization source; (4) ignores the reservedBits field, treating it as spare for future extension. The UE only acts on the SL-MIB contents if it is currently performing sidelink synchronization procedures (e.g., as a receiving UE evaluating or using a SyncRef UE), and applies the derived parameters only when this SyncRef UE has been selected according to the sidelink synchronization reference selection procedure (sl-SSB triggered synchronization).
results.evidence: TS 38.331, clause 5.8.11.3 (Actions related to reception of MasterInformationBlockSidelink)

results.question: Following the receipt of a MasterInformationBlockSidelink message, what specific operation must the UE execute?
results.reference: The UE must apply the values included in that received MasterInformationBlockSidelink message.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.9.4.2, Actions related to reception of MasterInformationBlockSidelink message
