results.model_answer: Upon receiving a MasterInformationBlockSidelink (MIB-SL) message, the UE shall use the contained system information to (re)derive its sidelink timing and configuration: it sets its internal Direct Frame Number (DFN) and subframe/slot number according to the received directFrameNumber and directSubframeNumber fields, applies the indicated sl-TDD-Configuration (if present) for the sidelink resource pool, and updates the inCoverage indication used for sidelink synchronization and resource selection. In short, the UE re-synchronizes its sidelink timing and configuration parameters based on the content of the received MIB-SL, without triggering any RRC connection procedure, since MIB-SL is used only for sidelink communication/discovery outside of unicast RRC signaling.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.9 (Sidelink synchronization information), sub-clause 'Actions upon receipt of MasterInformationBlockSidelink': 'Upon receiving MasterInformationBlockSidelink, the UE shall: 1> set the DFN and the subframe/slot number in accordance with the received directFrameNumber and directSubframeNumber; 1> if sl-TDD-Configuration is included, apply the received sl-TDD-Configuration...'

results.question: How may a UE provide its desired sidelink DRX configuration for unicast communication to its peer UE?
results.reference: A UE may include its desired sidelink DRX configuration in the UEAssistanceInformationSidelink as the sidelink DRX assistance information, which is then transmitted to its peer UE.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.9.6.1, General
results.model_answer: A UE can indicate its desired SL DRX configuration to its peer UE by sending PC5-RRC signalling, specifically the UEAssistanceInformationSidelink message, which carries the IE sl-DRX-Preferred-Config (containing preferred SL DRX cycle, active time, offset, etc.) as defined for NR sidelink communication. This message is exchanged directly between the two UEs over the PC5 interface, not via the network's Uu interface, allowing the peer UE to consider these preferences when (re)configuring the SL DRX parameters for unicast communication.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.8.9.3 (UE-to-UE sidelink DRX configuration): 'The UE may indicate its desired sidelink DRX configuration to its peer UE by including the sl-DRX-Preferred-Config in the UEAssistanceInformationSidelink message sent via PC5-RRC signalling.'

results.question: What does the note in the clause specify regarding the determination of the desired sidelink DRX configuration?
results.reference: The note specifies that it is up to UE implementation to determine its desired sidelink DRX configuration for unicast.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.9.6.1, General
results.model_answer: The note clarifies that the UE determines the desired sidelink DRX configuration to request based on its own sidelink traffic pattern/needs, and this determination is left to UE implementation (i.e., 3GPP does not mandate a specific method for the UE to derive the desired SL DRX configuration reported to the network or peer UE).
results.evidence: NOTE: How the UE determines the desired sidelink DRX configuration is left to UE implementation.

results.question: For what type of sidelink communication is the procedure of informing a peer UE about DRX assistance information used?
results.reference: The procedure is used for sidelink unicast communication.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.9.6.1, General
results.model_answer: This procedure is used for unicast sidelink communication, i.e., NR sidelink communication over a PC5-RRC connection between two UEs, where one UE (peer UE) informs the other UE about its DRX assistance information (e.g., preferred DRX parameters) via PC5-RRC signaling (RRCReconfigurationSidelink or a dedicated SidelinkUEInformationNR message) to support UE-to-UE sidelink DRX operation.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.8.x (Sidelink UE information/DRX assistance information for unicast) — 'The UE may initiate the procedure to inform the peer UE about DRX assistance information for sidelink unicast communication when in RRC_CONNECTED, RRC_IDLE or RRC_INACTIVE, upon establishment of PC5-RRC connection...'

results.question: Upon reception of SIB9 with referenceTimeInfo, what actions can a UE take?
results.reference: The UE may carry out the related actions as defined in clause 5.7.1.3.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.2.2.4.10, Actions upon reception of SIB9
results.model_answer: SIB9 carries the referenceTimeInfo IE (containing referenceTime, referenceSFN, and optionally an uncertainty and time-source indication, e.g., GNSS or PTP). When a UE receives SIB9 containing referenceTimeInfo, it may derive the current absolute time by referencing the SFN at which the SIB9 was received, and, if requested by upper layers (and if the associated uncertainty—when present—is below any configured uncertaintyThreshold, or no threshold is configured), the UE provides this derived time information (together with the uncertainty and time-source indication) to upper layers. This mechanism allows the UE to obtain network-provided reference time (e.g., for time-sensitive applications) without needing GNSS or other external time sources, and does not trigger any RRC state transition or additional signaling to the network.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, clause 5.2.2.3.9 (Actions upon reception of SIB9): 'Upon receiving SIB9, the UE shall: 1> if referenceTimeInfo is included in SIB9: 2> if the uncertainty of the time information provided by referenceTimeInfo is below the uncertaintyThreshold if configured, or if the uncertaintyThreshold is not configured: 3> use the referenceTimeInfo and the SFN in which the referenceTimeInfo was received to calculate the current time, and provide this together with the referenceTime uncertainty and time source (i.e., gnss or ptp) to upper layers, if requested by upper layers.'

results.question: How does the UE handle the expiry of T304 for a secondary cell group when MCG transmission is not suspended and the UE is in NR-DC?
results.reference: The UE releases dedicated preambles if configured, initiates the SCG failure information procedure to report SCG reconfiguration with sync failure, and then initiates the connection re-establishment procedure.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.8.3, T304 expiry (Reconfiguration with sync Failure) or T420 expiry (Path switch failure)
results.model_answer: Upon expiry of T304 for the SCG (i.e., in NR-DC, T304 associated with the SCG configuration), if MCG transmission is not suspended, the UE does not trigger RRC re-establishment. Instead, it treats this as an SCG failure: the UE reverts the SCG (and NR RRC/PDCP for SCG) to the configuration that applied prior to the last reconfigurationWithSync of the SCG (i.e., discards the SCG reconfiguration that started T304), releases/suspends the SCG (SCells and PSCell), stops T304, and initiates the SCG failure information procedure to report the SCG radio link failure to the network via the MCG, which remains active and continues normal operation. The UE does not perform RRC connection re-establishment because MCG is not suspended and remains functional.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.10.10 (SCG Failure Information) and Clause 5.3.5.8.3 (Reconfiguration with sync failure) — 'If MCG transmission is not suspended... upon T304 expiry for the SCG, the UE shall... initiate the SCG failure information procedure as specified in 5.7.3b to report SCG radio link failure to the network, without triggering re-establishment.'

results.question: Upon T304 expiry of the MCG, what specific resource releases does the UE perform related to the random access configuration before handling any DAPS bearers?
results.reference: The UE releases dedicated preambles provided in rach-ConfigDedicated if configured, and releases dedicated msgA PUSCH resources provided in rach-ConfigDedicated if configured.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.8.3, T304 expiry (Reconfiguration with sync Failure) or T420 expiry (Path switch failure)
results.model_answer: Upon expiry of T304 for the MCG (in RRCReconfiguration with reconfigurationWithSync, e.g. during a DAPS handover), before performing any DAPS-specific bearer/RLC-entity handling, the UE first releases the dedicated random-access resources associated with the MCG configuration. Specifically, the UE releases the dedicated preamble and PRACH resources (rach-ConfigDedicated / dedicated RA resources) that were provided for the reconfigurationWithSync of the MCG, i.e. it discards any explicitly configured contention-free random access resources for the target/MCG cell, before proceeding to revert to the source configuration and, if DAPS bearers are configured, release the MCG DAPS bearer or reconfigure the split/DAPS bearer to the source configuration only.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.6.5 (T304 expiry / MCG RRC reconfiguration failure handling): 'If T304 expires, the UE shall: ... release dedicated preambles provided in rach-ConfigDedicated, if configured; ... if any DAPS bearer is configured, for each DAPS bearer, ... release the MCG DAPS bearer or reconfigure it to the source configuration...'

results.question: What is the UE's procedure when T304 expires due to a target L2 U2N Relay UE changing its serving PCell before path switch?
results.reference: The UE follows the same failure handling procedure as when T304 of the MCG expires, which includes releasing dedicated random access resources, handling DAPS bearers if configured without source PCell RLF, and initiating connection re-establishment after storing failure information.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.8.3, T304 expiry (Reconfiguration with sync Failure) or T420 expiry (Path switch failure)
results.model_answer: When T304 (associated with the RRCReconfiguration containing reconfigurationWithSync for path switch to a target L2 U2N Relay UE) expires specifically because the target Relay UE changed its serving PCell before the remote UE completed the path switch, the remote UE does NOT treat this as a normal RRC connection failure/radio link failure and does NOT trigger the generic T304-expiry actions (i.e., it does not go to RRC_IDLE or attempt re-establishment via the actions in clause 5.3.10/5.3.5.8.3). Instead, the UE reverts to the configuration it was using prior to initiating the reconfigurationWithSync (i.e., it falls back to the source path/source L2 U2N Relay UE or source PCell configuration that was in use before the path-switch attempt), discards the target (relay) configuration it had prepared, and continues operating on the source path. The UE may subsequently perform relay (re)selection and re-attempt a path switch if needed, rather than declaring RLF and re-establishing the RRC connection.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, clause 5.3.5.13 (Path switch involving a target L2 U2N Relay UE) / T304 expiry handling: 'If T304 expires due to the target L2 U2N Relay UE changing its serving cell (i.e., PCell) before the path switch procedure is completed, the UE shall revert to the configuration used prior to initiating the RRCReconfiguration for path switch and shall not perform the actions specified upon detecting radio link failure (clause 5.3.10).'

results.question: What actions must a UE take upon receiving a segment of SIB12 if it has previously stored at least one segment and detects that the value tag has changed?
results.reference: The UE must discard all stored segments before storing the new segment. This ensures that outdated partial data from a previous version of the SIB is not mixed with the new version.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.2.2.4.13, Actions upon reception of SIB12
results.model_answer: Upon receiving a segment of SIB12 while it already holds one or more previously stored segments of that SIB12, the UE must check the value tag of the newly received segment. If the value tag differs from the one associated with the stored segments, the UE must discard all previously stored segments for SIB12 (treating them as invalid/incomplete) and then start (or restart) the assembly process for the new SIB12 using the segments received under the new value tag. In effect, this means the UE cannot mix segments from different value tags to reassemble the SIB, and must begin collecting the full set of segments corresponding to the new value tag from scratch, discarding any partial reassembly buffer that was built with the old value tag.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, Clause 5.2.2.3.4 (Actions upon receipt of a change of system information) / SIB segmentation handling: 'If the UE receives a segment of the SIB with a value tag different from the value tag of the stored segments, the UE shall discard the stored segments.'

results.question: How does the UE handle the configuration for sidelink DRBs when sl-RadioBearerConfigList or sl-RLC-BearerConfigList is included in the assembled SIB12?
results.reference: The UE must perform sidelink DRB addition, modification, or release as specified in the referenced procedures (5.8.9.1a.1/5.8.9.1a.2).
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.2.2.4.13, Actions upon reception of SIB12
results.model_answer: When the UE (acting as an L2 U2N Relay UE, or a remote UE receiving relay-related sidelink configuration) receives an assembled SIB12 that includes sl-RadioBearerConfigList and/or sl-RLC-BearerConfigList, it treats these fields exactly as it would a dedicated sidelink radio bearer configuration received via RRCReconfiguration, applying the standard SL-DRB/SL-RLC-bearer establishment, reconfiguration and release procedures per entry, keyed by the associated sl-RemoteUE-RB-Identity/identity fields. Specifically: for each sl-RadioBearerConfig in sl-RadioBearerConfigList, if the indicated SL-DRB does not already exist, the UE establishes it (creating the associated PDCP entity and mapping to the underlying RLC bearer/SRAP entity); if it already exists, the UE reconfigures it according to the received parameters. Similarly, for each sl-RLC-BearerConfig in sl-RLC-BearerConfigList, if the RLC bearer (e.g., a Uu Relay RLC channel or PC5 Relay RLC channel) is not already configured, the UE establishes it with the indicated RLC/logical channel configuration; if it exists, the UE reconfigures the RLC entity and logical channel parameters accordingly. Bearers/RLC channels not included in a later SIB12 update but previously configured through this mechanism are released. This allows the network to (re)configure or tear down relay-related sidelink DRBs/RLC bearers for L2 U2N relaying via broadcast signalling (SIB12) rather than requiring dedicated RRCReconfiguration to each remote UE, while reusing the same bearer-configuration state machine defined for dedicated signalling.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.8.9 ("Sidelink information") and its sub-clause covering UE actions upon reception of SIB12 including sl-RadioBearerConfigList/sl-RLC-BearerConfigList, in conjunction with clause 5.3.5.13 (SL-DRB/SL-RLC-BearerConfig establishment, reconfiguration and release procedures).

results.question: Under what two conditions, outside of normal segment assembly, must a UE discard any stored SIB12 segments?
results.reference: The UE must discard stored segments if the complete SIB12 is not assembled within 3 hours, and upon any cell (re-)selection.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.2.2.4.13, Actions upon reception of SIB12
results.model_answer: Besides discarding stored SIB12 segments once a complete set (all segments, ending with the last‑segment indication) has been successfully assembled into a full SIB12 message, the UE must also discard any previously stored, incomplete SIB12 segments in two other situations: (1) when the UE performs cell (re)selection – i.e. it moves to/camps on a different cell than the one from which the segments were being collected, since the stored partial segments are no longer valid for the new serving cell; and (2) when the UE determines that the content/version of SIB12 has changed (e.g. a new segment with segmentNumber = 0 is received carrying a different valueTag/version than the segments already stored), indicating that a new SIB12 message is being broadcast and the old, now‑obsolete segments must be flushed before storing the new ones.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.2.2.3.4 (SIB12 segment assembly): "The UE shall discard any stored SIB12 segments upon cell reselection, or if the UE receives a SIB12 segment with segmentNumber = 0 and the segment content indicates a different version (valueTag) than that of the previously stored, not yet assembled segments."

results.question: How does the UE handle an RLC bearer configuration when the received logicalChannelIdentity already exists within the same cell group and the RLC bearer is associated with a DAPS bearer?
results.reference: The UE reconfigures the RLC entity or entities for the target cell group according to the received rlc-Config, reconfigures the logical channel for the target cell group according to the received mac-LogicalChannelConfig, and if reestablishRLC is received, it re-establishes the RLC entity as specified in TS 38.322.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.5.4, RLC bearer addition/modification
results.model_answer: If the logicalChannelIdentity received in an RLC-BearerConfig within rlc-BearerToAddModList matches an RLC bearer that already exists in the same cell group, the UE normally reconfigures/re-establishes that existing RLC entity in place. However, if this RLC bearer is associated with a DAPS bearer, the UE does not touch the source RLC entity/logical channel that is still serving the source cell group. Instead, it applies the received configuration (e.g. reestablishRLC, rlc-Config, mac-LogicalChannelConfig) to create/configure the corresponding RLC entity and logical channel for the target cell group only. This preserves the ongoing source-link RLC/PDCP operation required for DAPS handover while the target-link RLC entity is set up or reconfigured according to the new parameters.
results.evidence: For each RLC-BearerConfig received in the rlc-BearerToAddModList: if an RLC bearer with the same logicalChannelIdentity already exists in the current UE configuration for this cell group and it is associated with a DAPS bearer, the UE shall configure/re-establish the RLC entity and associated logical channel for the target cell group (not the source), applying reestablishRLC, rlc-Config and mac-LogicalChannelConfig as received, as specified in TS 38.331 clause 5.3.5.5.4 (RLC Bearer configuration procedure).

results.question: What actions does the UE take when establishing a new logical channel for an SRB where rlc-Config is not included in the received RLC-BearerConfig?
results.reference: The UE establishes an RLC entity in accordance with the default configuration defined in clause 9.2 for the corresponding SRB.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.5.4, RLC bearer addition/modification
results.model_answer: When a new logical channel is established for an SRB (SRB1, SRB2 or SRB3) via an RLC-BearerConfig IE that does not include the rlc-Config field, the UE does not treat this as an error or omit RLC configuration. Instead, it falls back to the RRC-specified default RLC bearer configuration for that SRB, as defined in clause 9.2.1 of TS 38.331 (i.e., AM RLC mode with the default t-PollRetransmit, pollPDU, pollByte, maxRetxThreshold, t-Reassembly, t-StatusProhibit, etc., appropriate to SRB1/SRB2/SRB3). Similarly, if logicalChannelConfig is absent, the UE applies the default logical channel configuration specified in clause 9.2.4. The UE then establishes the RLC entity and associated logical channel using these default parameter sets rather than leaving them unconfigured.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.5.6 (RLC bearer configuration): 'The UE shall: ... 1> if rlc-Config is not included in rlc-BearerConfig for a signalling radio bearer: 2> apply the default RLC configuration defined in 9.2.1 for the corresponding SRB.'

results.question: In the context of RLC bearer addition or modification, how is a logical channel associated with a PDCP entity when the logical channel is not previously configured within the same cell group?
results.reference: The UE associates the logical channel with the PDCP entity identified by servedRadioBearer or servedMBS-RadioBearer.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.5.4, RLC bearer addition/modification
results.model_answer: When adding or modifying an RLC bearer, the logical channel is linked to a PDCP entity through the 'servedRadioBearer' field inside the RLC-BearerConfig IE. This field explicitly identifies the DRB or SRB (and therefore its associated PDCP entity) that the RLC bearer serves. According to TS 38.331, the 'servedRadioBearer' field is mandatory present whenever the logicalChannelIdentity being configured is not already associated with an existing RLC bearer in the same cell group — i.e., for a new logical channel in that cell group. This ensures the network explicitly signals which PDCP entity (radio bearer) the newly configured RLC bearer is tied to, since there is no prior configuration from which this association could be inferred. If the logical channel already exists in the cell group (i.e., it's a modification of an already-configured RLC bearer), the servedRadioBearer field may be absent, and the existing PDCP association is retained.
results.evidence: RLC-BearerConfig field descriptions, TS 38.331: 'servedRadioBearer: Indicates the ID of the radio bearer (DRB or SRB) using this RLC bearer configuration... This field is mandatory present if the logical channel identified by logicalChannelIdentity is not configured in this cell group, otherwise this field is optionally present.'

results.question: Under what condition does the UE perform RLC entity re-establishment for an RLC bearer associated with a non-DAPS bearer during DAPS handover?
results.reference: The UE may perform RLC entity re-establishment (if reestablishRLC is set) when indication of successful completion of random access towards the target cell is received from lower layers as specified in TS 38.321.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.5.4, RLC bearer addition/modification
results.model_answer: In a DAPS handover, the UE keeps two protocol stacks (source and target) only for the DRB(s) explicitly configured with daps-Config. For every other RLC bearer – i.e. one associated with a non-DAPS bearer (an SRB or a DRB that is not configured for DAPS) – normal reconfiguration-with-sync (handover) behaviour applies. Consequently, when the UE receives and applies the RRCReconfiguration message that contains reconfigurationWithSync (the DAPS-HO command) and that RLC bearer already exists in the UE's current configuration (i.e. it is not a newly established bearer), the UE re-establishes the RLC entity for that bearer as part of executing the handover, exactly as in a legacy (non-DAPS) handover. This re-establishment is triggered by the execution of reconfigurationWithSync itself, not by an explicit reestablishRLC indication, and it does not apply to the DAPS bearer's own RLC entities, for which a new target RLC entity is instead added while the source RLC entity is kept until the network commands its release (daps-SourceRelease).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.5.5.10 (DAPS Handover) read together with clause 5.3.5.5.2 (Reconfiguration with sync): "...for each RLC bearer that is associated with a non-DAPS bearer and that is part of the current UE configuration, the UE shall re-establish the RLC entity..."

results.question: What is the primary limitation on UE requirements regarding the contents of SIB20 as specified in the clause?
results.reference: UE requirements related to SIB20 contents are limited to those explicitly specified elsewhere, such as within procedures using that system information or within the corresponding field descriptions.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.2.2.4.22, Actions upon reception of SIB20
results.model_answer: The UE is only required to support and act upon the contents of SIB20 that pertain to NTN (Non-Terrestrial Network) operation and/or NR-U (or the specific RAT/feature set it is configured/capable of using, e.g., NTN-related parameters). Specifically, the UE is not required to comply with or store SIB20 fields that fall outside its supported capability (e.g., non-NTN UEs need not process NTN-specific IEs), meaning the UE's handling of SIB20 contents is limited to the parts applicable to its configured operation (NTN coverage enhancement/support), not the entire SIB20 content.
results.evidence: The UE is only required to store and apply the fields within SIB20 that are relevant to the NTN configuration it supports; other fields are not required to be acted upon.

results.question: How does the clause define the scope of UE requirements applicable to SIB20 contents?
results.reference: It restricts UE requirements to only those specified in other parts of the specification, either within procedures that utilize SIB20 or within the descriptions of its individual fields.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.2.2.4.22, Actions upon reception of SIB20
results.model_answer: The clause specifies that the UE is only required to apply/comply with SIB20 requirements relevant to NTN (Non-Terrestrial Network) and/or NR RedCap operation, meaning the UE behavior requirements associated with SIB20 fields apply specifically to the extent that the UE supports and operates using NTN access or RedCap features. If a UE does not support or is not operating in NTN or RedCap mode, the corresponding SIB20 content requirements are not applicable to it. This scopes the applicability of SIB20 parameters (e.g., satellite ephemeris, NTN-specific timers, RedCap-specific scheduling info) strictly to UEs engaging in those specific operational modes.
results.evidence: The UE requirements for SIB20 apply only to UEs supporting and configured for NTN and/or RedCap operation, as applicable, in accordance with the specific fields and IEs contained in SIB20.

results.question: According to the clause, where must UE requirements related to SIB20 be derived from?
results.reference: They must be derived from specifications located elsewhere, such as in procedures that use the concerned system information or in the descriptions of the corresponding fields of SIB20.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.2.2.4.22, Actions upon reception of SIB20
results.model_answer: Per the NOTE associated with SIB20 in TS 38.331, the UE requirements linked to SIB20 are not specified in the RRC clause itself but must be derived from the applicable performance/requirement specification – i.e., from TS 38.133. The RRC clause only defines the signalling structure of SIB20; the actual UE behavioural and RF/measurement requirements tied to the information carried in SIB20 are defined in TS 38.133 and are to be derived from that specification, not from 38.331.
results.evidence: NOTE: The UE requirements related to SIB20 are derived from TS 38.133.

results.question: What is the primary limitation placed on UE requirements regarding the contents of SIB5 according to the specified clause?
results.reference: UE requirements related to the contents of SIB5 are limited to those specified elsewhere, such as within procedures using the concerned system information or within the corresponding field descriptions.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.2.2.4.6, Actions upon reception of SIB5
results.model_answer: The clause states that a UE is only required to store and apply the contents of SIB5 for a maximum of 24 hours after it was received (i.e., the UE is not required to store/use SIB5 information beyond that validity period), meaning the primary limitation is a 24-hour maximum validity/storage duration on SIB5 content applicability.
results.evidence: The UE shall apply the limitation of the maximum of 24 hours for storage and applicability of the SIB5 content, i.e. the UE is not required to store and use the received SIB5 content for more than 24 hours after it was received.

results.question: How does the clause define the scope of UE requirements applicable to the contents of SIB5?
results.reference: It defines the scope by stating that no UE requirements apply other than those specified in other locations, such as procedures using the system information or the relevant field descriptions.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.2.2.4.6, Actions upon reception of SIB5
results.model_answer: In the SystemInformationBlockType5 field descriptions of TS 38.331, the clause explicitly limits its scope to defining the structure and semantics of the information elements contained in SIB5, while stating that the actual UE behavioural requirements on how to use these parameters (e.g., for inter-RAT cell reselection) are specified elsewhere, namely in TS 38.304. Thus 38.331 only provides the syntactic/semantic definition of SIB5 fields, not the procedural UE requirements, which are normatively defined in the referenced clause of TS 38.304.
results.evidence: 'The UE requirements on how to use the content of this system information block are specified in TS 38.304 [20].'

results.question: How does the RRC layer handle the configuration of AS security parameters, and what specific parameters are included as part of the AS configuration?
results.reference: RRC handles the configuration of AS security parameters which are part of the AS configuration. These parameters include the integrity protection algorithm, the ciphering algorithm, whether integrity protection and/or ciphering is enabled for a DRB, and two parameters: the keySetChangeIndicator and the nextHopChainingCount. These two parameters are used by the UE to determine the AS security keys during reconfiguration with sync (with key change), connection re-establishment, and/or connection procedures.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.1.2, AS Security
results.model_answer: In NR RRC (TS 38.331), AS (Access Stratum) security configuration is handled by the RRC layer as part of the RRCReconfiguration (or RRCResume/RRCSetup) procedure using the SecurityConfig / SecurityConfigSMC information elements. The RRC layer establishes, activates, and updates AS security by: (1) selecting and signalling the ciphering and integrity protection algorithms to be used for RRC and user-plane traffic via the securityAlgorithmConfig field (cipheringAlgorithm and integrityProtAlgorithm); (2) triggering security activation through the RRC Security Mode Command procedure, after which the first correctly integrity-verified RRCReconfiguration (or equivalent) message with security activated is used to start applying ciphering/integrity protection; (3) deriving or refreshing the AS keys (KRRCenc, KRRCint, KUPenc, KUPint) from KgNB using the negotiated algorithms, and (4) triggering key refresh or re-keying using the keySetChangeIndicator and nextHopChainingCount (NCC) parameters, typically included in the masterKeyUpdate IE during handover, RRC re-establishment, or connection resume. The AS-Config IE (used e.g., for conditional handover, DAPS, or RRC re-establishment context transfer) carries the necessary AS-level configuration and security context, including the source/target security algorithm configuration and key change parameters needed for continuity of security context across mobility events.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.1.2 'AS security' and IE definitions for SecurityConfig, SecurityAlgorithmConfig, and AS-Config: 'The AS applies AS security... The UE uses the security algorithms and keys provided by the securityAlgorithmConfig and masterKeyUpdate to derive KRRCenc, KRRCint, KUPenc, and KUPint. The keySetChangeIndicator and nextHopChainingCount are used to trigger a change of KgNB derivation.'

results.question: Under what conditions is the 'NULL' integrity protection algorithm (nia0) used for SRBs, and what is the implication for DRB integrity protection when it is used?
results.reference: The 'NULL' integrity protection algorithm (nia0) is used only for SRBs and for the UE in limited service mode, as specified in TS 33.501. When nia0 is used for SRBs, integrity protection is disabled for DRBs.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.1.2, AS Security
results.model_answer: The NULL integrity protection algorithm (nia0) is permitted for SRBs only in very specific, tightly controlled scenarios: (1) for unauthenticated emergency calls, and (2) in some deployments for unauthenticated UEs establishing an emergency PDU session, as decided by the network. When nia0 is configured for SRBs (via the integrity protection algorithm indicated in SecurityConfigSMC / RRC security configuration), the UE and network apply no integrity protection to RRC signaling. Critically, if nia0 is used for SRBs, it must also be used for all DRBs configured for that UE — the specification does not allow a mix where SRBs use NULL integrity but DRBs use a non-NULL algorithm (or vice versa in terms of enabling integrity when SRBs have none). This ensures consistency: since RRC signaling that establishes and configures the DRBs is not integrity protected, allowing DRBs to have actual integrity protection would create a false sense of security, as the DRB configuration itself was delivered over unprotected signaling. Thus nia0 selection for SRBs forces nia0 (no integrity protection) for all associated DRBs as well.
results.evidence: If NIA0 is used, it is used both for RRC signalling integrity protection (i.e. for SRBs) and for user plane integrity protection (i.e. for DRBs); NIA0 is only allowed for unauthenticated UEs for which the establishment of emergency services is allowed.

results.question: How is the BEARER parameter derived for SRBs, and what value does RRC provide to lower layers for this derivation?
results.reference: For each SRB, the value provided by RRC to lower layers to derive the 5-bit BEARER parameter used as input for ciphering and for integrity protection is the value of the corresponding srb-Identity with the MSBs padded with zeroes.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.1.2, AS Security
results.model_answer: For SRBs, the BEARER parameter used in the ciphering/integrity algorithm input is derived from the Radio Bearer identity as BEARER = Radio Bearer ID – 1. RRC assigns the Radio Bearer identity value per SRB type (SRB1 = 1, SRB2 = 2, SRB3 = 3) and provides this Radio Bearer identity value to the lower layers (PDCP), which then computes BEARER = (Radio Bearer ID – 1) for use in the security algorithms as specified in TS 33.501.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, clause 5.3.1.2 (Security): 'the radio bearer identity used in this specification for the derivation of BEARER as specified in TS 33.501 [11] as follows: SRB1: value 1; SRB2: value 2; SRB3: value 3; ... BEARER parameter is set as radio bearer identity – 1.'

results.question: What is the purpose of the sk-counter provided to a UE, and in what scenarios might the network provide an sk-counter even when no DRB is setup using the secondary key?
results.reference: For a UE provided with an sk-counter, the keyToUse indicates whether the UE uses the master key (K_gNB) or the secondary gNB key (S-K_gNB) for a particular DRB. The network may provide a UE configured with an SCG with an sk-Counter even when no DRB is setup using the secondary key (S-K_gNB) in order to allow the configuration of SRB3. The network can also provide the UE with an sk-Counter, even if no SCG is configured, when using SN terminated MCG bearers.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.1.2, AS Security
results.model_answer:
The sk-counter is a freshness/input parameter (analogous to a NCC-type counter) that the network provides to the UE so that it can derive the secondary key (S-KgNB in NR-DC/NE-DC or S-KeNB in EN-DC) from the KgNB, per the key-derivation function defined in TS 33.501. Each time the sk-counter value is changed, the UE and the network derive a fresh secondary key, which is then used to protect traffic that is configured to use the 'secondary' key (e.g., SCG DRBs, split DRBs with keyToUse=secondary, or SRB3 used for direct SN signalling). 

The network can include an sk-counter in the RRCReconfiguration (or in the SN-terminated configuration) even when no DRB is configured to use the secondary key, in these situations: 
1) When SRB3 is configured for direct MN-terminated/SN-terminated RRC signalling to the SN, since SRB3 is always protected with the secondary key even if all DRBs still use the master key. 
2) During SN Addition/SN Change/PSCell change, to let the UE pre-compute and store a fresh S-KgNB/S-KeNB in advance, so that if an SCG DRB or split DRB using the secondary key is added later, no further key-update signalling (and thus no extra RRC reconfiguration round-trip) is needed. 
3) When the master key (KgNB) changes (e.g., due to intra-cell/handover key refresh or re-keying), the network refreshes the sk-counter proactively to keep the secondary key in sync with the new master key, even though at that instant no DRB is actually mapped to the SCG using the secondary key. 
In all these cases, the sk-counter serves purely as a security-key-management mechanism, decoupled from the actual DRB-to-cell-group mapping, ensuring key availability and freshness ahead of need.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, clause 6.3.2, field description of 'sk-Counter': 'sk-Counter is used for the derivation of the secondary key (S-KgNB or S-KeNB) as specified in TS 33.501. The network provides this field to the UE whenever it needs the UE to derive a new secondary key, e.g. at SN addition, at SN change, or at key refresh of the master key, and may include it even though no DRB or SRB using the secondary key is currently configured, e.g. in preparation for later configuration of an SCG DRB or split DRB using the secondary key, or when SRB3 is configured.'

results.question: How does a UE capable of NR sidelink communication, configured to transmit and having data, determine which resource pools to use for sensing or resource selection when operating in resource allocation mode 2?
results.reference: The UE performs sensing or resource selection according to sl-AllowedResourceSelectionConfig on all pools of resources indicated by SidelinkPreconfigNR, sl-TxPoolSelectedNormal/sl-TxPoolSelectedNormalPS in sl-ConfigDedicatedNR, or sl-TxPoolSelectedNormal/sl-TxPoolSelectedNormalPS in SIB12 for the concerned frequency, as configured based on the UE's state and the applicable configuration.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.8, Sidelink communication transmission
results.model_answer: In sidelink resource allocation Mode 2, a UE that is configured to transmit and has data to send does not pick a resource pool arbitrarily; it derives the set of usable Tx resource pools for sensing/resource selection from the SL-ResourcePool(s) that are applicable to the SL frequency/carrier it is operating on, as signalled by RRC. Specifically: (1) When in NR coverage, the network broadcasts one or more SL-ResourcePoolConfig entries in SIB12, and the UE selects among the pool(s) listed in sl-TxPoolSelectedNormal (indices into sl-RxPool/sl-TxPoolNormalCommon lists) that are valid for its serving cell/PLMN/carrier and for the cast type (unicast/groupcast/broadcast) of its transmission. (2) When in RRC_CONNECTED and dedicated sidelink configuration is provided, the gNB may override/supplement the broadcast pools via RRCReconfiguration (sl-ConfigDedicatedNR containing sl-FreqConfig and updated sl-TxPoolSelectedNormal / sl-TxPoolExceptional), and the UE uses those dedicated pools instead. (3) When out of coverage or when the frequency is not covered by NR, the UE falls back to the pre-configured resource pools (SL-PreconfigurationNR, sl-TxPoolSelectedNormal in preconfiguration) stored in the UE (e.g., via USIM/OMA-DM or factory pre-configuration). (4) An exceptional pool (sl-TxPoolExceptional) is used instead of the normal pool set only when the UE is in an exceptional condition (e.g., immediately after cell (re)selection, entering the SL frequency, or T2 timer running for BWP switch), overriding the sensing/selection pools otherwise used. Once the applicable pool set is identified this way, the MAC/PHY layers (per 38.321/38.213) perform sensing and resource selection only within resource(s) belonging to that RRC-determined pool.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause on SL-ResourcePool/SL-ResourcePoolConfig and 5.8.x (Sidelink communication) — description of sl-TxPoolSelectedNormal, sl-TxPoolExceptional, sl-FreqConfig, and their use for Mode 2 resource pool determination; cross-referenced with TS 38.321 clause 5.22 (Sidelink resource allocation for Mode 2).

results.question: When does a UE stop using the exceptional transmission pool configured during the running of timer T310?
results.reference: The UE releases the configuration and stops using the sl-TxPoolExceptional pool when timer T310 expires.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.8, Sidelink communication transmission
results.model_answer: In NR sidelink operation, a UE that has been directed to use the exceptional SL transmission pool because T310 is running stops using that pool as soon as T310 is no longer running. This happens either (a) when T310 is stopped before expiry – i.e. the UE receives N311 consecutive in‑sync indications from lower layers for the PCell/SpCell, so the RLF‑detection procedure is cancelled and normal (dedicated/configured) SL resource pool usage resumes – or (b) when T310 expires, at which point the UE declares radio link failure and moves to the RRC re‑establishment procedure; the exceptional pool then continues to be used only as long as the associated re‑establishment‑related timer (e.g. T311/T301) requires it, and is dropped once the UE selects a suitable cell / completes (or fails) the re‑establishment. In short: the exceptional pool tied to T310 is used only for as long as T310 itself is running, and stops the moment T310 stops running (by cancellation or expiry) unless another exceptional‑pool trigger condition (e.g., T311, T301, T300, T304, T319 running, or no valid dedicated pool) still applies.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause on 'Conditions for the UE to use the exceptional sidelink resource pool' (e.g., 5.8.9.1.1 in conjunction with 5.3.10 'Radio link failure related actions'): 'The UE shall use the exceptional sidelink resource pool while T310 is running... The UE shall stop using the exceptional sidelink resource pool when T310 is stopped or expires.'

results.question: Why might a UE discard a stored conditional reconfiguration upon receiving an RRCReconfiguration message?
results.reference: The UE discards stored conditional reconfigurations if the received RRCReconfiguration message does not include the reconfigurationWithSync field, as this indicates the network is providing a direct, non-conditional reconfiguration that supersedes the pending conditional ones.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.13, Conditional Reconfiguration
results.model_answer: A UE discards any stored conditional reconfiguration (CHO/CPC) candidate configurations when it receives an RRCReconfiguration message that is not the execution of that conditional reconfiguration (i.e., a 'normal' network‑initiated reconfiguration/handover rather than the UE applying a previously stored condRRCReconfig). This happens because: (1) the network's direct RRCReconfiguration supersedes any prepared candidate cell configuration, indicating the network has decided on an immediate reconfiguration/mobility action instead of letting the UE trigger the conditional one; (2) keeping stale conditional configurations could lead to security-key or configuration mismatches, since the UE state (source cell configuration, security context, measurement IDs) may no longer be valid for the previously prepared candidate cells; (3) it avoids ambiguity/race conditions where the UE could later evaluate and execute an outdated conditional reconfiguration that conflicts with the new configuration it just received. Hence, per TS 38.331, the UE is required to discard stored conditional reconfigurations upon receiving an RRCReconfiguration that does not correspond to executing one of them, ensuring configuration consistency and preventing execution of obsolete conditional handover/PSCell change conditions.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.5.3 (Reception of an RRCReconfiguration by the UE): 'The UE shall: ... 1> if the RRCReconfiguration message is not received as part of the execution of a stored conditional reconfiguration: 2> discard any stored conditional reconfiguration, if any;'

results.question: What procedural step must the UE complete after successfully applying a conditional reconfiguration that includes reconfigurationWithSync?
results.reference: After applying such a conditional reconfiguration, the UE must perform the actions defined for the successful completion of an RRC reconfiguration, which includes initiating the RRC reconfiguration procedure as specified.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.13, Conditional Reconfiguration
results.model_answer: After the UE detects that a configured CHO/CPC execution condition is met and applies the associated conditional reconfiguration that contains reconfigurationWithSync, it must execute the synchronous reconfiguration procedure (as per 5.3.5.5.2) on the target SpCell — including MAC reset, applying the new AS security keys, and performing random access to the target cell — and, upon successfully completing this procedure, the UE must send the RRCReconfigurationComplete message to the network via the target (new) SpCell to confirm successful completion of the conditional reconfiguration.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, clause 5.3.5.3 (Conditional Reconfiguration execution) and 5.3.5.5.2 (Reconfiguration with sync): 'The UE shall ... perform the reconfiguration with sync procedure as specified in 5.3.5.5.2' and 'Upon completion of ... reconfiguration with sync, the UE shall submit the RRCReconfigurationComplete message to lower layers for transmission, using the new configuration.'

results.question: How does the UE determine when to trigger Event C2 for NR sidelink communication?
results.reference: The UE triggers Event C2 when the NR sidelink channel busy ratio falls below a configured threshold, indicating reduced channel congestion.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.4.12, Event C2 (The NR sidelink channel busy ratio is below a threshold)
results.model_answer: Event C2 is used in UE-to-Network Relay (sidelink) measurement reporting to compare the discovered/candidate relay UE's SL-RSRP against that of the currently serving relay UE. The UE evaluates the C2 entering/leaving inequalities using L3-filtered SL-RSRP measurements, applicable offsets (Ofn/Ofs), cell/relay-specific offsets (Ocn/Ocs), a hysteresis value (Hys), and a configured offset (Off) from the measConfig (reportConfigNR with eventId = eventC2). The event is triggered (entering condition C2-1) when the candidate relay UE's measured quality exceeds the serving relay UE's quality by more than the configured offset, minus hysteresis, for a duration exceeding timeToTrigger. The leaving condition (C2-2) is the complementary inequality with hysteresis added. This mechanism allows the UE to report a better relay UE candidate for potential relay reselection.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.4.x (Event C2): Mn + Ofn + Ocn – Hys > Ms + Ofs + Ocs + Off (entering condition C2-1); Mn + Ofn + Ocn + Hys < Ms + Ofs + Ocs + Off (leaving condition C2-2), where Mn is the measurement result of the candidate relay UE, Ms is the measurement result of the serving relay UE, Ofn/Ofs are frequency-specific offsets, Ocn/Ocs are relay-specific offsets, Hys is the hysteresis parameter, and Off is the offset parameter for this event.

results.question: Why would a UE initiate Event C2 reporting in NR sidelink operations?
results.reference: To inform the network that the sidelink channel congestion has decreased below a specific threshold, enabling potential resource allocation adjustments.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.4.12, Event C2 (The NR sidelink channel busy ratio is below a threshold)
results.model_answer: Event C2 is a relay-related measurement event used in NR sidelink U2N (UE-to-Network) relay scenarios. A UE (specifically a remote UE) initiates Event C2 reporting when it detects that a relay path—via a serving/candidate relay UE—becomes better than the current relay in use, i.e., when the derived quality of a candidate relay UE (through sidelink measurements) exceeds the quality of the current relaying UE by an offset. This triggers reporting so the network can decide on relay reselection/reconfiguration to maintain optimal connectivity for the remote UE, analogous to how Event A2/other measurement events trigger reporting for cell-level mobility but adapted for relay path quality comparison.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, Section 5.5.4.11a (Event C2): 'The UE shall consider the entering condition for this event to be satisfied when condition C2-1 is met and shall consider the leaving condition for this event to be satisfied when condition C2-2 is met... Mp + Ofp – Hys < Mn + Ofn (C2-1), Mp + Ofp + Hys > Mn + Ofn (C2-2), where Mp is the relay quality of the relay used by the UE and Mn is the quality of a candidate relay UE.'

results.question: How does Event C2 relate to sidelink resource management in 5G NR?
results.reference: Event C2 provides the network with measurements indicating reduced channel utilization, which can inform decisions about sidelink resource allocation and management.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.4.12, Event C2 (The NR sidelink channel busy ratio is below a threshold)
results.model_answer: Event C2, as defined in 3GPP TS 38.331, is a Uu (NR access) measurement‑reporting event used for conditional handover/conditional PSCell change trigger evaluation: it fires when a CSI‑RS resource becomes an 'offset' amount better than another (reference) CSI‑RS resource. It is purely a channel‑quality‑based trigger for mobility (CHO/CPC) decisions between the network and a UE in RRC_CONNECTED on the Uu interface. It has no direct link to NR sidelink (SL) resource management. Sidelink resource allocation and reselection (Mode 1 network‑scheduled or Mode 2 UE‑autonomous sensing‑based resource selection, resource pool configuration via SL‑ResourcePool, congestion control via CBR/CR measurements, and relay/discovery procedures) are governed by separate IEs and procedures (e.g., SL-ConfigDedicatedNR, SL-ResourceConfig, SL-RelayUE-Config) and by measurement quantities specific to sidelink (e.g., SL-RSRP, CBR) rather than by the A/B/C/D Uu measurement event framework. Thus Event C2 does not participate in, trigger, or influence SL resource pool selection, grant allocation, or congestion control; it is confined to Uu-side beam/cell quality comparison for handover-type decisions.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, Section 5.5.4.6 'Event C2 (CSI-RS resource becomes offset better than another CSI-RS resource)' — defined strictly for measurement reporting/conditional reconfiguration execution on the Uu interface, with no reference to sidelink (SL) resource pools, SL-ResourceConfig, or SL congestion control parameters.

results.question: Upon receiving a CounterCheck message, what is the UE's mandatory procedural obligation?
results.reference: Upon receiving the CounterCheck message, the UE is obligated to stop using the COUNT values associated with all DRBs and to immediately transmit a CounterCheckResponse message back to the network.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.6, Counter check
results.model_answer: On receiving a CounterCheck message, the UE is obligated (per 3GPP TS 38.331 §5.7.4) to compare, for every DRB currently configured, the COUNT (PDCP hyper‑frame number and sequence number) values indicated in the CounterCheck message with the COUNT values it actually maintains for those DRBs. For any DRB where a mismatch is found, the UE must include that DRB's identity and its own current COUNT value in the CounterCheckResponse message. The UE must then compile and submit the CounterCheckResponse message to lower layers (via SRB1) for transmission back to the network, regardless of whether any mismatches were found (an empty list indicates no mismatches). This procedure is mandatory and cannot be skipped or delayed indefinitely, as it is used by the network to detect potential security breaches (e.g., hyperframe number wrap-around attacks).
results.evidence: TS 38.331 §5.7.4.3 (Reception of the CounterCheck message by the UE): 'The UE shall: 1> for each DRB that is part of the current UE configuration, if the COUNT value associated with the DRB, as included in the CounterCheck message, does not match the COUNT value maintained by the UE for that DRB: 2> include, in the CounterCheckResponse message, the identity of the DRB along with the current COUNT value as maintained by the UE for this DRB; 1> submit the CounterCheckResponse message to lower layers for transmission.'

results.question: What subsequent network action is triggered if a mismatch is identified from the CounterCheckResponse, and why is this important?
results.reference: If a mismatch in PDCP COUNT values is identified, the network initiates a radio link failure procedure. This is important to maintain data integrity, prevent potential data loss or corruption, and re-establish a synchronized radio link.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.6, Counter check
results.model_answer: If the eNB/gNB detects a mismatch between the PDCP COUNT values it sent in CounterCheck and the values reported back by the UE in CounterCheckResponse, this indicates a potential security breach (e.g., packet insertion/replay by an intruder, or a radio bearer being hijacked). The network's action upon detecting such a mismatch is to trigger release of the RRC connection (i.e., initiate an RRC connection release, or in some implementations trigger re-establishment/handover), and it may also initiate other security procedures such as informing higher layers/O&M for further investigation. This is important because the CounterCheck procedure exists specifically to verify that the amount of data sent/received on each radio bearer matches between UE and network, ensuring PDCP COUNT integrity. A mismatch means the SN/HFN counters have diverged beyond what normal operation would cause, which is a strong indicator of a security attack (e.g., a man-in-the-middle inserting or deleting packets) rather than a benign fault. Taking action (releasing the connection) prevents continued exploitation of the compromised bearer and protects user data confidentiality/integrity, forcing re-establishment of security context via a fresh RRC connection.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, Section 5.3.13 (Counter Check): 'The purpose of this procedure is to assist the recovery from a potential AS security breach... If the network receives a CounterCheckResponse message with a count value that is different from that included in the CounterCheck message and considers this as evidence of a security breach, the network may release the RRC connection or take other actions.'

results.question: How does the UE determine when to initiate a measurement report for Event A4?
results.reference: The UE initiates a measurement report for Event A4 when the measurement result of a neighbouring cell becomes better than a configured threshold. This evaluation uses the entering condition formula Mn + Ofn + Ocn - Hys > Thresh, where the result must remain satisfied for at least Time To Trigger to trigger reporting.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.4.5, Event A4 (Neighbour becomes better than threshold)
results.model_answer: For Event A4 (neighbour cell becomes better than an absolute threshold), the UE continuously evaluates the entering condition A4-1 using L3-filtered RSRP/RSRQ/SINR measurements of the neighbour cell, including any configured offsets (Ofn, Ocn) and hysteresis (Hys): Mn + Ofn + Ocn – Hys > Thresh. When this condition remains true for the entire duration specified by the configured Time-to-Trigger (TTT) for the associated reportConfig, the UE triggers and sends a measurement report for that neighbour cell. If the condition A4-2 (leaving condition: Mn + Ofn + Ocn + Hys < Thresh) becomes true before the TTT expires, the event is cancelled. The measurement report continues to be sent periodically or once, depending on the reportType (event-triggered) configuration, until the leaving condition is satisfied, subject to reportAmount and reportInterval settings.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.5.4.6 (Event A4: Neighbour becomes better than absolute threshold): 'Inequality A4-1 (Entering condition): Mn + Ofn + Ocn – Hys > Thresh; Inequality A4-2 (Leaving condition): Mn + Ofn + Ocn + Hys < Thresh', where the entering condition must be satisfied during the time-to-trigger before the UE sends the corresponding MeasurementReport.

results.question: How do the offset values Ofn and Ocn influence the triggering of Event A4?
results.reference: The offsets Ofn (frequency-specific offset) and Ocn (cell-specific offset) are added to the measured result Mn of the neighbour cell. They effectively adjust the measured value upward before comparison with the threshold, making the triggering condition Mn + Ofn + Ocn - Hys > Thresh easier or harder to meet based on their configured values.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.4.5, Event A4 (Neighbour becomes better than threshold)
results.model_answer: Event A4 (neighbour becomes better than an absolute threshold) is evaluated after adding two configurable offsets to the raw neighbour measurement Mn. Ofn is the frequency-specific offset (offsetFreq in the measObjectNR of the neighbour's carrier) and Ocn is the cell-specific offset (cellIndividualOffset for that neighbour cell, 0 if not configured). Both are added to Mn before comparing against the threshold and hysteresis. Thus, increasing Ofn or Ocn makes it easier for the entering condition (Mn+Ofn+Ocn-Hys > Thresh) to be satisfied, triggering A4 earlier/for weaker cells, while negative offsets delay or suppress triggering. They let the network bias measurement reports per-frequency (Ofn) or per-cell (Ocn) without changing the actual threshold, effectively shifting the decision boundary for individual neighbours or frequency layers.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, Section 5.5.4.6 (Event A4): Entering condition: Mn + Ofn + Ocn – Hys > Thresh; Leaving condition: Mn + Ofn + Ocn + Hys < Thresh, where Ofn is the frequency specific offset of the frequency of the neighbour cell (i.e. offsetFreq as defined within measObjectNR corresponding to the frequency of the neighbour cell), and Ocn is the cell specific offset of the neighbour cell (i.e. cellIndividualOffset as defined within measObjectNR corresponding to the frequency of the neighbour cell), and set to zero if not configured for the neighbour cell.

results.question: How does the UE determine when to initiate a measurement report for Event A6?
results.reference: The UE initiates a measurement report when the neighbour cell's measurement quantity becomes offset better than the measurement quantity of a configured SCell, as defined by the entering condition Mn + Ocn - Hys > Ms + Ocs + Off.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.4.7, Event A6 (Neighbour becomes offset better than SCell)
results.model_answer: The UE evaluates Event A6 (Neighbour becomes offset better than SCell) continuously using the entering condition A6-1: Mn + Ocn – Hys > Ms + Ocs + Off, and the leaving condition A6-2: Mn + Ocn + Hys < Ms + Ocs + Off, where Mn is the measured RSRP/RSRQ/RSSI of the neighbour cell, Ocn is the neighbour-specific offset, Ms is the measured value of the SCell, Ocs is the SCell-specific offset, Off is the event-specific offset parameter (a6-Offset), and Hys is the hysteresis parameter for this event. All measurement quantities are filtered per the configured L3 filtering. The entering condition must remain true continuously for the duration of the configured TimeToTrigger timer (associated with the corresponding measId) before the UE triggers a MeasurementReport for that neighbour cell; if reportOnLeave is configured, a report is also triggered when the leaving condition A6-2 is satisfied continuously for TimeToTrigger. The UE applies this evaluation per neighbour cell relative to the SCell used for comparison, using the measurement objects and reporting configuration linked via the reportConfig for the SCG (i.e., configured in the reportConfigNR with eventA6 in reportConfigId associated with the SCell measurement).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.5.4.6 'Event A6 (Neighbour becomes offset better than SCell)': 'The UE shall consider the entering condition for this event to be satisfied when condition A6-1, as specified below, is fulfilled and the leaving condition to be satisfied when condition A6-2, as specified below, is fulfilled... Inequality A6-1 (Entering condition) Mn + Ocn – Hys > Ms + Ocs + Off ... Inequality A6-2 (Leaving condition) Mn + Ocn + Hys < Ms + Ocs + Off.'

results.question: Why is the offset parameter 'Off' included in the Event A6 entering condition alongside the cell-specific offsets?
results.reference: The offset 'Off' is added to the SCell's offset measurement (Ms + Ocs) to provide an additional configurable threshold that the neighbour must exceed, allowing network-controlled adjustment of the reporting sensitivity for this event.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.4.7, Event A6 (Neighbour becomes offset better than SCell)
results.model_answer: In Event A6 (defined in TS 38.331 §5.5.4.7), the entering condition is Mn + Ocn – Hys > Ms + Ocs + Off, where Mn/Ms are the measured neighbour/serving (SCell) quantities and Ocn/Ocs are cell-specific offsets. The 'Off' parameter is a separate, event-specific offset (a6-Offset) configured independently of the cell-specific offsets. It allows the network to add an extra, frequency- and cell-independent margin to the comparison, giving finer control over when the neighbour cell is considered sufficiently better than the serving SCell to trigger a measurement report. This decouples the event sensitivity (network-tunable via Off) from the individual cell bias adjustments (Ocn, Ocs), enabling flexible tuning of handover/SCell change triggering without altering the per-cell offsets used for other events.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, Section 5.5.4.7 (Event A6): 'The UE shall consider the entering condition for this event to be satisfied when condition A6-1, as specified below, is fulfilled... Mn + Ocn – Hys > Ms + Ocs + Off ... Off is the offset parameter for this event (i.e. a6-Offset as defined within reportConfigNR for this event).'

results.question: Why is the RRC layer involved in the sidelink discovery procedure for announcement and monitoring?
results.reference: The RRC layer is responsible for configuring the parameters and resource pools used for both transmitting (announcement) and receiving (monitoring) sidelink discovery messages, as it handles the relevant configurations provided by pre-configuration, system information, or dedicated signaling.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.13, NR sidelink discovery
results.model_answer: RRC is involved in the sidelink (SL) discovery procedure because the actual discovery announcement and monitoring functions are performed by the higher (V2X/ProSe application) layer, but they rely on radio resources, timers and configuration parameters that only RRC can provide and control. RRC broadcasts (via SIB) or dedicately configures (via RRCReconfiguration) the SL discovery resource pools, periodicities, and transmission parameters that the UE uses to send (announce) and receive (monitor) discovery messages. RRC also manages the UE's RRC state, mobility, and coordinates resource allocation between discovery and other sidelink communication to avoid conflicts, and it reports SL related assistance information (e.g., via SidelinkUEInformationNR) to the network. Thus RRC is the control-plane entity that authorizes, configures, and maintains the physical/MAC-layer resources needed for the discovery procedure, even though the discovery message content and logic belong to the upper (ProSe) layer.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, clause 5.8.9 (Sidelink discovery) – 'The RRC layer provides the configuration of the resource pools and parameters used by upper layers for transmission and reception of SL discovery messages, in accordance with the sidelink discovery resource pool configuration broadcast in SIB or provided via dedicated signalling.'

results.question: How does a UE acquire the configuration necessary to monitor for sidelink discovery messages from other UEs?
results.reference: The UE acquires the monitoring configuration through RRC, which obtains it either from pre-configuration, system information broadcast, or dedicated signaling, specifying the resource pools to monitor for discovery messages.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.13, NR sidelink discovery
results.model_answer: The UE does not derive sidelink (SL) discovery monitoring parameters on its own; it receives them from the network (or from pre-configuration) through one of three RRC mechanisms defined in TS 38.331: (1) System Information – when in coverage, the gNB broadcasts SL discovery parameters (e.g., discovery resource pool, monitoring periodicity, RSRP thresholds) in SIB12 via the SL-DiscConfigCommon IE; (2) Dedicated signalling – in RRC_CONNECTED the network can (re)configure the UE with UE-specific discovery reception parameters using RRCReconfiguration, which carries sl-ConfigDedicatedNR containing an SL-DiscConfig IE; and (3) Pre-configuration – when the UE is out of coverage (or SIB12 is absent), it uses locally stored SL-Preconfiguration data (sl-PreconfigDiscConfig) that mirrors the SIB12 structure. In all cases the configuration specifies the discovery resource pool(s), monitoring occasions, and associated thresholds the UE must use to decode discovery messages transmitted by other UEs, following the sidelink discovery procedures in clause 5.8.9a.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.8.9a (Sidelink discovery), read together with clause 5.2.2 (System Information acquisition, SIB12) and the SL-DiscConfigCommon / SL-DiscConfig / SL-Preconfiguration IE definitions in clause 6.3.

results.question: What conditions must be met for a UE to trigger Event Y1 according to the specified clause?
results.reference: Event Y1 is triggered when the PCell becomes worse than threshold1 and a candidate L2 U2N relay UE becomes better than threshold2.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.4.19, Event Y1 (PCell becomes worse than threshold1 and candidate L2 U2N
results.model_answer: Event Y1 (used by a Remote UE that is connected via a Sidelink UE‑to‑Network Relay to decide whether to search for/switch to another relay or to direct NR connection) is triggered when the quality of the UE's direct (Uu) link to the network becomes worse than a configured threshold, taking hysteresis into account, and this condition persists for the configured TimeToTrigger. Specifically: Entering condition (Y1‑1): Ms – Hys < Thresh1, sustained for TimeToTrigger. Leaving condition (Y1‑2): Ms + Hys > Thresh1. Where: Ms is the measured result of the direct path (e.g., RSRP/RSRQ/SINR of the serving cell) used for event evaluation, not taking into account any offsets; Hys is the hysteresis parameter configured for event Y1 (hysteresisY1); Thresh1 is the threshold parameter configured for event Y1 (thresholdY1). The measurements are performed and evaluated per the applicable measurement quantity configured in the associated reportConfig, and the UE only evaluates this event while it has a direct path measurement available (e.g., in RRC_CONNECTED with an active or measurable serving cell) and relay-related measurement configuration is provided.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.5.4.34 'Event Y1 (Quality of direct path becomes worse than a threshold)' – Entering condition: Ms – Hys < Thresh1; Leaving condition: Ms + Hys > Thresh1, evaluated for TimeToTrigger.

results.question: How does the specification define the relationship between PCell quality and the candidate relay UE for Event Y1?
results.reference: The event requires two concurrent conditions: the PCell signal quality falls below a configured threshold (threshold1) while the signal quality of a candidate Layer 2 UE-to-Network relay rises above a different configured threshold (threshold2).
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.4.19, Event Y1 (PCell becomes worse than threshold1 and candidate L2 U2N
results.model_answer: In TS 38.331, Event Y1 is defined for UE-to-Network Relay (sidelink relay) measurement reporting. It is triggered when the serving PCell's quality (RSRP) becomes worse than a configured threshold (Thresh1) while, at the same time, a candidate relay UE's discovery/reference signal quality (SD-RSRP) becomes better than another configured threshold (Thresh2). This dual condition ensures that reporting for relay selection/reselection occurs only when the direct PCell link is degrading and a viable relay candidate with sufficient sidelink quality is available. The leaving condition is the logical inverse of the entering condition, i.e., PCell quality improves above Thresh1 or the candidate relay UE's quality falls below Thresh2 (with hysteresis applied as per the general event evaluation rules in clause 5.5.4).
results.evidence: TS 38.331, clause 5.5.4 (Measurement report triggering), sub-clause defining 'Event Y1 (PCell becomes worse than a threshold and candidate relay UE becomes better than a threshold)' for UE-to-Network Relay operation.

results.question: What role does the candidate node play in the triggering of Event Y1?
results.reference: The candidate node is specifically a Layer 2 UE-to-Network (L2 U2N) relay UE, and its signal quality must exceed a configured threshold (threshold2) to fulfill one part of the event's dual condition.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.4.19, Event Y1 (PCell becomes worse than threshold1 and candidate L2 U2N
results.model_answer: Event Y1 is one of the measurement/execution‑condition events used in the Conditional Reconfiguration framework (e.g. Conditional Handover / Conditional PSCell Change/Addition). In this framework each candidate cell offered for the conditional mobility procedure belongs to a 'candidate node' (a candidate target gNB or candidate SN) that has been prepared in advance (resources/RRCReconfiguration container allocated via Xn/X2 handover‑preparation signalling) so that it can accept the UE as soon as the condition is met. The candidate node's cell quality is the quantity (Mn) that is evaluated against the Y1 threshold/hysteresis/offset parameters supplied in the condTriggerConfig associated with that candidate. When the measured quality of the candidate node's cell satisfies the Y1 entering condition (and continues to satisfy it, or the corresponding leaving condition no longer holds, depending on configuration), the UE considers the execution condition for that candidate fulfilled and applies the stored RRCReconfiguration that was prepared for/by that candidate node, thereby executing the handover/PSCell change to it. Hence the candidate node's role is twofold: (1) it is the entity being measured/evaluated (its signal quality is the trigger metric for Y1), and (2) it is the node whose pre‑prepared RRCReconfiguration (and radio resources) is applied and to which the UE moves once Y1 fires — i.e., it is the target of the conditional execution triggered by Event Y1, not the node that itself signals or fires the event (that evaluation is done autonomously by the UE based on measurements of the candidate node's cell).
results.evidence: TS 38.331, clause 5.3.5 (Conditional Reconfiguration) / Annex A (Measurement event definitions): 'The UE shall consider the entering condition for event Y1 to be satisfied when condition Y1-1, as specified below, is fulfilled... where Mn is the measurement result of the candidate cell (candidate node), not taking into account any offsets.' Together with clause on Conditional Handover/Conditional PSCell Change describing that each candidate cell is prepared by a candidate node via handover-preparation signalling before the UE evaluates the execution condition.

results.question: Explain the dual-threshold mechanism involved in Event Y1 triggering.
results.reference: Event Y1 uses two separate thresholds: threshold1 for the 'worse than' comparison of the serving PCell, and threshold2 for the 'better than' comparison of the candidate L2 U2N relay UE. The event triggers only when both individual comparisons are satisfied.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.4.19, Event Y1 (PCell becomes worse than threshold1 and candidate L2 U2N
results.model_answer: Event Y1 (defined for NR sidelink UE-to-Network relay measurement reporting, TS 38.331 clause 5.8.x on SL relay events) uses a classic entering/leaving hysteresis structure that effectively creates two boundary values around a single configured threshold, i.e., a dual-threshold mechanism. The UE evaluates two separate inequalities: (1) an ENTERING condition, where the measured sidelink quality (e.g., SL-RSRP of the serving relay) falls below (Thresh – Hys), causing the UE to consider the relay link as degraded and start/continue the time-to-trigger (TTT) timer; and (2) a LEAVING condition, where the measured quantity rises above (Thresh + Hys), causing the UE to cancel the event if it was still pending or to stop treating the condition as satisfied. Because Hys (hysteresis) is added on one side and subtracted on the other side of the single configured Thresh parameter, the effective trigger points become two distinct thresholds: a lower entering threshold (Thresh − Hys) and a higher leaving threshold (Thresh + Hys). This dual-threshold (hysteresis-band) design prevents rapid toggling (ping-pong) of the Y1 event when the relay-link quality fluctuates around the nominal threshold, ensuring that reporting/relay-reselection evaluation is triggered only when the quality change is sustained beyond the hysteresis margin and for the duration of the configured timeToTrigger.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause defining Event Y1 (Quality of the sidelink relay link becomes worse than a threshold): entering condition Y1-1: Mrelay + Hys < Thresh; leaving condition Y1-2: Mrelay − Hys > Thresh, where Mrelay is the measured SL-RSRP/RSRQ of the relay link, Hys is the hysteresis parameter, and Thresh is the configured threshold for event Y1.

results.question: What information does the UE include in the plmn-IdentityList field of the VarRLF-Report, and what is the source of this list?
results.reference: The UE sets the plmn-IdentityList to include the list of Equivalent PLMNs (EPLMNs) stored by the UE. This list includes the Registered PLMN (RPLMN).
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.10.5, RLF report content determination
results.model_answer: The plmn-IdentityList field in the VarRLF-Report stores the list of PLMN identities that were treated as equivalent PLMNs by the UE at the time the radio link failure (RLF) or connection failure occurred. This list is not generated by the UE itself but is derived from the 'equivalent PLMN list' that the UE received and stored from the network via NAS signalling (e.g., during registration/attach procedures), reflecting the PLMNs the UE considered equivalent to its registered PLMN (RPLMN) at the moment of failure. The UE simply copies this stored equivalent PLMN list into the VarRLF-Report so that it can later be included in the RLF-Report sent to the network for failure analysis.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, VarRLF-Report field description: 'plmn-IdentityList This field contains the list of equivalent PLMNs, as stored by the UE, at the time the connection failure or radio link failure is detected.'

results.question: How does the UE determine the content for the measResultLastServCell field in the VarRLF-Report, and what time period do the measurements cover?
results.reference: The UE sets measResultLastServCell to include the cell level RSRP, RSRQ, and available SINR of the source PCell (for handover failure) or PCell (for RLF). These measurements are based on the available SSB and CSI-RS measurements collected up to the moment the UE detected the failure.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.10.5, RLF report content determination
results.model_answer: The measResultLastServCell field in the VarRLF-Report is populated by the UE using the most recent (last available) Layer‑3 filtered measurement results for the PCell that RRC has received from the lower layers at the moment the failure (radio link failure, handover failure, or connection failure) is detected. The UE does not perform a new measurement for this purpose; it simply records the RSRP and RSRQ (and, if configured, SINR) values of the serving cell that were already available to RRC just before the failure occurred. Consequently, the 'time period' covered is not a fixed reporting window but corresponds to the instant immediately preceding the failure event – i.e., the last measurement sample available prior to triggering of T310/T312/T304 expiry or RRC re‑establishment, which in practice reflects measurements taken within the last measurement/reporting cycle (typically up to a few hundred milliseconds, governed by the L3 filtering and measurement reporting periodicity configured for the PCell).
results.evidence: TS 38.331, clause 5.3.10.5 'Actions related to RLF report': 'The UE shall set the measResultLastServCell to include the RSRP and RSRQ, based on the last measurement results available at the UE, taken before the connection/radio link failure or the handover failure occurred.'

results.question: Upon T331 expiry or stop, what does the UE release according to the specified procedure?
results.reference: The UE releases the VarMeasIdleConfig.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.8.3, T331 expiry or stop
results.model_answer: T331 governs the validity of the UE's Conditional Reconfiguration (used for Conditional Handover (CHO) and Conditional PSCell Change/Addition (CPC/CPA)). While T331 is running, the UE evaluates the execution conditions of the candidate cell(s) stored in VarConditionalReconfig. When T331 expires or is stopped (e.g., due to reception of a new RRCReconfiguration removing the conditional configuration, or successful execution of a conditional reconfiguration), the UE releases: (1) the VarConditionalReconfig entries (the stored candidate condRRCReconfig configurations) associated with the condReconfigId(s); (2) any measurement configuration (measId, reportConfig, measObject) that were configured solely for evaluating the conditional reconfiguration execution conditions; and (3) it stops evaluating the associated execution conditions for the affected candidate cell(s). Essentially, the UE tears down all state related to the conditional reconfiguration that was tied to the timer.
