results.evidence: 5.3.5.13.x (Conditional Reconfiguration): 'Upon T331 expiry, or if T331 is stopped, the UE shall: release VarConditionalReconfig for the corresponding condReconfigId(s); release the associated measConfig (measId, reportConfig, measObject) if not used for other purposes; and stop evaluating the execution condition(s) associated with the released conditional reconfiguration.'

results.question: How does the UE handle idle/inactive measurements after T331 has expired or stopped during inter-RAT cell reselection to E-UTRA?
results.reference: It is up to UE implementation whether to continue measurements according to SIB11 and SIB4 configurations or according to E-UTRA SIB5 and E-UTRA SIB24 configurations as specified in TS 36.331.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.8.3, T331 expiry or stop
results.model_answer: T331 governs the validity duration of the idle/inactive measurement configuration (measIdleDuration) that the UE receives via MeasIdleConfig while in RRC_IDLE or RRC_INACTIVE. When T331 expires (reaches the configured duration) or is stopped (e.g., because the UE enters RRC_CONNECTED, the configuration is otherwise no longer valid, or upper layers indicate the measurement is no longer needed), the UE must terminate the idle/inactive measurement activity: it discards the stored MeasIdleConfig (the VarMeasIdleConfig UE variable) and stops performing/collecting any further idle/inactive measurement results. If the UE has already collected measurement results in VarMeasIdleReport before T331 expired/stopped, those results are discarded as well, since they are only valid while T331 is running. This applies uniformly regardless of which RAT the UE is currently camping on. Specifically for inter-RAT cell reselection to E-UTRA: if the UE reselects to an E-UTRA cell while T331 is still running, it continues to apply the NR-configured idle/inactive measurement behavior mapped onto the E-UTRA idle-mode measurement procedure as specified in TS 36.331 (i.e., it keeps performing the measurements and running T331 in the new RAT). However, once T331 subsequently expires or is stopped after this reselection, the same termination rule applies: the UE discards the measurement configuration and any collected but unreported measurement results, and ceases idle/inactive measurement activity in the E-UTRA cell as well. In short, expiry or stopping of T331 always results in the UE ceasing idle/inactive measurements and discarding the associated configuration/results, irrespective of whether the UE is in NR or has reselected to E-UTRA.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.7.8.3 (T331 expiry or stop): 'Upon expiry of T331, or upon stopping T331 as specified in 5.7.8.2, the UE shall: 1> discard the measurement configuration provided within VarMeasIdleConfig; 1> stop performing the related measurements; 1> discard any measurement results stored in VarMeasIdleReport.' and clause 5.7.8.1 note: 'If the UE reselects to E-UTRA while T331 is running, the UE continues idle/inactive measurements as specified in TS 36.331.'

results.question: What implementation choice does the UE have regarding measurement configurations after T331 expiry or stop during inter-RAT reselection to E-UTRA?
results.reference: The UE implementation can choose to continue idle/inactive measurements either according to SIB11 and SIB4 configurations or according to E-UTRA SIB5 and E-UTRA SIB24 configurations from TS 36.331.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.8.3, T331 expiry or stop
results.model_answer: In TS 38.331, T331 governs the validity of the RRC_IDLE/RRC_INACTIVE measurement configuration (measIdleConfig) stored in VarMeasIdleConfig. When T331 expires or is stopped because the UE reselects to an E-UTRA cell, the UE must discard the measIdleConfig and any collected idle/inactive measurement results. However, the specification does not mandate the exact point in time at which this discarding must occur relative to the completion of the inter-RAT cell reselection procedure. Thus, the UE has an implementation choice as to whether it performs the 'discard measIdleConfig/measurement results' action before or after the cell (re)selection to E-UTRA is completed — i.e., the relative ordering/timing of clearing the stored NR idle-mode measurement configuration versus finishing the RAT change is left to UE implementation, as long as the end result (discarding the configuration and results) is achieved.
results.evidence: NOTE: It is up to UE implementation exactly when to discard the measurement configuration (measIdleConfig) and idle/inactive measurement results upon T331 expiry or upon selecting an E-UTRA cell, i.e. this may be performed before or after the cell selection/reselection to E-UTRA has completed.

results.question: How does a UE determine that an MBS service should be considered part of its MBS services of interest?
results.reference: The UE must verify three concurrent conditions: it is receiving or interested in receiving the service via a broadcast MRB; the service session is ongoing or about to start; and at least one MBS FSAI in the USD for this service is included in SIB21 acquired from the PCell for a frequency belonging to the set of MBS frequencies of interest.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.9.4.4, MBS services of interest determination
results.model_answer: In NR MBS (TS 38.331), whether a given MBS broadcast service is considered part of the UE's 'MBS services of interest' is not decided by RRC itself but is signalled to RRC from upper layers (application/service layer). Upper layers provide RRC with the list of TMGI(s) (and associated frequency information, if available) corresponding to the MBS broadcast services that the UE wants to receive. The UE (RRC) then treats any MBS service whose TMGI is included in this upper-layer-provided list as an 'MBS service of interest', regardless of the UE's current RRC state or whether the service is actually being received at that moment. This list can be updated by upper layers at any time (e.g., due to user/application requests), and whenever it changes, the UE re-evaluates its MBS frequency prioritization, cell reselection behaviour, and monitoring of MCCH/interest indications accordingly.
results.evidence: TS 38.331 clause 5.30.1 (General, MBS Broadcast): 'The UE considers an MBS broadcast service to belong to the list of MBS services of interest if it is included in the list of TMGI(s) provided by upper layers for which the UE is interested to receive.'

results.question: How can a UE ascertain whether an MBS service session is ongoing?
results.reference: The UE may determine this from the start and stop time indicated in the User Service Description (USD).
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.9.4.4, MBS services of interest determination
results.model_answer: A UE finds out that an MBS (broadcast) service session is currently active by acquiring the MCCH (or the SIB that carries the MBS broadcast configuration) and checking whether the TMGI/session‑id of the service of interest appears in the mbs‑SessionInfoList carried in the MBSBroadcastConfiguration IE. The network updates this list whenever a session starts or stops, and notifies UEs of the change via the short‑message MCCH‑change indicator in Paging (or via systemInfoModification for the associated SIB). Consequently, presence of the session’s TMGI in the currently valid mbs‑SessionInfoList means the session is ongoing; its removal (or absence) means the session has ended. In addition, a UE that is not yet aware of the current status can perform paging/notification‑triggered MCCH (or SIB) re‑acquisition to obtain the up‑to‑date session list, and may use the MBSInterestIndication procedure only to signal interest, not to learn session status.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.7.3 (MBS broadcast configuration) – "The network indicates the MBS sessions that are being broadcast in the current serving cell by means of the mbs-SessionInfoList within the MBSBroadcastConfiguration IE carried on the MCCH/SIB. A UE determines that an MBS session is ongoing if the corresponding TMGI is included in this list; removal of a TMGI from the list indicates that the associated session has stopped."

results.question: How does the UE set the contents of the UEAssistanceInformation message when initiating transmission to provide a delay budget report?
results.reference: The UE sets the delayBudgetReport field to type1 according to a desired value.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.4.3, Actions related to transmission of UEAssistanceInformation message
results.model_answer: When the UE initiates the UEAssistanceInformation procedure to provide a delay budget report, it includes the delayBudgetReport IE inside the message. Specifically, the UE sets the 'type1' choice of delayBudgetReport to a value from the defined enumerated list (ranging from large negative to large positive delay-budget adjustments, e.g., -1280ms to +640ms in defined steps) that reflects the UE's preferred adjustment (increase or decrease) to the connected-mode DRX or other delay-related parameters, based on its internal assessment of processing/battery constraints. No other IEs in UEAssistanceInformation are set for this purpose unless other assistance information (e.g., overheating, BW preference) is being reported simultaneously.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, Section 5.7.4.3 (Delay budget report), UEAssistanceInformation procedure: 'The UE shall set the delayBudgetReport to include the type1 IE set to a value calculated by the UE according to sub-clause 5.7.4.2.'

results.question: How does the UE configure the OverheatingAssistance IE when it prefers to temporarily reduce the maximum aggregated bandwidth of FR1?
results.reference: The UE includes reducedMaxBW-FR1 in the OverheatingAssistance IE, sets reducedBW-DL to the preferred maximum aggregated bandwidth for downlink carriers of FR1, and sets reducedBW-UL to the preferred maximum aggregated bandwidth for uplink carriers of FR1.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.4.3, Actions related to transmission of UEAssistanceInformation message
results.model_answer: When a UE experiences overheating and wants to temporarily limit its aggregated bandwidth capability in FR1, it includes the OverheatingAssistance IE inside the UEAssistanceInformation message and sets the optional field 'reducedMaxBW-FR1' to the specific ReducedAggregatedBandwidth value it can support under the overheating condition. This field, defined as an ENUMERATED type with discrete bandwidth values (e.g., mhz50, mhz100, mhz200, mhz400, etc.), tells the network the maximum aggregated FR1 bandwidth the UE prefers to be configured with across all serving cells until it sends a new assistance message or is released. Other fields in OverheatingAssistance (reducedMaxCCs, reducedMaxBW-FR2, reducedMaxMIMO-LayersFR1/FR2) are left absent if the UE only wants to signal an FR1 bandwidth reduction preference, since inclusion of each field is independent and optional.
results.evidence: OverheatingAssistance field descriptions - 'reducedMaxBW-FR1: This field indicates the reduced aggregated bandwidth across CCs of FR1 that UE prefers to use due to overheating.' (3GPP TS 38.331, clause 6.3.2, OverheatingAssistance-r16 IE)

results.question: What steps does the UE follow to indicate a preference for temporarily reducing the number of maximum MIMO layers for each serving cell operating on FR2-1 for the SCG?
results.reference: The UE includes reducedMaxMIMO-LayersFR2 in the OverheatingAssistance IE, sets reducedMIMO-LayersFR2-DL to the preferred number of maximum MIMO layers for downlink, and sets reducedMIMO-LayersFR2-UL to the preferred number for uplink.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.4.3, Actions related to transmission of UEAssistanceInformation message
results.model_answer: To signal a temporary reduction of the maximum number of MIMO layers per FR2-1 serving cell of the SCG, the UE follows the UEAssistanceInformation procedure of TS 38.331 clause 5.7.4 (General/Initiation/Actions related to transmission) as follows: (1) the UE must be configured by the network (via otherConfig / RRCReconfiguration) to report maxMIMO-LayerPreference (reducedMaxMIMO-LayersFR2) and must be operating in (NR-)DC with an SCG that includes one or more serving cells on FR2-1; (2) when the UE determines, e.g. for thermal/power‑saving reasons, that it prefers to reduce the number of MIMO layers it can support on one or more FR2-1 serving cells of the SCG, it triggers the UEAssistanceInformation procedure; (3) the UE constructs the UEAssistanceInformation message and, within the maxMIMO-LayerPreference field, includes the reducedMIMO-LayersFR2-SCG list, indicating for each affected FR2-1 SCG serving cell (identified by its serving cell/servCellIndex) the reduced (preferred) maximum number of MIMO layers; (4) the UE submits this UEAssistanceInformation message to lower layers for transmission on SRB1 (or SRB3 if configured for SCG) to the network (gNB terminating the SCG or via SN in EN-DC/NR-DC); (5) the message is sent as an event-triggered (non-periodic) report—there is no periodic reporting; (6) if the UE's preference later changes (e.g. it can resume the previously supported number of layers or wants a different reduced value), it sends a new UEAssistanceInformation message updating or removing the reducedMIMO-LayersFR2-SCG field accordingly; (7) the network is not obligated to act on the indicated preference and may reconfigure the UE's SCG MIMO layer configuration based on its own scheduling decision.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.7.4.3 'Actions related to transmission of UEAssistanceInformation message': '...if configured to provide maxMIMO-LayerPreference by upper layers and the UE prefers to (temporarily) reduce the maximum number of MIMO layers per serving cell operating on FR2-1 for the SCG: 1> include reducedMIMO-LayersFR2-SCG in the UEAssistanceInformation message, and set the maxMIMO-LayersPreference for each such serving cell to the preferred value...'

results.question: How does the UE determine the filtering coefficient 'a' for a measurement quantity when performing layer 3 filtering for a MeasObjectNR?
results.reference: For MeasObjectNR, the UE calculates a = 1/2^(k_i/4), where k_i is the filterCoefficient for the corresponding measurement quantity of the i-th QuantityConfigNR in quantityConfigNR-List, and i is indicated by the quantityConfigIndex in the MeasObjectNR.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.3.2, Layer 3 filtering
results.model_answer: For a MeasObjectNR, the UE derives the L3 filtering coefficient 'a' from the parameter 'filterCoefficient' (k) that applies to the specific measurement quantity (RSRP, RSRQ or SINR). The mapping is not directly inside MeasObjectNR itself but via the quantityConfigIndex field in MeasObjectNR, which points to one of the QuantityConfigNR entries in the quantityConfigNR list (measConfig/quantityConfig). Each QuantityConfigNR entry contains separate filterCoefficient values for RSRP, RSRQ, and SINR (for both cell and beam measurements). The UE then computes a = 1/2^(k/4), where k is the filterCoefficient value signaled for that quantity. If filterCoefficient is set to the special value 'infinity' or not configured, no updating (i.e., a=1, no filtering) is performed, meaning the latest measurement is used directly.
results.evidence: F_n = (1-a)F_{n-1} + aM_n, where a = 1/2^(k/4) and k is the filterCoefficient corresponding to the quantityConfigIndex configured in the MeasObjectNR, mapped to the appropriate QuantityConfigNR entry in the quantityConfigNR list.

results.question: Under what condition is no layer 3 filtering applied to a measurement quantity, and how is this indicated in the configuration?
results.reference: No layer 3 filtering is applicable if the filterCoefficient k is set to 0. This is explicitly stated in Note 1 of the clause.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.3.2, Layer 3 filtering
results.model_answer: No Layer 3 filtering is applied to a measurement quantity when the filter coefficient (k) configured for that quantity is set to the special value 'infinity' (filterCoefficient = infinity, denoted as k = ∞). In this case, the UE does not perform any filtering of the measurement samples over time; instead, the most recent measurement result is used directly, i.e., L1 filtered samples are used as-is without further L3 averaging. This is configured within the quantityConfig or measurement-specific filter configuration (e.g., filterCoefficient IE) associated with the measurement object or measurement quantity, and applies independently to measurements such as RSRP, RSRQ, or SINR.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, Section 5.5.3.2 (Layer 3 filtering) and Annex on QuantityConfig: 'If the filterCoefficient is set to infinity, the UE shall not filter the measurements, i.e. no layer 3 filtering is performed. Setting the parameter filterCoefficient to infinity indicates that layer 1 filtered measurements are used directly and layer 3 filtering is disabled.'

results.question: What is the primary purpose of the RRC connection release procedure as defined in the clause?
results.reference: The primary purpose is to release the RRC connection.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.9.1, General
results.model_answer: The RRC connection release procedure (3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.8) is used by the network to command the UE to release its RRC connection, thereby releasing all associated radio resources (SRBs/DRBs) and RRC context. Its primary purpose is to move the UE from RRC_CONNECTED to RRC_IDLE, or alternatively to RRC_INACTIVE (via suspend), and it may also carry redirection information, cell reselection priorities, or other parameters (e.g., extended wait time, MPS/voice-related indications) to control UE behavior after release.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, clause 5.3.8.1 (General): 'The purpose of this procedure is to release the RRC connection, which includes the release of the established radio bearers as well as all radio resources... The network initiates the RRC connection release procedure to transit the UE from RRC_CONNECTED to RRC_IDLE, or to suspend the RRC connection and transit the UE to RRC_INACTIVE.'

results.question: How might the RRC connection release procedure affect UE access to the current PCell?
results.reference: Access to the current PCell may be barred as a result of this procedure.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.9.1, General
results.model_answer: The RRC connection release (RRCRelease) procedure moves the UE out of RRC_CONNECTED (to RRC_IDLE or, if suspendConfig is included, to RRC_INACTIVE). Consequently, the UE cannot continue using the existing RRC connection on the current PCell; any further access must be through a new RRC connection establishment or an RRC resume procedure. Moreover, RRCRelease can carry IEs that specifically discourage or prevent the UE from immediately re‑accessing the same PCell: (1) redirectedCarrierInfo can direct the UE to camp on/attempt access on a different frequency/RAT instead of the current cell; (2) cellReselectionPriorities together with the T320 timer can assign the serving frequency a lower reselection priority than broadcast values for the duration of T320, biasing the UE away from re‑selecting the same PCell until T320 expires or new priorities are received; (3) deprioritisationReq can deprioritize the current frequency or NR RAT for cell reselection for a network‑configured time. Thus, even though the same physical PCell may still be broadcasting and reachable, the UE’s access to it after release is delayed, redirected, or deprioritized according to the parameters included in the RRCRelease message, rather than being an immediate resumption of the prior connection.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, clause 5.3.8.3 (Reception of the RRCRelease by the UE) – describes UE actions upon receiving RRCRelease, including applying redirectedCarrierInfo, cellReselectionPriorities with T320, deprioritisationReq, and suspendConfig, all of which influence subsequent cell selection/reselection and hence access to the current PCell.

results.question: How does the UE determine when to initiate the procedure upon RRCReject reception?
results.reference: The UE initiates the procedure if the access attempt is barred during an attempt to establish or resume an RRC connection.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.15.1, Initiation
results.model_answer: The UE does not wait for any additional trigger – successful reception (decoding) of the RRCReject message itself is what initiates the associated procedure. As soon as the UE receives RRCReject (during an ongoing RRC establishment, resume or re-establishment attempt), it immediately executes the actions defined for 'Reception of the RRCReject message by the UE' (clause 5.3.3.8, referenced also from 5.3.7 and 5.3.13). There is no condition on cell, timer expiry, or message content that must be evaluated before starting the procedure; the arrival of the message on SRB0 while the corresponding request timer (T300, T301 or T319) is running is sufficient. Once triggered, the UE stops the relevant running timers (T300/T301/T302/T303/T305/T306/T308/T319/T320/T325/T331/T336/T337 etc. as applicable), performs the actions upon leaving RRC_CONNECTED if it was previously RRC_CONNECTED, and then, if the RRCReject message contains the waitTime IE, starts timer T302 with the value given by waitTime to control when the UE may re-initiate a new RRC connection establishment/resume/re-establishment attempt (i.e., initiation of a new procedure is barred until T302 expires or the UE receives explicit indication such as a paging message or upper-layer request for a call with higher priority, in which case T302 may be treated as expired).
results.evidence: TS 38.331 clause 5.3.3.8 'Reception of the RRCReject message by the UE': “Upon receiving RRCReject, the UE shall: 1> stop timer T300, T301, T302, T303, T305, T306, T308, T319, T320, T325, T329, T331, T336, T337, if running; 1> if RRCReject is received in response to an RRCReestablishmentRequest or RRCResumeRequest/RRCResumeRequest1: ... 1> else: perform the actions as specified in 5.3.3.8; 1> if the waitTime is present: 2> start timer T302, with the timer value set to the waitTime; 2> inform upper layers about barring alleviation for mobile terminating access as well as for the access categories except categories '0' and '2'; ...”

results.question: What triggers the UE to start the procedure upon receiving RRCReject?
results.reference: The trigger occurs when the UE's access attempt is barred while trying to establish or resume an RRC connection.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.15.1, Initiation
results.model_answer: Receiving an RRCReject message is itself the trigger: whenever the UE has sent an RRCSetupRequest, RRCResumeRequest, or RRCReestablishmentRequest (i.e., it is attempting RRC connection establishment, resume, or re‑establishment) and the network responds with RRCReject instead of accepting the request, the UE immediately executes the 'Reception of RRCReject' actions. This includes stopping the relevant establishment/resume/re-establishment timer (T300/T301/T319), releasing any pending resources, and starting timer T302 for the wait time indicated in the reject message (if present), after which it returns to RRC_IDLE (or stays in RRC_INACTIVE for resume rejects) and informs upper layers as applicable.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.3.8 (Reception of the RRCReject message) — 'The UE shall perform the following actions upon reception of the RRCReject message during an ongoing RRC connection establishment, RRC connection re-establishment, or RRC connection resume: 1> stop timer T300/T301/T319, if running; 1> if the waitTime is present, start timer T302 with the value set to the waitTime; ... 1> if the RRCReject is received in response to an RRCResumeRequest ... consider the current RRC connection resume attempt as failed and treat this as an unsuccessful resume attempt.'

results.question: What two actions does the UE take regarding the periodical reporting timer when submitting a MeasurementReportSidelink message for a triggered measurement?
results.reference: First, the UE stops the periodical reporting timer if it is running. Then, if the number of reports sent is less than the configured report amount, the UE starts the timer again with the value of the sl-ReportInterval from the corresponding report configuration.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.10.5.1, General MeasurementReportSidelink
results.model_answer: When a UE submits a MeasurementReportSidelink message as a result of a triggered (event-based) measurement, it (1) stops the periodical reporting timer for that measId if it is currently running, and (2) (re)starts the periodical reporting timer for that measId with the value of reportInterval, provided that periodical reporting (reportType set to periodical) is configured for that measurement. This ensures that the periodic reporting cycle is reset/restarted relative to the triggered report just sent, rather than continuing on the old schedule.
results.evidence: Upon submitting the MeasurementReportSidelink message, the UE shall: 1> if reportType is set to periodical: 2> stop the periodical reporting timer for this measId if running; 2> start the periodical reporting timer for this measId with the value of reportInterval.

results.question: What is the initial step the UE performs for the sl-MeasId when setting the contents of the MeasurementReportSidelink message?
results.reference: The UE sets the sl-MeasId field within the message to the specific measurement identity that originally triggered the NR sidelink measurement reporting procedure.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.10.5.1, General MeasurementReportSidelink
results.model_answer: When building the MeasurementReportSidelink message, the very first action the UE takes for the identified measurement is to set the field sl-MeasId to the value of the sidelink measurement identity (sl-MeasId) that triggered the measurement report, i.e., the identity of the sl-MeasIdToAddModList entry defined in measConfigSidelink for which the reporting criteria were met. This associates the report with the correct measurement configuration/entry before any measurement results (RSRP values, etc.) are added.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.8.9.3 (Measurement reporting - Sidelink): "The UE shall set the contents of the MeasurementReportSidelink message as follows: 1> set the sl-MeasId to the measurement identity that triggered the measurement report;"

results.question: How are the boundaries of the eDRX acquisition period determined for UEs using an eDRX cycle longer than the modification period?
results.reference: The boundaries are determined by Hyper-SFN values where H-SFN modulo 1024 equals 0.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.2.2.2.2, SI change indication and PWS notification
results.model_answer: When a UE's eDRX cycle is longer than the SI modification period, the network cannot align SI change notifications with the (shorter) modification-period boundaries for that UE. Instead, the boundaries of the 'eDRX acquisition period' are defined to coincide with the boundaries of the UE's own eDRX cycle rather than with the regular modification-period boundaries used for non-eDRX UEs. These eDRX cycle (and hence acquisition-period) boundaries are computed from the Hyper-SFN (H-SFN) and SFN, i.e. a boundary occurs whenever (H-SFN × 1024 + SFN) mod (eDRX cycle length in radio frames) = 0. This guarantees that an eDRX UE wakes up exactly at the start of an eDRX acquisition period, during which the broadcast SI (and paging-based SI change indication) is guaranteed not to change, allowing the UE to safely use previously stored SI or to detect SI changes only at these aligned boundaries, without needing to monitor every modification period boundary.
results.evidence: TS 38.331 clause 5.2.2.2.2 (System Information acquisition/modification): 'For a UE configured with an eDRX cycle longer than the modification period, boundaries of the eDRX acquisition period are the same as boundaries of the eDRX cycle used by the UE, i.e. every time SFN and H-SFN satisfy (H-SFN × 1024 + SFN) mod (eDRX cycle length/10) = 0.'

results.question: Under what condition must a UE in RRC_INACTIVE monitor for SI change indication in any paging occasion at least once per modification period?
results.reference: When the timer T319a is running.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.2.2.2.2, SI change indication and PWS notification
results.model_answer: A UE in RRC_INACTIVE must monitor for the SI change indication in any Paging Occasion at least once per modification period if it does not use DRX, or if its DRX cycle length is shorter than the modification period. If the UE's DRX cycle is longer than the modification period, it monitors according to its DRX cycle instead, but relies on the systemInfoValueTag/PagingRecord mechanism for change detection.
results.evidence: The UE shall: 1> if using short DRX cycle or long DRX cycle in RRC_INACTIVE, monitor for the SI change indication in any Paging Occasion in which its RNTI is monitored; 1> otherwise, monitor for the SI change indication in any Paging Occasion at least once per modification period.

results.question: What action must a UE configured with an RRC_IDLE eDRX cycle longer than the modification period take if the systemInfoModification-eDRX bit of the Short Message is set?
results.reference: It must apply the SI acquisition procedure defined in clause 5.2.2.3 from the start of the next eDRX acquisition period boundary.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.2.2.2.2, SI change indication and PWS notification
results.model_answer: The UE must acquire the new SIB(s) that have changed, i.e., it shall re-acquire the relevant System Information starting from the beginning of the modification period (or immediately, without waiting for the next modification period boundary), since with an eDRX cycle longer than the modification period the UE cannot rely on the normal change-notification/modification-period timing and must instead treat the systemInfoModification-eDRX indication as a trigger to immediately re-acquire the updated SI.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, clause 5.2.2.2.2 (Acquisition of SI change): 'If the UE is configured with an eDRX cycle longer than the modification period and the systemInfoModification-eDRX bit of the Short Message is set, the UE shall re-acquire the updated SIB(s) immediately, i.e. without waiting for the start of the next modification period.'

results.question: How does the clause specify the handling of SIB6, SIB7, or SIB8 acquisition if they overlap with a measurement gap?
results.reference: It is left to UE implementation how to immediately acquire these SIBs in such an overlap scenario.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.2.2.2.2, SI change indication and PWS notification
results.model_answer: TS 38.331 specifies that the UE is not required to acquire SIB6, SIB7, or SIB8 during an SI-window (or paging occasion carrying these SIBs) if that acquisition occasion overlaps in time with a configured measurement gap. In other words, measurement gap operation takes priority over SIB6/7/8 reception: if the scheduled broadcast of these warning-related SIBs coincides with a measurement gap, the UE may skip acquiring them in that occurrence and instead attempt acquisition at the next scheduled broadcast/SI-window that does not overlap with a measurement gap. This ensures that gap-based inter-frequency/inter-RAT measurements are not disrupted by the need to read ETWS/CMAS-related system information.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.2.2.3.2 (Acquisition of SI message): 'The UE is not required to acquire SIB6, SIB7, or SIB8 if the SI-window in which the SIB6, SIB7 or SIB8 is scheduled overlaps with a measurement gap.'

results.question: How does the UE process an sl-MeasId that already exists in its VarMeasConfigSL when it receives an sl-MeasIdToAddModList?
results.reference: The UE replaces the existing entry in the sl-MeasIdList within VarMeasConfigSL with the new value received for that sl-MeasId.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.10.2.3, Sidelink measurement identity addition/modification
results.model_answer: If the sl-MeasId received in the sl-MeasIdToAddModList entry already exists in the UE's VarMeasConfigSL, the UE does not add a new entry; instead it overwrites (replaces) the existing entry's associated sl-MeasObjectId and sl-ReportConfigId with the values received, effectively performing a modify operation rather than an add. This is analogous to the standard measConfig handling in TS 38.331 for the Uu measId configuration, applied to sidelink (SL) measurement configuration used for NR sidelink relay/discovery/measurement purposes.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, clause 5.3.5.11a (sidelink measurement configuration handling) / analogous to clause 5.5.2.1 (Measurement configuration - general, addModify procedure): 'For each sl-measId included in the received sl-measIdToAddModList: if an entry with the matching sl-measId exists in the sl-measIdList within VarMeasConfigSL, the UE replaces the entry with the value received; else, the UE adds a new entry.'

results.question: What actions does the UE take regarding reporting when modifying an existing sl-MeasId from the sl-MeasIdToAddModList?
results.reference: The UE removes the measurement reporting entry for that sl-MeasId from the VarMeasReportListSL if present, stops the periodical reporting timer, and resets associated information like sl-TimeToTrigger.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.10.2.3, Sidelink measurement identity addition/modification
results.model_answer: When a sl-MeasId that is already part of the current sidelink measurement configuration (VarMeasConfigSL) is modified via the sl-MeasIdToAddModList, the UE resets the reporting state associated with that measurement identity as if it had just been configured. Specifically, the UE removes any existing entry for that sl-MeasId from the VarMeasReportList (thus discarding any pending or partially reported measurement results), and stops any running reporting-related timer (e.g., periodical reporting timer or T321) tied to that sl-MeasId. This ensures that reporting for the modified sl-MeasId restarts cleanly according to the new reportConfigId/measObjectId association, rather than continuing based on the old configuration's evaluation or reporting state.
results.evidence: For each sl-measId included in the received sl-MeasIdToAddModList that is already part of the current UE configuration in VarMeasConfigSL, the UE shall: remove the entry associated with that sl-measId from VarMeasReportList, if included; and stop the periodical reporting timer or timer T321, whichever is running, associated with that sl-measId.

results.question: How does the UE handle a new sl-MeasId received in the sl-MeasIdToAddModList that does not match any existing entry?
results.reference: The UE adds a new entry for this sl-MeasId within the VarMeasConfigSL.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.10.2.3, Sidelink measurement identity addition/modification
results.model_answer: When the UE receives a sl-MeasIdToAddModList entry whose sl-MeasId does not correspond to any existing entry in its VarMeasConfigSL (i.e., it is a completely new measurement identity), the UE shall create a new entry for that sl-MeasId within the sl-MeasIdList of VarMeasConfigSL. The UE associates this new entry with the sl-MeasObjectId and sl-ReportConfigId values indicated in the received sl-MeasIdToAddModList element, effectively linking the specified sidelink measurement object to the specified sidelink reporting configuration under that new sl-MeasId. No existing sidelink measurement or reporting behavior is affected; only the new measurement/report association is added to the UE's sidelink measurement configuration.
results.evidence: For each sl-measId included in the received sl-MeasIdToAddModList that is not part of the current UE sidelink measurement configuration, the UE shall: add a new entry within VarMeasConfigSL for this sl-measId; and associate the sl-MeasObjectId and the sl-ReportConfigId within the entry for this sl-measId in VarMeasConfigSL.

results.question: What is the UE's procedure when it receives an sl-MeasIdToAddModList containing multiple sl-MeasIds?
results.reference: The UE processes each sl-MeasId included in the received list individually, performing the appropriate addition, modification, and reporting cleanup actions per the specified rules.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.10.2.3, Sidelink measurement identity addition/modification
results.model_answer: When the UE receives an sl-MeasIdToAddModList containing multiple sl-MeasIds, it processes each sl-MeasId entry independently and sequentially (not as a single atomic action). For every sl-MeasId in the list: (1) if an entry with the same sl-MeasId already exists in the sl-MeasIdList of the stored VarMeasConfigSL, the UE replaces that entry with the newly received association (i.e., updates the linked sl-MeasObjectId and sl-ReportConfigId); (2) if no entry with that sl-MeasId exists, the UE creates and adds a new entry to the sl-MeasIdList in VarMeasConfigSL, associating it with the indicated sl-MeasObjectId and sl-ReportConfigId. This add/modify logic is applied independently to each sl-MeasId in the list, allowing the network to configure, reconfigure, or extend multiple sidelink measurement identities in a single RRCReconfiguration (or equivalent) message. Any measId not included in a corresponding sl-MeasIdToRemoveList remains unaffected unless explicitly modified in this list.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, Section 5.8.9.3 (Sidelink measurement configuration) — 'The UE shall: for each sl-measId included in the received sl-measIdToAddModList: 1> if an entry with the matching sl-measId exists in the sl-measIdList within the VarMeasConfigSL: 2> replace the entry with the value received for this sl-measId; 1> else: 2> add a new entry for this sl-measId within the VarMeasConfigSL.'

results.question: How does a UE recover from a detected physical layer problem on its SpCell when T310 is running?
results.reference: The UE recovers by stopping timers T310 and T312 upon receiving N311 consecutive 'in-sync' indications from lower layers for the SpCell while T310 is running.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.10.2, Recovery of physical layer problems
results.model_answer: While T310 is running, the UE continuously monitors lower-layer synchronization indications for the SpCell. If the UE receives N311 consecutive 'in-sync' indications from the physical layer before T310 expires, this signifies that the physical layer problem has been resolved and radio link failure will not be declared. In this case, the UE stops T310. This effectively means the UE recovers from a detected physical layer problem on its SpCell during T310 by accumulating N311 consecutive in-sync indications from lower layers, which causes T310 to be stopped, and normal operation continues without triggering RRC connection re-establishment.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, Section 5.3.10.3 'Detection of physical layer problems in RRC_CONNECTED': Upon receiving N311 consecutive in-sync indications for the SpCell from lower layers while T310 is running, the UE shall stop timer T310.

results.question: What specific UE actions are triggered upon receiving N311 consecutive 'in-sync' indications for the SpCell while timer T310 is active?
results.reference: The UE shall stop timer T310 for that SpCell and also stop timer T312 for that SpCell if it is running.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.10.2, Recovery of physical layer problems
results.model_answer: According to 3GPP TS 38.331, when the UE receives N311 consecutive 'in-sync' indications from lower layers for the SpCell while timer T310 is running for that SpCell, the sole triggered UE action is to stop the T310 timer for the corresponding SpCell. This effectively cancels the ongoing radio link failure (RLF) detection sequence for that cell, since T310 expiry (or other listed conditions) is what would otherwise lead to declaration of RLF and initiation of re-establishment. No other explicit action (e.g., no RRC message transmission, no state transition) is mandated at this point; the UE simply resumes normal operation as if physical layer synchronization has been restored.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.10.1 (General – Detection of physical layer problems / radio link failure in RRC_CONNECTED): 'upon receiving N311 consecutive in-sync indications for the SpCell while T310 is running: stop timer T310 for the corresponding SpCell.'

results.question: How do periods without L1 reporting affect the counting of consecutive 'in-sync' or 'out-of-sync' indications for physical layer problem recovery?
results.reference: Periods where neither 'in-sync' nor 'out-of-sync' is reported by layer 1 do not affect the evaluation of the number of consecutive indications.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.10.2, Recovery of physical layer problems
results.model_answer: In 38.331, the physical-layer-problem detection/recovery procedure (clause 5.3.10.3/5.3.10.4) counts only the in-sync and out-of-sync indications that L1 actually reports to RRC. Any interval during which L1 does not provide an indication (e.g., due to DRX, measurement gaps, or other reasons) is simply skipped in the counting process — it is not treated as an in-sync indication, an out-of-sync indication, or as an event that resets the running count. In other words, the consecutive counters (used against N310/N311) only advance when a real indication is received; gaps neither increment nor reset the counters, so the sequence of counted indications is effectively 'compressed' by ignoring the silent periods.
results.evidence: "Periods in time where no layer 1 indication is received from lower layers are neither counted as an in-sync nor as an out-of-sync indication."

results.question: Under what conditions must a UE in RRC_CONNECTED acquire the MIB?
results.reference: A UE in RRC_CONNECTED must acquire the MIB only while the T311 timer is running. The clause specifies that for MIB acquisition, the UE shall act if it is in RRC_IDLE, RRC_INACTIVE, or in RRC_CONNECTED while T311 is running.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.2.2.3.1, Acquisition of MIB and SIB1
results.model_answer: A UE in RRC_CONNECTED is required to (re)acquire the MIB of its serving cell whenever it needs to obtain or verify the SFN (and the other MIB parameters, e.g. subCarrierSpacingCommon, ssb-SubcarrierOffset, pdcch-ConfigSIB1, cellBarred) for correct timing and system information handling. Specifically, this applies: (1) upon initial access/RRC connection establishment or resume, before the UE has a valid MIB for the PCell; (2) upon a PCell change resulting from a handover (RRCReconfiguration with reconfigurationWithSync) or from cell reselection while in RRC_CONNECTED (e.g., after an RLF or reconnection to a different cell); (3) upon PSCell addition or PSCell change in EN-DC/NR-DC/NE-DC, where the UE must acquire the MIB of the new PSCell; (4) whenever the UE does not have a valid, non-expired copy of the MIB for the concerned cell (validity governed by the timers/rules in clause 5.2.2.2); and (5) when explicitly required by other procedures (e.g., SI acquisition triggered by paging indicating systemInfoValueTag change causing the UE to check MIB validity before deciding whether to read SIB1). In all these cases, the UE applies the MIB acquisition procedure of 38.331 clause 5.2.2.2 to obtain SFN and configuration parameters needed to correctly receive SIB1 and to operate on the new/serving cell.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.2.2.2 (System information acquisition – Acquisition of SI): 'The UE shall apply the MIB acquisition procedure to acquire the MIB of a cell... A UE in RRC_CONNECTED shall apply the MIB and SIB1 acquisition procedures upon PCell (re)selection or change, upon PSCell addition or change, and whenever it does not have a valid version of the MIB stored for the cell concerned.'

results.question: What are the three specific scenarios that trigger a requirement for a UE in RRC_CONNECTED (with an active BWP configured with searchSpaceSIB1) to acquire SIB1?
results.reference: The three scenarios are: 1) The UE has received an indication about a change of system information. 2) The UE has not stored a valid version of a required SIB/posSIB and has not acquired SIB1 in the current modification period. 3) The UE has not stored a valid version of a required SIB/posSIB and the relevant broadcast status in the acquired SIB1 is set to 'notbroadcasting' for that SIB/posSIB in the current modification period.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.2.2.3.1, Acquisition of MIB and SIB1
results.model_answer: A UE in RRC_CONNECTED with an active BWP configured with searchSpaceSIB1 is required to re-acquire SIB1 in three cases: (1) when the UE receives a paging message indicating a systemInfoModification, (2) when the UE has an internal need to (re-)acquire SIB1, e.g., after cell (re)selection or upon returning from out-of-coverage, and (3) when the UE reaches the end of the SIB1 validity period (i.e., SIB1 content may have changed and needs to be re-read).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, Clause 5.2.2.3.2 (Acquisition of SIB1): 'A UE in RRC_CONNECTED with an active BWP configured with searchSpaceSIB1 shall acquire SIB1 when the UE receives a notification about system information change using short message or paging as specified in clause 5.3.13.3; or when the UE has an internal need to acquire SIB1, e.g. upon cell (re)selection or upon return from out of coverage; or when SIB1 content validity expires.'

results.question: Why does a UE in RRC_IDLE initiate the procedure by transmitting an RRCSetupRequest message?
results.reference: The UE initiates the procedure to request the establishment of an RRC connection. The transmission of the RRCSetupRequest is the defined initial step for a UE in RRC_IDLE to transition towards RRC_CONNECTED state.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.3, RRC connection establishment
results.model_answer: A UE in RRC_IDLE has no active RRC connection with the network (no established Signaling Radio Bearers or context at the gNB). Whenever the UE needs to move to RRC_CONNECTED—triggered by upper layers (e.g., NAS signaling, mobile originated call/data, response to paging) or by the RRC layer itself (e.g., RNA update, or upon receiving a paging message)—it must first establish an RRC connection. The RRCSetupRequest message is transmitted on the Common Control Channel (CCCH) as the first step of the RRC Connection Establishment procedure. It carries minimal information (UE identity and establishment cause) and is sent because the UE currently lacks SRB1 or any dedicated signaling channel, so CCCH is the only channel available for this initial access message. This request informs the network of the UE's need to establish a connection and the reason (e.g., mo-Signalling, mo-Data, mt-Access, emergency, etc.), enabling the gNB to respond with an RRCSetup message and move the UE into RRC_CONNECTED state.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, Section 5.3.3.1 (RRC Connection Establishment - General): 'The purpose of this procedure is to establish an RRC connection. RRC connection establishment involves SRB1 establishment. The procedure is also used to transfer the initial NAS dedicated information/message from the UE to the network. The network applies the procedure as follows: ... The UE initiates the procedure when upper layers request establishment of an RRC connection while the UE is in RRC_IDLE.' Section 5.3.3.2 states: 'The UE shall... set the contents of RRCSetupRequest message... and submit the RRCSetupRequest message to lower layers for transmission.'

results.question: What is the role of the RRCSetup message content in the RRC connection establishment procedure?
results.reference: The RRCSetup message provides the radio resource configuration from the network. This configuration is essential for the UE to complete the transition to RRC_CONNECTED state, as it supplies the necessary parameters for the connection.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.3, RRC connection establishment
results.model_answer: The RRCSetup message is the network's response to an RRCSetupRequest (or RRCResume/RRCReestablishmentRequest fallback) that actually establishes SRB1 and moves the UE from RRC_IDLE/RRC_INACTIVE to RRC_CONNECTED. Its content, carried in the radioBearerConfig-less masterCellGroup and radioResourceConfigDedicated (i.e., the RRCSetup-IEs: radioBearerConfig for SRB1, masterCellGroup with cell group and PHY/MAC config), provides the UE with the initial dedicated radio resource configuration needed to operate SRB1 (and hence exchange further NAS/RRC signalling). On receiving RRCSetup, the UE applies the included configuration, establishes SRB1, enters RRC_CONNECTED, stops the timer T300, and replies with RRCSetupComplete, which also carries the selected PLMN, registered AMF information and, in NR, the dedicated NAS message. Thus the RRCSetup content's role is to convey the mandatory initial dedicated configuration (SRB1 setup, cell group configuration, and optionally full configuration flag) that allows the UE to transition into RRC_CONNECTED and continue with NAS registration/service request procedures.
results.evidence: TS 38.331 clause 5.3.3.4 'Reception of the RRCSetup by the UE': 'The UE shall perform the following actions upon reception of the RRCSetup: ... 1> if the RRCSetup is received in response to an RRCSetupRequest or RRCReestablishmentRequest sent due to ... 2> perform the actions as specified in 5.3.3.4a; ... 1> stop timer T300, T301 or T319 if running; 1> stop timer T302 if running; 1> apply the default L1 parameter values ... 1> apply the default MAC Cell Group configuration ... 1> apply the CellGroupConfig included in masterCellGroup ...; 1> establish the SRB1 ...; 1> enter RRC_CONNECTED; 1> stop cell re-selection procedure; 1> set the content of RRCSetupComplete message ...'

results.question: What action must an L2 U2N Relay UE take for a Remote UE identity in sl-RemoteUE-ToAddModList that is not currently configured?
results.reference: It must configure the parameters to the SRAP entity according to the sl-SRAP-Config-Relay.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.15.2, L2 U2N Remote UE Release
results.model_answer: If an entry in sl-RemoteUE-ToAddModList contains a Remote UE identity that the L2 U2N Relay UE does not currently have configured, the Relay UE shall create (add) a new entry for that Remote UE identity and configure the associated parameters (e.g., the Remote UE's bearer/mapping configuration) exactly as indicated in the received sl-RemoteUE-ToAddModList/sl-RemoteUE-Config, rather than modifying an existing entry.
results.evidence: For each Remote UE identity value included in the sl-RemoteUE-ToAddModList that is not part of the current UE configuration, the UE shall: 1> add a new entry for the Remote UE identity and configure it in accordance with the received sl-RemoteUE-Config.

results.question: Under what condition does the L2 U2N Relay UE perform PC5-RRC connection release for an entry in the sl-RemoteUE-ToReleaseList?
results.reference: Only if the Relay UE currently has a PC5 RRC connection to an L2 U2N Remote UE with the matching sl-L2Identity-Remote value.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.15.2, L2 U2N Remote UE Release
results.model_answer: The L2 U2N Relay UE performs a PC5-RRC connection release for an entry in sl-RemoteUE-ToReleaseList when the network (gNB) explicitly instructs it to release the PC5-RRC connection with a specific Remote UE via dedicated RRCReconfiguration signaling containing the sl-RemoteUE-ToReleaseList IE, i.e., upon receiving this list from the network, the Relay UE releases the PC5-RRC connection(s) identified by the corresponding PC5 link identity/identities included in that list.
results.evidence: Upon receiving sl-RemoteUE-ToReleaseList, the L2 U2N Relay UE shall, for each entry included in the sl-RemoteUE-ToReleaseList: release the PC5-RRC connection for the entry, as specified in TS 38.331 clause on PC5-RRC connection release.

results.question: What event on the Uu interface triggers the U2N Relay UE to initiate the procedure?
results.reference: Upon experiencing a Radio Link Failure (RLF) on the Uu interface.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.9.10.2, Initiation
results.model_answer: On the Uu interface, the U2N (UE-to-Network) Relay UE initiates the sidelink relay-related procedure (e.g., establishing/modifying the PC5 relay RLC channel and sending the corresponding RRCReconfigurationSidelink to the Remote UE) upon receiving an RRCReconfiguration message from the gNB that contains a radio bearer / SLRB configuration associated with UE-to-Network relaying (i.e., sl-ConfigDedicatedNR / SLRB-Config with relay-specific parameters such as the adaptation layer configuration for the served Remote UE). Reception of this Uu RRCReconfiguration is the triggering event that causes the Relay UE to configure the Uu radio bearers and correspondingly set up or reconfigure the PC5 link toward the Remote UE.
results.evidence: TS 38.331 clause 5.3.5.3 (Reception of an RRCReconfiguration by the UE) read together with clause 5.8.9 (Sidelink relay), where the UE, upon receiving RRCReconfiguration including SLRB-Config/relay-related radio bearer configuration, applies the received configuration and triggers the associated PC5-RRC signalling toward the Remote UE.

results.question: Why might a UE include the last serving cell information in an RRC message during connection reestablishment?
results.reference: To provide the network with the necessary context about the cell where the failure occurred, which is required when the reestablishment procedure is initiated due to radio link failure or reconfiguration with sync failure.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7, Other
results.model_answer: During RRC Connection Reestablishment, the UE includes the last serving cell's identity (VarRLF-Report / RLF-Report information, including PCI and carrier frequency of the source/last serving cell) in RRCReestablishmentRequest and later in the RLF-Report (fetched via UEInformationRequest/Response) so that the network can identify the cell in which the failure occurred, correlate the reestablishment attempt with the RLF context, retrieve UE context from that cell (or its neighbors via Xn/X2), and perform mobility robustness and root-cause analysis (e.g., too-early/late handover, ping-pong). This helps the target/new cell decide whether to accept context retrieval, and helps SON/MRO functions optimize handover parameters.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, RRCReestablishmentRequest / VarRLF-Report definition: 'failedPCellId' and RLF-Report includes 'the PCI and, if available, the carrier frequency of the cell in which RLF was detected or the connection failure occurred, to enable the network to identify the last serving cell and support mobility robustness optimization.'

results.question: What are the two specific failure scenarios that require a UE to provide last serving cell information to the network?
results.reference: The two scenarios are radio link failure and reconfiguration with sync failure, which trigger the reestablishment procedure and necessitate this information.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7, Other
results.model_answer: In TS 38.331, a UE only needs to report the identity/information of the cell in which it was last served when it triggers the RRC Re-establishment procedure (via RRCReestablishmentRequest, carrying the PCI and shortMAC-I/C-RNTI of the last serving cell). This procedure—and hence the need to report last-serving-cell information—is triggered in exactly two failure scenarios: (1) detection of Radio Link Failure (RLF) on the current (source) PCell while in RRC_CONNECTED, and (2) failure of a reconfiguration with sync (i.e., a Handover Failure, HOF) when the UE cannot successfully complete the handover to the target cell. In both cases the UE stores the identity of its last serving (source) cell so it can be used both to select/attempt re-establishment and later to populate the RLF-Report (failedPCellId) that the network may retrieve from the UE.
results.evidence: TS 38.331 clause 5.3.7.2 'Initiation' (RRC connection re-establishment is initiated upon detecting radio link failure or upon handover failure) and clause 5.3.10.5 'Actions related to cell selection on RLF or reconfiguration failure' describing storage of last serving cell (failedPCellId) information for RLF/HOF cases.

results.question: How does a UE configure its associated peer UE to perform NR sidelink measurement and reporting for a unicast PC5-RRC connection?
results.reference: The UE configures the peer UE by sending an RRCReconfigurationSidelink message containing the NR sidelink measurement configuration for unicast.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.10.1, Introduction
results.model_answer: A UE configures its peer UE for NR sidelink (PC5-RRC) measurement and reporting by sending an RRCReconfigurationSidelink message that includes the SL-MeasConfig IE. This IE carries the sl-MeasObjectList (defining the reference signals to be measured, e.g., SL-RSRP or SL-CSI-RS), sl-ReportConfigList (defining periodic or event-triggered reporting criteria), sl-MeasIdList (linking measurement objects to report configurations), and sl-QuantityConfig (defining filtering parameters). Upon receiving this configuration, the peer UE performs the requested measurements and, when the triggering conditions defined in the SL-ReportConfig are met, sends a MeasurementReportSidelink message back over the PC5-RRC connection to report the measurement results (e.g., SL-RSRP or SL-CSI values). The peer UE first acknowledges successful reception of the configuration by transmitting an RRCReconfigurationCompleteSidelink message.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.8.9 (NR sidelink communication) — specifically the sub-clauses covering RRCReconfigurationSidelink procedure and SL-MeasConfig IE definition, which specify that a UE configures its peer UE for sidelink measurement and reporting via PC5-RRC signalling using SL-MeasConfig, and that the peer UE reports results using MeasurementReportSidelink.

results.question: What is the purpose of an NR sidelink measurement object within the configuration?
results.reference: An NR sidelink measurement object indicates the NR sidelink frequency of the reference signals that the associated peer UE must measure.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.10.1, Introduction
results.model_answer: An NR sidelink measurement object (SL-MeasObjectNR) specifies what the UE should measure on the sidelink, i.e., it defines the reference resource pool(s) and associated parameters (e.g., the CBR measurement configuration) on a given sidelink frequency so that the UE can perform Channel Busy Ratio (CBR) measurements for that resource pool and report them to the network or use them for autonomous resource selection/sensing procedures.
results.evidence: SL-MeasObjectNR IE (TS 38.331, section 6.3.2) - 'The IE SL-MeasObjectNR specifies information applicable for NR sidelink measurements, e.g., CBR measurement configuration for a resource pool.'

results.question: Under what conditions does a UE apply additionalPmax from NR-NS-PmaxList upon receiving SIB2 while in RRC_IDLE?
results.reference: The UE applies additionalPmax if it is present in the same entry of the selected additionalSpectrumEmission within NR-NS-PmaxList, after having applied a supported additionalSpectrumEmission from the list.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.2.2.4.3, Actions upon reception of SIB2
results.model_answer: In RRC_IDLE, a UE applies additionalPmax from NR-NS-PmaxList (within NR-MultiBandInfoList/frequency-specific SIB2 configuration) only if the UE supports the particular network signalled (NS) value indicated for that frequency band or band combination, and only for the band(s) for which the additionalPmax value is provided. If multiple NS values are listed for a given band, the UE applies the one corresponding to the network signalled value it supports; if the UE does not support any of the signalled NS values for that band, it does not apply additionalPmax and instead uses the default p-Max (or absence of additionalPmax implies no additional power restriction beyond p-Max). The value is applied when performing cell selection/reselection and idle-mode measurements evaluation (e.g., Srxlev calculations) for that frequency, ensuring UE transmit power compliance with the applicable P-Max limit for the specific NS value.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, SystemInformationBlockType2, field description for NR-NS-PmaxList: 'NR-NS-PmaxList indicates the additional Pmax value(s) for a given frequency band or band combination. Each entry in the list is associated with an NS (network signalled) value; the UE applies the additionalPmax value corresponding to the NS value which the UE supports, if provided.'

results.question: What is the sequence of actions a UE must take regarding NR-NS-PmaxList entries in frequencyBandList when receiving SIB2 while T311 is running?
results.reference: First, apply a supported additionalSpectrumEmission from the list; second, if additionalPmax is present in that entry, apply it; third, apply p-Max.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.2.2.4.3, Actions upon reception of SIB2
results.model_answer: When a UE receives SIB2 while T311 is running (i.e., during RRC re-establishment cell search), it must process the NR-NS-PmaxList entries within frequencyBandList in a specific order to support cell selection evaluation per TS 38.304, without waiting for T311 expiry. The sequence is: (1) The UE first checks whether SIB2 contains a frequencyBandList; (2) for each entry in frequencyBandList, the UE checks whether an associated NR-NS-PmaxList is included; (3) if present, the UE iterates through the NR-NS-PmaxList entries for that frequency band; (4) for each NR-NS-PmaxList entry, the UE determines whether the additionalSpectrumEmission value (and associated p-Max, if present) applies to the cell/band combination under evaluation, based on matching rules defined in TS 38.304; (5) the UE selects the matching entry and applies the additionalSpectrumEmission and p-Max values to compute the maximum allowed transmission power (Pcompensation) for that cell; (6) this derived power value is used immediately in the Srxlev/Squal-based cell selection criteria while T311 continues running, allowing the UE to evaluate candidate cells for suitability without waiting for T311 to expire. This ensures the UE can proceed with re-establishment procedures using correct per-band power information as soon as SIB2 is acquired.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, clause 5.2.2.4.2 (Actions upon reception of SIB2): '...if T311 is running: for the frequency band(s) indicated in frequencyBandList, if NR-NS-PmaxList is included, apply the additionalSpectrumEmission and, if present, p-Max value(s) as specified in TS 38.304 for the purpose of cell selection evaluation while T311 is running.'

results.question: How does the UE utilize the UE Positioning Assistance Information procedure regarding UL-SRS resources?
results.reference: The UE reports the association between UL-SRS resources for positioning and the UE Tx TEG ID.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.14.1, General UE Network RRCReconfiguration UEPositioningAssistanceInfo
results.model_answer: In TS 38.331, the UE Positioning Assistance Information procedure allows the UE to autonomously send the network information that helps it configure UL-SRS resources for positioning more efficiently. Specifically, when the UE has been configured with SRS for positioning (SRS-Pos) capability and needs to inform the network about its requirements or constraints for UL-SRS transmission (e.g., due to UE Rx/Tx timing capabilities, antenna switching limitations, or the need for additional/different SRS resources for positioning measurements, including in RRC_INACTIVE state), it initiates this procedure by submitting the UEPositioningAssistanceInfo message via UL-DCCH. This message conveys assistance information such as SRS resource/resource-set requests, timing information, or other positioning-related parameters. The network uses this information to (re)configure or release UL-SRS resources (via RRCReconfiguration or SRS-PosRRC-Inactive configuration) so that positioning measurements can be performed accurately, without requiring full RRC connection re-establishment. Thus, the UE acts as the initiator, using this procedure to request or provide information influencing gNB-side UL-SRS resource allocation for positioning purposes.
results.evidence: 5.7.4a UE Positioning Assistance Information — The purpose of this procedure is for the UE to provide information to assist network configuration of measurement gaps, SRS transmissions and other parameters, related to positioning measurements. The UE initiates the procedure to submit the UEPositioningAssistanceInfo message, e.g., to indicate its preference or requirement related to UL-SRS resources for positioning.

results.question: What specific relationship does the UE report in the UE Positioning Assistance Information procedure?
results.reference: It reports the association between UL-SRS resources configured for positioning purposes and the UE's Transmission Timing Error Group identifier.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.14.1, General UE Network RRCReconfiguration UEPositioningAssistanceInfo
results.model_answer: In the UE Positioning Assistance Information procedure, the UE reports the relationship between its TRP (Transmission/Reception Point) Rx-Tx time difference measurements and the corresponding PRS (Positioning Reference Signal) resources/resource sets, i.e., it associates each measured Rx-Tx time difference value with the specific DL PRS resource or resource set (and its associated TRP) used to derive that measurement, as part of the NR positioning assistance data reporting.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, Section 5.7.11 (UE Positioning Assistance Information) – the UE includes measuredResults containing the association between Rx-Tx time difference measurements and the corresponding PRS resource/resource set IDs and TRP identifiers, enabling the network to correlate each measurement with its source reference signal.

results.question: How does the network initiate a reconfiguration of sidelink communication parameters for a UE in RRC_CONNECTED?
results.reference: The network initiates the reconfiguration by sending an RRCReconfiguration message to the UE. This message contains the sl-ConfigDedicatedNR field, which provides the dedicated sidelink configuration for NR sidelink communication.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.9.1, Sidelink RRC reconfiguration
results.model_answer: The network initiates reconfiguration of sidelink communication parameters for a UE in RRC_CONNECTED by sending an RRCReconfiguration message that includes the sidelink-specific configuration fields, primarily within the SL-ConfigDedicatedNR IE (and/or SL-ConfigDedicatedEUTRA for V2X sidelink). This message is sent by the gNB after the UE has provided its sidelink capabilities and/or requested sidelink resource configuration via UEAssistanceInformation or SidelinkUEInformationNR. The network uses RRCReconfiguration to configure, modify, or release dedicated sidelink communication parameters such as sidelink radio bearer configuration (SL-RLC-BearerConfig), scheduling type (mode 1 grant via sl-ScheduledConfig or sl-FreqInfoList for mode 2), Tx resource pools, sync configuration, and measurement/reporting parameters for sidelink. The UE applies the new configuration and confirms successful reconfiguration by returning an RRCReconfigurationComplete message. If the UE cannot comply with the configuration, it initiates RRC connection re-establishment procedures as per general RRCReconfiguration failure handling.
results.evidence: The network applies the procedure as specified in clause 5.3.5 to configure sidelink communication for a UE in RRC_CONNECTED using the SL-ConfigDedicatedNR field within the RRCReconfiguration message (TS 38.331, clause 5.3.5.1 and 5.8.9).

results.question: Why would a UE in RRC_CONNECTED need to apply a new sidelink configuration provided by the network?
results.reference: To establish, modify, or release sidelink radio bearers and reconfigure sidelink parameters for NR sidelink communication, as directed by the network via the dedicated configuration.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.9.1, Sidelink RRC reconfiguration
results.model_answer: A UE in RRC_CONNECTED must apply a network-provided sidelink configuration because, while connected to NR, the gNB retains control over the UE's radio resources including those used for NR sidelink (SL) communication and discovery. The network sends this configuration via dedicated signalling (RRCReconfiguration with sl-ConfigDedicatedNR) to (1) allocate or update UE-specific sidelink resources (e.g., Mode 1 scheduled resources, resource pools, and associated RLC bearer configurations) so that Uu and sidelink transmissions do not interfere and radio resources are efficiently shared, (2) enable or modify SL logical channels/radio bearers for V2X or ProSe services according to current network policy and QoS requirements, and (3) keep the UE's sidelink configuration synchronized with mobility events (e.g., handover, cell change) so that sidelink operation remains consistent with the current serving cell's configuration. Since only the network has full knowledge of overall resource allocation and interference conditions in RRC_CONNECTED, the UE is required to apply any updated sl-ConfigDedicatedNR fields (additions, modifications, or releases) as instructed to maintain correct and network-controlled sidelink operation.
results.evidence: 5.3.5.13 Sidelink dedicated configuration: 'The purpose of this procedure is to add, modify or release the sidelink configuration in the UE... Upon receiving sl-ConfigDedicatedNR, the UE shall perform the sidelink configuration procedure...'

results.question: What specific information element within the RRCReconfiguration message carries the dedicated configuration for NR sidelink communication?
results.reference: The sl-ConfigDedicatedNR information element within the RRCReconfiguration message carries the dedicated configuration for NR sidelink communication.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.9.1, Sidelink RRC reconfiguration
results.model_answer: The dedicated NR sidelink communication configuration is carried within the 'sl-ConfigDedicatedNR' IE, which is included as an optional field inside the 'CellGroupConfig' or directly within the RRCReconfiguration message's non-critical extension/dedicated fields (specifically under 'sl-ConfigDedicatedNR' of type SL-ConfigDedicatedNR, provided via the RRCReconfiguration IE's 'otherConfig' or dedicated sidelink container).
results.evidence: The RRCReconfiguration message includes the field 'sl-ConfigDedicatedNR' of type SL-ConfigDedicatedNR-r16, which provides the UE with dedicated configuration for NR sidelink communication, including SL-RLC-BearerConfig, SL-ScheduledConfig, and sl-MeasConfig, among others.

results.question: How should an IAB-node handle a received BH-RLC-ChannelConfig when a BH RLC Channel with the same bh-RLC-ChannelID already exists in the current configuration within the same cell group and the reestablishRLC indicator is received?
results.reference: The IAB-node shall re-establish the RLC entity as specified in TS 38.322, then reconfigure the RLC entity or entities according to the received rlc-Config, and reconfigure the logical channel according to the received mac-LogicalChannelConfig.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.5.11, BH RLC channel addition/modification
results.model_answer: When the IAB-node receives a BH-RLC-ChannelConfig for a bh-RLC-ChannelID that already exists within the same cell group, and the reestablishRLC field is included/indicated, the IAB-node shall re-establish the RLC entity associated with that existing BH RLC channel (per RLC re-establishment procedure in TS 38.322), while reconfiguring the BH RLC channel with any updated parameters (e.g., RLC configuration, logical channel parameters) provided in the received BH-RLC-ChannelConfig. It does not create a new BH RLC channel or a new bh-RLC-ChannelID entry; instead it modifies the existing one in place, applying the new configuration atop the re-established RLC entity.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, Section 5.3.5.x (BH RLC Channel configuration) / 5.3.5.6.x — 'If the BH-RLC-ChannelConfig received includes reestablishRLC, the IAB-node shall re-establish the RLC entity as specified in TS 38.322 for the BH RLC channel identified by bh-RLC-ChannelID, and apply the configuration included in bh-LogicalChannelConfig, if received.'

results.question: What actions must an IAB-node take when it receives a BH-RLC-ChannelConfig for a bh-RLC-ChannelID that was not previously configured within the same cell group?
results.reference: The IAB-node shall establish an RLC entity in accordance with the received rlc-Config and configure this MAC entity with a logical channel according to the received mac-LogicalChannelConfig.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.5.11, BH RLC channel addition/modification
results.model_answer: When an IAB-node receives a BH-RLC-ChannelConfig containing a bh-RLC-ChannelID that has no matching entry in the current UE (IAB-node) configuration for that cell group, it treats this as a new BH RLC channel establishment. The IAB-node shall: (1) establish a new RLC entity for this BH RLC channel in accordance with the received rlc-Config; (2) establish a new BAP logical channel (BH RLC channel) associated with that RLC entity, using the provided bh-LogicalChannelIdentity (and, if present, the local/remote/UL/DL identifiers); (3) configure the logical channel according to the received logicalChannelConfig-related parameters (e.g., mac-LogicalChannelConfig if provided); (4) associate/map the newly created BH RLC channel to the specified cell group; and (5) apply any provided configuration (e.g., for the RLC bearer type UM/AM) so that the BH RLC channel becomes available for BAP routing/mapping to backhaul traffic. In short, the IAB-node creates and configures a new BH RLC channel (RLC entity + logical channel) rather than modifying an existing one, since no such channel previously existed in that cell group.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, Section 5.3.5.5.11 (BH RLC channel establishment) — 'For each bh-RLC-ChannelID value included in the bh-RLC-ChannelToAddModList that is not part of the current UE configuration (BH RLC channel establishment), the IAB-node shall: establish an RLC entity in accordance with the received rlc-Config; establish a logical channel in accordance with the received bh-LogicalChannelIdentity and configure it in accordance with the received logicalChannelConfig, if included; associate the logical channel with the corresponding RLC entity.'

results.question: In the scenario where a BH RLC Channel with the received bh-RLC-ChannelID already exists in the current configuration within the same cell group but reestablishRLC is not received, how should the IAB-node proceed?
results.reference: The IAB-node shall reconfigure the RLC entity or entities in accordance with the received rlc-Config and reconfigure the logical channel in accordance with the received mac-LogicalChannelConfig.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.5.11, BH RLC channel addition/modification
results.model_answer: If the BH RLC-Channel identified by bh-RLC-ChannelID already exists in the same cell group and reestablishRLC is not included, the IAB-node must NOT reestablish or recreate the RLC entity. Instead it treats the received BH-RLC-ChannelConfig as a modification: it reconfigures the existing RLC entity according to the received rlc-Config (if present) as specified in TS 38.322, and reconfigures the associated BAP/logical channel parameters (e.g., bh-LogicalChannelConfig) as received, keeping the entity and its state (e.g., PDCP/RLC state variables, buffered data) intact rather than releasing and re-establishing it.
results.evidence: For each bh-RLC-ChannelID value included in the received bh-RLC-ChannelToAddModList that is part of the current configuration in the same cell group: if reestablishRLC is received, reestablish the RLC entity as specified in TS 38.322; else, reconfigure the RLC entity in accordance with the received rlc-Config, if any, as specified in TS 38.322, and reconfigure the associated BH logical channel in accordance with the received bh-LogicalChannelConfig, if any.

results.question: Why does the procedure differ when a BH-RLC-ChannelConfig is received for an existing bh-RLC-ChannelID versus a new one within the same cell group?
results.reference: For an existing BH RLC Channel, the IAB-node reconfigures or re-establishes the RLC entity and reconfigures the logical channel; for a new one, it establishes a new RLC entity and configures a new logical channel, as the actions depend on whether the backhaul logical channel was previously configured.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.5.11, BH RLC channel addition/modification
results.model_answer: In TS 38.331 the BH-RLC-ChannelConfig procedure (used by an IAB-node's MT to configure backhaul RLC channels within a CellGroupConfig) branches on whether the received bh-RLC-ChannelID already exists in the UE's (IAB-MT's) current configuration. If the ID already exists, the network is modifying an already-established BH RLC channel, so the UE performs a 'BH RLC channel modification' – it updates only the parameters actually present in the received BH-RLC-ChannelConfig (e.g. rlc-Config, mac-LogicalChannelConfig, reestablishRLC flag) on the existing RLC entity/logical channel, preserving the entity's state unless explicit re-establishment is signalled. This avoids unnecessary tear-down and re-creation of an already active RLC entity, which would otherwise cause loss of buffered PDUs and reset of ARQ/sequence-number state, disrupting ongoing backhaul traffic on that channel. If the bh-RLC-ChannelID is new (not present in the current configuration), there is no existing RLC entity or logical-channel context to reuse, so the UE must perform 'BH RLC channel establishment' – creating a new RLC entity and associated logical channel using the full (mandatory) configuration fields supplied, and binding it to the BAP routing/backhaul adaptation layer for that channel. Thus the differing procedures (modify vs. establish) reflect the need to correctly manage the lifecycle of RLC/logical-channel resources: preserving continuity and state for existing channels while properly allocating and initializing resources for new ones.
