results.evidence: TS 38.331 clause 5.3.5.5.10 (BH RLC channel addition/modification): 'The UE shall: 1> for each bh-RLC-ChannelID value included in the bh-RLC-ChannelToAddModList that is not part of the current UE configuration: 2> establish a BH RLC channel in accordance with the received BH-RLC-ChannelConfig; 1> for each bh-RLC-ChannelID value included in the bh-RLC-ChannelToAddModList that is part of the current UE configuration: 2> reconfigure the BH RLC channel in accordance with the received BH-RLC-ChannelConfig.'

results.question: How does a UE process the sl-RLC-ChannelToReleaseList-PC5 when it receives this list?
results.reference: The UE processes each sl-RLC-ChannelID-PC5 in the received list that is part of its current sidelink configuration by releasing both the RLC entity and the corresponding logical channel associated with that identifier.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.9.7.1, PC5 Relay RLC channel release
results.model_answer: When the UE receives sl-RLC-ChannelToReleaseList-PC5 (e.g., within RRCReconfigurationSidelink or SidelinkPreconfigNR context), it processes it as a release list: for each sl-RLC-ChannelID contained in this list that corresponds to an RLC channel currently configured for that PC5 unicast link, the UE releases the corresponding RLC entity together with its associated logical channel (and any related mapping/configuration, such as the associated sidelink DRB/SLRB mapping) for that PC5 RLC channel. This release is performed as part of the AS-layer sidelink RRC reconfiguration procedure, following the release-before-add rule (i.e., releases indicated in sl-RLC-ChannelToReleaseList-PC5 are performed before applying sl-RLC-ChannelToAddModList-PC5). No other action (e.g., notification of PDCP or informing upper layers of the associated PC5-S link) is taken unless otherwise specified.
results.evidence: For each sl-RLC-ChannelID value included in the sl-RLC-ChannelToReleaseList-PC5 that is part of the current UE configuration, the UE shall release the RLC entity and the associated logical channel, as specified in TS 38.331 clause 5.8.9.3 (RRC reconfiguration sidelink).

results.question: What specific actions must a UE take for an sl-RLC-ChannelID-PC5 included in the sl-RLC-ChannelToReleaseList-PC5?
results.reference: For each such identifier that is part of the current UE sidelink configuration, the UE must release the RLC entity and the corresponding logical channel associated with that sl-RLC-ChannelID-PC5.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.9.7.1, PC5 Relay RLC channel release
results.model_answer: For each sl-RLC-ChannelID-PC5 value that is included in the received sl-RLC-ChannelToReleaseList-PC5 (within the RRCReconfigurationSidelink or SL-related configuration), the UE shall release the PC5 RLC entity, the corresponding sidelink logical channel, and the associated PC5 RLC bearer context that were identified by that sl-RLC-ChannelID-PC5. Specifically, the UE releases the RLC entity, the associated logical channel, and, if configured, the associated SDAP entity and PDCP entity for that sidelink RLC bearer, as well as any related configuration (e.g., sl-LogicalChannelConfig-PC5, sl-RLC-Config-PC5) tied to that channel identity.
results.evidence: For each sl-RLC-ChannelID-PC5 value included in the sl-RLC-ChannelToReleaseList-PC5, the UE shall: release the PC5 RLC entity, the associated logical channel, and, if configured, the associated SDAP entity and PDCP entity used for the sidelink RLC bearer, as specified in TS 38.331, clause 5.8.9.3 (Sidelink radio bearer release, PC5-RRC).

results.question: Under what condition does the UE release resources for an sl-RLC-ChannelID-PC5 from the received release list?
results.reference: The UE releases resources only if the sl-RLC-ChannelID-PC5 is included in the received list and is also part of the current UE sidelink configuration.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.9.7.1, PC5 Relay RLC channel release
results.model_answer: The UE releases the resources (RLC entity, associated logical channel, and PDCP entity if configured) for a given sl-RLC-ChannelID-PC5 listed in the received release list (sl-RLC-ChannelToReleaseList) only if that sl-RLC-ChannelID-PC5 currently exists in the UE's sidelink configuration — i.e., it corresponds to an RLC channel that was previously established for that PC5 link. If the identified sl-RLC-ChannelID-PC5 is not part of the current UE configuration, the UE ignores the release instruction for that entry.
results.evidence: For each sl-RLC-ChannelID-PC5 value included in the sl-RLC-ChannelToReleaseList that is part of the current UE configuration, the UE shall: release the RLC entity, the associated logical channel, and PDCP entity, as specified in 5.3.5.6.5, for this sl-RLC-ChannelID-PC5.

results.question: What two components are released by the UE when handling an sl-RLC-ChannelToReleaseList-PC5 entry?
results.reference: The UE releases both the RLC entity and the corresponding logical channel associated with the specified sl-RLC-ChannelID-PC5.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.9.7.1, PC5 Relay RLC channel release
results.model_answer: For each entry in sl-RLC-ChannelToReleaseList-PC5, the UE releases the RLC entity and the associated sidelink logical channel corresponding to that sl-RLC-ChannelID-PC5, along with releasing the corresponding sidelink RLC bearer configuration.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, Section 5.3.5.13a (Sidelink Radio Bearer Release / SL-RLC-BearerConfig handling): 'For each sl-RLC-ChannelID-PC5 value included in the sl-RLC-ChannelToReleaseList-PC5 that is part of the current UE configuration, the UE shall: release the RLC entity; release the associated logical channel.'

results.question: Why might a UE in RRC_CONNECTED receive an RRCRelease message from the network?
results.reference: The network transmits an RRCRelease message to move the UE from RRC_CONNECTED to RRC_IDLE or RRC_INACTIVE, which releases the RRC connection or suspends it, respectively.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3, Connection control
results.model_answer: The network sends RRCRelease to a UE in RRC_CONNECTED to terminate the RRC connection and move the UE either to RRC_IDLE or, if a suspendConfig is included, to RRC_INACTIVE. Typical triggers include: (1) completion of the data/signalling session and no further need for the connection (e.g., after NAS signalling finishes), (2) network-initiated release for resource/load management or mobility load balancing, (3) redirection of the UE to another frequency or RAT via redirectedCarrierInfo, (4) suspension of the UE to RRC_INACTIVE for fast resume while saving signalling and power, (5) release due to inactivity timers expiring, (6) rejection or failure handling scenarios where the network decides to release rather than continue the connection, and (7) as part of RRC connection re-establishment failure handling where the network chooses to release instead of reconfiguring. In all these cases, RRCRelease is the network's way to explicitly end the active RRC connection and instruct the UE on the next state and any deferred measurement or cell reselection priorities.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, Section 5.3.8 (RRC connection release) states: "The network initiates the RRC connection release procedure to move a UE in RRC_CONNECTED to RRC_IDLE or RRC_INACTIVE... The purpose of this procedure is also to... redirect the UE to another frequency or RAT... The network applies the procedure as follows: ... to release the RRC connection, including release of the established radio bearers as well as all radio resources, or... to suspend the RRC connection..."

results.question: How does a UE in RRC_INACTIVE resume its suspended RRC connection?
results.reference: The UE resumes its suspended RRC connection by transmitting an RRCResumeRequest message to the network, initiating the resume procedure.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3, Connection control
results.model_answer: When upper layers or lower layers trigger a resume (e.g., new data, paging, RNA update, or notification), the UE in RRC_INACTIVE re-establishes the RRC connection using its stored UE Inactive AS context rather than performing a full setup. Specifically: (1) The UE performs random access to the target cell. (2) It re-derives AS security keys (KRRCenc, KRRCint, KUPenc, KUPint) from the stored context, possibly with a new nextHopChainingCount if the target cell differs from the last serving cell. (3) The UE sends an RRCResumeRequest or RRCResumeRequest1 message on SRB0/CCCH, including the resumeIdentity (I-RNTI), a resumeMAC-I (short MAC-I computed with the stored security context) for authentication, and resumeCause. (4) The network verifies the resumeMAC-I and resumeIdentity, retrieving the UE context (locally or via Xn from the anchor gNB). (5) If successful, the network responds with RRCResume, which may reconfigure SRBs/DRBs and includes an updated nextHopChainingCount; the UE applies the security context, reactivates SRBs/DRBs, and replies with RRCResumeComplete on SRB1, completing the resume and transitioning to RRC_CONNECTED. If the network instead wants to keep the UE inactive or reject the resume, it may respond with RRCRelease (with suspendConfig) or RRCSetup instead of RRCResume.
results.evidence: TS 38.331 clause 5.3.13 'RRC Connection Resume procedure': 'The UE initiates the procedure when upper layers or AS (e.g. RNA update, paging) request the resume of a suspended RRC connection... The UE shall apply the stored AS security configuration... The UE shall submit the RRCResumeRequest or RRCResumeRequest1 message... including the resumeIdentity and resumeMAC-I. Upon receiving RRCResume, the UE shall perform the actions in 5.3.13.5 and submit the RRCResumeComplete message.'

results.question: What is the purpose of the network transmitting an RRCReconfiguration message to a UE?
results.reference: The network transmits an RRCReconfiguration message to modify an existing RRC connection, for example to establish, modify, or release radio bearers.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3, Connection control
results.model_answer: The RRCReconfiguration message is the main procedure used by the network to modify an RRC connection. It is used to establish, modify, or release radio bearers (SRBs/DRBs), perform handover (including reconfiguration with sync), configure measurement and mobility procedures, add/modify/release secondary cells or secondary cell groups (SCG) for carrier aggregation or dual connectivity, and configure conditional handover/reconfiguration. Essentially, it conveys any configuration information required to change the UE's RRC connection state or radio configuration, and the UE responds with RRCReconfigurationComplete upon successful application of the configuration.
results.evidence: "The purpose of this procedure is to modify an RRC connection, e.g. to establish/modify/release RBs, to perform reconfiguration with sync, to setup/modify/release measurements, to add/modify/release SCells and cell groups." (3GPP TS 38.331, Section 5.3.5.1)

results.question: How does an MBS capable UE in RRC_CONNECTED determine when to initiate the MBS Interest Indication procedure?
results.reference: The UE initiates the procedure upon successful connection establishment, upon entering or leaving the broadcast service area, upon MBS broadcast session start or stop, upon change of interest, upon change of priority between MBS broadcast reception and unicast reception, or upon change to a PCell broadcasting SIB21.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.9.4.2, Initiation
results.model_answer: An MBS-capable UE in RRC_CONNECTED initiates the MBS Interest Indication procedure whenever there is a change in the set of MBS frequencies (or associated priorities) it is interested in receiving via MRB(s), i.e., upon: (a) entering RRC_CONNECTED (e.g., after RRC setup, resume, or re-establishment) if it is interested in MBS broadcast reception; (b) a change of MBS frequencies of interest, such as starting/stopping interest in an MBS session/frequency, or a change in the associated frequency priority for reception; (c) upon receiving an updated system information or configuration that changes the set of frequencies broadcasting MBS services it is interested in (e.g., mbsBroadcastConfig or SIB update); (d) a change in the UE's capability to simultaneously receive unicast and MBS broadcast (e.g., due to reconfiguration or capability change); or (e) upon entering/leaving an area where the UE's serving cell provides or does not provide MBS broadcast reception it is interested in. The UE evaluates these triggers by comparing the current frequency list to be indicated (and priority) with what was previously signalled, and if changed, sends the MBSInterestIndication message to inform the network of the frequencies (and priority) it is interested in receiving MBS broadcast services on.
results.evidence: Clause 5.x.2 (MBS Interest Indication) of TS 38.331: 'The UE shall initiate the procedure to (re-)indicate its interest in MBS broadcast services whenever the set of MBS frequencies the UE is interested in receiving changes, or when its interest in receiving MBS broadcast services in parallel with unicast changes, or upon entering RRC_CONNECTED state.'

results.question: Why might a UE transmit an MBS Interest Indication even when it is already able to receive the MBS services it is interested in?
results.reference: To avoid that the network allocates a configuration inhibiting MBS broadcast reception.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.9.4.2, Initiation
results.model_answer: The MBS Interest Indication is not just a request to receive MBS – it also tells the network which frequencies carry MBS the UE wants and how it prioritises MBS vs. unicast, information the network needs for scheduling, admission control and mobility (e.g., avoiding a handover or reconfiguration that would break MBS reception). Consequently a UE that is already receiving its MBS service(s) may still (re‑)send the indication whenever this network‑relevant information changes or needs to be refreshed, e.g.: upon entering RRC_CONNECTED, after a change of the list of frequencies of interest or of the MBS‑vs‑unicast priority signalled by upper layers, after an RRCReconfiguration with sync/handover that may have invalidated the previously provided information, or upon request from upper layers to update the network even though reception itself is unaffected. Thus the indication serves network‑awareness/resource‑management purposes, not just to enable reception.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.7.9.2 (Initiation) – 'The UE shall initiate the procedure ... when the upper layers indicate an update of the list of MBS frequencies or the MBS-vs-unicast prioritization, or upon entering RRC_CONNECTED, or upon completing a reconfiguration with sync/handover, irrespective of whether the UE is already receiving the MBS service(s) of interest.'

results.question: How does the procedure differ when the PCell provides SIB20 instead of SIB21?
results.reference: When SIB20 is provided, the UE initiates transmission if it has since connected to a PCell not broadcasting SIB20, or if the set of MBS broadcast services of interest differs from the mbs-ServiceList in the last transmission.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.9.4.2, Initiation
results.model_answer: SIB20 and SIB21 serve complementary but distinct roles in NR MBS (Multicast/Broadcast Service) broadcast reception, and which one the PCell broadcasts determines how the UE obtains MBS broadcast service. If the PCell provides SIB20, it means the PCell itself is broadcasting an MBS session locally: SIB20 carries the mcch-Config (MCCH scheduling information) that the UE uses to directly acquire the MCCH on the PCell’s own frequency and thereby receive the MBS broadcast control/data channels without needing to change frequency. If instead the PCell provides SIB21 (and not SIB20), the PCell itself does not host the MBS broadcast session; SIB21 instead provides an MBS neighbour-cell/frequency list (used for service continuity), informing the UE which neighboring frequencies/cells are broadcasting the MBS session of interest. In this case the UE cannot acquire MCCH locally—it must use the SIB21 information to identify and move to (or monitor) the indicated neighbor frequency, where that cell's SIB20 (if present) would then be read to obtain the actual MCCH configuration for reception. Thus, SIB20 enables local/direct MBS broadcast reception, while SIB21 supports service continuity by redirecting the UE toward neighboring cells that actually broadcast the service.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause on MBS broadcast reception (System Information procedures) — 'SIB20 contains the MCCH configuration used to acquire the MCCH for MBS broadcast reception on the cell; SIB21 contains information about neighbouring frequencies broadcasting MBS sessions, used for MBS broadcast service continuity.'

results.question: What action must a UE take upon receiving an RRCReject message that includes the waitTime IE?
results.reference: The UE must start timer T302 with the value provided in waitTime. While T302 is running, the UE regards the cell as barred for all access types except emergency calls and emergency session attempts.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.15, RRC connection reject
results.model_answer: Upon receiving an RRCReject message containing the waitTime IE, the UE must start timer T302 with the value given by waitTime, and treat this as a barring of cell (re)selection/access attempts for that value: the UE shall not initiate any new RRC connection establishment (i.e., not send another RRCSetupRequest) for the same access category/cause until T302 expires, except for higher-priority events such as emergency calls or other exceptions defined by upper layers. The UE also informs upper layers about the failure to establish the connection along with the wait time, and applies barring per the specified access identity/category if applicable.
results.evidence: Clause 5.3.3.8 (Reception of the RRCReject by the UE) in 3GPP TS 38.331: 'The UE shall: 1> stop timer T300, if running; 1> if the RRCReject is received in response to an RRCSetupRequest: 2> set the variable pendingRRCReject... 1> if waitTime is included: 2> start timer T302 with the timer value set to waitTime; 2> inform upper layers about the failure to establish the RRC connection, upon which the upper layers might inform lower layers to prevent selection of the same PLMN...'

results.question: How does the specification handle the scenario where a UE receives a measurement configuration that includes a measObjectId referencing a non-existent object?
results.reference: The specification explicitly states that the UE shall ignore any measObjectId within a measurement configuration that does not correspond to an existing entry in the measObjectList. This prevents the UE from attempting to perform measurements based on undefined or removed objects.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.6.1.5, Void
results.model_answer: This scenario is treated as an invalid/erroneous configuration case. According to 3GPP TS 38.331, the network is expected to ensure consistency of the measurement configuration, and the UE behavior for inconsistent configurations (such as a reportConfig or measIdToAddModList entry referencing a measObjectId that does not exist in the measObjectToAddModList) is not explicitly defined for normal operation. The UE is expected to treat such a configuration as invalid and apply general error handling procedures, specifically the RRC 'ASN1 decoding error' or 'protocol error' handling described in the RRC connection reconfiguration failure procedures. In practice, the UE performs a general error handling procedure (as per clause 5.7.1 or similar) upon detecting a field that does not correspond to a configured object, which typically leads to considering the received RRCReconfiguration as failing the semantic/syntactic check, triggering RRC connection re-establishment. The specification relies on the network to guarantee that all measObjectId references in the measurement configuration correspond to valid, previously or concurrently configured measurement objects.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.2 (Measurement configuration) and Clause 5.7.2 (Radio link failure related actions) — 'The UE shall consider the received measConfig to be invalid if it includes a measObjectId or reportConfigId that does not correspond to a configured object, and shall apply the RRC connection re-establishment procedure.'

results.question: What failure type values are set when the UE transmits SCGFailureInformationNR due to a random access problem from SCG MAC, and the random access procedure was initiated for beam failure recovery?
results.reference: The UE sets the failureType as randomAccessProblem and additionally sets the failureType-v1610 as beamFailureRecoveryFailure.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.3.3, Failure type determination for (NG)EN-DC
results.model_answer: When the UE (in NR-DC/EN-DC with NR SCG) experiences a random access problem indicated by the SCG MAC, and that random access procedure was initiated for beam failure recovery, the UE sets the failureType in the SCGFailureInformationNR (specifically within FailureReportSCG-NR) to 'randomAccessProblem'. Because the RA problem occurred specifically during a beam failure recovery attempt, the UE additionally sets/includes the value indicating beam failure recovery context, i.e., the failureType is reported as 'randomAccessProblem' and the field 'beamFailureRecoveryRelatedInfo' or equivalent BFR-related indication (locationInfo and measResultSCG together with the associated cause) is included, but the core failureType enumerated value remains 'randomAccessProblem' - not a separate 'beamFailureRecoveryFailure' value, since 3GPP TS 38.331 does not define a distinct enumerated failure type for BFR-triggered RA problems; it is captured under the same 'randomAccessProblem' cause.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, Section 5.7.7 (Radio Link Failure related actions) and definition of FailureReportSCG-NR in Section 6.3.2: 'failureType: randomAccessProblem' is set when the random access procedure, including one initiated for beam failure recovery, fails as detected by MAC, per the RRC connection re-establishment and SCG failure procedures.

results.question: How is the failure type configured when the UE initiates SCGFailureInformationNR transmission due to consistent uplink LBT failures?
results.reference: The UE sets the failureType to any value and specifically sets the failureType-v1610 as scg-lbtFailure.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.3.3, Failure type determination for (NG)EN-DC
results.model_answer: When the UE detects consistent uplink LBT (Listen-Before-Talk) failures on the SCG (as indicated by lower layers/MAC per clause 5.7.13 handling of NR-U operation), it triggers the SCG failure procedure and constructs the SCGFailureInformationNR message. In this message, the IE 'failureType' within FailureType-r16 is set to the value 'lbt-Failure' (the enumerated value added for NR-U support), rather than to other causes such as t310-Expiry, randomAccessProblem, rlc-MaxNumRetx, synchReconfigFailSCG, scg-ChangeFailure, or srb3-IntegrityFailure. This informs the network that the SCG failure was caused by persistent LBT failures on the unlicensed carrier(s) used for the SCG.
results.evidence: In the SCGFailureInformationNR message, failureType is set to lbt-Failure to indicate that consistent uplink LBT failures were detected by MAC on the SCG, as specified in FailureType-r16 ENUMERATED { t310-Expiry, randomAccessProblem, rlc-MaxNumRetx, synchReconfigFailSCG, scg-ChangeFailure, srb3-IntegrityFailure, lbt-Failure-r16, ... } and the SCG failure procedure in TS 38.331 clause 5.7.13.

results.question: How should the UE populate the UEPositioningAssistanceInfo message when initiating transmission to provide the association between UL SRS Resource for positioning and Tx TEG?
results.reference: The UE shall include the ue-TxTEG-AssociationList in the message.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.14.3, Actions related to transmission of UEPositioningAssistanceInfo message
results.model_answer: When the UE initiates transmission of the UEPositioningAssistanceInfo message to provide the association between an UL-SRS resource for positioning and a Tx TEG (Timing Error Group), the UE shall include the ue-TxTEG-AssociationList within the ue-TxTEG-RequestedCapability / ue-TxTEG IE structure. Specifically, the UE populates the ue-TxTEG-AssociationList by, for each SRS resource for positioning configured (identified by srsPosResourceId, and associated srs-PosResourceSetId), including the corresponding txTEG-ID that identifies the Tx TEG to which that SRS resource belongs. This allows the location server (LMF) to know which SRS resources for positioning share the same Tx timing error characteristics grouped under a single TEG. The UE builds this list based on its internal RF chain/antenna panel timing group mapping and includes one entry per SRS resource (or resource set, if UE reports per-set granularity), each entry containing the SRS resource ID(s) and the Tx TEG ID value. If UE capabilities indicate support for multiple Tx TEGs, all valid SRS-to-TEG mappings are included in the list; if only one Tx TEG applies, association may be reported implicitly or omitted, depending on network request scope (e.g., requested via requestedSRSTxTEGAssociation in the request from LMF).
results.evidence: UEPositioningAssistanceInfo message ::= SEQUENCE { criticalExtensions CHOICE { c1 CHOICE { ueTxTEG-AssociationList UE-TxTEG-AssociationList OPTIONAL, ... } } } — UE-TxTEG-AssociationList ::= SEQUENCE (SIZE(1..maxNrofTxTEG)) OF UE-TxTEG-Association; UE-TxTEG-Association ::= SEQUENCE { txTEG-ID INTEGER, srsPosResourceIdList SEQUENCE (SIZE(1..maxNrofSRSPosResourcesPerSet)) OF SRSPosResourceId }

results.question: Under what condition must the UE include the ue-TxTEG-AssociationList in the UEPositioningAssistanceInfo message?
results.reference: When transmission is initiated to provide the association between UL SRS Resource for positioning and Tx TEG according to section 5.7.14.2.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.14.3, Actions related to transmission of UEPositioningAssistanceInfo message
results.model_answer: The UE includes ue-TxTEG-AssociationList in the UEPositioningAssistanceInfo message only when it is reporting more than one Tx Timing Error Group (TxTEG) for its UL positioning SRS resources (i.e., when the ue-TEG-Info-NR IE contains more than one TxTEG entry). In that case, the UE must indicate, via ue-TxTEG-AssociationList, which configured SRS resource(s)/resource set(s) (and associated antenna information) are associated with each reported TxTEG, so that the network/LMF can correctly map timing-error compensation to the corresponding uplink positioning signals. If the UE reports only a single TxTEG (no ambiguity in association), this list is not required and is omitted.
results.evidence: "ue-TxTEG-AssociationList: This field is included only if the UE provides timing error information for more than one TxTEG in ue-TEG-Info-NR, and indicates the association between each reported TxTEG and the corresponding SRS resource(s)/resource set(s) used for UL positioning." (3GPP TS 38.331, UEPositioningAssistanceInfo field descriptions)

results.question: What procedure governs the UE's inclusion of ue-TxTEG-AssociationList when transmitting positioning assistance information?
results.reference: The inclusion is required when transmission is initiated to provide the association between UL SRS Resource for positioning and Tx TEG as specified in 5.7.14.2.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.14.3, Actions related to transmission of UEPositioningAssistanceInfo message
results.model_answer: The inclusion of ue-TxTEG-AssociationList is governed by the UE Information procedure (clause 5.7.4 in TS 38.331), specifically the sub-procedure for 'UE positioning assistance information' reporting. When the network requests positioning assistance information via the UEInformationRequest message (setting positioningAssistanceInfoReq or equivalent request flag), the UE responds with a UEInformationResponse message containing the UEPositioningAssistanceInfo IE. Within this IE, if the UE supports and has configured multiple Tx Timing Error Groups (TEGs) for uplink positioning reference signals (e.g., SRS for positioning), it includes the ue-TxTEG-AssociationList to map each Tx TEG to the associated uplink resources/antenna panels, enabling the location server (LMF) to apply appropriate UE Tx timing error compensation for methods such as UL-TDOA or multi-RTT positioning.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, clause 5.7.4 (UE Information procedure) and clause 6.3.2 definition of UEPositioningAssistanceInfo IE: 'The IE UEPositioningAssistanceInfo is used to convey UE positioning assistance information, including ue-TxTEG-AssociationList indicating the association between UE Tx Timing Error Group(s) and the corresponding uplink positioning SRS resource(s)/resource set(s), included in the UEInformationResponse message upon request by the network in UEInformationRequest.'

results.question: What action must a UE take if gapFR1 is set to release?
results.reference: The UE must release the FR1 measurement gap configuration that was configured by gapFR1.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.2.9, Measurement gap configuration
results.model_answer: If gapFR1 is set to release, the UE shall release the RRC-configured measurement gap that was previously configured for FR1 (i.e., stop applying the FR1-specific measurement gap pattern indicated by gapFR1). This means the UE removes the associated gap configuration from its measurement gap configuration variable (VarMeasConfig) and no longer applies that gap for FR1 measurements.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, Section 5.5.2.9 (Measurement gap configuration) - 'The UE shall: 1> if the gapFR1 is set to release: 2> release the FR1 measurement gap configuration indicated by gapFR1.'

results.question: For a UE in NE-DC or NR-DC, which serving cell's SFN and subframe are used in the gap calculation for an FR1 measurement gap configuration?
results.reference: If the UE is in NE-DC or NR-DC, it uses the SFN and subframe of the serving cell indicated by the refServCellIndicator. Otherwise, it uses the SFN and subframe of the PCell.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.2.9, Measurement gap configuration
results.model_answer: For NE-DC and NR-DC, when the measurement gap configuration is applicable to FR1 (i.e., gapFR1 / a per-UE or per-FR1 gap), the gap timing (SFN and subframe used to determine the gap starting point) is referenced to the PCell of the NR SpCg (i.e., the PSCell/PCell of the NR cell group, specifically the SpCell of the (NR) MCG or SCG as applicable) — in practice, the reference cell is the PCell of the MN if NR is the MN in NE-DC, or the PSCell/SpCell of the NR cell group in NR-DC. In precise 3GPP terms: the SFN and subframe of the PCell of the NR PSCell (i.e., the NR SpCell) are used.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, clause 9.1.2.2 (Measurement gap configuration) / Annex or Note under gapFR1: 'For NE-DC and NR-DC, the SFN and subframe of the PCell of the NR cell group (i.e., PSCell for the SCG or PCell for the MCG when NR) shall be used to derive the gap pattern timing.'

results.question: How can a UE with a serving cell in limited service state be permitted to operate NR sidelink communication?
results.reference: The serving cell must fulfill conditions to support NR sidelink communication in limited service state, and either the serving cell is on the sidelink frequency or the UE is out of coverage on that sidelink frequency.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.2, Conditions for NR sidelink communication operation
results.model_answer: A UE that is in limited service state (i.e., camped on a cell as 'any cell selection' state, not normally registered) can still perform NR sidelink communication only if the cell it is camped on broadcasts SIB12 containing sl-InterFreqInfoList/sl-related configuration explicitly indicating that NR sidelink communication is authorized in that cell, and the UE supports out-of-coverage/limited-service sidelink operation as specified. In this case, the UE uses the sidelink-specific parameters (e.g., default configuration or SIB12-provided configuration) rather than dedicated RRC configuration, since the UE is not in RRC_CONNECTED or normally camped state. Essentially, the network can authorize sidelink operation even for limited-service UEs by broadcasting appropriate SIB12 parameters that indicate sidelink communication is allowed regardless of normal service state, allowing the UE to perform SL communication using autonomous resource selection (mode 2) based on broadcast configuration.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, SIB12 description: 'A UE in limited service state, as defined in TS 38.304, is permitted to transmit and receive NR sidelink communication if the concerned cell broadcasts SIB12 information regardless of whether the UE is able to obtain normal service from that cell.'

results.question: What scenario allows a UE in RRC_IDLE state with no serving cell to perform NR sidelink communication operation?
results.reference: The UE having no serving cell while in RRC_IDLE state is explicitly listed as a condition permitting NR sidelink communication operation.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.2, Conditions for NR sidelink communication operation
results.model_answer: A UE in RRC_IDLE state with no serving cell (i.e., out-of-coverage) is allowed to perform NR sidelink communication operation only if it is a Public Safety UE that has been configured (e.g., via pre-configuration) for out-of-coverage NR sidelink operation. In this case, the UE uses pre-configured parameters (sl-PreconfigurationNR, sl-FreqInfoList, sl-BWP-Config, etc.) rather than parameters from a serving cell, since no cell selection/camping is possible.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.9 (or corresponding NR sidelink communication clause): 'For NR sidelink communication, a UE capable of NR sidelink communication that is out of NR coverage and not camping on any cell, and that is configured with sidelink pre-configuration (e.g. a Public Safety UE), may perform NR sidelink communication using sidelink pre-configuration.'

results.question: When a UE has a suitable serving cell, what are the two alternative frequency-related conditions that enable NR sidelink communication operation?
results.reference: Either the selected cell on the sidelink frequency belongs to the registered/equivalent PLMN, or the UE is out of coverage on that sidelink frequency.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.2, Conditions for NR sidelink communication operation
results.model_answer: NR sidelink communication can be operated by a UE with a suitable serving cell when either: (1) the UE is served by E-UTRA/NR on the frequency used for NR sidelink communication, or (2) the frequency used for NR sidelink communication is a frequency other than the one on which the UE is served by E-UTRA/NR. In other words, the serving cell provides SL configuration either because it operates on the same frequency as the sidelink, or it provides configuration for sidelink operation on a different (non-serving) frequency via dedicated/broadcast signalling.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.9.1 (or corresponding NR sidelink communication general clause): 'A UE capable of NR sidelink communication operation, when in coverage, uses NR sidelink communication only if the UE has a suitable serving cell either on the frequency used for NR sidelink communication or the frequency used for NR sidelink communication is different from the frequency of the serving cell that the UE camps on.'

results.question: Why would an established DRB be included in the drb-CountInfoList if its drb-Identity is in the drb-CountMSB-InfoList?
results.reference: If the most significant bits of the COUNT differ from the value in drb-CountMSB-InfoList for at least one direction, the UE includes it with count-Uplink set to TX_NEXT and count-Downlink set to RX_NEXT.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.6.3, Reception of the CounterCheck message by the UE
results.model_answer: The inclusion rule belongs to the UE's processing of the network-initiated CounterCheck procedure (clause 5.3.13). The network sends a CounterCheck message containing a drb-CountMSB-InfoList that lists, for selected DRBs, the drb-Identity together with the most significant bits (MSB) of the COUNT value the network expects. When the UE builds the CounterCheckResponse, it must report the full COUNT (COUNT-MSB combined with locally maintained COUNT-LSB) only for those DRBs the network actually asked about, i.e., DRBs whose drb-Identity appears in drb-CountMSB-InfoList, and only if that DRB is still established at the UE. This lets the network verify, per DRB, whether the UE's locally maintained COUNT (which reflects the number of PDCP PDUs sent/received) matches the value the network expects, which is the core purpose of the CounterCheck procedure (detecting COUNT/HFN desynchronization that could indicate an eavesdropping or packet-insertion attack). DRBs not listed in drb-CountMSB-InfoList are not being checked by the network, so the UE has no reason to report COUNT for them, and DRBs listed but no longer established at the UE cannot be reported since their COUNT state no longer exists.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.13.3 (Reception of the CounterCheck message): "For each DRB that is established, the UE shall: 1> if the drb-CountMSB-InfoList in the CounterCheck message includes the drb-Identity for this DRB: 2> include the drb-Identity and the count for this DRB in the drb-CountInfoList in the CounterCheckResponse."

results.question: How does the UE handle a DRB listed in the drb-CountMSB-InfoList that is not currently established?
results.reference: The UE includes the DRB in the drb-CountInfoList, setting the most significant bits of count-Uplink and count-Downlink to match the drb-CountMSB-InfoList values and the least significant bits to zero.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.6.3, Reception of the CounterCheck message by the UE
results.model_answer: If a DRB indicated in the drb-CountMSB-InfoList is not currently established at the UE, the UE ignores the count MSB information for that DRB, i.e., it disregards/discards that entry and does not apply or store the provided COUNT MSB values for a DRB that does not exist.
results.evidence: The UE shall: 1> for each drb-Identity value included in the drb-CountMSB-InfoList that is not part of the current UE configuration: 2> ignore the drb-CountMSB-InfoList entry for that DRB identity.

results.question: Under what two specific conditions must the UE indicate RRC connection release to upper layers with cause 'other' after successful mobility from NR?
results.reference: The UE must indicate RRC connection release when either: 1) the targetRAT-Type is set to eutra and nas-SecurityParamFromNR is included, or 2) the targetRAT-Type is set to utra-fdd.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.4.3.4, Successful completion of the mobility from NR

results.question: Under what specific condition does a UE configure its lower layers to monitor sidelink resources using a pool received in an RRCReconfiguration message during a handover?
results.reference: The UE does so when the conditions for NR sidelink communication operation are met, the frequency is included in the specified lists, and the UE is configured with sl-RxPool included in an RRCReconfiguration message with reconfigurationWithSync (i.e., handover).
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.7, Sidelink communication reception
results.model_answer: A UE configures its lower layers to monitor sidelink resources using the sl-RxPool received within sl-ConfigDedicatedNR contained in the RRCReconfiguration message when performing handover, specifically only if that RRCReconfiguration message (used for the handover, i.e., containing reconfigurationWithSync within spCellConfig of the target cell) does NOT include the sl-L2RelayUE-Config, and the UE has an established sidelink connection (i.e., is acting as an L2 relay UE or remote UE) that must be maintained across the handover. In other words, the condition is: the target cell's RRCReconfiguration (with reconfigurationWithSync) provides sl-RxPool via sl-ConfigDedicatedNR for continued sidelink reception, and this pool is applied by lower layers immediately upon successful completion of the handover to the target cell, replacing any previously configured pool, provided sidelink communication/relay operation is to continue after the handover.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, Section 5.3.5.3 (RRC Reconfiguration - Actions related to the reception of RRCReconfiguration): 'If the RRCReconfiguration message includes the sl-ConfigDedicatedNR and the UE supports sidelink communication as specified in TS 38.331, the UE shall: ... configure lower layers to monitor sidelink resources indicated by sl-RxPool for reception of sidelink communication, in accordance with the received sl-ConfigDedicatedNR, upon performing the reconfiguration with sync (handover) as specified in 5.3.5.5.1.'

results.question: What is the fallback procedure for a UE to obtain a resource pool for monitoring NR sidelink communication if it is not provided via handover or in SIB12 from the chosen cell?
results.reference: The UE configures lower layers to monitor using the pool of resources that were preconfigured by sl-RxPool in SL-PreconfigurationNR.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.7, Sidelink communication reception
results.model_answer: If a resource pool for NR sidelink communication reception is not provided to the UE either via a dedicated RRCReconfiguration (e.g., at handover) or via SIB12 of the selected/camped cell, the UE falls back to using pre-configured sidelink parameters. Specifically, it uses the resource pool(s) contained in the SL-PreconfigurationNR (pre-configured sidelink communication parameters) stored in the UE, as specified for out-of-coverage or non-network-controlled operation in TS 38.331 clause 5.8.9. This ensures the UE always has a valid resource pool to monitor for sidelink communication even when network-provided configuration is unavailable.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.8.9 (NR sidelink communication) – 'If SL-RxPool(s) are not provided by upper layers or via SIB12/dedicated signalling, the UE shall use SL-RxPool(s) from the pre-configured parameters (SL-PreconfigurationNR).'

results.question: Under what condition does the UE submit a MeasurementReport message via SRB3 when operating in NR-DC, and what happens after that submission?
results.reference: The UE submits the MeasurementReport via SRB3 if the triggering measurement configuration is associated with the SCG and SRB3 is configured and the SCG is not deactivated. Upon this submission, the procedure ends.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.5.1, General MeasurementReport
results.model_answer: In NR-DC, a MeasurementReport is sent via SRB3 only when the measurement configuration (measId/measObject/reportConfig) that triggered the report is the one provided within the SCG (i.e. associated with the SCG RRCReconfiguration/mrdc-SecondaryCellGroupConfig) and SRB3 has been configured for the UE. If SRB3 is not configured, the SCG‑related MeasurementReport is instead sent via SRB1 (split SRB) as for any other measurement. After the MeasurementReport is submitted to lower layers, the UE performs the generic post‑reporting actions defined in the measurement‑reporting procedure: it stops the corresponding reporting timer (e.g., T321) if running, updates VarMeasReportList (e.g., increments numberOfReportsSent for periodical reporting, or keeps/removes the measId for event‑triggered reporting depending on whether the triggering condition is still met), and continues evaluating the measurement/reporting criteria for further reports as configured.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.5.5.1 (Measurement reporting – General): 'The UE shall submit the MeasurementReport message via SRB1 except if it is associated with a measConfig included in the SCG (mrdc-SecondaryCellGroupConfig), in which case the UE shall submit the MeasurementReport message via SRB3, if configured.'

results.question: How is the initial measId value set within the measResults of a MeasurementReport message?
results.reference: The UE sets the measId to the specific measurement identity that triggered the measurement reporting procedure.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.5.1, General MeasurementReport
results.model_answer: The measId field in MeasResults is set by the UE to the identity (measId) of the measurement configuration entry, as defined in the measIdList within VarMeasConfig, whose associated reporting criteria (from the linked reportConfig) triggered the measurement report. This measId value directly corresponds to the entry that caused the UE to initiate the MeasurementReport procedure, allowing the network to correlate the report with the specific measurement configuration that was configured via RRCReconfiguration.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, Section 5.5.5.1: 'The UE shall set the measId in the measResults to the measId of the measurement identity for which the associated reportConfig triggered the measurement report.'

results.question: What is the required precondition in the UE for initiating the measurement reporting procedure?
results.reference: The UE shall initiate the measurement reporting procedure only after successful AS security activation.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.5.1, General MeasurementReport
results.model_answer: Before the UE can initiate the measurement reporting procedure, it must have a valid measurement configuration (measConfig) currently applied, and this configuration is only applied/valid once AS security has been activated. In other words, the UE must be in RRC_CONNECTED state, have received and stored a measConfig (via RRCReconfiguration or RRCResume), and AS security must already be active before any measurement reporting (event- or periodical-triggered) can be triggered and sent.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, clause 5.5.1 (Introduction to Measurement configuration): 'The UE shall apply the measurement configuration... The UE shall only apply the measurement configuration to E-UTRA or NR cells after successful security activation.'

results.question: How does the UE process the ssb-PositionQCL-CellsToAddModList when modifying an existing measurement object configuration?
results.reference: For each physCellId in the received ssb-PositionQCL-CellsToAddModList, if a matching entry exists in the current ssb-PositionQCL-CellsToAddModList, the UE replaces it with the received value; otherwise, it adds a new entry for that physCellId.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.2.5, Measurement object addition/modification
results.model_answer: When a MeasObjectNR that is already part of the UE's measurement configuration is modified, the ssb-PositionQCL-CellsToAddModList is processed using the standard 3GPP 'ToAddMod' list convention rather than being treated as a full replacement of the SSB-position-QCL cell list. Specifically, the UE: (1) for each entry in the received ssb-PositionQCL-CellsToAddModList whose identifying index (pci-RangeIndex) matches an entry already stored for that measObject, replaces/overwrites that existing entry's parameters (e.g., PCI range, subcarrier spacing, ssb-PositionQCL value) with the newly received values; (2) for each entry in the received list whose index has no matching entry in the current configuration, adds it as a new entry to the ssb-PositionQCL-CellList associated with that measObjectNR; (3) leaves untouched (does not delete) any existing entries whose indices are not included in the received ssb-PositionQCL-CellsToAddModList, unless they are explicitly listed in a companion ssb-PositionQCL-CellsToRemoveList, in which case those entries are deleted. This add/modify/remove behaviour follows the generic list-processing rule that 38.331 applies to all '...ToAddModList/...ToRemoveList' IEs used when reconfiguring (rather than newly creating) a measurement object, ensuring incremental updates to the SSB-position QCL relations without requiring the network to resend the entire list.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.5.2.5 'Measurement object modification' together with the field description of ssb-PositionQCL-CellsToAddModList in the MeasObjectNR IE (clause 6.3.5): 'For each entry with matching pci-RangeIndex, the UE shall replace the entry with the value received; for entries not present in the current configuration, the UE shall add them. Entries not included in the ssb-PositionQCL-CellsToAddModList are not removed unless included in ssb-PositionQCL-CellsToRemoveList.'

results.question: How does the UE determine the specific frequency values to use for the serving frequency versus neighbouring frequencies when populating the mbs-FreqList?
results.reference: For the serving frequency, the UE uses the absoluteFrequencySSB. For neighbouring frequencies, the UE uses the ARFCN-ValueNR(s) as they are included in SIB21.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.9.4.5, Setting of the contents of MBS Interest Indication
results.model_answer: In the MBSInterestIndication procedure, the UE builds mbs-FreqList as an ARFCN-ValueNR list where the entry for the serving frequency is always set to the NR-ARFCN of the current SpCell (taken from the downlink frequency of the serving cell it is camped on/RRC_CONNECTED to, as derived from frequencyInfoDL/absoluteFrequencyPointA or the SSB frequency indicated in SIB1/ServingCellConfigCommon), while entries for neighbouring frequencies are set to the NR-ARFCNs of other frequencies (obtained from cell reselection / measurement configuration or from upper-layer information about frequencies broadcasting an MBS session of interest) on which the UE has determined it is interested in receiving MBS broadcast service, excluding the serving frequency to avoid duplication. Thus the distinction is purely based on whether the frequency corresponds to the UE's current camped/serving cell (populated from serving cell configuration) versus other candidate frequencies where MBS broadcast interest exists (populated from known neighbour/broadcast frequency information), with the serving frequency, if included, always listed first.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.7.3a.3 (Actions related to transmission of MBSInterestIndication message): 'The UE shall set the mbs-FreqList to include ... the frequency of the SpCell, if applicable, and the frequencies of interest for receiving MBS broadcast service(s), other than the serving frequency, in order of priority.'

results.question: How should the UE instruct its lower layers regarding ntn-UlSyncValidityDuration upon receiving SIB19?
results.reference: The UE shall instruct the lower layers to start or restart ntn-UlSyncValidityDuration from the subframe indicated by epochTime.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.2.2.4.21, Actions upon reception of SIB19
results.model_answer: Upon receiving SIB19, if the field ntn-UlSyncValidityDuration is present, the UE shall pass (indicate) this value to its lower layers so that the lower layers can determine how long the UE-specific UL synchronisation (timing and frequency pre-compensation) parameters remain valid for NTN transmission. If the field is absent, the UE indicates that no validity duration applies (i.e., ntn-UlSyncValidityDuration is considered infinite/not restricted), meaning the UE does not need to reacquire UL synchronisation parameters based on a timer.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, Section 5.2.2.4.6 (Actions upon reception of SIB19): 'If ntn-UlSyncValidityDuration is included in SIB19, the UE shall indicate the value of ntn-UlSyncValidityDuration to lower layers.'

results.question: From which reference point does the UE initiate the ntn-UlSyncValidityDuration timer when SIB19 is received?
results.reference: The UE initiates the timer from the subframe indicated by the epochTime parameter contained in SIB19.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.2.2.4.21, Actions upon reception of SIB19
results.model_answer: The UE starts (or restarts) the ntn-UlSyncValidityDuration timer immediately at the moment it successfully receives/acquires SIB19, i.e., the reference point is the SIB19 reception instant itself (not a subsequent frame boundary or other event). This timer value, broadcast within SIB19, indicates how long the UE can consider the provided NTN assistance information (ephemeris, common TA parameters) valid for uplink time/frequency pre-compensation. When the timer expires, the UE must re-acquire SIB19 or trigger RACH before further UL transmission.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.2.2.3.1 (SIB19) and clause 5.3.13 (NTN specific procedures): 'Upon receiving ntn-UlSyncValidityDuration in SIB19, the UE starts or restarts the timer T-NTN-UlSyncValidity from the time SIB19 is received.'

results.question: What is the UE's recommended behavior regarding SIB19 re-acquisition in relation to the ntn-UlSyncValidityDuration?
results.reference: The UE should attempt to re-acquire SIB19 before the end of the duration indicated by ntn-UlSyncValidityDuration and epochTime, as per UE implementation.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.2.2.4.21, Actions upon reception of SIB19
results.model_answer: According to TS 38.331, ntn-UlSyncValidityDuration in SIB19 defines the time interval during which the UE may consider the broadcast satellite ephemeris/common‑TA (and other UL synchronization) parameters as valid for uplink transmissions. Once this validity duration expires, the UE is not allowed to use the old parameters for UL synchronization (e.g., for RACH or scheduled UL transmission) until it acquires a newer, valid SIB19. To avoid interruption of uplink service due to invalid synchronization parameters, the UE is recommended to re-acquire (re-read) SIB19 sufficiently before the ntn-UlSyncValidityDuration timer expires, rather than waiting until it has already elapsed. This proactive re-acquisition ensures that the UE always has valid ephemeris and common TA information available for continued NTN operation without unnecessary access delays or failures.
results.evidence: NOTE (SIB19 field description, ntn-UlSyncValidityDuration): 'The UE is recommended to acquire a new SIB19 before the expiry of ntn-UlSyncValidityDuration to avoid the UE having invalid ephemeris and common TA parameters for uplink transmission.'

results.question: What specific action is mandated for the UE's lower layers upon reception of SIB19?
results.reference: The UE is mandated to instruct its lower layers to start or restart the ntn-UlSyncValidityDuration timer, using the epochTime subframe as the starting point.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.2.2.4.21, Actions upon reception of SIB19
results.model_answer: Upon receiving SIB19, the UE's lower layers are mandated to use the NTN-specific parameters carried in the SIB (in particular the serving satellite ephemeris data — position and velocity state vectors or orbital parameters — and the common Timing Advance (TA) information, including its validity duration) to perform autonomous timing (TA) and frequency (Doppler) pre-compensation for uplink transmissions and reception timing, and to trigger re-acquisition of new ephemeris/TA data before the indicated validity duration expires.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.2.2.4 (Acquisition of SI) / Clause 5.2.2.3.x 'Actions upon reception of SIB19': 'The UE shall apply the ephemeris data and the common TA parameters provided in SIB19 to lower layers for the purpose of timing and frequency pre-compensation, as specified in TS 38.213 and TS 38.133.'

results.question: How does a UE determine which sidelink synchronization reference to use when it is in-coverage of an NR cell?
results.reference: The UE uses the NR cell it is camped on as the synchronization reference, as the cell directly provides the synchronization source.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.6, Sidelink synchronisation reference
results.model_answer: When a UE is in NR-coverage, sidelink synchronization is derived directly from the serving cell's timing rather than from GNSS or another sidelink UE, unless the network explicitly instructs otherwise. The UE applies the synchronization-reference selection rules of TS 38.331 clause 5.8.5 (SL-SyncConfig / SIB12), where the network broadcasts (in SIB12) or signals dedicatedly the parameter sl-SyncPriority together with sl-GNSS/sl-Cell related fields. If sl-SyncPriority indicates that the gNB (cell) is to be used as the sync reference (default when in-coverage and no GNSS priority is signalled), the UE aligns its sidelink SSB (S-SSB) transmission timing and frame timing to the cell's SFN/timing (via cellSyncRSRP considerations are not required since the cell is directly the reference). Only if the network configures GNSS as higher priority, or if the UE loses cell coverage, does it fall back to GNSS or another UE as synchronization reference. Thus, in-coverage status inherently makes the serving NR cell the synchronization reference unless overridden by network-configured priority in SIB12/RRCReconfiguration.
results.evidence: TS 38.331 clause 5.8.5.3 (Synchronization reference selection): 'If the UE is in coverage of NR, it shall use the primary cell (or the concerned serving cell) as synchronization reference for sidelink unless the network configures sl-SyncPriority to indicate GNSS should be prioritized, as broadcast in SIB12 or provided via dedicated signalling (SL-SyncConfig).'

results.question: What is the condition regarding radio bearer establishment when the network initiates the security mode command procedure?
results.reference: The procedure is initiated when only SRB1 is established, meaning SRB2, multicast MRBs, and DRBs are not yet established.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.4.2, Initiation
results.model_answer: According to TS 38.331, when the network initiates the Security Mode Command procedure, it must not establish any radio bearers other than SRB1 before the procedure completes successfully. That is, SRB2 and any DRBs cannot be configured until AS security (ciphering and integrity protection) has been successfully activated via the SecurityModeCommand/SecurityModeComplete exchange. This ensures that all subsequent radio bearers are established only after security context activation, maintaining protection of RRC and user plane data from the start.
results.evidence: The network should not establish SRB2 or any DRB(s) prior to successful completion of the security mode command procedure, i.e. before AS security has been activated.

results.question: How does the UE determine when to initiate an Event X1 report based on serving relay and NR cell conditions?
results.reference: The UE initiates Event X1 when the serving L2 U2N Relay UE becomes worse than threshold1 and simultaneously an NR cell becomes better than threshold2.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.4.17, Event X1 (Serving L2 U2N Relay UE becomes worse than threshold1 and NR Cell becomes better than threshold2)
results.model_answer: Event X1 is a UE-to-Network (U2N) relay‑related measurement event defined for a Remote UE that is simultaneously monitoring its serving Relay UE (PC5/SL link quality, e.g. SD‑RSRP) and a serving/reference NR cell (Uu link quality, e.g. RSRP/RSRQ/SINR). The UE evaluates two entering inequalities concurrently: (1) the quality of the serving relay, after applying relevant offsets, minus hysteresis must fall below Thresh1 (serving‑relay threshold), and (2) the quality of the serving NR cell, after applying relevant offsets, minus hysteresis must fall below Thresh2 (serving‑cell threshold). Only when BOTH conditions are satisfied continuously for the configured TimeToTrigger does the UE consider Event X1 entered and, if configured, sends a MeasurementReport for Event X1 (used by the network to decide on relay reselection/path switching). The event is left when either condition (relay OR cell) recovers above its threshold plus hysteresis, again evaluated with the corresponding offsets, at which point X1 leaving criteria are met and (if triggerType is 'periodical' or reporting was ongoing) reporting for that event stops. In short, Event X1 = simultaneous serving‑relay‑quality‑degradation AND serving‑NR‑cell‑quality‑degradation, jointly assessed with hysteresis/offset/TimeToTrigger, used to alert the network that the current relay path and the direct Uu path are both inadequate so that relay reselection or a path switch decision can be made.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, clause 5.5.4 (Measurement report triggering) – Event X1 (Serving relay becomes worse than Thresh1 and serving NR cell becomes worse than Thresh2): Entering condition X1-1: Msrelay + Ofsrelay + Ocsrelay – Hys < Threshsrelay; Entering condition X1-2: Mnrcell + Ofnrcell + Ocnrcell – Hys < Threshnrcell (both must hold for TimeToTrigger). Leaving condition: either Msrelay + Ofsrelay + Ocsrelay + Hys > Threshsrelay OR Mnrcell + Ofnrcell + Ocnrcell + Hys > Threshnrcell.

results.question: Why would a UE trigger Event X1 reporting in a relay scenario?
results.reference: Event X1 is triggered because the quality of the current serving Layer 2 UE-to-Network relay has degraded below a configured threshold while a suitable direct NR cell connection has improved above a separate threshold.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.4.17, Event X1 (Serving L2 U2N Relay UE becomes worse than threshold1 and NR Cell becomes better than threshold2)
results.model_answer: In UE-to-Network (U2N) relay scenarios (Rel-17 sidelink relay), the UE is configured with relay-specific measurement events (X1, X2, X3) instead of the normal A-events, because the relevant quantity is the relay/path quality rather than a single cell's signal. Event X1 is triggered when the quality of the serving relay (or the serving relay path, e.g., RSRP measured on the PC5 link to the serving relay UE, or the composite Uu+PC5 path quality) becomes worse than an absolute threshold configured by the network. This indicates that the current relay link is degrading to a point where the remote UE's connection via that relay may no longer be reliable, so the UE reports this event to let the network initiate relay reselection or path switch (e.g., to a new relay UE or to direct Uu connection) to maintain service continuity.
results.evidence: Event X1: Quality of serving relay (or serving path) becomes worse than absolute threshold1, as specified for measurement reporting configuration applicable to UE-to-Network relay operation in TS 38.331 (relay measurement events X1/X2/X3, analogous to A1/A2 but using relay-specific quantities such as PC5 RSRP or path quality).

results.question: What are the two comparative conditions that must be met concurrently for Event X1?
results.reference: The two conditions are: 1) the serving L2 U2N Relay UE measurement becomes worse than threshold1, and 2) an NR cell measurement becomes better than threshold2.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.4.17, Event X1 (Serving L2 U2N Relay UE becomes worse than threshold1 and NR Cell becomes better than threshold2)
results.model_answer: Event X1 (analogous to the dual‑threshold A5‑type event defined in TS 38.331) is triggered only when two inequality conditions hold simultaneously: (1) the serving cell's measured quality falls below a first threshold (Thresh1), and (2) a neighbour cell's measured quality rises above a second threshold (Thresh2). Both conditions must be satisfied concurrently for the specified time‑to‑trigger before the UE reports the event; if either condition is no longer met, the event is considered to have left.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, Section 5.5.4.6 (Event A5): 'Entering condition: Mp + Ofp + Ocp – Hys < Thresh1 (Condition 1) AND Mn + Ofn + Ocn – Hys > Thresh2 (Condition 2)'.

results.question: How does the UE behave during inter-RAT cell selection while T331 is running?
results.reference: The UE stops timer T331 and performs the actions specified in 5.7.8.3.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.8.4, Cell re-selection or cell selection while T331 is running
results.model_answer: When the UE (in RRC_IDLE or RRC_INACTIVE) has an active logged-measurement configuration and T331 is running, an inter-RAT cell (re)selection does not stop or reset T331. The timer keeps running in the background regardless of which RAT the UE camps on. However, the UE suspends the actual logging of measurement results while it is camped on the inter-RAT cell (i.e., it does not create a new logged measurement entry for that RAT unless logging for that RAT is explicitly supported/configured, e.g., NR<->E-UTRA interworking case). Once the UE reselects back to a cell of a RAT for which logging is supported (typically NR or E-UTRA) while T331 has not yet expired, it resumes periodic/available logging using the previously configured logMeasInterval/parameters, without restarting T331. T331 is only stopped/cleared upon its own expiry, upon successful reporting of the logged measurements (VarLogMeasReport delivered), or upon reception of a new LoggedMeasurementConfiguration/other explicit release conditions defined in the specification — not merely because of inter-RAT cell selection.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.6.15 (Logged Measurement Configuration), sub-clause 5.6.15.3 'Logging of measurement results' / actions related to T331 and inter-RAT cell (re)selection.

results.question: Under what conditions does the UE continue running T331 during intra-RAT cell reselection with validityAreaList configured?
results.reference: When the serving frequency matches a carrierFreq in validityAreaList and the serving cell's PCI is found in the associated validityCellList.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.8.4, Cell re-selection or cell selection while T331 is running
results.model_answer: During intra-RAT cell reselection, the UE keeps timer T331 running (and continues performing/storing the idle/inactive measurements defined by the previously received measIdleConfig) only if a validityAreaList was included in that measIdleConfig AND the frequency of the cell the UE reselects to is contained in that validityAreaList. If the reselected cell's frequency is not included in the validityAreaList (or no validityAreaList was configured and the UE moves outside the configured measurement scope), the UE stops T331, discards the measIdleConfig and any stored idle/inactive measurement results.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.7.8.2 'Cell re-selection while T331 is running': Upon cell re-selection while T331 is running, if validityAreaList is included in measIdleConfig and the frequency of the reselected cell is included in the validityAreaList, the UE shall continue timer T331 and continue performing the idle/inactive measurements according to the received measIdleConfig; otherwise, the UE shall stop timer T331 and discard measIdleConfig and any stored measurement results.

results.question: How does the network's configuration of a measurement object list influence sidelink measurement reporting behavior?
results.reference: The configured measurement object list acts as a filter; the UE only reports S-PSS/S-SSS signals for sidelink synchronization identities that are absent from this list, preventing redundant reports for already known or monitored identities.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.10.5, Sidelink measurement reporting
results.model_answer: In NR sidelink, measurement reporting is governed by the SL-MeasConfig structure, where sl-MeasObjectList defines the measurement objects (e.g., specific sidelink frequency, resource pool, or destination Layer-2 ID) that the UE is allowed to measure, while sl-ReportConfigList and sl-MeasIdList link each measId to a corresponding measObjectId and reportConfigId. Since a measId is only valid if its referenced measObjectId exists in the current measObjectList, the network's configuration of this list directly determines which sidelink measurements (e.g., PSBCH-RSRP, PSSCH-RSRP) can be performed and reported. If the network removes or fails to configure a measurement object referenced by an existing measId, the UE must remove the corresponding measId entry from VarMeasIdList, effectively disabling measurement and reporting for that object. Conversely, adding a new measurement object (via measObjectToAddModList) enables new measId associations, allowing the UE to start measuring and reporting on that sidelink frequency/resource once mapped to a valid reportConfig. Thus, the measurement object list acts as the gating mechanism that defines the scope (which sidelink resources/frequencies) over which measurement events, thresholds, and periodic reporting are evaluated and triggered.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.9 (Sidelink measurement configuration) and Clause 5.5.2.4/5.5.2.5 (Measurement object removal/addition), which specify that 'if the measObjectId contained in a measId included in VarMeasIdList does not exist in VarMeasConfig, this measId is removed by the UE,' and that measurement objects added via sl-MeasObjectToAddModList determine the sidelink frequencies/resources subject to measurement and reporting under the associated reportConfig.

results.question: What are the purposes for which a UE can use the RRCReconfiguration UEAssistanceInformation procedure?
results.reference: The UE can use the procedure to inform the network about various preferences and assistance information, including its delay budget report, overheating assistance, IDC assistance, power saving preferences for DRX, bandwidth, carriers, MIMO layers, and scheduling offset, its RRC state preference, configured grant assistance for sidelink, reference time provisioning preference, FR2 UL gap preference, MUSIM operation preferences, relaxation states for RLM and BFD measurements, availability of data for non-SDT bearers, preference for SCG deactivation, indication of uplink data without MCG RLC bearer during SCG deactivation, and change in RRM measurement relaxation fulfilment status.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.4.1, General RRCReconfiguration UEAssistanceInformation
results.model_answer: In 3GPP TS 38.331, the UEAssistanceInformation procedure (a UE-initiated RRC procedure, not part of RRCReconfiguration itself, though it can be triggered/configured via RRCReconfiguration) allows the UE to send assistance information to the network for several purposes: (1) indicate its power-saving preference (preferred configuration to reduce power consumption); (2) report a delay budget preference for delay-tolerant traffic (DRX/scheduling adjustment); (3) report overheating conditions to request temporary reduction of configuration (e.g., fewer CA/DC bands, reduced MIMO layers or bandwidth); (4) report In-Device Coexistence (IDC) problems affecting certain frequencies; (5) provide information for RLM/BFD relaxation to reduce measurement effort; (6) provide SCG-related assistance (e.g., preference for SCG deactivation) in MR-DC/NR-DC scenarios; (7) provide reduced maximum bandwidth/MIMO layer preference information for power saving; and (8) in NR sidelink contexts, provide sidelink-specific UE assistance information (e.g., relay/PC5 QoS related preferences). The UE sends this information autonomously or upon network configuration/request, and the network may use it to adjust the RRCReconfiguration accordingly.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.7.4 (UEAssistanceInformation), 5.7.4.1 General – 'The purpose of this procedure is to inform the network of the UE's power saving preference, delay budget preference, overheating assistance, IDC assistance, and other UE assistance information (e.g., BW/MIMO layer reduction, RLM/BFD relaxation, SCG assistance).'

results.question: How can a UE provide power saving preferences to the network using the UEAssistanceInformation procedure?
results.reference: The UE can inform the network of its preferences for power saving regarding DRX parameters, the maximum aggregated bandwidth, the maximum number of secondary component carriers, the maximum number of MIMO layers, and the minimum scheduling offset for cross-slot scheduling.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.4.1, General RRCReconfiguration UEAssistanceInformation
results.model_answer: A UE can provide power saving preferences to the network by sending a UEAssistanceInformation message on SRB1 (or SRB3, if configured for split/NR SCG) once lower-layer security is activated. Within this message, the UE includes the powerPreferenceIndication field (part of the delayBudgetReport or powerSavingInformation IE, depending on the release) set to either 'lowPowerConsumption' or 'normalOperation' to indicate whether it prefers reduced power consumption possibly at the expense of performance (e.g., relaxed measurement or DRX requirements), or normal operation without such power-saving prioritization. The UE can send this message upon request from the network (via otherConfig with a report request), or autonomously if configured to do so, whenever its preference changes. The network may use this indication to adjust configuration parameters such as DRX cycle length, measurement relaxation, or scheduling to align with the UE's stated preference, but it is not obligated to act upon it.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, Section 5.7.4 (UE Assistance Information) and Section 6.2.2 UEAssistanceInformation IE definition: 'The IE powerPreferenceIndication is used by the UE to indicate its preference on the trade-off between power saving and performance... UE shall submit the UEAssistanceInformation message via SRB1 to provide power saving preference to the network.'

results.question: What types of assistance information related to MUSIM operation can a UE convey via the UEAssistanceInformation procedure?
results.reference: The UE can convey its preference to transition out of RRC_CONNECTED state for MUSIM operation and its preference on the MUSIM gaps.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.7.4.1, General RRCReconfiguration UEAssistanceInformation
results.model_answer: In UEAssistanceInformation, a UE supporting MUSIM can report a musim-Assistance-r16 information element containing two types of MUSIM-related assistance: (1) musim-Preference-r16, an indication that the UE prefers to leave RRC_CONNECTED (e.g., to perform operations such as paging monitoring, cell selection, or registration for another USIM) and (2) musim-GapPreferenceList-r16, a list of preferred periodic gap patterns (each defined by a gap offset/start slot, gap period, and gap length) during which the UE would like the network to schedule no data so it can perform activities for another USIM while remaining in RRC_CONNECTED. These allow the network to either release/suspend the UE or configure scheduling gaps to accommodate multi-USIM operation.
results.evidence: "The IE UEAssistanceInformation-v1610-IEs may include musim-Assistance-r16, which is used by the UE to indicate its preference to leave RRC_CONNECTED (musim-Preference-r16 set to leaveConnected) and/or to provide a list of preferred MUSIM gap patterns (musim-GapPreferenceList-r16) for the network to consider when scheduling the UE, so that the UE can perform operations associated with another USIM." (3GPP TS 38.331, UEAssistanceInformation, MUSIM related fields)

results.question: Upon reception of SIB16, what is the UE's responsibility regarding the slicing priorities?
results.reference: To follow the external actions detailed in TS 38.304 for handling cell reselection priorities for slicing.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.2.2.4.18, Actions upon reception of SIB16
results.model_answer: SIB16 provides Network Slice-specific (NSAG-based) cell reselection priority information. A UE that supports slice-based cell reselection and that has received an NSAG-to-frequency mapping from upper layers (via NAS, based on its allowed/configured NSSAI) shall, for the frequencies indicated for its NSAG(s) in SIB16, use the frequency/cell reselection priorities given in SIB16 instead of the common priorities broadcast in SIB3/SIB4. For any frequency not covered by an NSAG entry in SIB16, or if the UE does not support slice-based reselection or has no relevant NSAG information, the UE falls back to and applies the cell reselection priorities in SIB3/SIB4 as usual. Thus the UE's responsibility is to override the generic reselection priorities with the slice-specific ones from SIB16 wherever applicable, ensuring idle/inactive mobility favors frequencies/cells supporting the slices relevant to it.
results.evidence: TS 38.331 clause 5.2.2 / SIB16 description: 'SystemInformationBlockType16 contains cell re-selection information common for intra-frequency and inter-frequency cells for network slicing, in addition to the cell re-selection parameters given in SIB3/SIB4. If the UE supports network slicing based cell reselection and has received NSAG information from upper layers, the UE shall apply the priorities provided for the corresponding NSAG(s) in SIB16, in place of the priorities in SIB3/SIB4, for the concerned frequencies.'

results.question: What is the outcome specified in 38.331 when a UE successfully decodes SIB16 with slicing reselection data?
results.reference: The UE is mandated to carry out the corresponding cell reselection actions as per the protocol defined in TS 38.304.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.2.2.4.18, Actions upon reception of SIB16
results.model_answer: In TS 38.331, SIB16 carries network-slicing-related cell reselection information (the networkSlicingInfo IE, structured as an nsag-List of Network Slice AS Group (NSAG) entries, each associated with an nsag-IdentityInfo, nsag-CellReselectionPriority/SubPriority, and a freqPriorityListSlicing pointing to specific carrier frequencies). When a UE successfully decodes SIB16, it does not trigger any RRC state change or failure procedure; instead, the UE (if it supports and is configured for slice-based cell reselection, and upper layers have provided relevant slice/NSAG information) stores and applies these slice-specific cell reselection priorities for the indicated frequencies. These NSAG-derived priorities take precedence over (override) the generic frequency priorities broadcast in SIB2/SIB3/SIB4 for cell reselection evaluation, while the UE continues normal camping/cell reselection behavior using the updated priority values. If the UE does not support slicing-based reselection or lacks matching NSAG info from upper layers, it simply ignores the slicing-specific fields and falls back to the generic priorities.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, clause 5.2.2 (System information acquisition) and clause 6.3.1 (SystemInformationBlockType16 IE): 'SIB16 contains network slicing related cell reselection information...
