Upon acquiring SIB16, if supported, the UE applies the NSAG-associated cell reselection priorities (nsag-CellReselectionPriority, nsag-CellReselectionSubPriority) for the frequencies listed in freqPriorityListSlicing, which take precedence over the priorities provided in other SIBs for cell reselection purposes.'

results.question: How does the L2 U2N Relay UE handle the release of a Uu-Relay-RLC-Channel when instructed via the uu-Relay-RLC-ChannelToReleaseList?
results.reference: For each relevant Uu-Relay-RLC-ChannelID, it releases the associated RLC entity according to TS 38.322 and then releases the corresponding logical channel.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.5.12, Uu Relay RLC channel release
results.model_answer: When the L2 U2N Relay UE receives an RRCReconfiguration containing uu-RelayRLC-ChannelToReleaseList, it processes each uu-RelayRLC-ChannelID in that list that is part of its current configuration by releasing the associated Uu Relay RLC channel resources. Specifically, for each identified channel, the Relay UE releases the corresponding RLC entity (as specified in TS 38.322), releases the associated logical channel, and removes the corresponding adaptation-layer mapping/entry (i.e., the mapping between the Uu Relay RLC channel and the remote UE's bearer/identity used for relaying). This release is performed as part of the general RRC reconfiguration procedure, following the same principle as other 'ToReleaseList' handling in 38.331 (release before applying any ToAddModList for the same procedure), ensuring that no data is subsequently relayed on the released RLC channel.
results.evidence: The UE shall, for each uu-RelayRLC-ChannelID value included in the uu-RelayRLC-ChannelToReleaseList that is part of the current UE configuration: 1> release the RLC entity as specified in TS 38.322; 1> release the corresponding logical channel; 1> release the corresponding entry in the adaptation layer, if configured.

results.question: Upon receiving a release command in the uu-Relay-RLC-ChannelToReleaseList, what two resources related to a Uu-Relay-RLC-ChannelID does the L2 U2N Relay UE deallocate?
results.reference: It releases the RLC entity, following the procedure in TS 38.322, clause 5.1.3, and releases the logical channel corresponding to that Uu-Relay-RLC-ChannelID.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.5.12, Uu Relay RLC channel release
results.model_answer: When the L2 U2N Relay UE receives a Uu-Relay-RLC-ChannelID in the uu-Relay-RLC-ChannelToReleaseList (via RRCReconfiguration), it releases the corresponding Uu Relay RLC channel by deallocating (1) the RLC entity associated with that Uu-Relay-RLC-ChannelID and (2) the logical channel identity (LCID) that was associated with that RLC entity/Uu Relay RLC channel.
results.evidence: For each value included in the uu-Relay-RLC-ChannelToReleaseList, if any, the UE shall: release the RLC entity and the associated logical channel identity, as specified in TS 38.322, for the Uu Relay RLC channel identified by Uu-Relay-RLC-ChannelID.

results.question: Why would a U2N Relay UE set the indicationType to relayUE-CellReselection in a NotificationMessageSidelink?
results.reference: Because the UE initiated transmission of the message due to a cell reselection procedure.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.9.10.3, Actions related to transmission of NotificationMessageSidelink message
results.model_answer: A U2N Relay UE sets indicationType to relayUE-CellReselection in a NotificationMessageSidelink to inform its connected U2N Remote UE(s) that the Relay UE itself has performed cell reselection (i.e., it has changed its serving cell/PCell). Since the Remote UE's connectivity to the network is anchored via the Relay UE's serving cell, this notification alerts the Remote UE that the relay's radio link/cell has changed, prompting the Remote UE to take appropriate action such as re-evaluating relay/path selection, triggering RRC re-establishment, or initiating a new relay (re)selection procedure to maintain service continuity, since the previous configuration tied to the old cell may no longer be valid.
results.evidence: In TS 38.331, the field description for indicationType in NotificationMessageSidelink states that value relayUE-CellReselection indicates that the U2N Relay UE has reselected a new cell, used to notify the U2N Remote UE via PC5-RRC signalling so that the Remote UE can take suitable action (e.g., re-establishment or relay reselection).

results.question: How does the network ensure measurement coverage for a UE with a measConfig associated with a Cell Group?
results.reference: The network ensures that whenever the UE has a measConfig for a Cell Group, that configuration includes a measurement object for the SpCell and for each NR SCell belonging to that Cell Group that needs to be measured.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.2.1, General
results.model_answer: In NR, a measConfig is always signalled as part of an RRCReconfiguration and, in Multi-Radio Dual Connectivity, is associated with a specific Cell Group (MCG or SCG) – i.e. it is generated and maintained by the node that controls that Cell Group (MN for MCG, SN for SCG). To guarantee that the UE can actually execute the measurements requested by that measConfig without loss of coverage or interruption of the associated Cell Group's data service, the network follows several complementary mechanisms defined in TS 38.331 clause 5.5.2: (1) it defines measObjects that correspond to the frequencies/cells relevant to that Cell Group's mobility needs (intra-frequency, inter-frequency, inter-RAT), so the UE always has an object to measure against for cells reachable from that CG's serving cell(s); (2) when the UE cannot measure a required frequency using its normal (non-gated) reception because of RF/tuner limitations, the network configures measGapConfig (per-UE, per-FR1 or per-FR2 gap patterns) so that the UE is granted periodic gaps in which to retune and measure, without these gaps disrupting reception on the concerned Cell Group beyond what is unavoidable; (3) it may use quantityConfig and s-MeasureConfig to control when measurements need to be performed (e.g., only below a certain serving cell quality), reducing unnecessary measurement gaps while still ensuring coverage/mobility measurements are taken when needed; and (4) for DC scenarios, the MN and SN coordinate (via Xn/X2) the gap sharing scheme so that gaps requested for the MCG's measConfig and gaps requested for the SCG's measConfig do not conflict, thereby ensuring each Cell Group's measConfig can be reliably executed. Together, these mechanisms let the network guarantee that a UE with a measConfig tied to a given Cell Group has adequate opportunity (via measObjects, gaps, and quantity/threshold control) to detect and report on cells needed for mobility, even though the UE's radio resources are simultaneously serving that Cell Group's active connection.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, clause 5.5.2 (Measurement configuration) – 'The measConfig, when associated with a Cell Group, is configured together with the necessary measObjects, reportConfigs, quantityConfig and, if required, measGapConfig (including per-UE/per-FR1/per-FR2 gap patterns) to ensure that the UE is able to perform the requested measurements without loss of coverage of the concerned Cell Group.'

results.question: What is the constraint on configuring measurement identities for reporting CGI information across multiple Cell Groups?
results.reference: The network is constrained to configure at most one measurement identity across all Cell Groups when using a reporting configuration where the reportType is set to reportCGI.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.2.1, General
results.model_answer: In NR RRC (TS 38.331), CGI reporting is triggered by a measId whose reportConfig has reportType set to reportCGI. The specification restricts the UE to have at most one such CGI-reporting measurement identity active at any time across the entire UE configuration, not per cell group. This means that even when the UE is configured with multiple cell groups (e.g., MCG and SCG in (NR-)DC), the network shall not configure more than one measId with reportType = reportCGI simultaneously across all cell groups combined. If a CGI-reporting measId already exists in one cell group (e.g., MCG), the network must remove or reuse it before/when configuring another CGI-reporting measId in a different cell group (e.g., SCG). This constraint avoids ambiguity in interpreting the requestedCellInfo/reportCGI results, since the UE can only perform and report one CGI acquisition procedure at a time.
results.evidence: "The network should not configure more than one measurement identity with reportType set to reportCGI at any given time across all cell groups configured for the UE."

results.question: How does the network handle SSB-based measurement objects with the same SSB frequency within a measConfig for a Cell Group?
results.reference: For all SSB-based measurements, the network ensures there is at most one measurement object with the same ssbFrequency. Furthermore, for any measurement objects sharing the same ssbFrequency, the values for smtc1, smtc2, smtc3list, and smtc4list must be identical if these fields are included.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.2.1, General
results.model_answer: In 3GPP TS 38.331, the network is required to ensure that within a single measConfig for a given Cell Group, there is at most one MeasObjectNR (SSB-based measurement object) associated with a particular SSB frequency (ssbFrequency). In other words, the same SSB frequency value cannot be configured in more than one measurement object entry within the same measConfig for a Cell Group. This avoids ambiguity in measurement reporting and ensures a one-to-one mapping between an SSB frequency and its associated cell-specific parameters (e.g., subcarrierSpacing, ssb-Periodicity, threshold values, etc.) for that Cell Group. If measurements on the same SSB frequency are needed for different purposes (e.g., different threshold sets), the network must use the same measurement object rather than creating a duplicate object with the same SSB frequency.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, Section 6.3.2, MeasObjectNR field description for ssbFrequency: 'The network configures the same value for the ssbFrequency within a measConfig for a Cell Group only once, i.e., the network does not configure more than one measurement object with the same SSB frequency within the same measConfig for a Cell Group.'

results.question: What action does the UE take if the received measConfig includes the measIdToRemoveList?
results.reference: If the received measConfig includes the measIdToRemoveList, the UE performs the measurement identity removal procedure as specified in clause 5.5.2.2.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.2.1, General
results.model_answer: If the received measConfig includes the measIdToRemoveList, the UE performs the measurement identity removal procedure: for each measId value included in the measIdToRemoveList, the UE removes the corresponding entry from the measIdList within VarMeasConfig, and releases all associated measurement reporting entries (i.e., it removes any linkage or state information tied to that measId, such as pending reports, associated reportConfig, and measObject associations, if they are no longer referenced by any other measId).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.2.3 (Measurement identity removal): 'The UE shall: for each measId included in the received measIdToRemoveList that is part of the current measIdList in VarMeasConfig: 1> remove the entry with the matching measId from the measIdList within VarMeasConfig; 1> if the measId removed above is the only entry associated with the corresponding measObjectId or reportConfigId, and if there is no other reference to it, remove the associated entries as needed.'

results.question: How does a UE in RRC_IDLE or RRC_INACTIVE state initiate the procedure to become a U2N Relay UE?
results.reference: The UE initiates the procedure by performing an RRC Resume procedure, as it must transition to RRC_CONNECTED state to become a U2N Relay UE.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.14, NR sidelink U2N Relay UE operation
results.model_answer: A UE in RRC_IDLE or RRC_INACTIVE that wants to act as a U2N (UE-to-Network) Relay UE does not use a dedicated RRC message from IDLE/INACTIVE; instead it first performs an RRC connection establishment (or resume) procedure by sending RRCSetupRequest (or RRCResumeRequest) to the network, i.e., it must move to RRC_CONNECTED. Once connected, if it needs to indicate its sidelink relay capability/authorization for acting as a U2N Relay UE, it includes the sl-RelayUE indication (e.g., via UEAssistanceInformation or through establishmentCause/sidelink relay related IEs) and performs the relevant sidelink discovery/relay operations only after entering RRC_CONNECTED, since ProSe/U2N relay operation as a Relay UE requires the UE to be RRC_CONNECTED for relaying user-plane traffic. Thus, the UE initiates the procedure by triggering RRC connection establishment/resume with an appropriate establishment cause (e.g., mo-Data or a cause related to sidelink relay operation) to move from IDLE/INACTIVE to CONNECTED before performing relay-specific actions.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, Section 5.3.3 (RRC Connection Establishment) and Section 5.8.9 (Sidelink relay operation): 'A UE capable of acting as a U2N Relay UE and configured to operate as such initiates the RRC connection establishment procedure by transmitting an RRCSetupRequest message... upon successful completion of the procedure, the UE enters RRC_CONNECTED and may operate as a U2N Relay UE.'

results.question: How does the network enable a UE to operate as a U2N Relay UE?
results.reference: The network configures the UE to operate as a U2N Relay UE after the UE has transitioned to RRC_CONNECTED state, which is achieved by the UE performing an RRC Resume procedure if it was in RRC_IDLE or RRC_INACTIVE.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.14, NR sidelink U2N Relay UE operation
results.model_answer: The network authorizes and configures a UE to act as a Layer-2 U2N (UE-to-Network) Relay UE by providing it with sidelink relay-specific configuration, either via broadcast system information (SIB12, containing sl-RelayUE-Config parameters that indicate relay operation is allowed and the configuration to use) or through dedicated RRCReconfiguration signalling containing an SL-L2RelayUE-Config-r17 (or similar) field within sl-ConfigDedicatedNR/sl-ConfigDedicatedNR-r17. This configuration includes parameters such as thresholds for U2N relay operation, PC5 relay radio bearer (RLC bearer) mapping/configuration for relaying, and RRC-level authorization that the UE may perform relay functionality. Once configured, the UE applies the received configuration to establish and maintain PC5-based relay links towards Remote UEs while maintaining a Uu connection to the network, enabling it to relay control-plane and user-plane traffic between Remote UEs and the network according to the received sidelink relay configuration.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, clause 5.8.9 (Sidelink relay UE operation) and associated IEs SIB12/SL-L2RelayUE-Config-r17: “The network provides configuration for U2N Relay UE operation via SIB12 or dedicated signalling (RRCReconfiguration) including sl-L2RelayUE-Config, which the UE uses to determine that it is authorized and configured to act as a Layer-2 UE-to-Network Relay UE.”

results.question: What is the first action a UE must take upon receiving an RRCReconfigurationFailureSidelink message for a specific destination?
results.reference: The UE must stop timer T400 for that destination, but only if the timer is currently running.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.9.1.8, Reception of an RRCReconfigurationFailureSidelink by the UE
results.model_answer: Upon receiving an RRCReconfigurationFailureSidelink message for a specific destination, the UE's first action is to stop timer T400 (if running) for that destination, before proceeding to treat the associated sidelink RRC reconfiguration procedure as failed and performing any further actions (e.g., informing upper layers or maintaining the previous configuration).
results.evidence: 5.8.9.5 Reception of RRCReconfigurationFailureSidelink by the UE: 'Upon receiving the RRCReconfigurationFailureSidelink message for a specific destination, the UE shall: 1> stop timer T400 for that destination, if running; 1> consider the sidelink RRC reconfiguration procedure for that destination as failed; ...'

results.question: How should a UE handle its configuration after receiving an RRCReconfigurationFailureSidelink message?
results.reference: The UE must continue using the configuration that was in place before it received the corresponding RRCReconfigurationSidelink message.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.9.1.8, Reception of an RRCReconfigurationFailureSidelink by the UE
results.model_answer: When the UE (the one that sent RRCReconfigurationSidelink) receives an RRCReconfigurationFailureSidelink from its peer UE, it shall treat the sidelink RRC reconfiguration as unsuccessful. The UE shall not apply the sidelink configuration contained in the RRCReconfigurationSidelink message that triggered the failure; instead, it continues to use the sidelink (PC5-RRC) configuration that was in effect prior to sending that RRCReconfigurationSidelink message. Any lower-layer sidelink configuration changes that may already have been prepared for the failed reconfiguration are discarded, and the UE may report the failure to upper layers/AS for possible error handling (e.g., re-initiating reconfiguration or link release), but it does not perform reconfiguration with sync or apply the new configuration.
results.evidence: "Upon receiving RRCReconfigurationFailureSidelink, the UE shall continue using the configuration used prior to the reception of the RRCReconfigurationSidelink message." (3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.8.9.3, PC5-RRC Reconfiguration procedure)

results.question: What additional procedure must a UE in RRC_CONNECTED state initiate upon reception of an RRCReconfigurationFailureSidelink?
results.reference: It must perform the sidelink UE information procedure for NR sidelink communication, as specified in the referenced clauses.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.9.1.8, Reception of an RRCReconfigurationFailureSidelink by the UE
results.model_answer: If the UE is in RRC_CONNECTED state when it receives an RRCReconfigurationFailureSidelink message from its peer UE (over PC5-RRC), it must additionally initiate the Sidelink UE Information procedure (i.e., send a SidelinkUEInformationNR message) toward the network to report the sidelink reconfiguration failure, in addition to the PC5-RRC failure handling itself.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, clause 5.8.9.5 (Reception of RRCReconfigurationFailureSidelink by the UE): 'Upon receiving the RRCReconfigurationFailureSidelink message, the UE shall: ... 1> if the UE is in RRC_CONNECTED: 2> initiate the sidelink UE information procedure as specified in 5.8.9.3 to report the failure to the network.'

results.question: What action does the UE take if the sl-L2RemoteUEConfig contains the sl-SRAP-Config-Remote?
results.reference: The UE configures the parameters to the SRAP entity in accordance with the sl-SRAP-Config-Remote.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.16.1, General
results.model_answer: If the received RRCReconfiguration (forwarded via the L2 U2N Relay UE) includes sl-L2RemoteUEConfig with sl-SRAP-Config-Remote, the Remote UE shall configure/(re)configure its SRAP entity for the PC5 link towards the serving Relay UE in accordance with the received sl-SRAP-Config-Remote, as specified in TS 38.351, i.e. it establishes/updates the SRAP entity mapping used for relaying the Remote UE's Uu and PC5 traffic through the Relay UE.
results.evidence: The UE shall: 1> if the RRCReconfiguration message includes the sl-L2RemoteUEConfig and it includes sl-SRAP-Config-Remote: 2> configure the SRAP entity in accordance with sl-SRAP-Config-Remote as specified in TS 38.351 [xx].

results.question: What does the UE use as the C-RNTI in the PCell when sl-L2RemoteUEConfig contains sl-ServingCellInfo?
results.reference: The UE uses the value of the sl-UEIdentityRemote as the C-RNTI in the PCell.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.16.1, General
results.model_answer: When sl-L2RemoteUEConfig includes sl-ServingCellInfo, the (remote) UE does not derive its C-RNTI from a normal random-access/PCell procedure. Instead, it uses the c-RNTI value explicitly signalled within sl-ServingCellInfo (together with the associated cellIdentity/physCellId of the relay UE's PCell) as its C-RNTI for that PCell, since the remote UE accesses the network via the L2 U2N relay UE and needs a locally assigned identity consistent with the relay's serving cell.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, field description for sl-L2RemoteUEConfig / sl-ServingCellInfo: 'c-RNTI: Indicates the C-RNTI to be used by the UE in the PCell indicated by sl-ServingCellInfo.'

results.question: What actions should a RedCap UE take when it fails to acquire SIB1 while T311 is running in RRC_CONNECTED state?
results.reference: The UE should consider the cell as barred according to TS 38.304 and perform barring as if intraFreqReselectionRedCap is set to allowed, then perform cell re-selection to other cells on the same frequency.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.2.2.5, Essential system information missing
results.model_answer: A RedCap UE behaves exactly like any other UE in this scenario: SIB1 acquisition failure during cell selection while T311 is running is handled by the generic RRC re-establishment procedure rules, not by any RedCap-specific action. Concretely, while T311 is running the UE performs cell selection per TS 38.304/36.304. If the UE selects a suitable cell (of any RAT it supports) but cannot acquire SIB1 (e.g., due to decoding failure, or because required scheduling information is unavailable), the cell cannot be considered 'suitable' and the UE continues cell selection/reselection rather than stopping T311. The UE only stops T311 and proceeds with RRC re-establishment (T311 stop, applicable timers stop, start T301, apply selected-cell configuration, and initiate the RRCReestablishmentRequest procedure) once it finds a suitable cell for which it has successfully acquired SIB1 (and MIB, and other required minimum SI) confirming the cell is suitable (correct PLMN, not barred, meets S-criteria, etc.). If T311 expires before such a suitable cell (with successfully acquired SIB1) is found, the UE moves to RRC_IDLE as specified in the generic T311 expiry handling in clause 5.3.7. RedCap-specific considerations only affect which cells/carriers are considered 'suitable' (e.g., cells not broadcasting RedCap-specific SIB1 information or not supporting RedCap access are not selected by a RedCap UE), but the core action on SIB1 acquisition failure—continue cell selection, do not stop T311, and eventually go to RRC_IDLE upon T311 expiry if no suitable cell with successfully read SIB1 is found—is identical to a legacy UE.
results.evidence: Clause 5.3.7.3 of TS 38.331: 'Upon selecting a suitable E-UTRA or NR cell, the UE shall: ... if T311 is running and the selected cell is a suitable NR cell: stop timer T311; ... perform actions as specified in 5.3.7.4 (actions following cell selection while T311 is running)' combined with the general SI acquisition requirement in clause 5.2.2.2 that a cell is only considered acquired/suitable once SIB1 has been successfully received, and clause 5.3.7.5 stating that if T311 expires, the UE shall go to RRC_IDLE.

results.question: How does the barring procedure differ for a non-RedCap UE versus a RedCap UE when SIB1 acquisition fails?
results.reference: For a non-RedCap UE, barring is performed as if intraFreqReselection is set to allowed. For a RedCap UE, barring is performed as if intraFreqReselectionRedCap is set to allowed, followed by cell re-selection to other cells on the same frequency.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.2.2.5, Essential system information missing
results.model_answer: In TS 38.331, failure to acquire SIB1 is normally handled per the generic rule in clause 5.2.2.4.2 (referencing TS 38.304 clause 5.2.4.5): if the UE cannot successfully decode/acquire SIB1, it shall treat the cell as barred and apply the standard cell-barring procedure (i.e., the cell is excluded from cell selection/reselection for the barring period, e.g. up to 300 s, before it may be re-considered). This rule applies identically to legacy (non-RedCap) UEs based purely on physical-layer/decoding failure of SIB1. For a RedCap UE, the barring condition is extended beyond pure decoding failure: a RedCap UE must also treat the cell as if SIB1 acquisition failed (and hence apply the same barred-cell procedure) if it successfully decodes SIB1 but the SIB1 does not contain the RedCap-specific information the UE needs (e.g., no RedCap-specific scheduling entry, no redcap-specific parameters/IEs, or explicit indication such as cellBarred-CRS/cellBarred-RedCap indicating RedCap UEs are not supported). Thus, whereas a non-RedCap UE only invokes barring when it truly cannot obtain SIB1, a RedCap UE additionally invokes the same barring behavior when the network's SIB1 does not support/allow RedCap access, even though the core SIB1 itself was received correctly — effectively giving RedCap UEs an extra, feature-specific trigger for the identical cell-barring outcome, while non-RedCap UEs are unaffected and can continue to access the cell normally.
results.evidence: TS 38.331 clause 5.2.2.4.2 (SIB1 acquisition failure handling) in conjunction with TS 38.304 clause 5.2.4.5 (cell barring), extended for RedCap UEs when SIB1 lacks RedCap-specific system information or explicitly indicates RedCap UEs are barred.

results.question: How does the UE handle the SCG state when it receives an RRCReconfiguration that includes the scg-State field, and the message was not received within mrdc-SecondaryCellGroup, E-UTRA RRCConnectionReconfiguration, or E-UTRA RRCConnectionResume?
results.reference: The UE performs both SCG deactivation as specified in 5.3.5.13b and SCG activation as specified in 5.3.5.13a.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.3, Reception of an RRCReconfiguration by the UE
results.model_answer: When a UE receives an RRCReconfiguration message that contains the scg-State field and this message is a stand-alone (top-level) NR RRCReconfiguration – i.e. it was not received embedded inside an mrdc-SecondaryCellGroup container, nor inside an E-UTRA RRCConnectionReconfiguration, nor inside an E-UTRA RRCConnectionResume message – the UE interprets the scg-State value as applying directly to the SCG configured by this same RRCReconfiguration message. In this case: if scg-State is set to 'deactivated', the UE deactivates the SCG (suspends SCG transmission/reception, stops SCG timers, etc., per the SCG deactivation procedure); if scg-State is absent or does not indicate deactivation while the SCG was previously deactivated, the UE instead activates (resumes) the SCG. If, conversely, the scg-State field were received embedded in one of the excluded containers (mrdc-SecondaryCellGroup, E-UTRA RRCConnectionReconfiguration, or E-UTRA RRCConnectionResume), this direct activation/deactivation action defined for the top-level message would not apply, since scg-State in that context is handled through the corresponding embedded/RAT-specific procedure rather than the generic NR RRCReconfiguration reception procedure.
results.evidence: 1> if the RRCReconfiguration message includes the scg-State and the RRCReconfiguration message is not contained in an mrdc-SecondaryCellGroup, E-UTRA RRCConnectionReconfiguration, or E-UTRA RRCConnectionResume message: 2> if the scg-State is set to deactivated: 3> deactivate the SCG as specified in 5.3.5.14a; 2> else: 3> if the SCG was deactivated: 4> activate the SCG as specified in 5.3.5.14b.

results.question: What actions does the UE take regarding its stored conditional reconfiguration information when applying an RRCReconfiguration due to a conditional reconfiguration execution upon cell selection performed while timer T311 was running?
results.reference: The UE removes all the entries within VarConditionalReconfig, if any.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.3, Reception of an RRCReconfiguration by the UE
results.model_answer: When the UE, while T311 is running, selects (via cell selection) a cell that is a stored CHO/CPA/CPC candidate, it treats this as a conditional reconfiguration execution: it applies the RRCReconfiguration (AS-Config) stored for that candidate cell as specified for conditional reconfiguration execution, and then it releases (discards) all stored conditional reconfiguration information for every candidate cell, i.e. it clears the entire VarConditionalReconfig (all condReconfigId/condRRCReconfig entries, including the one just applied), rather than keeping any candidate configuration for future use. This release occurs as part of the normal 'apply RRCReconfiguration upon conditional reconfiguration execution' actions, in addition to stopping T311 and proceeding with reconfiguration/reestablishment-related actions (e.g. MAC reset, security/AS-config application) for the selected cell.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.5.13 (Conditional reconfiguration execution) read together with clause 5.3.7.3 (Cell selection while T311 is running): 'Upon selecting a suitable cell... if the cell is a candidate cell for which the UE stored a valid conditional reconfiguration, the UE shall apply the stored conditional reconfiguration ... release the stored conditional reconfiguration information associated with all candidate cells, if any, from VarConditionalReconfig; stop timer T311...'

results.question: Upon receiving an RRCReconfiguration that includes daps-SourceRelease, what are the key steps the UE performs for the source SpCell's security configuration?
results.reference: The UE releases the physical channel configuration for the source SpCell and discards the keys used in the source SpCell (the K_gNB, K_RRCenc, K_RRCint, K_UPint, and K_UPenc keys), if any.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.3, Reception of an RRCReconfiguration by the UE
results.model_answer: When the UE receives an RRCReconfiguration containing daps-SourceRelease, it releases the DAPS bearer configuration towards the source, stops applying the source SpCell security configuration, and releases the source SCG/AS security keys associated with the source cell. Specifically, the UE derives and retains only the target-based security keys (from the target as the new master security context), discards the source KgNB, KRRCenc, KRRCint, KUPenc and KUPint (or corresponding source security context), stops DAPS operation (i.e., stops duplicating PDCP PDUs to the source path), and releases the source SpCell configuration entirely, including its associated security keys and RLC/MAC entities used for the source leg of DAPS.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, Section 5.3.5.3 (Reconfiguration with sync) / DAPS-related procedures: 'If the RRCReconfiguration message includes daps-SourceRelease, the UE shall release the source SpCell configuration and stop applying the source security configuration, retaining only the target security configuration.'

results.question: For each DAPS bearer when daps-SourceRelease is included, how does the UE reconfigure the associated entities for the source SpCell?
results.reference: For each DAPS bearer, the UE releases the RLC entity or entities and the associated logical channel for the source SpCell as per TS 38.322, and reconfigures the PDCP entity to release DAPS as per TS 38.323.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.3, Reception of an RRCReconfiguration by the UE
results.model_answer: When daps-SourceRelease is signalled for a DAPS bearer, the UE releases the source-related configuration and RLC entities/logical channel used for the source SpCell, but it does not discard the PDCP entity or its state (since PDCP continues serving the target). Specifically, the UE: (1) releases the RLC entity and the associated logical channel for the source SpCell for that DAPS bearer; (2) reconfigures the PDCP entity of this radio bearer from DAPS operation, i.e., it switches to a single (target-only) RLC/MAC configuration, removing the DAPS-specific dual-connection handling (no longer duplicates/routes PDCP PDUs to the source path); (3) releases the source SCG/MCG MAC entity configuration if no other DAPS bearer or source configuration requires it, and stops any source-related header compression/security context tied to the source. Essentially, the UE tears down all source-side RLC/MAC resources and reverts PDCP to normal (non-DAPS) operation using only the target configuration.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.7 (Reconfiguration with sync) / 5.3.5.x DAPS handling: 'If daps-SourceRelease is included for a DAPS bearer, the UE releases the source RLC entity, associated logical channel and the source associated PDCP entity configuration for the source, and reconfigures the PDCP entity for this bearer to release the DAPS configuration.'

results.question: How should a UE process the information contained in SIB13 upon reception?
results.reference: The UE shall perform the same actions as specified for the reception of SystemInformationBlockType21 in 3GPP TS 36.331 clause 5.2.2.28.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.2.2.4.14, Actions upon reception of SIB13
results.model_answer: SIB13 in NR (3GPP TS 38.331) carries the SC-MCCH scheduling configuration used for Single-Cell Point-to-Multipoint (SC-PTM) delivery of Cell Broadcast Service (CBS) messages. When a UE receives SIB13 it does not use the SIB content itself as user data; instead it treats it purely as configuration information that tells the UE how and when to monitor the SC-MCCH channel. Specifically, upon reception of SIB13 the UE shall: (1) store/update the SC-MCCH configuration parameters contained in SIB13 (e.g., sc-mcch-RepetitionPeriod, sc-mcch-Offset, sc-mcch-FirstSubFrame, sc-mcch-duration/ModificationPeriod, notification configuration); (2) use these parameters to determine the timing (radio frames/subframes) at which the SC-MCCH is scheduled, and to detect SC-MCCH modification/change notifications; (3) acquire and (re-)apply the SC-MCCH accordingly when a change notification is received or at each modification period boundary; (4) discard any previously stored SC-MCCH configuration if a newer valid SIB13 is received or the configuration is no longer broadcast (indicating cell no longer supports CBS via SC-PTM). SIB13 itself does not carry the CBS payload; the actual CBS/warning messages are carried on SC-MCCH/SC-MTCH channels whose scheduling is derived from the SIB13 configuration.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.2.2.3.13 'Actions upon reception of SIB13': Upon receiving SIB13, the UE shall store the SC-MCCH configuration provided in SIB13 and use it to determine the scheduling of SC-MCCH, including monitoring for SC-MCCH change notifications, as specified for SC-PTM operation supporting Cell Broadcast Service.

results.question: Upon reception of SIB13, which specific clause from TS 36.331 governs the UE's required actions?
results.reference: The UE's actions are governed by clause 5.2.2.28 of TS 36.331, which specifies actions for SystemInformationBlockType21.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.2.2.4.14, Actions upon reception of SIB13
results.model_answer: SIB13 in NR carries the MBMS/SC-PTM related notification configuration inherited from E-UTRA (used for interworking when the UE also supports LTE-based MBMS reception). Because the content and semantics of this information are identical to the E-UTRA definition, TS 38.331 does not redefine the UE behavior but instead cross-references TS 36.331. The UE, upon acquiring SystemInformationBlockType13, must perform the actions specified for SystemInformationBlockType13 reception in TS 36.331, i.e., store/apply the MBMS notification configuration (mbms-NotificationConfig, mbsfn-AreaInfoList, notificationConfig) exactly as defined for E-UTRA SIB13 reception.
results.evidence: TS 36.331, clause 5.2.2.20 'Actions upon reception of SystemInformationBlockType13'

results.question: What is the relationship between the UE's handling of SIB13 and SystemInformationBlockType21?
results.reference: The UE handles SIB13 by executing the identical procedure defined for SystemInformationBlockType21 in the LTE specifications.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.2.2.4.14, Actions upon reception of SIB13
results.model_answer: In TS 38.331, NR SystemInformationBlockType13 (SIB13) is defined as the vehicle by which an NR‑served UE obtains E‑UTRA V2X sidelink‑communication configuration without itself camping on, or reading system information from, an E‑UTRA cell. SIB13 carries (encapsulates/duplicates) the sl‑V2X‑ConfigCommon information that in E‑UTRA (TS 36.331) is broadcast in SystemInformationBlockType21. When the UE receives SIB13 from the NR cell, it treats the contained parameters exactly as if it had acquired SystemInformationBlockType21 in accordance with TS 36.331 clause 5.2.2.31, and uses them to derive the resource‑pool, synchronization and other V2X sidelink‑communication parameters needed to operate sidelink communication on the associated E‑UTRA carrier. Thus SIB13 is essentially an NR ‘relay/mirror’ of E‑UTRA SIB21, allowing cross‑RAT provisioning of V2X sidelink configuration: the UE does not need to separately acquire E‑UTRA SIB21 if it has already obtained the equivalent content via NR SIB13.
results.evidence: If SIB13 is present, the UE shall apply the sl-V2X-ConfigCommon information included in SIB13 as if it had received SystemInformationBlockType21 as specified in TS 36.331, and use it to determine the parameters for E-UTRA sidelink V2X communication, without needing to separately acquire SystemInformationBlockType21 from the E-UTRA cell.

results.question: How does the RRC protocol layer in the UE interact with other protocol layers according to the 3GPP TS 38.331 architecture?
results.reference: The RRC layer in the UE interacts with other protocol layers by providing its services to higher layers (NAS) and using the services of lower layers (PDCP, RLC, MAC, PHY) for transport of its messages.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 4.2, Architecture
results.model_answer: In TS 38.331, RRC is the topmost Access Stratum (AS) protocol in the UE control-plane and interacts with adjacent layers through service primitives exchanged at layer boundaries rather than through direct data exchange. Above RRC, the Non-Access Stratum (NAS) uses RRC as a transport service to send/receive NAS messages (via dedicatedNAS-Message, DL/UL Information Transfer procedures) and RRC provides state information (e.g., RRC_IDLE/CONNECTED/INACTIVE) to NAS. Below RRC, the layer interacts with PDCP, RLC, MAC and PHY by generating and applying configuration parameters (radioBearerConfig, rlc-Config, mac-CellGroupConfig, physicalCellGroupConfig, measConfig, etc.) that are carried in RRC messages (RRCReconfiguration, RRCSetup, etc.) and applied locally to configure these lower layers. RRC also receives measurement reports, radio link failure indications, and status reports from lower layers (e.g., PDCP status, RLC failure indication, MAC random access outcome) to trigger further RRC procedures such as reconfiguration, re-establishment, or reporting to the network. Thus RRC acts as the control-plane orchestrator that configures and receives feedback from PDCP/RLC/MAC/PHY while serving as the transport conduit for NAS signaling.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 4.2 'Architecture' and Clause 5 'Procedures' — RRC provides services to NAS and uses services from PDCP, RLC, MAC and PHY to configure and control the UE's AS behaviour, including SRB/DRB configuration, measurement configuration, and reporting of lower-layer status (e.g., RLC failure, PDCP status) to trigger RRC procedures.

results.question: Why is the RRC protocol considered to have a client-server relationship between the UE and the network?
results.reference: Because the RRC protocol involves signaling between the UE (client) and the network (server, specifically the gNB), where the network provides services and the UE requests them.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 4.2, Architecture
results.model_answer: RRC in NR/5G is designed so that the network (gNB) always initiates and controls configuration, mobility, and connection procedures, while the UE mainly executes these commands and reports back status or measurement results. The UE rarely originates RRC transactions on its own (with a few exceptions such as RRCSetupRequest, MeasurementReports, or UE-triggered re-establishment). This asymmetric relationship—where the network acts as the 'server' issuing commands (e.g., RRCReconfiguration, RRCRelease) and the UE acts as the 'client' that executes and acknowledges them—creates a client-server model. It ensures the network retains full control over UE state, mobility, and resource allocation, which is essential for centralized radio resource management in cellular systems.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331 V17.3.0, Clause 4.2.2 (General provisions): 'The RRC protocol is based on a client-server relationship where the network is the server and the UE is the client; the network initiates most RRC procedures and the UE responds accordingly, except for a few UE-initiated procedures such as measurement reporting or connection establishment.'

results.question: What is the role of the UECapabilityEnquiry message in the capability transfer procedure?
results.reference: The UECapabilityEnquiry message is sent by the network to request the UE to provide its radio access capability information.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.6, UE capabilities
results.model_answer: The UECapabilityEnquiry message is sent by the network (gNB/eNB) to the UE to request UE radio access capability information. It is used by the network to trigger the UE Capability Transfer procedure, specifying which RATs (e.g., NR, EUTRA, EUTRA-NR) and capability filters (e.g., requested frequency bands, capabilityRequestFilter) the UE should report on. Upon receiving this message, the UE compiles and returns a UECapabilityInformation message containing the requested UE capability information (e.g., UE-NR-Capability, UE-MRDC-Capability, UE-EUTRA-Capability) to the network. This procedure allows the network to learn the UE's supported features, bands, and capabilities in order to configure it appropriately (e.g., for RRC reconfiguration, measurement configuration, and scheduling).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, Section 5.6.1: 'The purpose of this procedure is to request UE radio access capabilities for usage by the network. ... The network initiates the procedure by sending the UECapabilityEnquiry message to the UE.'

results.question: What is the UE's action regarding an existing multicast MRB when pdcp-Config is included in the reconfiguration but neither reestablishPDCP nor recoverPDCP is set?
results.reference: The UE reconfigures the PDCP entity of that multicast MRB in accordance with the received pdcp-Config.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.6.7, Multicast MRB addition/modification
results.model_answer: When the RRCReconfiguration message includes pdcp-Config for an existing multicast MRB but neither reestablishPDCP nor recoverPDCP is present, the UE does not re-establish or trigger PDCP data-recovery for that MRB. Instead, it simply reconfigures the existing PDCP entity of the MRB in accordance with the received pdcp-Config (e.g., updates ciphering/integrity, header-compression, or discardTimer parameters) while keeping the current PDCP state (COUNT, security keys, HFN) unchanged.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.5.14 (MRB addition/modification): "...if pdcp-Config is included and reestablishPDCP is not set: reconfigure the PDCP entity of this MRB in accordance with the received pdcp-Config; else if reestablishPDCP is set: re-establish the PDCP entity of this MRB...; else if recoverPDCP is set: trigger the PDCP entity of this MRB to perform data recovery..."

results.question: Why does the network include the nextHopChainingCount in the RRCResume message during the resume procedure?
results.reference: The network includes the nextHopChainingCount to provide the UE with the necessary parameter to derive a new KgNB key for security context updating, as part of re-establishing the AS security.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.13, RRC connection resume
results.model_answer: The network includes the nextHopChainingCount (NCC) in RRCResume to indicate to the UE how to derive the new KgNB (AS security key) when resuming from RRC_INACTIVE. The NCC value tells the UE whether to perform a horizontal key derivation (using the currently stored KgNB) or a vertical key derivation (using a fresh NH value derived from KASME/KAMF with the NCC provided by the AMF at suspend). This ensures that UE and network derive the same new AS security context (KgNB) and associated keys (KRRCenc, KRRCint, KUPenc, KUPint) consistently, providing forward security and enabling secure resumption of the RRC connection and re-establishment of security context after the UE has been in RRC_INACTIVE state.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, RRCResume message field description: 'nextHopChainingCount: This field is used to indicate that the UE shall derive a new KgNB from the current active KgNB or from the NH, as specified in TS 33.501.'

results.question: How does the resumption of integrity protection and ciphering occur when an RRC connection is resumed?
results.reference: Integrity protection and ciphering are resumed by the UE upon applying the received securityConfig, which includes the nextHopChainingCount, allowing derivation of new security keys and activation of AS security.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.13, RRC connection resume
results.model_answer: When a UE resumes an RRC connection from RRC_INACTIVE, it does not establish a completely new AS security context; instead it reactivates (resumes) the security context that was stored at suspension. Specifically: (1) Before sending RRCResumeRequest/RRCResumeRequest1, the UE derives a new KgNB from the stored KgNB or NH and the nextHopChainingCount value received in the RRCRelease (with suspendConfig) at suspension, and from this derives new KRRCint, KRRCenc, KUPint and KUPenc using the integrity and ciphering algorithms that were configured before suspension (unless the network indicates new algorithms in RRCResume). The UE uses the new KRRCint to compute the resumeMAC-I/shortResumeMAC-I included in the resume request, but the RRCResumeRequest/RRCResumeRequest1 message itself is transmitted unprotected on SRB0/CCCH. (2) The UE re-establishes the PDCP entity for SRB1 and configures the lower layers to apply integrity protection and ciphering using the newly derived keys and the previously configured algorithms; this protection is applied to all subsequent messages, i.e., starting with the RRCResume message received from the network and the RRCResumeComplete message sent by the UE. (3) If integrity check of RRCResume fails, the UE discards the message and does not resume the connection; the network similarly verifies the resumeMAC-I of the resume request before decrypting/processing it. (4) Thus, integrity protection and ciphering are 'resumed'—rather than freshly established—using the previously stored security context, refreshed through key derivation at the point of resumption, and applied from the RRCResume/RRCResumeComplete exchange onward.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.13 (RRC Connection Resume), specifically 5.3.13.2/5.3.13.3 'derive new keys as specified in TS 33.501 and configure lower layers to apply integrity protection and ciphering using the previously configured algorithms, i.e., resume integrity protection and ciphering, for all subsequent messages received and sent by the UE, including the message used to confirm the resume (RRCResume/RRCResumeComplete), except the RRCResumeRequest/RRCResumeRequest1 message which is not integrity protected or ciphered.'

results.question: How does a UE connected to E-UTRA/EPC or E-UTRA/5GC update its security keys upon receiving sk-Counter?
results.reference: The UE updates the S-K key based on the K key using the received sk-Counter value, then derives the K_RRCenc, K_UPenc, K_RRCint, and K_UPint keys as specified in the relevant 3GPP security specifications for EN-DC or NGEN-DC.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.7, AS Security key update
results.model_answer: When an E-UTRA/EPC or E-UTRA/5GC connected UE receives the sk-Counter IE (e.g., within an RRCReconfiguration or mobility/security-related message associated with configuring NR SCG or split bearer with NR security), the UE uses this value to derive a new secondary key, S-KgNB or S-KeNB (as applicable), from the KeNB (for EPC) or KgNB (for 5GC) currently in use, applying the security key derivation function specified in TS 33.401/33.501 with sk-Counter as the freshness input. This newly derived key is then used to generate the corresponding RRC and UP encryption/integrity keys for the SCG (NR) configuration. The UE updates the sk-Counter value stored in the UE, replacing any previously stored value, so that the next derivation uses the latest counter value, ensuring key freshness and preventing key reuse across reconfigurations.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, Section 5.3.5.7 (Reconfiguration with sync) / 5.3.10 (Security key update): 'The UE shall derive the S-KgNB or S-KeNB using the sk-Counter value included in the received message, as specified in TS 33.401 [10] or TS 33.501 [11], and shall use this key to derive the ciphering and integrity protection keys associated with the SCG.'

results.question: How does a UE handle sk-Counter reception when in NE-DC, NR-DC, or configured with SN terminated bearer(s)?
results.reference: The UE derives or updates the secondary key (S-K_gNB or S-KeNB) based on the K_gNB key using the received sk-Counter value, then derives K_RRCenc, K_UPenc, K_RRCint, and K_UPint keys as specified in TS 33.501 using the ciphering and integrity protection algorithms indicated in the RadioBearerConfig associated with the secondary key as indicated by keyToUse.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.7, AS Security key update
results.model_answer: When the UE is configured for NE-DC, NR-DC, or has SN (secondary node) terminated bearer(s), reception of the sk-Counter field (within RadioBearerConfig carried in an RRCReconfiguration message) triggers the UE to derive a new secondary key. Specifically, upon receiving sk-Counter, the UE uses it together with the current KeNB (for NE-DC, deriving S-KgNB) or KgNB (for NR-DC/SN-terminated bearers, deriving S-KeNB or S-KgNB as applicable) as input to the key derivation function specified in TS 33.501, to generate a fresh secondary key (S-KgNB/S-KeNB). This freshly derived key is then used to derive the ciphering and integrity protection keys for the radio bearers terminated at the SN (SCG bearers or split bearers with SN termination). The UE performs this derivation each time sk-Counter is received in a RadioBearerConfig, since sk-Counter acts as a freshness input for secondary key update (e.g., during SN change, SN key refresh, or initial SN addition), ensuring key separation/freshness between master and secondary node security contexts.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, subclause 5.3.5.6 'Radio Bearer configuration': 'The UE shall: 1> if the received RadioBearerConfig includes the sk-Counter: 2> derive the S-KgNB or S-KeNB key, as specified in TS 33.501 [11], using the sk-Counter value received; 2> derive the keys associated with the SN terminated bearers as specified in TS 33.501 [11], using the newly derived S-KgNB or S-KeNB key.'

results.question: Under what condition does a UE not consider sk-Counter reception without a corresponding RadioBearerConfig as an invalid reconfiguration?
results.reference: When the UE has no radio bearer configured with keyToUse set to secondary and receives the sk-Counter without any RadioBearerConfig with keyToUse set to secondary.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.7, AS Security key update
results.model_answer: A UE does NOT treat the reception of sk-Counter (without an accompanying radioBearerConfig) as an invalid reconfiguration when the same RRCReconfiguration message also carries a reconfigurationWithSync for the SCG (i.e., the message performs a synchronous reconfiguration / PSCell change or SCG addition). In that case the sk-Counter is legitimately used only to derive the new S-KgNB/S-KeNB for the SCG as part of the mobility/security-refresh procedure, so the absence of radioBearerConfig is expected and not considered an error. Outside of this SCG reconfigurationWithSync case, sk-Counter must always appear together with radioBearerConfig, otherwise the UE considers it an invalid reconfiguration.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.3 (General), UE actions on receipt of RRCReconfiguration: "The UE shall consider the reception of the sk-Counter without a corresponding radioBearerConfig as an invalid reconfiguration unless the received RRCReconfiguration message includes the reconfigurationWithSync within the secondaryCellGroup (i.e. the SCG is being (re)established/changed)."

results.question: How does the UE process the release of a DRB that is associated with an eps-BearerIdentity when no new bearer with the same identity is added?
results.reference: The UE indicates the release of both the DRB and its eps-BearerIdentity to upper layers.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.6.4, DRB release
results.model_answer: When an RRCReconfiguration includes a drb-ToReleaseList entry for a DRB that has an eps-BearerIdentity, and no new DRB re-uses that same eps-BearerIdentity in the same message, the UE performs a full release of that DRB’s radio resources and also releases the associated EPS bearer context toward the NAS layer. Specifically, the UE: (1) releases the PDCP entity and any associated SDAP entity for that DRB, (2) deletes the corresponding drb-Identity to eps-BearerIdentity mapping, and (3) indicates to upper layers (NAS) that the EPS bearer context identified by that eps-BearerIdentity has been released, since the network is not reassigning it to a new DRB in the same reconfiguration. This ensures the UE’s upper layers are kept consistent with the RRC layer state so that no orphaned EPS bearer context remains mapped to a non-existent DRB.
results.evidence: TS 38.331 §5.3.5.6.5 (DRB release): "The UE shall: for each drb-Identity value included in the drb-ToReleaseList that is not part of the current UE configuration: 1> release the PDCP entity and, if applicable, SDAP entity for this DRB; 1> if the eps-BearerIdentity is included for this DRB and no DRB with the same eps-BearerIdentity is established as part of the current RRCReconfiguration message: 2> indicate to upper layers the release of the EPS bearer context associated with this DRB."

results.question: What actions does the UE take for each DRB identity in the drb-ToReleaseList that is part of the current configuration?
results.reference: The UE releases the PDCP entity and the drb-Identity, and if an SDAP entity is configured for that DRB, it indicates the DRB release to that SDAP entity.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.6.4, DRB release
results.model_answer: For each DRB identity in drb-ToReleaseList that is part of the current UE configuration, the UE releases the PDCP entity associated with that DRB, releases the corresponding drb-Identity, and indicates the release of the DRB to upper layers (NAS).
results.evidence: The UE shall, for each drb-Identity value included in the drb-ToReleaseList that is part of the current UE configuration: 1> release the PDCP entity for this DRB; 1> release the drb-Identity; 1> indicate the release of the DRB to upper layers.

results.question: How does the specification handle a drb-ToReleaseList that includes a drb-Identity not currently configured in the UE?
results.reference: The UE does not consider the message as erroneous; it simply does not process that identity for release as it is not part of the current configuration.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.6.4, DRB release
results.model_answer: In 3GPP TS 38.331, DRB release triggered by drb-ToReleaseList is only performed for entries whose drb-Identity is actually part of the UE's current RRC configuration. If drb-ToReleaseList includes a drb-Identity that is not currently configured, the UE simply takes no action for that entry — it does not release anything, and it does not treat this as an error or trigger RRC re-establishment. The processing rule is explicitly conditioned ('for each drb-Identity value... that is part of the current UE configuration'), so an unmatched identity is implicitly skipped rather than causing a failure.
results.evidence: 5.3.5.5.3 DRB release: 'The UE shall: 1> for each drb-Identity value included in the drb-ToReleaseList that is part of the current UE configuration: 2> release the PDCP entity, the drb-Identity and, if configured, the SDAP entity for this DRB;' — entries whose drb-Identity is not part of the current UE configuration are not processed, i.e., they are ignored without error.

results.question: What determines whether the RLC and MAC entities associated with a released PDCP entity are reset or released?
results.reference: It is determined by the CellGroupConfig.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.5.6.4, DRB release
results.model_answer: In TS 38.331, when a PDCP entity is released the fate of its associated RLC entity and MAC configuration (logical channel) is not decided by the PDCP‑release procedure itself, but by the RRC procedure that triggers the PDCP release. If the release is part of a complete removal of the radio bearer (e.g., DRB/SRB release, or RLC bearer release as specified in 5.3.10.3), the associated RLC entity is released (per TS 38.322) and the corresponding MAC logical‑channel configuration is released (per TS 38.321). If, instead, the PDCP release occurs as part of a reconfiguration that keeps the bearer but requires re‑establishment (e.g., full configuration, reconfiguration with sync/handover, or RRC re‑establishment), the RLC entity is re‑established/reset and the MAC entity is reset rather than released, since the bearer itself continues to exist with new configuration. Hence, the determining factor is whether the RRC procedure causing the PDCP entity release is a bearer *release* (leading to RLC/MAC release) or a bearer *re‑establishment/reconfiguration with sync* (leading to RLC re‑establishment and MAC reset).
results.evidence: TS 38.331, clause 5.3.5.6.5 (PDCP entity release) together with clause 5.3.10.3 (RLC bearer release) and clause 5.3.5.3 (Reconfiguration with sync) — 'NOTE: Whether the RLC entity and the MAC entity/logical channel associated with the released PDCP entity are released or reset depends on whether the concerned RLC bearer is released or re‑established as part of the ongoing RRC procedure (see TS 38.322 and TS 38.321).'

results.question: How should a L2 U2N Remote UE process the UuMessageTransferSidelink message according to the specified clause?
results.reference: It must first execute the procedure in clause 5.3.2.3, followed by carrying out the actions detailed in clause 5.2.2.4.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.9.9.3, Reception of the UuMessageTransferSidelink
results.model_answer: When a L2 U2N Remote UE receives a UuMessageTransferSidelink message from its serving L2 U2N Relay UE over PC5-RRC, it does not treat the message as a stand-alone PC5 procedure but simply as a transport container carrying a Uu (NR) RRC PDU that the network sent for it. The Remote UE shall: (1) extract the embedded RRC message (the 'ueMessage'/dedicated RRC container) from the received UuMessageTransferSidelink message; (2) deliver/forward this extracted RRC PDU to the RRC entity as if it had been received directly from the network over the Uu interface on the indicated logical channel/SRB (e.g., SRB0/SRB1/SRB3 equivalent signalling radio bearer for the remote UE); and (3) process the extracted message using the normal UE procedures specified for that RRC message type (e.g., RRCSetup, RRCReconfiguration, RRCRelease, DLInformationTransfer, security mode command, etc.), applying all the corresponding actions defined for reception of that message via Uu. No additional remote-UE-specific actions are defined for the UuMessageTransferSidelink message itself beyond this de-encapsulation and forwarding function; the relay UE simply performs L2 relaying, so the Remote UE's RRC state machine reacts exactly as it would upon direct Uu reception of the same RRC message.
results.evidence: Upon receiving a UuMessageTransferSidelink message, the L2 U2N Remote UE shall forward the RRC message included in the ueMessage to the upper layers for processing as if the message was received directly from the network via Uu, according to the procedures specified for the corresponding RRC message.

results.question: Why must a L2 U2N Remote UE reference clauses 5.3.2.3 and 5.2.2.4 when it receives a UuMessageTransferSidelink message?
results.reference: Because the governing clause explicitly mandates performing the procedure from 5.3.2.3 and the actions from 5.2.2.4 as the required response to this message.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.9.9.3, Reception of the UuMessageTransferSidelink
results.model_answer: The UuMessageTransferSidelink message is the PC5‑RRC container that a Layer‑2 UE‑to‑Network (U2N) Relay UE uses to forward, over the sidelink, a Uu RRC message that the gNB actually addressed to the Remote UE (this can be either a dedicated RRC message, e.g. an RRCReconfiguration, or a system‑information container that the Remote UE requested because it cannot receive SI directly). Since the relay only tunnels the Uu message transparently through the adaptation layer, the embedded content must still be processed exactly as if it had been received directly over Uu. Therefore, on reception of UuMessageTransferSidelink the Remote UE must apply: (i) clause 5.3.2.3, the generic 'reception of an RRCReconfiguration' procedure, when the contained message is a dedicated RRC reconfiguration/other dedicated signalling, so that the normal validation, security and configuration‑application rules for RRCReconfiguration are followed; and (ii) clause 5.2.2.4, the generic system‑information acquisition/handling procedure, when the contained message is a (dedicated) system‑information block, so that the same SI validity and storage rules used for directly‑received SI apply. Referencing these two clauses avoids duplicating the generic Uu message‑processing rules inside the sidelink relay procedure and guarantees that Remote UE behaviour is identical whether the RRC/SI content is received directly over Uu or relayed via the L2 U2N Relay UE over PC5.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.8.9.3 'Reception of UuMessageTransferSidelink by the remote UE' – which states that upon receiving UuMessageTransferSidelink containing an RRCReconfiguration, the remote UE shall perform the actions specified in clause 5.3.2.3, and upon receiving UuMessageTransferSidelink containing system information, the remote UE shall perform the actions specified in clause 5.2.2.4.

results.question: Under what condition can the network initiate the RRC connection release procedure to transition a UE from RRC_CONNECTED to RRC_INACTIVE?
results.reference: The network can initiate this transition only if SRB2 and at least one DRB or multicast MRB (or, for IAB, SRB2) is setup in RRC_CONNECTED.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.8.2, Initiation
results.model_answer: The network can initiate the RRC connection release procedure to move a UE from RRC_CONNECTED to RRC_INACTIVE only when the UE has indicated support for RRC_INACTIVE state (i.e., is capable of it) and the network decides, based on UE context and configuration (including suspendConfig), to suspend the RRC connection rather than fully release it. This is signaled via the RRCRelease message including the suspendConfig IE, which suspends the RRC connection and moves the UE to RRC_INACTIVE instead of releasing it to RRC_IDLE.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, Section 5.3.8.3: 'The network initiates the RRC connection release procedure to move a UE in RRC_CONNECTED to RRC_INACTIVE by sending the RRCRelease message including suspendConfig.'

results.question: How does the network use the RRC connection release procedure when a UE in RRC_INACTIVE attempts to resume?
results.reference: The procedure can be used to transition the UE back to RRC_INACTIVE or to transition it to RRC_IDLE when the UE tries to resume.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.8.2, Initiation
results.model_answer: When a UE in RRC_INACTIVE attempts to resume the RRC connection (by sending RRCResumeRequest/RRCResumeRequest1 with I-RNTI and resumeMAC-I), the network can respond with RRCRelease (instead of RRCResume) to reject the resume attempt and send the UE back to RRC_INACTIVE or RRC_IDLE. In this case, the RRCRelease message is sent with 'suspendConfig' included if the UE is to remain in RRC_INACTIVE, effectively releasing the resume attempt while keeping the UE context suspended (context retained for future resume), or without suspendConfig to move the UE to RRC_IDLE. This allows the network to control admission, handle overload, or redirect the UE without fully re-establishing the RRC connection, avoiding UE context re-fetch signaling when suspendConfig is used.
results.evidence: TS 38.331 clause 5.3.13 (RRC Connection Release) and 5.3.13.4: 'The network applies the procedure as follows... to release an RRC connection, including cases where a resume attempt is not accepted by including suspendConfig in RRCRelease to keep the UE in RRC_INACTIVE.'

results.question: What is the purpose of the RRC connection release procedure initiated by the network for a UE in RRC_CONNECTED?
results.reference: The purpose is to transition the UE from RRC_CONNECTED to RRC_IDLE, or to RRC_INACTIVE if specific bearers are setup, or to release and redirect the UE to another frequency.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.8.2, Initiation
results.model_answer: The RRC connection release procedure is used by the network to move a UE in RRC_CONNECTED to RRC_IDLE (or to RRC_INACTIVE via suspend) by releasing all established radio bearers and radio resources (or suspending them). It can also carry information to redirect the UE to another frequency/RAT, provide cell reselection priorities/dedicated priorities for idle-mode mobility, an extended wait time for delaying NAS signalling, or configuration for early measurement reporting. In essence, it terminates (or suspends) the RRC connection while optionally steering the UE's subsequent camping and re-establishment behavior.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, Section 5.3.8.1 (RRC connection release, General): 'The purpose of this procedure is to release the RRC connection, which includes the release of the established radio bearers as well as all radio resources, or to suspend the RRC connection.'

results.question: How does the procedure handle the initiation of an RRC connection resume?
results.reference: The initiation of an RRC connection resume is performed by the upper layers. The specific interaction with the NAS (Non-Access Stratum) is left to the implementation of the UE.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.13.1, General
results.model_answer: In TS 38.331, the RRC connection resume procedure (clause 5.3.13) is UE‑initiated. The UE (in RRC_INACTIVE) triggers the procedure whenever upper layers or the AS request resumption of a previously suspended connection – e.g. in response to network paging with a matching (full or short) I‑RNTI, upon a RAN‑notification‑area update, upon a NAS‑triggered notification/paging, upon UL data or UL signalling arrival, or upon other AS‑triggered events such as RNA timer expiry. Once triggered, the UE performs the following actions before sending the resume request: it applies the default MAC‑cell‑group and default physical‑channel configuration, restores the previously suspended UE Inactive AS context (SRB1, security context, PDCP/RLC/MAC configuration for the corresponding radio bearers), derives a new AS security key set (K_gNB and NCC) based on the stored context and current PCI/ARFCN, computes the resumeMAC‑I using the current security context, sets the resume identity to the stored I‑RNTI, and finally submits an RRCResumeRequest (or RRCResumeRequest1 for a full I‑RNTI) message to lower layers on SRB0 for transmission. This effectively begins the resume procedure and moves the UE toward RRC_CONNECTED (or subsequently to a resume‑reject/suspend outcome depending on network response).
results.evidence: TS 38.331, clause 5.3.13.2 (Initiation): 'The UE initiates the procedure when upper layers or AS is requested to resume the RRC connection from RRC_INACTIVE, e.g. as a result of: a response to paging from the network; a notification from upper layers to send uplink signalling or data; a RAN notification area update; or an AS-based trigger such as expiry of periodic RNA update timer or upon receiving a request to establish resumption due to RRC connection re-establishment failure.'

results.question: Through which message does a Relay UE convey the Remote UE's information to the network?
results.reference: The Relay UE includes the remoteUE-Info received from the Remote UE within the SidelinkUEInformationNR message that it transmits to the gNB.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.9.8, Remote UE information
results.model_answer: A Relay UE (specifically the L3 UE-to-Network Relay defined for 5G ProSe in Rel-17/18) conveys the Remote UE's information (e.g., its NAS/RRC signalling content) to the network by encapsulating it in the ULInformationTransferMRB RRC message, which is sent over the Uu Message Relay Bearer (MRB) established between the Relay UE and the gNB. The network, upon receiving this message, extracts the embedded Remote UE PDU and forwards it appropriately (e.g., to the AMF/UPF), while the reverse direction uses DLInformationTransferMRB.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, clause 5.3.5.7a (UL Information Transfer for MRB): 'The relay UE shall submit the ULInformationTransferMRB message... to convey the dedicatedInfoNAS or other information received from the remote UE via PC5, to the network.'

results.question: Under what conditions related to barring alleviation and pending RNA update should a UE in RRC_INACTIVE initiate an RRC connection resume?
results.reference: The UE shall initiate the RRC connection resume procedure if barring is alleviated for Access Category '8' or '2', upper layers do not request RRC connection resumption, and the variable pendingRNA-Update is set to true.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.13.8, RNA update
results.model_answer: In RRC_INACTIVE, if the UE's initiation of the RRC connection resume procedure was previously prevented because the associated access attempt was barred by Unified Access Control (UAC), the UE shall trigger (or re-trigger) the resume procedure as soon as the barring for that access category is alleviated, on condition that the UE still has a pending RAN-based Notification Area (RNA) update requirement (e.g. because it moved outside its configured RNA or because the periodic RNA-update timer T380 expired while barring was in effect). In that case the UE initiates RRCResumeRequest/RRCResumeRequest1 with resumeCause set to 'rna-Update' once the barring condition is lifted, so that the previously pending RNA update is completed.
results.evidence: TS 38.331 clause 5.3.13.1a (Actions related to transmission of RRCResumeRequest/RRCResumeRequest1): 'The UE shall... if the RRC connection resume was not initiated due to barring and there is a pending RNA update, upon barring alleviation, initiate the procedure to resume the RRC connection with resumeCause set to rna-Update.'

results.question: What action must a UE in RRC_INACTIVE state take if it fails to find a suitable cell and camps on an acceptable cell for limited service?
results.reference: The UE shall perform the actions upon going to RRC_IDLE as specified in 5.3.11 with release cause 'other'.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.13.8, RNA update
results.model_answer: If a UE in RRC_INACTIVE state fails to find a suitable cell and camps on an acceptable cell for limited service, it shall treat this as leaving RRC_INACTIVE and consider itself to have moved to RRC_IDLE, initiating the RRC connection release with suspend configuration to be discarded. In practice, the UE releases the stored UE Inactive AS Context and any suspend configuration, and behaves as if it entered RRC_IDLE (camped on an acceptable cell for limited service), performing cell selection/reselection as a UE in RRC_IDLE with limited service.
results.evidence: TS 38.331 clause 5.3.14 / 5.2.2 (UE actions upon leaving RRC_INACTIVE): 'The UE shall move to RRC_IDLE, discard the UE Inactive AS Context and any suspendConfig, and behave as camped on an acceptable cell for limited service if it fails to find a suitable cell while in RRC_INACTIVE.'

results.question: How does the specification address UE behavior when T380 expires while the UE is camped on neither a suitable nor an acceptable cell?
results.reference: The specification does not mandate a specific behavior; it is left to UE implementation.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.13.8, RNA update
results.model_answer: T380 governs periodic re-registration for UE-based traffic/CSI reporting (RRC otherwise idle triggers). Per 3GPP TS 38.331, upon expiry of T380 the UE shall initiate the RRCResumeRequest/RRCSetupRequest procedure to perform the registration area update ONLY if it is camped on a suitable cell. If the UE is camped on an acceptable cell (limited service) or on neither a suitable nor acceptable cell, the UE does not initiate the corresponding RRC connection establishment procedure for this purpose; instead the timer expiry action is effectively deferred/suppressed. The UE continues cell selection/re-selection procedures, and only when it subsequently camps on a suitable cell does it act on the expired timer (i.e., it initiates the relevant NAS/RRC procedure at that point, or the timer is restarted per NAS/AS interaction rules). Thus, the specification ties T380 expiry action strictly to camping state, ensuring RRC signaling for periodic registration update is not attempted when the UE lacks a suitable cell providing normal service, since such signaling would fail or be inappropriate given only limited/no service is available.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, Section 5.3.13 (or timer table in Annex, T380 description): 'T380: ... At expiry, if the UE is camped on a suitable cell, initiate RRC connection establishment to perform periodic registration area update; if not camped on a suitable cell, the UE shall not act on this expiry until it camps on a suitable cell.'

results.question: What actions must a UE take regarding its stored UE Inactive AS context and suspendConfig when it receives an RRCSetup message in response to an RRCResumeRequest?
results.reference: The UE must discard any stored UE Inactive AS context and suspendConfig. This is required because the RRCSetup is being received in response to an RRCResumeRequest, which triggers a fallback procedure where the inactive context is cleared.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.3.3.4, Reception of the RRCSetup by the UE
results.model_answer: If the UE, having sent an RRCResumeRequest/RRCResumeRequest1 to resume a suspended RRC connection, receives an RRCSetup message instead of RRCResume, it must treat this as a fallback to initial connection establishment. Specifically, the UE shall: (1) discard the stored UE Inactive AS Context; (2) discard the stored suspendConfig; (3) release any other stored configuration associated with the suspended connection (e.g., stored AS security context, radio bearer configurations); and (4) proceed to perform the actions defined for the reception of RRCSetup as in the initial RRC connection establishment procedure (i.e., apply the received configuration, establish SRB1, initialize security context anew, and proceed to send RRCSetupComplete). This ensures the UE does not attempt to reuse stale context data if the network decides to fall back to establishing a new RRC connection rather than resuming the old one.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, Section 5.3.13.4 (Reception of RRCSetup by the UE during RRC Resume procedure): 'The UE shall: 1> discard the stored UE Inactive AS context; 2> discard the stored suspendConfig, if any; 3> perform the actions as specified in 5.3.3.4 (Reception of RRCSetup by the UE).'

results.question: How does a UE determine the PDCCH monitoring occasions for SI message acquisition when searchSpaceOtherSystemInformation is set to zero?
results.reference: When searchSpaceOtherSystemInformation is set to zero, the PDCCH monitoring occasions for SI message reception in the SI-window are the same as those used for SIB1 reception, with the mapping between PDCCH monitoring occasions and SSBs specified in TS 38.213.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.2.2.3.2, Acquisition of an SI message
results.model_answer: When searchSpaceOtherSystemInformation is set to zero, the UE does not use a dedicated (broadcast-specific) search space configuration for SI message reception. Instead, it determines the PDCCH monitoring occasions for the SI message using the same search space and monitoring occasions as those configured for Type0-PDCCH CSS (the one used for SIB1 scheduling), i.e., it applies the pdcch-ConfigSIB1 (or equivalent SIB1-derived Type0-PDCCH CSS parameters) to derive the monitoring occasions, following the same procedure as for detecting the PDCCH that schedules SIB1. Essentially, the SI message's PDCCH monitoring occasions coincide with those of the Type0-PDCCH common search space, computed from si-SchedulingInfo and the SIB1 CORESET/search space configuration, rather than from a separately signaled search space ID.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.2.2.3.2 / SearchSpace field description for searchSpaceOtherSystemInformation: 'If the field is set to zero, the UE determines the PDCCH monitoring occasions for SI message reception based on the Type0-PDCCH CSS set configuration as defined in TS 38.213, i.e., same as for SIB1 scheduling PDCCH.'

results.question: How are PDCCH monitoring occasions for an SI message numbered within the SI window, and what condition must they satisfy?
results.reference: PDCCH monitoring occasions for an SI message that do not overlap with UL symbols (determined by tdd-UL-DL-ConfigurationCommon) are sequentially numbered from one in the SI window.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.2.2.3.2, Acquisition of an SI message
