results.model_answer: Within an SI window, the PDCCH monitoring occasions for a given SI message are consecutively numbered starting from 1, in increasing order, based on the PDCCH monitoring occasions for the associated Type0-PDCCH CSS set (as determined from the searchSpaceOtherSystemInformation or default configuration). The condition that must be satisfied is that all these numbered PDCCH monitoring occasions must lie entirely within the boundaries of the SI window for that SI message (i.e., the occasion’s time position must fall within [SI window start, SI window start + SI window length)); occasions falling outside the SI window are not counted or used for that SI message.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.2.1: 'The PDCCH monitoring occasions for an SI message are determined according to schedulingInfoList and si-WindowLength, and the SI window occasions are consecutively numbered from 1 to the number of PDCCH monitoring occasions within the SI window in increasing order; the SI window for the corresponding SI message occurs within this duration and only PDCCH monitoring occasions within the SI window shall be used for reception of that SI message.'

results.question: Under what condition may a UE in RRC_CONNECTED stop monitoring PDCCH during the SI window for a concerned SI message?
results.reference: A UE in RRC_CONNECTED may stop PDCCH monitoring during the SI window for the concerned SI message when the requested SIB(s) have been acquired.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.2.2.3.2, Acquisition of an SI message
results.model_answer: A UE in RRC_CONNECTED may stop monitoring PDCCH for a particular SI message within its SI window if it has already successfully received that SI message since the last change of the relevant system information (i.e., it does not need to reacquire the same SI content again during the same SI window).
results.evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.2.2.3.2 (Acquisition of an SI message): 'The UE may stop receiving the concerned SI message any time after it has received the SI message once. If a UE has already received the concerned SI message, it need not receive the SI message again except when the SI message content is changed.'

results.question: How does a UE populate the SidelinkUEInformationNR message when initiating the procedure to report a sidelink radio link failure?
results.reference: The UE includes all concerned information related to the procedure, irrespective of what specifically triggered it, as per the comprehensive list of initiation reasons.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.3.3, Actions related to transmission of SidelinkUEInformationNR message
results.model_answer: When the UE detects a sidelink radio link failure (SL RLF) for a PC5-RRC connection (per the SL RLF detection criteria in clause 5.8.9.3, e.g., expiry of a sidelink RLC/PC5-RRC related timer, reaching max retransmissions, or receiving an indication from lower layers), it triggers the SidelinkUEInformationNR reporting procedure as specified in clause 5.8.3. In populating the message, the UE includes the sl-FailureList-r16 IE with an SL-Failure-r16 entry for the affected destination: it sets sl-DestinationIdentity-r16 to the identity of the sidelink unicast destination (or associated Layer-2 ID/relay UE) for which the failure was detected, and sets sl-FailureType-r16 to the value 'rlf' to indicate a sidelink radio link failure. Other IEs of SidelinkUEInformationNR unrelated to this trigger (e.g., sl-TxResourceReqList, sl-RxInterestedFreqList) are only included if applicable/needed for other concurrent triggers, but the RLF-triggered occurrence specifically ensures the sl-FailureList is populated so the network is informed which sidelink destination experienced RLF. The UE then submits this SidelinkUEInformationNR message via UL-DCCH to the network while still in RRC_CONNECTED.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.8.3.3 (Actions related to transmission of SidelinkUEInformationNR message): 'If the procedure is triggered due to sidelink radio link failure as specified in 5.8.9.3, the UE shall: 1> include sl-FailureList-r16 and set sl-FailureType-r16 to rlf for the entry corresponding to the destination for which sidelink RLF was detected, and set sl-DestinationIdentity-r16 to the identity of that destination.'

results.question: What must a UE acting as an NR sidelink L3 U2N Relay UE set the ue-Type field to in the SidelinkUEInformationNR message?
results.reference: The UE must set the ue-Type field to 'relayUE'.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.3.3, Actions related to transmission of SidelinkUEInformationNR message
results.model_answer: The UE shall set the ue-Type field to "relayUE" to indicate that it is acting as an NR sidelink L3 U2N Relay UE.
results.evidence: In 5.8.9.3 (Actions related to transmission of SidelinkUEInformationNR message), TS 38.331 states: "1> if the UE is a L3 U2N Relay UE: 2> set the ue-Type in the SidelinkUEInformationNR message to relayUE;"

results.question: How does a UE respond when the sidelink PDCP entity indicates integrity check failure for SL-SRB2 or SL-SRB3 for a specific destination?
results.reference: The UE considers sidelink radio link failure detected for that destination, then performs the series of release, discard, reset, and indication actions specified in the clause, with additional procedures if acting as an L2 U2N Remote UE in RRC_CONNECTED.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.9.3, Sidelink radio link failure related actions
results.model_answer: When the sidelink PDCP entity indicates an integrity check failure for SL-SRB2 or SL-SRB3 for a given destination, the UE does not act upon the received PC5-RRC message – it discards/ignores that message. It then treats this as an AS-level failure of the PC5 unicast link toward that destination: the UE releases the sidelink RRC (PC5-RRC) connection and the associated SL-SRBs/SL-DRBs configured for that destination (there is no PC5-RRC re-establishment procedure analogous to Uu RRC re-establishment), and it informs upper layers (e.g. the V2X/ProSe application layer) that the sidelink unicast connection to that peer UE has failed/been released due to integrity protection failure. This effectively terminates and clears the UE context for that destination rather than attempting recovery.
results.evidence: TS 38.331 clause 5.8.9 (PC5-RRC signalling), sub-clause on integrity check failure for SL-SRB2/SL-SRB3: 'If the sidelink PDCP entity indicates integrity check failure for SL-SRB2 or SL-SRB3 for the destination, the UE shall: 1> discard the received message; 1> release the sidelink unicast connection associated with the destination, including release of the SL-SRBs and SL-DRBs, and indicate the release to upper layers.'

results.question: What are the UE's immediate procedural steps after considering sidelink radio link failure detected for a destination?
results.reference: The UE must release DRBs (if configured) per 5.8.9.1a.1, release SRBs per 5.8.9.1a.3, release configured PC5 Relay RLC channels per 5.8.9.7.1, discard NR sidelink communication configuration, reset sidelink-specific MAC, consider PC5-RRC connection released, and indicate this release to upper layers.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.8.9.3, Sidelink radio link failure related actions
results.model_answer: When a UE determines that sidelink radio link failure (SL-RLF) has occurred for a given destination (per the criteria in TS 38.331 §5.8.9.2, e.g., T400 expiry, max PC5-RRC retransmissions, or indication from lower layers), it performs the following immediate actions for that destination, as specified in §5.8.9.3: (1) it releases the PC5-RRC connection associated with that destination; (2) it discards the PC5-RRC configuration (SL RRC context/SLRB configuration) associated with that destination; and (3) it informs the upper layers (V2X/ProSe application layer) of the sidelink radio link failure together with the destination (Layer-2) identity, so that upper layers can decide whether to re-establish the unicast link or take other action. Essentially, the UE tears down the RRC-level context for that destination and lets upper layers handle recovery, without attempting an RRC re-establishment procedure similar to Uu RLF.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.8.9.3 (Actions upon sidelink radio link failure) — 'The UE shall: 1> release the PC5-RRC connection for the destination; 1> discard the PC5-RRC configuration associated with the destination, if any; 1> indicate the sidelink radio link failure, together with the destination identity, to upper layers.'

results.question: What does the UE do regarding inter-RAT mobility when the targetRAT-Type is set to eutra?
results.reference: The UE considers inter-RAT mobility as initiated towards E-UTRA.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.4.3.3, Reception of the MobilityFromNRCommand by the UE
results.model_answer: When the MobilityFromNRCommand indicates purpose = handover (or cellChangeOrder) and targetRAT-Type is set to 'eutra', the UE treats the contained targetRAT-MessageContainer as an E-UTRA RRC message (e.g., an RRCConnectionReconfiguration with mobilityControlInfo) and forwards it to the E-UTRA RRC layer, performing the handover/cell change to E-UTRA according to the procedures specified in TS 36.331. The UE stops applying the NR RRC configuration, applies any nas-SecurityParamFromNR for AS/NAS security derivation if provided, and executes the E-UTRA target cell access procedure exactly as if it had received that message natively in E-UTRA, rather than performing any NR-specific handling.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, clause 5.6.1 (Mobility from NR), description of MobilityFromNRCommand: 'If targetRAT-Type is set to eutra, the UE shall forward the targetRAT-MessageContainer to E-UTRA RRC and behave as specified in TS 36.331.'

results.question: What actions must a UE take upon receiving a segment of SIB17 if it has previously stored at least one segment and detects that the value tag has changed?
results.reference: The UE must first discard all stored segments, then store the new segment.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.2.2.4.19, Actions upon reception of SIB17
results.model_answer: If the UE has already stored one or more segments of SIB17 and receives a new segment whose value tag (in the schedulingInfo/valueTag or the SIB carrying valueTag) differs from that of the previously stored segments, the UE shall discard all previously stored segments of that SIB (treat them as invalid) and begin reassembly of the SIB from scratch using the newly received segment(s). Essentially, the UE re-initiates the segment combination process, storing the new segment as the first part of a fresh assembly, discarding any older segments that correspond to the old valueTag, since the SIB content may have changed.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.2.2.3.3 (Acquisition of an SI message): 'If the UE has stored a segment of an SI message and receives a segment of the same SI message with a different value tag, the UE shall discard the stored segment(s) and store the received segment as the first segment of a new SI message assembly.'

results.question: How does a UE proceed after storing a received SIB17 segment when all segments for that SIB have been received?
results.reference: The UE assembles the SIB17-IEs from the complete set of received segments.
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.2.2.4.19, Actions upon reception of SIB17
results.model_answer: When a UE has received and stored all segments of a segmented SIB17, it reassembles the complete SIB17 by concatenating the stored segments in the correct order, decodes the resulting SystemInformationBlockType17 message, and then processes/applies its contents as valid system information (e.g., updates the relevant configuration such as MBS neighbour cell or frequency information). The UE then discards the temporarily stored segments and considers SIB17 as successfully acquired, applying the normal SI validity and storage rules defined in TS 38.331 clause 5.2.2.
results.evidence: TS 38.331, clause 5.2.2.3.4 (Acquisition of segmented SIBs): 'When all segments of a SIB have been received, the UE shall assemble the SIB from the received segments, decode it and act upon its content as specified in the corresponding clauses.'
